faqs.question: What is the maximum annual subsidy provided for boat insurance, and how is it determined?

faqs.question: How does the Government determine the rate of subsidy for boat insurance, and is there a possibility of changes over time?
faqs.answer: The Government periodically reviews and may revise the rate of subsidy, considering factors affecting the insurance premium and overall scheme dynamics.

faqs.question: Is the maximum limit of ₹20,000 for annual insurance subsidy subject to change, and how is it determined?

faqs.question: What factors contribute to the Government's decision to revise the rate of subsidy for boat insurance?
faqs.answer: The rate of subsidy may be adjusted by the Government in response to changes in insurance dynamics, economic factors, or policy considerations.

faqs.question: Can an applicant qualify for the subsidy if their boat is not registered as mechanized?
faqs.answer: No, eligibility requires ownership of a registered mechanized boat to avail the subsidy on the annual insurance premium.

name: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana: Accident Insurance Scheme - Uttarakhand

faqs.answer: After verification, the Fisheries Department processes the insurance and issues an insurance certificate to the fisherman.

faqs.question: Who processes the claim after submission?
faqs.answer: The Department of Fisheries, in coordination with the insurance agency, verifies the claim documents and facilitates the disbursement of the claim amount.

name: Assistance for Installation of Sprinkler / Drip Micro Irrigation Systems
description: The scheme “Assistance for Installation of Sprinkler / Drip Micro Irrigation Systems" was launched by the Department of Agriculture and Farmer's Welfare, Union Territory of Puducherry. Through this scheme, the Marginal Farmers, Small farmers, Scheduled Caste/ Schedule Tribe Farmers, Women Farmers, Big Farmers and Institutions are provided with a subsidy on the total cost (or) ₹ 25,000/‐ per hectare whichever is less for the installation of Sprinkler / Drip Micro Irrigation Systems.
benefits: Subsidy of 90% of the total cost (or) ₹ 25,000/‐ per hectare whichever is less for Marginal Farmers, Small Farmers, Scheduled Caste/ Schedule Tribe and Women Farmers. Subsidy of 70% of the total cost (or) ₹ 25,000/‐ per hectare whichever is less for Big Farmers/ Institutions. The beneficiaries so selected will be intimated individually if the farmer completes the work on their own fund, the subsidy amount will be released by an Electronic clearing system in the farmer's bank accounts. If the farmer chooses manufacturers/ dealers, the subsidy amount will be released directly to the manufacturers/dealers' bank account after obtaining a satisfactory completion letter from the concerned farmer.
eligibility: The applicant should be a Marginal Farmer/ Small farmer/ Scheduled Caste Farmer/ Schedule Tribe Farmer/ Women Farmer/ Big Farmers/ Institutions. The farmers should own cultivable agricultural land in the Union Territory of Puducherry along with own/leased tubewell with adequate water and pumping system.. The farmers who have already availed the maximum subsidy amount during the past 10 years for the sprinkler irrigation system and the past 8 years for the drip irrigation systems are not eligible.. The farmers who have already installed micro irrigation system under this component and availed part of the maximum subsidy amount to install a micro-irrigation system during the past 10 years / 8 years in the additional area will be considered and they will be paid the balance amount duly deducting the already noted assistance from the maximum subsidy amount.. The land in which the installation of the micro irrigation system under this component, the period of 10 years for the sprinkler irrigation system and 8 years for the drip irrigation system will not be considered even if ownership has been changed.. Farmers who have availed of sprinkler irrigation systems earlier are also eligible for drip irrigation systems and vice‐versa, if the farmer opts to cultivate for intercrop for 3 years..
documents: A Revenue Certificate in the prescribed format issued by an authority not below the rank of Deputy Tahsildar of the Revenue Department. Photocopy of the Field Measurement Book (FMB) sketch of the land consented for the installation of micro irrigation system, electricity policy card of the tubewell used for irrigation, First

page bearing name, address and account number and last transaction page of Bank passbook. Farmers belonging to Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribes should enclose the Caste Certificate issued by an authority not below the rank of Deputy Tahsildar of the Revenue Department for claiming preference.

faqs.question: What is the maximum subsidy amount provided per hectare under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The maximum subsidy amount is [?]25,000 per hectare, or 90% of the total cost for Marginal, Small, Scheduled Caste/Schedule Tribe, and Women Farmers, and 70% for Big Farmers/Institutions.

faqs.question: Is there a specific duration for which the land should be owned for eligibility?
faqs.answer: Farmers must own cultivable land in the Union Territory of Puducherry to be eligible for the scheme, with no specific duration mentioned.

faqs.question: Can farmers who previously availed subsidies apply for additional areas under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers who installed micro-irrigation systems in the past 10 or 8 years can apply for additional areas, and the balance amount will be paid after deducting the previously noted assistance.

faqs.question: How is the subsidy amount released to manufacturers/dealers if chosen by the farmer?
faqs.answer: If farmers choose manufacturers/dealers, the subsidy amount is released directly to their bank account after obtaining a satisfactory completion letter from the concerned farmer.

faqs.question: Can farmers choose between completing the work independently or involving manufacturers/dealers?
faqs.answer: Yes, farmers have the option to either complete the work on their own or involve manufacturers/dealers, with the subsidy amount released accordingly.

faqs.question: Are farmers eligible for the scheme if they have previously installed micro irrigation systems?
faqs.answer: Farmers who have installed micro irrigation systems in the past 10 years for sprinkler systems or 8 years for drip systems are eligible, with the balance subsidy amount paid after deducting any previously received assistance.

faqs.question: What preference documentation is required for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe farmers?
faqs.answer: Farmers from Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe backgrounds should enclose a Caste Certificate issued by an authority not below the rank of Deputy Tahsildar of the Revenue Department for claiming preference.

faqs.question: Which documents are mandatory for farmers applying for this irrigation scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers need a Revenue Certificate, Field Measurement Book (FMB) sketch, electricity policy card of the tubewell, and bank passbook photocopies, including the first page with personal details and the last transaction page.

faqs.question: What is the time frame considered for ownership changes in the land under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The period of 10 years for sprinkler irrigation and 8 years for drip irrigation is not considered for ownership changes in the land where Micro Irrigation systems are installed.

faqs.question: Can farmers who previously received subsidies for sprinkler irrigation also apply for drip irrigation?
faqs.answer: Yes, farmers who availed sprinkler irrigation subsidies earlier are eligible for drip irrigation systems, and vice versa, provided they cultivate intercrop for three years.

faqs.question: How is the subsidy amount released to the beneficiaries, and what conditions apply?
faqs.answer: The subsidy amount is released through an Electronic clearing system. If farmers complete the work independently, the subsidy goes to their bank accounts. If manufacturers/dealers are chosen, the subsidy is released to their bank account upon satisfactory completion.

faqs.question: What percentage of the total cost is subsidized for Big Farmers and Institutions under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Big Farmers and Institutions are eligible for a 70% subsidy or [?]25,000 per hectare, whichever is less, for the installation of Sprinkler/Drip Micro Irrigation Systems.

name: "Agricultural Income Tax Holiday" under the "Assam Tea Industries Special Incentives Scheme"
description: Launched in 2020, the scheme "Assam Tea Industries Special Incentives Scheme (ATISIS)" by the Finance (Institutional Finance) Department, Government of Assam, aims to ensure long-term financial sustainability of the Tea industry and to incentivize manufacturers to move from Crush, Tear, Curl tea to Orthodox tea production. The scheme is implemented by the Finance Department and the Industries & Commerce Department, Government of Assam, through multiple implementing agencies, including banks and the District Industries & Commerce Centre. The applications for this scheme are accepted online through a dedicated portal with a Direct Benefit Transfer mechanism for reimbursement.
benefits: Benefit Period: 3 years of Agricultural Income Tax holiday. Applicable Financial Years: 2022-23 to 2024-25. Condition: Returns must be filed within the due date; if not filed on the due date, interest and penalty will be applicable.
eligibility: The applicant must be a tea plantation across all sizes.. The applicant must be a tea manufacturing unit manufacturing Crush, Tear, Curl Tea, Orthodox Tea, or Speciality tea including Green tea, Oolong Tea, White tea, Yellow tea and Purple tea.. The applicant must be located entirely in Assam.. The applicant must not have any part of the plantation or manufacturing facility located outside the State of Assam..
documents: Agricultural Income Tax Return Filing Documents. Tea Estate Registration Certificate. Common Documents for All Benefits. Aadhaar Card. Permanent Account Number Card. Business Registration Certificate. Bank Account Details. Address Proof of Unit Location in Assam.

Address Proof of Unit Location in Assam.

faqs.answer: The agricultural income tax holiday applies to the financial years 2022-23, 2023-24, and 2024-25.

faqs.question: What is the most important condition I must fulfill to continue enjoying the agricultural income tax holiday benefits?
faqs.answer: You must file your tax returns within the due date for each applicable financial year to maintain the tax holiday benefit.

faqs.question: What consequences will I face if I fail to file my tax returns by the due date during the tax holiday period?
faqs.answer: If you do not file returns by the due date, interest and penalty charges will become applicable despite the tax holiday.

faqs.answer: You are eligible if you manufacture Crush, Tear, Curl tea, Orthodox tea, or Speciality tea including Green tea, Oolong tea, White tea, Yellow tea, and Purple tea.

faqs.answer: Yes, your entire tea plantation must be located within the State of Assam without any part outside the state.

faqs.answer: No, you cannot qualify if any part of your plantation or manufacturing facility is located outside the State of Assam.

faqs.answer: You can be eligible as either a tea plantation across all sizes or as a tea manufacturing unit producing the specified types of tea.

faqs.question: What is the primary objective behind offering this agricultural income tax holiday to tea industry participants?
faqs.answer: The scheme aims to ensure long-term financial sustainability of the tea industry and incentivize manufacturers to move from Crush, Tear, Curl tea to Orthodox tea production.

faqs.question: Which government departments are responsible for implementing this agricultural income tax holiday scheme in Assam?
faqs.answer: The scheme is implemented by the Finance Department and the Industries & Commerce Department, Government of Assam.

faqs.question: What agencies will be involved in the actual implementation and processing of my tax holiday application?
faqs.answer: The scheme is implemented through multiple agencies including banks and the District Industries & Commerce Centre along with the government departments.

faqs.question: How can I apply for this agricultural income tax holiday and what is the application submission method?
faqs.answer: Applications for this scheme are accepted online through a dedicated portal with a streamlined digital submission process.

faqs.question: What mechanism is used for providing the tax holiday benefits and how will I receive confirmation of the same?
faqs.answer: The scheme uses a Direct Benefit Transfer mechanism for processing and confirming the agricultural income tax holiday benefits.

name: Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure
description: The scheme envisages value addition and processing at farmers level so as to enhance their income by selling more marketable and processed produce in the market. For creation of Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure including scientific Storage capacity, the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Govt. of India is implementing capital subsidy sub-scheme “Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure (AMI)” of Integrated Scheme for Agricultural Marketing (ISAM) across the country and is continued till 31.03.2026 Projects for creation of storage infrastructure (50-5000 MT for Private &Cooperatives and 50-10,000 MT for State agencies) and other marketing infrastructure projects (other than storage) are eligible for assistance under the scheme. AMI is an open ended, demand driven, credit linked, back ended subsidy scheme. Beneficiaries viz, Individuals, Agri-preneurs, farmers, FPOs, Cooperatives, and state agencies etc. are eligible for assistance. Under the scheme, the subsidy @ 25% for plain areas and 33.33% for NER, hilly area, Women/SC/ST promoters & FPOs etc is available for development of Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure Projects including storage infrastructure, Infrastructure for development/Upgradation of Rural Haats as Grameen Agricultural Market (GrAMs), Common Facilitation Centre for FPOs, Marketing infrastructures in market yards, Infrastructure for direct marketing, Mobile infrastructure for post-harvest operations including reefer vans, Stand-alone cold storages up to 1000 MTs, Integrated Value Chain (IVC) Projects up to primary processing stage etc. Assistance under the sub-scheme is inter-alia available to Individuals, Farmers, Group of farmers/growers, Registered Farmer Produce Organizations (FPOs) / FPCs, firms, companies, corporations, NGOs, SHGs, Cooperatives, Cooperative Marketing Federations, Autonomous Bodies of the Government, Local Bodies, Panchayats, State Agencies etc.

name: Atma Nirbhar Bagwani Yojana

name: Atma Nirbhar Krishi Yojana
description: Atma Nirbhar Krishi Yojana (ANKY) is an ambitious scheme launched by the Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh with the aim of promoting self-reliance in the agriculture sector. Under this scheme, farmers are provided with financial assistance and support for various agricultural activities. The scheme focuses on scientific land terracing, doubling cropping, farm mechanization, and apiculture among other activities. Farmers can avail loans of up to Rs. 1.60 lakhs without collateral to invest in these activities. The implementation of the scheme is overseen by a state-level committee headed by the Chief Minister. Various banks participate in providing loans under this scheme, enabling farmers to access financial resources easily.
benefits: Financial assistance for agricultural activities: The scheme provides financial support to farmers for activities like scientific land terracing, doubling cropping, farm mechanization, and apiculture. Loan without collateral: Farmers can avail loans up to Rs. 1.60 lakhs without the need for collateral, facilitating access to financial resources. Enhanced productivity: By implementing modern farming techniques and practices, farmers can improve their productivity and income. Empowerment of farmers: The scheme empowers farmers by providing them with financial resources and technical assistance to enhance their agricultural practices. Promotes self-reliance: ANKY aims to make farmers self-reliant by enabling them to invest in various agricultural activities and reduce dependence on external factors. Encourages diversified cropping: The scheme promotes the cultivation of different crops, including fruits like apple, kiwi, orange, areca nut, walnut, and persimmon, leading to diversification and increased income for farmers. Support for women in agriculture: ANKY provides a platform for women farmers and members of self-help groups to access financial resources and contribute to the agricultural sector.

faqs.answer: Yes, farmers from all districts of Arunachal Pradesh are eligible to apply for the Atmanirbhar Krishi Yojana and Atmanirbhar Bagwani Yojana. These schemes are aimed at benefiting farmers across the state and promoting agricultural and horticultural activities in Arunachal Pradesh.

name: Arun Pig Development Scheme
department: Animal husbandry, Veterinary and Dairy Department
description: The scheme “Arun Pig Development Scheme” was launched by the Department of Animal Husbandry, Veterinary & Dairy Development, Government of Arunachal Pradesh in the financial year 2019-20 with a focus on pig rearing. Among the livestock species, the pig finds an important place as it is being reared by socio-economically weaker sections of the society especially in the states like Arunachal Pradesh where most of people prefer non-veg cuisines with special attractions for Pork. The pig as compared to other livestock species has a great potential to contribute to a faster economic return to the farmers, because of certain inherent traits like high fecundity, better-feed conversion efficiency, early maturity, and short generation interval. Pig farming also requires small investments in buildings and equipment. Objective Genetic improvement of the indigenous pigs of Arunachal Pradesh for productivity enhancement by crossbreeding with the exotic breed(s) to a desired level of combination of exotic and local inheritance, Improvement of indigenous pig rearing by the rural people by selective breeding, Livelihood earning Maintenance of well-planned crossbred animals at farmers’ field Expansion of piggery husbandry and support mechanism to propagate pig rearing in rural areas Ensure that the breeds introduced, and crossbreds produced and propagated in the state are adapted to local environmental conditions and emerging climatic challenges, Strengthen support mechanisms and development of the sector in respect of feeding, housing, and health care besides value addition and marketing of the product with value chain development. Scientific rearing and motivation of farmers for integrated piggery farming. Important Features Seeing the low interest of the actual grass root level farmer for the credit link schemes and their poor success rate, a new venture for piggery development in the state through direct intervention by the Department of AHV&DD, GoAP in terms of upgradation of genetic resources, and other peripherals, a new and innovative scheme is proposed for Budget Announcement 2019-20 for sustainable development and poverty alleviation of Farmers through Pig Rearing in potential districts of Arunachal Pradesh. Livelihood earning, improvement of indigenous pig rearing by the rural people by selective breeding along with maintenance of well-planned crossbred animals at farmers’ fields. Expansion of piggery husbandry and support mechanism to propagate pig rearing in rural areas. Ensure that the breeds introduced, and crossbreds produced and propagated in the state are adapted to local environmental conditions and emerging climatic challenges.
benefits: farmers will be given piggery subsidy (25% beneficiary contribution and 75% government contribution). Piglets will be procured by the District Administration and handed over to the farmers after ensuring that a suitable sty was constructed by the selected farmer. name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Exchange Programme
department: Farmer Welfare and Agriculture Development Department
description: The “Annapurna Scheme” was launched by the Department of Farmers Welfare and Agricultural Development, Government of Madhya Pradesh. The “Seed Exchange Programme” component of the scheme aims to improve the economic status of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe small and marginal farmers by providing them with economic assistance to access improved seeds of high-yielding foodgrain crops, thereby increasing productivity and production. The scheme is implemented by the Directorate of Agriculture through the District Panchayats, Sub-Directorate of Agriculture, and the Senior Agriculture Development Officer. The applications for this scheme are accepted by the Rural Agriculture Extension Officer based on targets set according to the population of the target groups and the district's demand.
benefits: Provision of improved seeds of high-yielding varieties of foodgrain crops. 75% subsidy on the actual price of the seed provided in exchange. The maximum limit of the subsidy is ₹1,500/-. Seeds of suitable varieties for the land and area will be provided in equal quantity compared to the seed provided by the farmer. The provision is limited to a maximum area of one hectare. Certified seed will be provided. Conditions The seeds supplied must be of the improved variety, prioritizing those that are suitable for or prevalent in the area. If certified seed is scarce, or depending on the specific crop condition, true form seed may be distributed only with the permission of the Director of Agriculture. If the farmer provides seed of a different crop for exchange, the seed given by the farmer must be worth 25% of the actual price of the certified seed of the requested crop. The improved seed provided to the farmer will not exceed the requirement for one hectare. The seed received from the beneficiary farmer must be sold through auction (Ghosh Vikray) at the local Agricultural Produce Market Committee by a designated committee. Cash received as the farmer's share or resulting from the auction of the grain provided by the farmer must be deposited into the Government Treasury by challan under Head 0401 Agriculture Work, Other Deposit - 800 Other Deposit. If a farmer who previously received seed is given seed again, it must not be for the same crop or variety provided in prior years.
eligibility: The applicant must belong to the Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe category.. The applicant must be a small or marginal farmer.. The applicant must be unable to afford the purchase of improved varieties of high-yielding foodgrain crops.. Post-Selection Conditions. The farmer must exchange their existing crop or seed for the improved seeds..

faqs.question: What are the specific socioeconomic and landholding categories that must be met by applicants wishing to participate in this particular assistance program?
faqs.answer: The applicant must be categorized as a small or marginal farmer. Additionally, the applicant must belong to either the Scheduled Caste or the Scheduled Tribe category.

faqs.question: If I am a former beneficiary, am I permitted to receive improved seeds again, and if so, are there any restrictions on the crop or variety?
faqs.answer: Yes, but if an old farmer is provided seed again, it must be for a different crop or variety than those previously supplied in prior years.

faqs.question: Is there a strict maximum limit imposed on the amount of improved seed that can be provided to a single beneficiary farmer, based on land measurement?
faqs.answer: Yes, the provision of improved seeds is strictly limited to the requirement necessary for a maximum area of 1 hectare.

faqs.question: What is the maximum financial amount or ceiling placed on the subsidy component provided to the selected beneficiaries for the cost of the exchange seed?
faqs.answer: The subsidy provided is limited to a maximum amount of ₹1,500/-.

faqs.question: What specific quality standard or certification level must the high-yielding variety seed supplied to the eligible farmers generally adhere to?
faqs.answer: Certified seed will be provided. If certified seed is scarce, the Director of Agriculture may permit the distribution of true form seed for specific crops.

faqs.question: If I offer seed of a crop different from the high-yielding seed I wish to receive, how is the required value of my provided seed calculated?
faqs.answer: The seed provided by the farmer must be equivalent to 25% of the actual price of the requested certified seed of the crop they wish to receive.

faqs.question: What unique action must a farmer perform concerning their existing harvest or crops in order to successfully receive the improved seeds provided by the program?
faqs.answer: Applicants must provide their existing crop or seed to be exchanged for the improved, high-yielding variety seeds offered under the scheme.

faqs.question: During the official approval process by the Janpad Panchayat’s Agriculture Standing Committee, how is priority assigned among the selected applicants?
faqs.answer: Names that are listed first in the approved primary list of farmers prepared by the Rural Agriculture Extension Officer will be given priority.

faqs.question: For how long will the prepared waiting list of farmers, whose names were not prioritized in the final selection, remain valid or active?
faqs.answer: The waiting list is considered final and remains valid only until the current crop season concludes.

faqs.question: What exact percentage of the actual price of the improved seed being provided in exchange will be covered by the subsidy available under the guidelines?
faqs.answer: Applicants are eligible for a 75% subsidy on the actual price of the seed provided in exchange by the distribution organization.

faqs.question: When exchanging my existing crop or seed, will the improved seeds I receive in return be provided based on mass or volume equivalence?
faqs.answer: The improved seeds of suitable varieties will be provided in a quantity equal to the quantity of the seed provided by the farmer for exchange.

faqs.question: Is there a prerequisite concerning my existing financial capacity to purchase high-yielding varieties of foodgrain crops before applying for this benefit?
faqs.answer: Yes, the applicant must be a farmer who is currently unable to afford the purchase of improved varieties of high-yielding foodgrain crops.

faqs.question: When selecting the type of improved seed to provide, what key characteristic or factor is given the primary consideration by the implementing authorities?
faqs.answer: Priority is given to improved varieties of foodgrain crops that are suitable for or prevalent in the specific geographical area of the farmer.

faqs.question: How many potential farmers, relative to the actual established district target, does the Rural Agriculture Extension Officer typically select initially?
faqs.answer: The Rural Agriculture Extension Officer selects 1.5 times the number of required beneficiaries compared to the established physical target.

name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Multiplication Programme
department: Farmer Welfare and Agriculture Development Department
description: The “Annapurna Scheme” was launched by the Department of Farmers Welfare and Agricultural Development, Government of Madhya Pradesh. The “Seed Exchange Programme” component of the scheme aims to improve the economic status of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe small and marginal farmers by providing them with economic assistance to access improved seeds of high-yielding foodgrain crops, thereby increasing productivity and production. The scheme is implemented by the Directorate of Agriculture through the District Panchayats, Sub-Directorate of Agriculture, and the Senior Agriculture Development Officer. The applications for this scheme are accepted by the Rural Agriculture Extension Officer based on targets set according to the population of the target groups and the district's demand.
benefits: Provision of Breeder or Certified I Grade Seeds for seed production. A 75% subsidy is provided on the Breeder or Certified Seed. The subsidy is applicable for a maximum area of 1 hectare. The payment of registration fees required by the Seed Certification Agency, including the application fee, registration fee, inspection fee, and sample fee, is covered from the scheme funds. Conditions The produced seeds must be made available to other Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe farmers under the scheme at a fair price in the subsequent year. An agreement (Anubandh) must be executed between the department and the beneficiary through the Seed Production Committee or Farm Superintendent to ensure seed production, marketing (muktjan), and payment according to policy. The entire agricultural methodology (Sampuurna Krishi Kaaryamaala) must be adopted for higher production. Undesirable plants (Avaanchhaniy Paudhon) must be separated to maintain seed purity. The raw seed produced under the program will undergo grading, processing, stacking, and packing at the Government Agricultural Farm or at the processing center of the Seed Corporation or other institutions if facilities are unavailable at the farm. The expenditure incurred on grading, processing, stacking, and packing of raw seeds produced at Government Agricultural Farms may be met by the Deputy Director of Agriculture from the scheme funds, provided the prepared seed is used only under the scheme. The remaining amount, after deducting the processing expenditure from the prescribed price of the supplied seed, must be deposited in the Government Treasury by challan towards payment to the Government Agricultural Farm.

faqs.question: How much financial assistance, calculated as a%age of the total seed price, will be granted to the successful participating farmers?
faqs.answer: A 75% subsidy is provided on the cost of the Foundation (Aadhaar) or Certified I grade (Pramanit I shreni) seed supplied for participation in the program.

faqs.question: Is it a mandatory requirement for all cultivators participating in this production component to officially register with the quality control institution?
faqs.answer: Yes, cultivators are mandatorily required to register with the Seed Certification Agency (Bija Pramanikaran Sanstha).

faqs.question: What is the minimum land area required for a cultivator to dedicate to this particular agricultural activity to qualify for the benefits?
faqs.answer: The production activity must be undertaken in a minimum area of $1/2$ acre (0.2 hectare) by the participating cultivator.

faqs.question: Does the land where the production work takes place need to be situated within a certain proximity to designated government facilities?
faqs.answer: Yes, the applicant's land must be located within a 10 kilometer perimeter of the selected Government Agricultural Farms (Shaaskiya Krishi Prakshetra).

faqs.question: What is the official deadline for submitting the mandatory application form for quality certification after the sowing of the crops has been completed?
faqs.answer: The registration application form must be submitted within 20 days of sowing or before the final date fixed by the government.

faqs.question: If a large number of eligible individuals apply, how is the official priority list for the selection process determined?
faqs.answer: The Gramin Krishi Vistar Adhikari (Rural Agricultural Extension Officer) selects 1.5 times the target, and priority is given to the names listed first on the approved list.

faqs.question: Who is responsible for bearing the cost of mandatory fees related to application, inspection, and sample testing required by the certification body?
faqs.answer: The payment for registration fees, including the application fee, registration fee, inspection fee, and sample fee, is covered using funds from the scheme budget.

faqs.question: Is there a defined maximum limit on the total land area for which a farmer can receive the subsidized planting material under this program?
faqs.answer: Yes, eligibility for the 75% subsidy is restricted to a maximum area of 1 hectare for each participating farmer.

faqs.question: Which specific grades or classifications of high-yielding food grain seeds will be distributed to the selected beneficiaries for multiplication?
faqs.answer: Foundation (Aadhaar) or Certified I grade (Pramanit I shreni) seed of high-yielding food grain crops will be made available for production.

faqs.question: What is the obligation regarding the distribution or utilization of the certified quality seed produced under the umbrella of this program?
faqs.answer: The produced certified seed must be made available at prescribed rates to other Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe farmers under the scheme in the subsequent year.

faqs.question: How must the remaining 25% of the actual cost of the quality seed, after the subsidy is applied, be settled by the applicant?
faqs.answer: The remaining seed cost must be settled by the cultivator either in cash (nagad) or through their own seed, which will be valued at the support price.

faqs.question: Where will the activities necessary for post-harvest preparation, such as grading, stacking, and packing of the raw produce, be performed?
faqs.answer: These processes will be conducted at the Government Agricultural Farm or, if facilities are unavailable there, at the processing center of the Seed Corporation or other institutions.

faqs.question: What steps must the farmer take concerning cultivation practices to ensure the purity and quality of the final high-yielding production?
faqs.answer: The complete agricultural methodology (Sampuurna Krishi Kaaryamaala) must be adopted for higher production, and undesirable plants (Avaanchhaniy Paudhon) must be removed to maintain seed purity.

faqs.question: Is there any specific legal document or formal understanding that needs to be executed between the farmer and the implementing department?
faqs.answer: Yes, an agreement (Anubandh) must be executed between the department and the beneficiary through the Seed Production Committee or Farm Superintendent to ensure production, marketing, and payment are compliant with policy.

name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Production Programme
department: Farmer Welfare and Agriculture Development Department
description: The “Annapurna Scheme” was launched by the Department of Farmers Welfare and Agricultural Development, Government of Madhya Pradesh. The “Seed Production Programme” component of the scheme aims to improve the economic condition of small and marginal farmers belonging to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes by providing economic assistance for improved seeds, thereby increasing productivity and production. The scheme provides Foundation or Certified Grade I seeds of improved, high-yielding food grain crops to selected farmers for seed production up to a limit of 1 hectare, along with a 75% subsidy on the actual cost of the seed.
benefits: Provision of Foundation or Certified Grade I seeds of improved varieties of high-yielding food grain crops for seed production. Eligibility for a 75% subsidy on the actual cost of the Foundation or Certified seed up to a maximum area of 1 hectare. Payment for registration (application fee, registration fee, inspection fee, and sample fee) with the Seed Certification Agency will be covered from the scheme budget. Technical training and necessary information will be provided by the Rural Agricultural Extension Officer, Senior Agricultural Development Officer, and Subject Matter Specialist (Sub-Divisional level). Guaranteed procurement of the produced seed by the Seed Production Committee or Farm Superintendent at government-fixed rates. Expenditure related to the grading, processing, stocking, and packing of raw seeds produced on Government agricultural farms can be carried out by the Deputy Director of Agriculture from the scheme budget. Conditions The farmer must utilize the seed provided for a maximum area of 1 hectare and a minimum area of 0.2 hectares (1/2 acre). The farmer must adopt the complete package of agricultural practices for higher production. The farmer must ensure the removal of undesirable plants to maintain seed purity. The farmer must sign an agreement with the department through the Seed Production Committee or Farm Superintendent regarding seed production, procurement, and payment according to the policy. The farmer must pay the remaining 25% of the seed cost in cash or by providing their own seed. If the farmer provides their own seed, the price of that seed will be determined based on the support price. The produced Certified Seed must be made available to other Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe farmers under the scheme in the subsequent year. The expenditure incurred on processing, grading, stocking, and packing will be deducted from the fixed price of the supplied seed, and the remaining amount must be deposited into the government treasury.
eligibility: The applicant must belong to the Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe.. The applicant must be a small or marginal farmer.. The applicant must be willing to participate in the “Seed Production Programme”.. The applicant must operate within the 10-kilometer periphery of the selected Government agricultural farms.. The applicant must conduct the program on a minimum area of 0.2 hectares (1/2 acre).. The applicant must be eligible for a maximum grant up to 1 hectare.. The applicant must mandatorily register with the Seed Certification Agency.. The plan includes the food grain crops Paddy (Dhan), Jowar, Bajra, Maize, Kodo, Kutki, Ragi (for Kharif), and Wheat (Gehu), Barley (Jau) (for Rabi).. faqs.question: Must participants intending to increase agricultural productivity necessarily belong to the specific population groups known as Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe categories?
faqs.answer: Yes, participation in the Seed Production Programme is exclusively limited to small and marginal farmers who are confirmed members of the Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe communities.

faqs.question: What specific farming techniques are mandated during the growing season to ensure the produced seeds meet the required purity standards?
faqs.answer: Farmers must adopt the complete package of agricultural practices for higher production and mandatorily ensure the removal of undesirable plants to maintain seed purity.

faqs.question: If I receive Foundation or Certified seed through the program, what%age of the actual seed cost must be contributed by the farmer?
faqs.answer: The farmer must pay the remaining 25% of the seed cost; the scheme provides a 75% subsidy on the actual cost of the Foundation or Certified seed.

faqs.question: What is the smallest required area of land, measured in either hectares or acres, that a participant must use for the seed production program?
faqs.answer: The program must be conducted by the farmer on a minimum area of 1/2 acre (0.2 hectares).

faqs.question: Am I restricted on the maximum amount of land I can use to sow the Foundation or Certified seed that is provided to me by the department?
faqs.answer: Yes, the farmer must utilize the seed provided for a maximum area of 1 hectare.

faqs.question: How close must my farming operation be located to a designated Government agricultural farm to qualify for the seed supply program?
faqs.answer: The applicant must reside and operate their farm within the 10-kilometer periphery of the selected Government agricultural farms.

faqs.question: If the number of applicants exceeds the available targets, what criteria determine which names receive priority selection?
faqs.answer: Preference should be given to the names listed first in the approved list of beneficiaries.

faqs.question: What quality level of seeds, such as Foundation or Certified Grade, will be made available to farmers participating in the production activity?
faqs.answer: Farmers will be provided with Foundation or Certified Grade I seeds of improved, high-yielding food grain varieties.

faqs.question: Do the requirements state that I must hold a particular size of land holding, such as being classified as a small or marginal farmer, to qualify?
faqs.answer: Yes, the applicant must meet the criteria of being identified as a small farmer or a marginal farmer.

faqs.question: Is there a maximum limit set on the agricultural land area for which an applicant can receive subsidized seed under this production initiative?
faqs.answer: The eligibility for the grant is limited up to a maximum area of 1 hectare.

faqs.question: Must an interested applicant explicitly declare their intention or willingness to participate in the entire Seed Production Programme process?
faqs.answer: Yes, the applicant must be willing and interested in participating in the Seed Production Programme.

faqs.question: Which specific high-yielding food grain crops are included for seed production purposes during the Kharif and Rabi seasons under these guidelines?
faqs.answer: Kharif crops include Paddy (Dhan), Jowar, Bajra, Maize, Kodo, Kutki, and Ragi; Rabi crops include Wheat (Gehu) and Barley (Jau).

faqs.question: What administrative steps are required to ensure the purity and quality of the crop produced, specifically regarding certification standards?
faqs.answer: It is mandatory for the farmers to register with the Seed Certification Agency, and this application must be submitted within 20 days of sowing or before the government-fixed final date.

faqs.question: If I am required to cover the remaining 25% of the improved seed cost, how can I make this required contribution?
faqs.answer: The remaining amount can be paid in cash or by providing your own seed, the price of which will be valued based on the support price.

name: Assistance to Scheduled Caste Farmers for Installation of Submersible / Centrifugal Motor Pumpsets With Accessories
description: The scheme “Assistance to Scheduled Caste Farmers for Installation of Submersible / Centrifugal Motor Pumpsets With Accessories" was launched by the Department of Agriculture and Farmer's Welfare, Union Territory of Puducherry. Through this scheme, the farmers from the Scheduled Caste Category are provided with a grant of 90% subsidy towards the installation of suitable Submersible / Centrifugal motor pump sets with accessories, subject to a maximum of ₹60,000/‐ per tubewell per individual.
benefits: 90% subsidy towards the installation of suitable Submersible / Centrifugal motor pump sets with accessories, subject to a maximum of ₹60,000/‐ per tubewell per individual. NOTE: The subsidy amount shall be released through the Electronic Clearing System (ECS) if the applicant has undertaken the construction with his/her funds. In case, he/she has availed himself/herself loan from the Nationalized Bank / Co‐operative Bank towards the construction of the tubewell, the subsidy amount shall be remitted to the Bank against the loan account of the beneficiary.
eligibility: The applicant should be from the Scheduled Caste Category.. The applicant should be a farmer in the Union Territory of Puducherry.. The tubewell in which the submersible/centrifugal motor pump sets is going to be erect and should have been registered in Pondicherry Ground Water Authority, Puducherry.. The applicant should hold a minimum of 1.5 acres of land under the command area of the tubewell to be constructed and the applicant should have ownership of the land at least for 2 years and should have a clear ownership title deed in his/her name. The eligible land holding of 1.5 acres should be in favour of the applicant farmer or in favour of the spouse or favour of the member of a joint/undivided family.. The farmers who have already availed themselves of the subsidy for the said purpose within 5 years are not entitled to any benefit under this scheme.. The applicant should not convert the lands for a maximum period of 10 years from the date of construction of the tubewell/filter point to any purpose other than agriculture and should execute a bond accordingly..

faqs.question: Can the land be mortgaged, sold, or transferred during the 10-year commitment period?
faqs.answer: No, the land cannot be mortgaged, sold, or transferred to any other person during the 10-year commitment period specified in the affidavit.

faqs.question: What action may the government take if a beneficiary breaches the scheme's conditions?
faqs.answer: In case of a breach, the government may take legal action and initiate recovery/cancellation of subsidy from the beneficiary.

faqs.question: How is the subsidy amount released if the applicant uses personal funds for construction?
faqs.answer: If the applicant uses personal funds for construction, the subsidy amount is released through the Electronic Clearing System (ECS).

faqs.question: What is the role of the Pondicherry Ground Water Authority in the scheme?
faqs.answer: The authority issues the registration certificate, permit, and energization certificate for the tubewell.

faqs.question: Can the applicant convert the land for purposes other than agriculture during the 10-year restriction period?
faqs.answer: No, the applicant is prohibited from converting the land for any purpose other than agriculture during the 10-year restriction period.

faqs.question: What authority registers the tubewell in which the pump sets are to be installed?
faqs.answer: The tubewell should be registered with the Pondicherry Ground Water Authority, Puducherry.

faqs.question: What should beneficiaries submit after selection to affirm their commitment to the scheme's conditions?
faqs.answer: Upon selection, beneficiaries must submit an affidavit, signed before a Notary Public, committing to retain and use the land for agriculture for a period of 10 years.

faqs.question: Is there a time restriction for applicants who have previously availed themselves of the subsidy?
faqs.answer: Farmers who have received the subsidy for the same purpose within the last 5 years are not eligible for benefits under this scheme.

faqs.question: Who issues the certificate for ownership of the land, and what rank should the officer hold?
faqs.answer: The certificate for land ownership must be issued by an officer not below the rank of Deputy Tahsildar.

faqs.question: Are there any restrictions on converting the land after tubewell construction?
faqs.answer: Applicants are prohibited from converting the land for purposes other than agriculture for a period of 10 years, as specified in a bond.

faqs.question: What is the minimum land requirement for eligibility under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Applicants must hold a minimum of 1.5 acres of land under the command area of the tubewell, with ownership for at least 2 years.

faqs.question: How is the subsidy amount disbursed if the applicant has availed a loan for tubewell construction?
faqs.answer: The subsidy is remitted to the bank against the loan account if the applicant has taken a loan from a Nationalized Bank or Co-operative Bank.

name: Assistance to Scheduled Castes for Fisheries: Fish Collection Cum Patrolling Boat Gujarat
department: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department
description: The scheme "Assistance to Scheduled Castes for Fisheries" with the component of "Fish Collection Cum Patrolling Boat" introduced by the Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Co-operation Department, Government of Gujarat, aims to increase fish production in reservoirs and provide employment to Scheduled Caste (SC) individuals engaged in inland fisheries. Through this scheme, financial assistance is provided for purchasing fish collection cum patrolling boats, thereby supporting SC leaseholders involved in reservoir-based fisheries. The scheme is implemented by the Commissioner of Fisheries, Government of Gujarat. Objectives: To increase fish production by rearing fish in reservoirs and provide employment to scheduled caste (SC) people involved in inland fisheries activities. To boost fish farming or fishing activities in freshwater bodies by scheduled caste (SC) fish farmers and fishermen. Fishing in reservoirs, aquaculture in ponds, and catch from rivers increase fish production and boost inland fisheries through scheduled caste (SC) fish farmers and fishermen. The main objective is to provide employment opportunities to Scheduled Caste fishermen in the state and increase fish production.
benefits: The unit cost to Scheduled Caste Leaseholders is ₹5,00,000/-. Assistance is provided at 75% of the unit cost, which is ₹3,75,000/-, or 75% of the purchase price, whichever is less. The Unit cost for a four-wheel vehicle for the transport of fish to a Scheduled Caste lessee is ₹6,00,000/-. name: Assistance to Scheduled Caste Farmers for Sinking Tubewell
description: The scheme “Assistance to Scheduled Caste Farmers for Sinking Tubewell" was launched by the Department of Agriculture and Farmer's Welfare, Union Territory of Puducherry. Through this scheme, the farmers from the Scheduled Caste Category are provided with a grant of 90% subsidy towards the construction of tubewell/filter point in Puducherry subject to a maximum of ₹1,80,000 per tubewell/filter point per individual.
benefits: Grant of 90% subsidy to General Farmers towards construction of tubewell/filter point in the Union Territory of Puducherry subject to a maximum of ₹1,80,000 per tubewell/filter point per individual. The total cost incurred towards the construction of the tubewell shall be taken into account for the calculation of the subsidy.
eligibility: The applicant should belong to the Scheduled Caste Community. The applicant should be an Indian National and native of the Union Territory of Puducherry by birth or by continuous residence for the past 5 years.. The applicant must obtain the necessary permit to sink a new/replacement tubewell/filter point from Pondicherry Ground Water Authority, Puducherry.. The tubewell/Filter point should have been constructed through a departmental power rig/hand bore set or should have been constructed with a No Objection Certificate of the Agriculture Department for engaging private drilling machinery registered with Pondicherry Ground Water Authority under departmental supervision.. The applicant should hold a minimum of 1.5 acres of land under the command area of the tubewell/filter point to be constructed.. The applicant should have ownership of the land for at least 2 years and a clear ownership title deed in his/her name.. The eligible land holding of 1.5 acres should be in favour of the applicant farmer, spouse, or a member of the joint/undivided family.. Farmers who have already availed themselves of the subsidy for the same purpose within 5 years are not entitled to any benefit under this scheme.. The casing pipes should have a BIS certificate and should have been purchased from an authorized dealer/M/s.PASIC Ltd.. The brand of pipes is left to the choice of the applicant but pipes should be BIS certified and should have been purchased either from PASIC or from the list of authorized dealers.. The applicant should not convert the lands for a minimum period of 10 years from the date of construction of the tubewell/filter point to any purpose other than agriculture and should execute a bond accordingly..
documents: Nationality, Nativity, and Caste certificate issued by an officer, not below the rank of Deputy Tahsildar. The certificate for land ownership issued by an officer, not below the rank of Deputy Tahsildar. A copy of the PERMIT obtained from the Pondicherry Ground Water Authority, Puducherry, for sinking a New/Replacement tubewell/filter point. The Registration Certificate for the tubewell/filter point, issued by Pondicherry Ground Water Authority, Puducherry. In the case of a new service connection, provide a copy of the energization letter obtained from the Pondicherry Ground Water Authority, Puducherry. If the tubewell/filter point was constructed using private machinery, submit (i) a copy of the NOC issued by the competent authority and (ii) a copy of the License for the private machinery issued by the Pondicherry Ground Water Authority, Puducherry. Original bills for the expenses incurred in the construction of the tubewell/filter point. In the case of those who have availed themselves of a Bank loan, provide an attested copy of the original bills and a certificate from the Bank to that effect. Include a copy of the Aadhaar card, Farmers Identity Card, and the front page of the Bank passbook.

faqs.answer: Applicants must obtain a permit from Pondicherry Ground Water Authority and adhere to the conditions set by the Agriculture Department.

faqs.answer: Applicants have the freedom to choose the brand of pipes, but they must be BIS certified and purchased from either PASIC or authorized dealers.

faqs.question: What is the objective of the scheme "Assistance to Co-operative Irrigation Societies, M. N. R.-10 (General Area)"?
faqs.answer: The objective of the scheme "Assistance to Co-operative Irrigation Societies, M. N. R.-10 (General Area)" is to enhance agricultural productivity in Gujarat by providing financial and technical support to cooperative irrigation societies formed by farmers from a common geographical area, enabling them to establish water distribution systems using pumps and electric motors on wells and agar creeks.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for the "Assistance to Co-operative Irrigation Societies, M. N. R.-10 (General Area)" scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme is exclusively open to cooperative irrigation societies that are legally formed by groups of farmers who collectively own or cultivate agricultural land within the state of Gujarat.

faqs.question: What type of assistance is provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Under the "Assistance to Co-operative Irrigation Societies, M. N. R.-10 (General Area)" scheme, financial support is provided to enable the installation of water distribution systems, including pumps and electric motors, to aid irrigation efforts for member farmers of the cooperative societies.

faqs.question: What is the geographical coverage of the scheme?
faqs.answer: The "Assistance to Co-operative Irrigation Societies, M. N. R.-10 (General Area)" scheme is applicable across the entire state of Gujarat and can be availed by any qualifying cooperative irrigation society within the state.

faqs.question: Which department is responsible for overseeing this scheme?
faqs.answer: The Agriculture and Co-operation Department of the Government of Gujarat is responsible for formulating, monitoring, and administering the "Assistance to Co-operative Irrigation Societies, M. N. R.-10 (General Area)" scheme.

faqs.question: Where can the application form be obtained for this scheme?
faqs.answer: The application form for the "Assistance to Co-operative Irrigation Societies, M. N. R.-10 (General Area)" scheme can be obtained free of cost from the District Registrar's Office, and it can be downloaded from the official website.

faqs.question: What is the cost of the application form for this scheme?
faqs.answer: There is no fee associated with the application form for the scheme; it is provided free of cost by the District Registrar Office and through the scheme’s official portal.

faqs.question: Is there any preference or reservation for specific groups under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The Scheme is applicable to the General category.

name: Assistance for Tools, Equipment, Shorting/Grading Equipment, PHM Equipment for Scheduled Tribes (HRT-3)
department: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department
description: The scheme “Assistance for Tools, Equipment, Shorting/Grading Equipment, PHM Equipment for Scheduled Tribes (HRT-3)” is implemented by the Directorate of Horticulture, Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Co-operation Department, Government of Gujarat. Under the scheme, financial assistance is provided to farmers belonging to the Scheduled Tribes category as well as to farmer groups and cooperative societies for purchasing various tools, equipment, sorting/grading equipment, and Post-Harvest Management (PHM) equipment. This includes plastic crates with equipment such as weights, packing materials, sorting/grading machinery, etc.
benefits: The Scheduled Tribes farmers will be eligible for assistance up to 75% of the cost of the Tools/Equipment or ₹3,750/-, whichever is less. Farmer groups/cooperative societies will be eligible for assistance of 90% of the cost of equipment or up to ₹7,50,000/-, whichever is less, for the installation of Post-Harvest Management (PHM) Equipment.
eligibility: The beneficiary should be a permanent resident of Gujarat.. The beneficiary should belong to the Scheduled Tribes.. The individual farmer or farmer groups/Cooperative Societies are eligible to avail benefits under the scheme.. Note 01: The tool/equipment has to be purchased from the authorised dealer of the empanelled manufacturer for the purpose of price discovery as notified by the Department of Agriculture from time to time.. Note 02: Companies empanelled by the Department of Agriculture for tarpaulin seats and their regulations will have to be implemented as per the norms.. Note 03: Companies empanelled by the Agriculture Department for plastic crates and have to implement as per its norms..

faqs.question: What assistance is available for farmer groups/cooperative societies under the scheme?

faqs.answer: The scheme covers various tools, equipment, sorting/grading equipment, and Post-Harvest Management (PHM) equipment, including plastic crates with equipment such as weights, packing materials, sorting/grading machinery, etc.

faqs.answer: Beneficiaries must be permanent residents of Gujarat and belong to the Scheduled Tribes category.

name: Assistance in Trellise Mandap for Cultivation of Vegetable Crops
department: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department
description: The scheme "Assistance in Trellise Mandap for Cultivation of Vegetable Crops" by the Agriculture and Co-operation Department, Government of Gujarat, aims to promote sustainable and structured vegetable crop cultivation by extending financial assistance to eligible farmers for building kachha, semi-pucca, and pucca trellis mandaps using materials like wood, bamboo, GI wire, and plastic wire. This initiative not only supports effective vegetable cultivation techniques but also improves the productivity and longevity of vegetable crops grown on trellises.
benefits: > Monetary Assistance: General Farmers: 50% of unit cost or ₹80,000/- per hectare- SC/ST Farmers: 75% of unit cost or ₹1,20,000/- per hectare- Devipoojak Farmers: 90% of cost or ₹46,800/- per hectare > Input Support: Wood/Bamboo Supports: 1,600 units per hectare- GI Wire (12–18 gauge) or Plastic Wire: 400 kg per hectare- Recommended Plant Spacing: 2.5 x 2.5 meters (approximate) > Coverage Limit: Maximum Area: 2.00 hectares per Khata Validity: Assistance duration: 3 years
eligibility: The applicant should be a farmer. The applicant should be a resident of Gujarat.. The applicant should be engaged in vegetable cultivation.. The applicant should be willing to construct trellis mandaps..
documents: 7/12 Certificate. Aadhaar Card. Bank Pass Book/Cancelled Cheque.

faqs.question: What is the main objective of the scheme "Assistance in Trellise Mandap for Cultivation of Vegetable Crops"?
faqs.answer: The main objective of the scheme is to encourage the adoption of structured farming methods by supporting farmers with financial assistance for constructing kachha, semi-pucca, or pucca trellis mandaps to improve vegetable crop productivity and quality.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply under the scheme "Assistance in Trellise Mandap for Cultivation of Vegetable Crops"?
faqs.answer: All farmers residing in the state of Gujarat who are engaged in vegetable cultivation are eligible to apply under the "Assistance in Trellise Mandap for Cultivation of Vegetable Crops" scheme.

faqs.question: What are the financial benefits available to farmers under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Under the "Assistance in Trellise Mandap for Cultivation of Vegetable Crops" scheme, General category farmers are entitled to receive 50% of the unit cost or ₹80,000/- per hectare, SC/ST category farmers receive 75% of the cost or ₹1,20,000/- per hectare, and Devipoojak farmers are eligible for 90% of the cost or ₹46,800/- per hectare.

faqs.question: Is there a limit on the area of land for which assistance can be availed?
faqs.answer: Yes, the assistance under the scheme "Assistance in Trellise Mandap for Cultivation of Vegetable Crops" is limited to a maximum of 2.00 hectares per Khata, and farmers cannot claim benefits for land beyond this limit.

faqs.question: What are the materials that farmers are expected to use for constructing the trellis mandap?
faqs.answer: Farmers availing benefits under the "Assistance in Trellise Mandap for Cultivation of Vegetable Crops" scheme are expected to use approved materials such as bamboo or wooden supports (1,600 units per hectare), GI wire of 12–18 gauge or plastic wire (400 kg per hectare) to ensure durable and efficient structures.

faqs.question: Is there any specific spacing required for the trellis structure under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, the scheme "Assistance in Trellise Mandap for Cultivation of Vegetable Crops" recommends a spacing of approximately 2.50 meters by 2.50 meters for the trellis structure to ensure optimal crop growth and structural balance.

faqs.question: What is the validity period of the assistance once it is approved?
faqs.answer: Once approved, the financial assistance under the "Assistance in Trellise Mandap for Cultivation of Vegetable Crops" scheme remains valid for a period of three years, within which the farmer is expected to construct and utilize the trellis structure.

faqs.question: Are farmers from Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, or Devipoojak communities given any special benefit?
faqs.answer: Yes, farmers belonging to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, or Devipoojak communities are given higher subsidy percentages under the "Assistance in Trellise Mandap for Cultivation of Vegetable Crops" scheme, thereby ensuring inclusive and equitable access to agricultural infrastructure support.

faqs.question: Can farmers from all districts of Gujarat apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, the "Assistance in Trellise Mandap for Cultivation of Vegetable Crops" scheme is applicable across the entire state of Gujarat, allowing farmers from any district to apply, provided they meet the eligibility conditions.

faqs.question: What are the steps to apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: To apply for the “Assistance in Trellise Mandap for Cultivation of Vegetable Crops,” the applicant must visit the iKhedut (https://ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in/site/) portal, fill out the online application form, upload the required documents, and submit the form electronically.

faqs.question: Is there any income limit or financial background criteria for applying under this scheme?
faqs.answer: There is no individual or family income limit specified in the guidelines for eligibility under the "Assistance in Trellise Mandap for Cultivation of Vegetable Crops" scheme, making it accessible to all farmers irrespective of their economic background.

faqs.question: What documents are required for applying under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers applying for the "Assistance in Trellise Mandap for Cultivation of Vegetable Crops" scheme must submit a copy of their Aadhaar Card, 7/12 Certificate, and either a Bank Passbook or a Cancelled Cheque for bank account verification.

name: Assam Tea Plantations Provident Fund Scheme
department: Tea Tribes and Adivasi Welfare Department
description: The "Assam Tea Plantations Provident Fund Scheme" is a Social Security Scheme for the Plantation Workers in Assam. The scheme was launched by the Assam Tea Employees Provident Fund Organization, Government of Assam. The scheme aims to provide compulsory savings and social security to tea garden workers and employees in Assam against contingencies like old age, death, and invalidity. The scheme provides a provident fund where both the employee and employer contribute 12% of wages, which accumulates interest at a rate declared by the Board. The applicant must be a daily wage worker or an employee of a plantation or tea factory earning up to ₹6,500/- per month. The scheme is implemented by the Assam Tea Employees Provident Fund Organization and administered by a Board of Trustees. The applications for claims are accepted through the employer or garden management.
benefits: Provident Fund Accumulation: Members receive credit for their own contribution of 12% of wages and an equal 12% contribution from the employer. Interest: The accumulated deposits earn interest at a rate declared by the Board every year. Final Settlement: The total credit balance with interest is paid to the member or nominee upon retirement, resignation, death, or invalidity. Refundable Advances: Members can avail advances up to 25% of the balance or nine months' pay (whichever is less) for marriage, death ceremonies, medical treatment, or children's higher education. Housing Advance: A non-refundable advance is available for constructing or purchasing a dwelling house, equal to 24 months' wage, total contribution, or housing cost, whichever is less. Hardship Relief: A non-refundable advance is granted in cases of hardship due to natural calamities or the closure of a plantation.
eligibility: The applicant must be employed in a tea plantation or a tea factory in Assam.. The applicant must receive a monthly salary of up to ₹6,500/-.. The applicant must be a daily wage worker (eligible from the first day of work)..
documents: Bank Account Details: A Bank Passbook or official bank document containing the Bank Account Number, Name of the Banker, Branch Name, and IFS Code. Proof of Employment: An Employment Identity Card or Service Certificate issued by the Tea Garden Manager to substantiate that the applicant is an employee of a plantation or tea factory. Proof of Wages: A Wage Slip or Salary Certificate to substantiate that the applicant's monthly salary is up to ₹6,500/

or that they are a daily wage worker. Nomination Details: A Nomination Form or Declaration of Family Members to designate a beneficiary for the release of funds in the event of the member's death. Death Certificate: A Death Certificate of the member (Required only for Family Pension or Deposit Linked Insurance claims by a nominee). Medical Certificate: A Medical Certificate issued by a competent authority (Required only for Invalid Pension claims due to accident or invalidity).

Bank Account Details: A Bank Passbook or official bank document containing the Bank Account Number, Name of the Banker, Branch Name, and IFS Code.- Proof of Employment: An Employment Identity Card or Service Certificate issued by the Tea Garden Manager to substantiate that the applicant is an employee of a plantation or tea factory.- Proof of Wages: A Wage Slip or Salary Certificate to substantiate that the applicant's monthly salary is up to ₹6,500/- or that they are a daily wage worker.- Nomination Details: A Nomination Form or Declaration of Family Members to designate a beneficiary for the release of funds in the event of the member's death.- Death Certificate: A Death Certificate of the member (Required only for Family Pension or Deposit Linked Insurance claims by a nominee).- Medical Certificate: A Medical Certificate issued by a competent authority (Required only for Invalid Pension claims due to accident or invalidity).

faqs.question: As a daily wage worker in a tea garden, when do I become eligible to join the Provident Fund scheme?
faqs.answer: You are eligible to become a member of the scheme and entitled to benefits from the very first day of your work.

faqs.question: What is the maximum monthly salary limit for an employee to be eligible for membership in this Provident Fund scheme?
faqs.answer: Employees receiving a monthly salary of up to ₹6,500/- are eligible to become members of the scheme.

faqs.question: How much of my wages must be contributed to the Provident Fund, and does the employer also contribute?
faqs.answer: You contribute 12% of your wages, and the employer matches this with an equal contribution of 12%.

faqs.question: Can I withdraw money from my Provident Fund account to pay for the construction or purchase of a house?
faqs.answer: Yes, a non-refundable advance is granted equivalent to 24 months' wages, your total contribution, or the cost of the house, whichever is less.

faqs.question: What happens to the money I deposit into the Provident Fund account over the years of my employment?
faqs.answer: Your deposits are credited with interest at a rate declared by the Board every year until you withdraw the amount.

faqs.question: Is it possible to get an advance from my Provident Fund balance for my children's higher education expenses?
faqs.answer: Yes, you may be granted an advance of up to 25% of your credit balance or nine months' pay, whichever is less.

faqs.question: What financial support is available from the fund if I face hardship due to a natural calamity?
faqs.answer: A non-refundable advance is granted to members facing hardship due to natural calamities or the closure of a plantation.

faqs.question: Am I allowed to take an advance from my Provident Fund for expenses related to a marriage or death ceremony?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can avail an advance up to 25% of your balance or nine months' pay for such ceremonies.

faqs.question: How is the "wages" calculated for the purpose of the 12% deduction for the Provident Fund contribution?
faqs.answer: Wages include dearness allowances, the value of food concessions, and amounts received for plucking tea leaves.

faqs.question: What information must I provide to ensure that my Provident Fund payments are credited directly to me?
faqs.answer: You must furnish your Bank Account Number, Name of the Banker, and Branch with IFS code to your garden manager.

faqs.question: How will I receive the payment if my Provident Fund claim amount is more than ₹5,000/-?
faqs.answer: Payments of ₹5,000/- and above are made directly to your individual Bank Account.

faqs.question: What happens to my Provident Fund balance if I resign or retire from my service at the tea garden?
faqs.answer: In the event of retirement or resignation, the Board pays back the entire amount standing at your credit with interest.

name: Assistance Towards Sugarcane Supplied By The Sugarcane Growers
description: The scheme "Assistance Towards Sugarcane Supplied By The Sugarcane Growers" was launched by the Department of Agriculture, Government of Goa. The scheme aims to assist the Sugarcane Growers to take up sugarcane cultivation in Goa. The scheme provides financial assistance based on the actual tonnage of canes weighed at the Sugar factory weighbridge, determined by the Fair & Remunerative Price (FRP) fixed by the National Federation of Co-operative Sugar Factories Limited, New Delhi. The applicant must be a farmer cultivating sugarcane in the State of Goa, possess a valid Krishi Card, and bear the cost of harvesting and transporting the harvested cane to Sanjivani Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana, Dayanandnagar Dharbandora. The scheme is implemented by the Directorate of Agriculture. The applications for this scheme are accepted via registration through Sanjivani Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana (SSSKL).
benefits: Financial assistance is provided based on the Fair & Remunerative Price (FRP) fixed by the National Federation of Co-operative Sugar Factories Limited, New Delhi, from time to time. Farmers will be paid based on the actual tonnage of canes weighed at the Sugar factory weighbridge. > Conditions The farmers must harvest and supply the sugarcane on their own to Sanjivani Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana (SSSKL). The harvested cane must be loaded and brought to Sanjivani Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana, Dayanandnagar Dharbandora by the farmer on his own cost. The farmer must duly sign the GAR 32 form, which is used in the submission process by Sanjivani Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana to the Zonal Agricultural Office. The Government or Sanjivani Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana will not take any responsibility to harvest and transport the sugarcane.
eligibility: The applicant must be a farmer.. The applicant must be cultivating sugarcane in Goa.. The applicant must possess a valid Krishi Card issued by the Directorate of Agriculture.. The applicant must ensure the sugarcane area is verified by the representatives of the Zonal Agriculture Office of the respective Taluka, along with the Fieldman of Sanjivani Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana (SSSKL).. The applicant must be issued an area certificate following verification of the sugarcane area.. The applicant must be present for the inspection of the harvested cane by the Fieldman of Sanjivani Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana (SSSKL) or any representative of the Agriculture Department..
documents: Valid Krishi Card Issued By The Directorate Of Agriculture. Area Certificate (Issued After Verification By Zonal Agriculture Office/Sanjivani Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana Fieldman). Duly Signed GAR 32 Of The Farmer (Used For Submission By Sanjivani Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana). Weigh Slips (Used For Submission By Sanjivani Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana). Details Of Farmer Who Have Supplied Cane (Used For Submission By Sanjivani Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana).
Valid Krishi Card Issued By The Directorate Of Agriculture.
Area Certificate (Issued After Verification By Zonal Agriculture Office/Sanjivani Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana Fieldman).
Duly Signed GAR 32 Of The Farmer (Used For Submission By Sanjivani Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana).
Weigh Slips (Used For Submission By Sanjivani Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana).

faqs.question: What specific criteria must be fulfilled regarding my agricultural activities in order to qualify as an eligible participant under this support program?
faqs.answer: To be considered eligible, you must be a farmer actively cultivating sugarcane within the geographical limits of the State of Goa.

faqs.question: When is the specific calendar timeframe during which the processing factory is expected to carry out the formal registration process for eligible sugarcane growers?
faqs.answer: Sanjivani Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana Limited (SSSKL) is mandated to register the farmers cultivating sugarcane during the month of May.

faqs.question: If I have a genuine and unique case that does not strictly meet all the established scheme clauses, which specific official has the power to grant an exception?
faqs.answer: The Minister of Agriculture is empowered to relax any or all clauses or conditions of the scheme in genuine cases.

faqs.question: Who specifically is responsible for inspecting the area where I am growing sugarcane, and what is the outcome of a successful physical check of the cultivation site?
faqs.answer: The sugarcane area must be verified by representatives of the Zonal Agriculture Office, along with the Fieldman of Sanjivani Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana Limited (SSSKL). After verification, an area certificate will be issued to you.

faqs.question: What is the total operational period established for this financial assistance program, starting from its introduction year?
faqs.answer: The scheme came into force starting from the year 2025-26 and is scheduled to remain operational for two years, until the end of 2026-27.

faqs.question: Is there a mandatory document required from the Directorate of Agriculture that I must possess and ensure is up-to-date at the time of application for this financial support?
faqs.answer: Yes, all participating farmers must possess a valid Krishi Card that has been duly issued by the Directorate of Agriculture.

faqs.question: On what specific metric or tonnage measure will the final financial assistance amount be calculated and subsequently provided to me?
faqs.answer: The payment of financial assistance will be strictly based on the actual tonnage of canes recorded when weighed at the Sugar factory weighbridge.

faqs.question: Which national authority determines the rate or price formula used to calculate the financial assistance I receive for the tonnage of sugarcane supplied?
faqs.answer: The financial assistance is provided according to the Fair & Remunerative Price (FRP) which is fixed from time to time by the National Federation of Co-operative Sugar Factories Limited, New Delhi.

faqs.question: Am I personally responsible for covering the expenses associated with the logistics, such as loading and transporting the harvested cane to the designated processing location?
faqs.answer: Yes, the harvested cane must be loaded and brought to Sanjivani Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana, Dayanandnagar Dharbandora, entirely at the farmer's own cost.

faqs.question: Who is primarily responsible for performing the activities of harvesting the sugarcane crop and ensuring its subsequent delivery to the processing facility?

benefits: Under this scheme: Bee families (bees, including the queen bee) and bee colonies (bee boxes) are provided with a 40% subsidy (maximum cost per bee box is ₹2,000/- and per bee colony is ₹2,000/-). 50 bee boxes are provided in plain areas and 25 in hilly areas. For example, if a bee box and bee colony cost ₹200/-, the farmer has to deposit ₹120/- at the concerned Horticulture Mobile team Centre. The government bears a subsidy of ₹80/-, and the farmer receives the box for ₹120/-. If a farmer wishes to keep bee colonies in their own orchards, financial assistance of ₹350/- per bee colony is provided. If a farmer wants to receive training, the department provides a free seven-day beekeeping training program. Along with the training, the farmer is given ₹100/- per day (totaling ₹700/-) and ₹50/- per day (totaling ₹350/-). A total of ₹1,050/- is provided to each beneficiary.

faqs.question: How can farmers apply for training?

name: Bhesaj Krishi Vikas Yojana (Herbal Cultivation Programme)

eligibility: The applicant must be a livestock farmer, a farmer producer company, a registered company under Section 8, or a self-help group based in Uttarakhand..
