name: Breed Multiplication Farm Entrepreneurship
description: It is proposed to make available a 50% capital subsidy (limited to Rs. 2.00 Crore) to the interested entrepreneur for the construction of cattle sheds, equipment, procurement of elite bull mothers etc. The entrepreneur will establish a breed multiplication farm (BMF) and produce elite heifers using sexed semen or IVF technology. Disease-free heifers (free from at least TB, JD & Brucella) produced at the BMF will be sold to interested farmers and HGM bulls born at BMF will be procured by semen stations for semen production, subject to qualifying Minimum Standards for production of frozen semen. BMF will also act as the training centre to conduct training for farmers and entrepreneurs. There is no system available in the country for producing disease-free elite animals of indigenous breeds of cattle and buffalo or exotic breeds of cattle. Therefore it is proposed to establish breed multiplication farms through an entrepreneurship model to make available disease-free high-yielding heifers/pregnant heifers /cows preferably of indigenous breeds of cattle/buffaloes in the country.
benefits: Construction of cattle sheds. Procurement of elite bull. Purchase of relevant equipment, mothers etc. Establish breed multiplication farms and produce elite heifers using sex-sorted semen or IVF technology. Maximum Subsidy will not exceed Rs 2.00 Cr. Indicative cost of the model project for the establishment of Breed Multiplication Farm S No Particulars Total Cost (Rs in lakh) 1 Purchase of cows in first lactation/ 2nd lactation 200 2 Construction of cow sheds 10 sq. meter per cow (sheds to house 200 cows and its followers 100 3 Construction of isolation shed 2.5 4 Administration block 20 5 Feed 8 fodder store room 40 6 Tractor 75 HP, with agriculture implements. 10 7 Dairy equipment (BMC, stainless steel Milk cans, digital milko tester, deep freezer etc.) 5 8 Shed for Agri implements 22.5 9 Chaff cutter (electric) 1 Total 401
eligibility: The applicant shall be an entrepreneur-aggregator /private individual, SHGs/FPOs/FCOs/ JLGs and Section 8 companies who have their registered offices in India.. Entrepreneur/applicant shall have appropriate experience in breeding or rearing dairy animals. The entrepreneur/applicant will be responsible for arranging land of suitable size and location. At least having ownership/lease deed of 5 acres of land.. The entrepreneur/applicant will make its own arrangement for the procurement of feed and fodder as per the requirement of the farm. The entrepreneur will establish a breed multiplication farm of at least 200 milch cows/buffalo and use the latest breeding technology to continuously upgrade the stock..
documents: Copy of Certificate of Incorporation and Partnership Deed, if any. For individuals, a copy of their Aadhar card along with a Bank statement. Proof of their activity: Certificate of experience in breeding and rearing of dairy animals from the local Govt. Veterinarian. copy of ownership document/lease deed. Commitment letter from the supplier of feed and fodder. Affidavit (Annexure
III). Note: Download forms from here .

name: Bakri Palan Yojana
description: The scheme "Bakri Palan Yojana" was introduced by the Department of Animal Husbandry, Government of Uttarakhand. benefits: Self-employment in goat rearing is facilitated by providing beneficiaries with a goat unit comprising 10 female goats and 1 male goat for a period of 10 to 14 months. The total cost of the unit is ₹70,000/-, of which 90% (₹63,000/-) is funded by the State Government, and the remaining 10% (₹7,000/-) is contributed by the beneficiary.

documents: Aadhaar Card Bank Account details Caste Certificate Other supporting documents as required

faqs.question: What is the main benefit provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Beneficiaries are supported with one goat-rearing unit consisting of 10 female and 1 male goat, aged between 10 to 14 months.

faqs.question: Is this scheme meant to promote self-employment?
faqs.answer: Yes, the scheme helps beneficiaries generate self-employment through goat rearing.

faqs.question: Is there any contribution from the beneficiary under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, the beneficiary has to contribute ₹7,000, which is 10% of the total cost.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to benefit from this scheme?
faqs.answer: General category individuals, Scheduled Castes (SC), and Scheduled Tribes (ST) listed in the SECC (Socio-Economic and Caste Census) are eligible.

faqs.answer: The interested person must present their proposal during an open meeting of the Gram Sabha.

faqs.question: Can I submit the proposal to the Gram Panchayat Secretary?

faqs.answer: Yes, the DBT amount is given for purchasing goats.

faqs.question: How long does the whole process take after Gram Sabha approval?
faqs.answer: Benefits are typically disbursed within 1 to 2 months post-selection.

name: Beej Swalamban Yojna
description: The main objective of starting the Mukhyamantri Beej Swavalamban Yojana is to provide up to 50% subsidy by the Agriculture Department for providing seeds to the small and marginal general farmers of the state. Apart from this, free mini kits are to be provided to the farmers living below the poverty line. So that the farmers of the state take steps towards prosperity and self-reliance by producing seeds in their fields. And they can be encouraged to produce seeds for use in their farm. By getting the benefit of this scheme, farmers will be able to produce good crops at low cost. Due to this their economic condition will also increase. This scheme of state funds was started as a pilot project in the Kota, Bhilwara, and Udaipur agriculture blocks of the state. By expanding the scheme from the year 2018-19, the scheme is being implemented in all the blocks of the state. Under the plan:- Selection of crop: - Seed production program of notified varieties of jowar, soyabean, groundnut, moong, moth, and urad in the Kharif season and wheat, barley, and gram crops of less than 10 years duration in the Rabi season.1. Formation of farmers group :- Under the scheme, a group is formed by selecting farmers who are progressive and interested in the cultivation of a particular crop. Selection of 30 to 50 farmers in each group, by whom the area sown of that crop would be generally 50 to 100 hectares.1. Selection of seed producer members in the group: - As per requirement, 2-4 seed-producing farmers are selected from the farmer group by the group itself. The rest of the group will be those farmers who will use the above-produced seeds for sowing in the coming year.1. Free seed distribution :- Provision to make available the desired base/certified seeds (Stage-I) free of cost to the seed-producing farmers of each farmer group.1. Training and Rogging for seed production: - There is a provision to spend Rs.30/- per farmer and a maximum of Rs.1500/- per training on one-day training of a group. Three one-day training programs are organized to give complete information about the seed production process to the farmers of the group. Payment to be made to farmers for Rogging (Rs.1000/- /Hect.) DBT/RTGS to the concerned seed producer is done on the account of the farmer.
benefits: The seeds produced by the group of farmers will be used by the rest of the farmers for production in the next year.
eligibility: Farmers, who are interested in progressive and crop-specific farming.
documents: Copy of Aadhaar Card. Copy of Bank Passbook.

faqs.question: What are the benefits under the scheme ?
faqs.answer: The seeds produced by the group of farmers will be used by the rest of the farmers for production in the next year.

faqs.question: Who can get the benefits of the scheme ?

name: Balram Talab Yojana
department: Farmer Welfare and Agriculture Development Department
description: The scheme "Balram Talab Yojana" was launched by the Farmer Welfare and Agricultural Development Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh. The scheme aims to support agriculture activities on a sustainable basis by conservation of rainwater in the field, enriching surface and groundwater availability. Only those farmers who have installed drip or sprinkler sets in financial year 2017-18 or thereafter and currently in operational condition will be granted approval for subsidized pond construction.
benefits: General category farmers receive 40% of the construction cost or maximum ₹80,000/- as subsidy. Small and marginal farmers receive 50% of the construction cost or maximum ₹80,000/- as subsidy. Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe category farmers receive 75% of the construction cost or maximum ₹1,00,000/- as subsidy. Disbursement The subsidy will be disbursed to the beneficiary based on the progress of pond construction. The subsidy will be provided within 30 days based on the evaluation by the Soil Conservation Staff. Conditions All conditions and eligibility must be verified by the Soil Conservation Survey Officer before subsidy benefits are provided. Before providing the benefit under this scheme, verification of the land will be conducted by the Conservation Survey Officer. From a security perspective, it is mandatory to install a board at the pond site to prevent drowning incidents. This must be installed at the farmer's own expense. In the absence of a board, if any accident occurs, the farmer will be solely responsible.
eligibility: The applicant must be a permanent resident of Madhya Pradesh.. The applicant must possess agricultural land.. The applicant must have installed drip or sprinkler sets in financial year 2017-18 or thereafter, and these must be currently in operational condition, to be eligible for subsidized pond construction.. The applicant must construct the pond on their own land. Subsidy will not be provided for pond construction on leased land..
documents: Aadhaar Card Identity Card Permanent Residence Certificate Bank Account Passbook Passport Size Photograph Khasra Document Caste Certificate Demand Draft Document Registered Mobile Number

faqs.question: What is the maximum financial assistance available for constructing a pond on agricultural land under this government initiative for water conservation?
faqs.answer: The maximum subsidy provided is ₹1,00,000/- for Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe farmers, representing 75% of construction costs, while general category and small-marginal farmers receive up to ₹80,000/-.

faqs.question: If I belong to the Scheduled Caste category and want to build a rainwater harvesting structure, what%age of the total construction cost will the state government bear?
faqs.answer: Farmers from Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe categories receive 75% of the construction cost as subsidy, with a maximum limit of ₹1,00,000/-, for building rainwater conservation structures.

faqs.question: Is it mandatory for farmers to have any specific irrigation equipment already installed on their farmland before they can apply for assistance?
faqs.answer: Yes, only those farmers who have installed drip or sprinkler irrigation sets in financial year 2017-18 or thereafter, and these systems are currently operational, are eligible for subsidized pond construction approval.

faqs.question: Can a farmer who has previously received benefits under this water conservation program apply again for constructing another pond on different agricultural land?
faqs.answer: No, the benefit of this scheme is provided to each farmer only once, meaning a farmer cannot apply multiple times even if they own different parcels of agricultural land.

faqs.question: What is the minimum requirement regarding land ownership for farmers interested in participating in this rainwater harvesting scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers must construct the pond on their own agricultural land as subsidy will not be provided for pond construction on leased or rented land, making land ownership a mandatory requirement.

faqs.question: How much time does it typically take for the subsidy amount to be transferred to the beneficiary's bank account after the pond construction is completed?
faqs.answer: The subsidy is provided within 30 days based on the evaluation and assessment conducted by the Soil Conservation Staff after completion of the construction work.

faqs.question: Are farmers from all social and economic categories eligible to participate in this agricultural water management program being implemented statewide?
faqs.answer: Yes, all categories of farmers including general category, small and marginal farmers, and Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe farmers are eligible to avail benefits under this scheme.

faqs.question: What happens if a farmer who has received subsidy does not install the mandatory safety signboard at the pond location as required?
faqs.answer: In the absence of a mandatory safety board at the pond site, if any drowning or accident occurs, the farmer will be solely and completely responsible for all consequences.

faqs.question: Is there any difference in the subsidy%age provided to small and marginal category farmers compared to general category farmers under this initiative?
faqs.answer: Yes, small and marginal farmers receive 50% of construction costs or maximum ₹80,000/-, which is higher than the 40% or maximum ₹80,000/- provided to general category farmers.

name: Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana
description: The scheme “Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana”, implemented by the Department of Horticulture, Government of Haryana, aims to protect horticultural farmers from market price fluctuations and compensate them if they receive low prices for their produce in the market. Objectives: To reduce the financial risk for farmers during periods of low market prices for vegetables and fruits by ensuring a protected price. To encourage diversification in agriculture by supporting horticultural farmers. Crops covered under the scheme: Crops: Ladyfinger, Chilli, Bottle Gourd, Bitter Gourd, Cabbage, Radish, Tomato, Onion, Potato, Cauliflower, Carrot, Peas, Capsicum, Brinjal, Turmeric, Garlic, Mango, Kinnow, Guava, Litchi, Plum
benefits: To make vegetable growers risk free. To fix protected price for the crops (Ladyfinger, Chilli, Bottle Gourd, Bitter Gourd, Cabbage, Radish, Tomato, Onion, Potato, Cauliflower, Carrot, Peas, Capsicum, Brinjal, Turmeric, Garlic, Mango, Kinnow, Guava, Litchi, Plum) In case of selling of fruits/vegetables at lower prices in the market within the prescribed period, the difference in price upto the protected price will be compensated by the Government to the registered farmers. Note: The incentive amount will be released into the Aadhar linked bank account of the farmer.
eligibility: The applicant should be a landowner, lessee, or tenant farmer in Haryana.. The farmer should cultivate one of the 21 listed crops.. Note 1: Registration on the Meri Fasal, Mera Byora portal (https://fasal.haryana.gov.in/) during the sowing period is mandatory.. Note 2: The land and crop details must be certified by the Horticulture Department..
documents: Identity Proof i.e. Aadhaar Card Proof of land ownership or lease agreement (for tenant farmers) Registration proof from the Meri Fasal, Mera Byora portal J
Form for the sale of produce Bank account details linked with Aadhaar Any other documents if required
Proof of land ownership or lease agreement (for tenant farmers)
Registration proof from the Meri Fasal, Mera Byora portal
J-Form for the sale of produce
Bank account details linked with Aadhaar

faqs.question: What is the Bhavantar Bharpayee Yojana (BBY)?
faqs.answer: BBY is a unique scheme by the Haryana Government to compensate horticulture producers when they receive lower prices for their produce in the market. It aims to reduce the risk of price volatility and encourage crop diversification among farmers.

faqs.question: Which crops are covered under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme covers 21 crops: Okra (Bhindi), Chili, Bottle Gourd (Lauki), Bitter Gourd (Karela), Cabbage (Patta Gobhi), Radish (Mooli), Tomato, Onion, Potato, Cauliflower (Phool Gobhi), Carrot (Gajar), Pea (Matar), Capsicum (Shimla Mirch), Brinjal (Baingan), Turmeric (Haldi), Garlic (Lahsun), Mango (Aam), Kinnow, Guava (Amrud), Litchi, and Ber.

faqs.question: What is the primary objective of the scheme?
faqs.answer: The main objectives are to mitigate the risk of low prices during the sale of vegetables and fruits by providing compensation up to a protected price and to encourage farmers to diversify their crops.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to benefit from the scheme?
faqs.answer: Landowners, lessees, or tenant farmers cultivating the specified crops are eligible to benefit from the scheme.

faqs.question: Is registration mandatory to avail benefits under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, farmers must register on the "Meri Fasal, Mera Byora" portal during the sowing period to avail benefits under the scheme.

faqs.question: Where can farmers register for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Registration facilities are available at Saral Kendras, e-Disha Kendras, Marketing Board offices, Horticulture Department offices, Agriculture Department offices, and internet kiosks.

faqs.question: Who verifies the registered crop area?
faqs.answer: The Horticulture Department verifies the crop area registered by the farmers.

faqs.question: Is there any fee for registration under the BBY?
faqs.answer: No, the registration for the scheme is free of cost.

faqs.question: When is the registration period open for the BBY?
faqs.answer: Registration is open only during the specified period, which is announced by the authorities. Farmers should register within this timeframe to be eligible for benefits.

faqs.question: Is it mandatory to sell produce through 'J-Forms' to avail benefits?
faqs.answer: Yes, to avail benefits under the scheme, it is mandatory to sell the produce through 'J-Forms'.

faqs.question: Where can farmers upload their sales details under the scheme?
faqs.answer: After selling their produce using 'J-Forms', farmers can upload their sales details on the BBY e-portal (www.bby.hortharyana.gov.in). Facilities for this are available at the respective Market Committee offices.

faqs.question: How is the compensation calculated under the scheme?
faqs.answer: If the wholesale price of the produce during the sale period is less than the protected price, the government compensates the difference to the registered farmers. The compensation is based on the quantity sold through 'J-Forms' and the per-acre production determined as per the scheme's guidelines.

faqs.question: How is the average daily wholesale price determined?
faqs.answer: The average daily wholesale price is determined based on the daily prices from designated mandis by the Mandi Board, following the scheme's standards and guidelines.

faqs.question: How is the compensation amount disbursed to farmers?
faqs.answer: The compensation amount is directly credited to the farmer's Aadhaar-linked bank account.

name: Compensation Amount Towards Cattle Injury Caused by Forest Animals
description: Launched on 6th February 2024, the scheme "Compensation Amount towards Cattle Injury Caused by Forest Animals" by the Forest Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh, provides compensation in case of death of cattle due to attacks by wild animals. The cattle owner will receive a relief amount. The nearest forest officer must be informed in writing or verbally within 48 hours of the incident, and the dead cattle should not be removed from the place of death.
benefits: ₹1,000/- as immediate assistance for wild animal injury. ₹30,000/- for medical expenses (normal injury). ₹1,00,000/- for permanent disability and full treatment cost.
eligibility: The cattle of the owner should have been injured by a wild animal, as defined under the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972.. The cattle owner should have reported the incident to the nearest forest officer within 48 hours of its occurrence.. The cattle owner should be able to provide necessary proof or verification documents as required by the Forest Department.. The compensation applies only to cattle owners who are residents of Madhya Pradesh..
documents: Bank Account Details/ Bank Passbook Certificate or Panchnama issued by Doctor/Sarpanch/Panchayat Secretary/Local Body Bills Related to Payment of Treatment Undergone Certificate issued by a Competent Government Doctor in case of Permanent Disability Other Necessary Documents, if required
Certificate or Panchnama issued by Doctor/Sarpanch/Panchayat Secretary/Local Body
Bills Related to Payment of Treatment Undergone
Certificate issued by a Competent Government Doctor in case of Permanent Disability

faqs.question: What is this scheme about?
faqs.answer: This scheme provides compensation for the loss of animals or injuries to individuals caused by wild animals under the Forest Department of Madhya Pradesh.

faqs.question: When was the scheme launched?
faqs.answer: The scheme was launched on February 6, 2024.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for compensation?
faqs.answer: Farmers, cattle owners, and individuals who suffer losses due to wild animal attacks are eligible. However, injuries caused by snakes, moles, and other poisonous animals are not covered.

faqs.question: How much compensation is given for injured animals?
faqs.answer: Up to 50% of the applicable compensation amount is provided for injured animals.

faqs.question: How can I apply for compensation?
faqs.answer: You can apply through the Madhya Pradesh Lok Sewa Guarantee Portal by registering, logging in, selecting the scheme, filling in the required details, and uploading the necessary documents.

faqs.question: What is the time limit to report an incident?
faqs.answer: The nearest forest officer must be informed within 48 hours of the incident.

faqs.question: Where should I report my claim?
faqs.answer: Report the claim to the nearest forest officer in writing or verbally, ensuring the dead cattle remain at the place of death.

faqs.question: What documents are required for application?
faqs.answer: You will need ID proof, proof of ownership of the animal, incident report, and other relevant certificates.

faqs.question: How long does it take for an appeal to be processed?
faqs.answer: The first appeal is resolved within 30 working days.

faqs.question: Where can I get more information about the scheme?
faqs.answer: Visit the Madhya Pradesh Lok Sewa Guarantee Portal or contact the nearest forest department office for details.

name: Cultivation of Aromatic Plants under MGNREGA - Centre for Aromatic Plants
description: The “Cultivation of Aromatic Plants under MGNREGA” scheme is implemented by the Centre for Aromatic Plants (CAP), Selaqui, Dehradun, under the Department of Horticulture, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to encourage farmers in rural areas to grow aromatic plants by providing them free planting material, technical help, and wage support through MGNREGA.
benefits: Under MGNREGA, when aromatic cultivation is undertaken, the wages for the work done by the labourers in land preparation and related activities are paid by the Rural Development Department, and the farmer does not have to pay the wages. The Centre for Aromatic Plants (CAP) provides free planting material along with technical support, consultancy, and monitoring services to the farmers.
eligibility: The applicant must be a farmer residing in a rural area of Uttarakhand.. The farmer must be interested in aromatic plant cultivation.. The farmer must either legally own agricultural land or have leased land for a minimum period of 10 years..
documents: Identity proof Land record documents Mobile Number Other supporting documents as required

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers residing in rural areas of Uttarakhand who are interested in aromatic cultivation and either own agricultural land legally or have leased land for at least 10 years are eligible to apply.

faqs.question: What type of support is provided to farmers under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers receive free planting material, free technical guidance, consultancy, and monitoring from CAP, Selaqui. In addition, labour wages for cultivation activities are paid by the Rural Development Department under MGNREGA.

faqs.question: Do farmers have to pay labour wages for cultivation work?
faqs.answer: No. All labour wages related to land preparation and cultivation under the scheme are paid by the Rural Development Department through MGNREGA. The farmer does not bear this cost.

faqs.question: How can a farmer apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Interested farmers must pass a resolution in an open meeting of the Gram Sabha and submit their proposal to CAP, Selaqui, through the Block Development Officer (BDO).

faqs.question: What happens after the farmer submits the proposal?
faqs.answer: After receiving the proposal, CAP prepares a financial estimate for the selected crop and forwards it to the Block Development Officer or Chief Development Officer for approval.

faqs.question: Who approves the proposal for aromatic cultivation?
faqs.answer: The proposal is reviewed and approved by the Block Development Officer (BDO) or the Chief Development Officer (CDO) of the concerned area.

faqs.question: How do farmers receive planting materials?
faqs.answer: After approval, the BDO requests planting materials from CAP, which are then provided free of cost to the selected farmers at the nearest distribution point or roadside delivery site.

name: Construction of Artesian Wells in Scheduled Tribe Areas
description: The scheme “Construction of Artesian Wells in Scheduled Tribe Areas” was launched by the Department of Minor Irrigation, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide free irrigation facilities to farmers in Scheduled Tribe-dominated areas through the construction of artesian wells, thereby enhancing agricultural productivity. It is a 100% state government-funded scheme.
benefits: Under the scheme, free irrigation facilities will be made available to farmers. Artesian wells are established in areas dominated by Scheduled Tribes.
eligibility: The beneficiary must be a resident of Uttarakhand.. The beneficiary must be a farmer engaged in agricultural activities.. Collective irrigation projects will be constructed under the scheme.. The name of the proposed village must be included in the list of Scheduled Tribe-dominated villages issued by the Department of Social Welfare.. The project site must be suitable for the construction of artesian wells.. A sufficient irrigated area must be available for the project.. The project cost must not exceed ₹4.00 lakh per hectare, and the benefit-cost ratio must be greater than 1.0..
documents: Documents are required as per the department’s guidelines prescribed for this scheme.

faqs.question: Who can benefit from this scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers residing in Scheduled Tribe-dominated areas of Uttarakhand and actively engaged in agricultural activities are eligible for the scheme.

faqs.question: In which areas is the scheme implemented?
faqs.answer: The scheme is generally implemented in selected areas of Udham Singh Nagar and some areas of Nainital districts where artesian wells are suitable.

faqs.question: What types of projects are constructed under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Collective irrigation projects are constructed under this scheme.

faqs.question: How can a village become eligible for this scheme?
faqs.answer: The proposed village must be included in the list of Scheduled Tribe-dominated villages issued by the Department of Social Welfare.

faqs.question: What is the maximum cost allowed per hectare for the project?
faqs.answer: The project cost should not exceed ₹4.00 lakh per hectare.

faqs.question: How can proposals be submitted?
faqs.answer: Proposals can be submitted through Gram Sabha, Gram Panchayat, Zila Parishad, or other departmental channels to the division, sub-division, or other offices.

faqs.question: How is financial approval obtained?
faqs.answer: After DPR scrutiny, the proposal is sent to the Government of Uttarakhand for financial approval.

faqs.question: Is there any cost to farmers for irrigation under this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, free irrigation facilities are provided to farmers through the constructed artesian wells.

name: Crop Cluster Development Programme
description: The Crop Cluster Development Programme (CCDP) in Baagwani Villages is a comprehensive scheme focused on the development of backward and forward integration in horticulture farming. The program aims to enhance farmer socio-economic security, achieve nutritional security, establish transparent institutional delivery mechanisms, generate rural employment, increase horticultural crop area and productivity, and develop organized marketing of horticultural products. It addresses the challenges faced by small farmers in selling to modern markets, such as supermarkets and large retailers, by promoting the collectivization of produce through farmer groups and educating them about modern technologies. The CCDP emphasizes the need for a coordinated supply chain, including aggregation of produce, market linkages, access to quality inputs and agro-services, and post-harvest management infrastructure. By facilitating access to fair and remunerative markets and ensuring adherence to global standards, the program aims to achieve the goals of quality, quantity, and seamless delivery.
benefits: Improved access to inputs and services for farmers Increased farmers' income and socio-economic security Promotion of sustainable agriculture-based livelihoods Enhancement of market linkages and organized marketing of horticultural products Reduction of post-harvest losses Creation of employment opportunities in rural areas Increase in horticultural crop area, productivity, and production
eligibility: Only Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) registered under the Companies Act in Haryana are eligible to submit project proposals and avail assistance under the scheme.. FPOs must have a minimum of 150 shareholders with a financial strength of at least Rs. 00 lakh in their bank account.. The FPOs should have an area of at least 500 acres under horticulture crops, although this requirement may be flexible based on the project's viability.. FPOs must have a business plan with backward and forward linkages of their produce.. Disputed FPOs or those not meeting the eligibility criteria mentioned above will not be considered eligible..
documents: Completed project proposal form Registration certificate of the FPO under the Companies Act List of Directors and applicants of the FPO Business plan with backward and forward linkages of the produce Financial statements and bank account details of the FPO Land ownership or lease documents Any other documents specified in the application guidelines

faqs.question: What is the objective of the CCDP?
faqs.answer: The CCDP aims to strengthen sustainable agriculture-based livelihoods, improve farmer socio-economic security, promote organized marketing of horticultural products, and increase productivity and income of horticulture farmers.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for assistance under the CCDP?
faqs.answer: Only Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) registered under the Companies Act in Haryana are eligible to submit project proposals and avail assistance under the scheme.

faqs.question: What are the benefits of the CCDP for farmers?
faqs.answer: The benefits of the CCDP include improved access to inputs and services, increased income, promotion of sustainable livelihoods, enhanced market linkages, reduced post-harvest losses, creation of employment opportunities, and increased horticultural crop area and productivity.

faqs.question: What are the exclusions under the CCDP?
faqs.answer: The CCDP excludes projects not proposed by eligible FPOs, FPOs with inadequate financial strength or a disputed status, and those not meeting the minimum shareholder and horticulture crop area requirements.

faqs.question: What documents are required for the CCDP application?
faqs.answer: The required documents may include a completed project proposal form, FPO registration certificate, list of Directors and applicants, business plan, financial statements, bank account details, and land ownership or lease documents.

faqs.question: What is the assistance pattern under the CCDP?
faqs.answer: The assistance ranges from 70% to 90% of the eligible project cost for various components, such as collection centers, primary processing centers, packing and packaging materials, allied activities, e-platforms, and retail outlets.

faqs.question: How is the assistance disbursed?
faqs.answer: The assistance is released in three installments of 25%, 40%, and 35% based on the progress of the project, utilization of previous installments, achievement of physical milestones, and completion of the project.

name: Community Canning & Training On Fruit Preservation
description: The office of the Deputy Director of Agriculture (Fruit Preservation) Assam runs under the scheme of Community Canning and Training in fruit preservation with a view to disseminate to the people specially the women section about the techniques of preparation of various preserved items such as Jam, Jelly, Pickles, Squash, Sauce, Chutney etc. from locally available seasonal fruits and vegetables. For this purpose trainings are conducted both at field levels and also in the centers itself with active guidance by staffs in the centers. At present there are 21 (Twenty one) Community Canning and Training Centers covering 19 (Nineteen) districts (The Diphu center is under the control of District council). Each of these centers are headed by one officer in the rank of Sub- Divisional Agricultural Officer (SDAO). Since inception these Community Canning and Training Centers have gained considerable popularity among public who have received the benefits on fruits and vegetable preservation in their respective areas. Apart from forwarding the facilities for preparation of various preserved items training programs are also undertaken by this centers and various ladies group, organization and N.G.O’s have been immensely benefited from such functions of the centers. Out of the activities of these centers some revenue is also earned and which is deposited to Govt. account at time to time.
benefits: To forward facilities to the public, in particular to ladies and housewives, throughout the state, for preservation of fruits and vegetables. Home scale preservation and canning of seasonal fruits and vegetables under expert technical supervision and guidance for consumption in lean periods. To encourage the preparation of value added produce such as Jam, Jelly, Squash, Juice, Sauce, Chutney, Pickles etc. at nominal charges. To impart training on home scale preservation of fruits and vegetables for 1 days, 3 days and 6 days to the ladies, housewives through various organization like Mahila samity, SHG, College girls etc. specially in rural areas (Dairly processing comes under 1 day training). To train personals to start small scale cottage industries in fruits and vegetables for self employment. The duration of these training will be of 7 to 15 days. To provide certificates to the trained personals so that they can start their own enterprise.
eligibility: To impart training on home scale preservation of fruits and vegetables for 1 days, 3 days and 6 days to the ladies, housewives through various organization like Mahila samity, SHG, College girls etc. specially in rural areas (Dairly processing comes under 1 day training). To train personals to start small scale cottage industries in fruits and vegetables for self employment. The duration of these training will be of 7 to 15 days. To provide certificates to the trained personals so that they can start their own enterprise..
documents: Aadhaar Card. Voter Card. Pan Card. A valid Bank Account. And Rests as per own district Community Canning and Training Centers.
And Rests as per own district Community Canning and Training Centers.

faqs.question: What is preservation of fruit in horticulture?
faqs.answer: Preservation - "the techniques of extending the storage life of the produce without deteriorating its edible quality for further use". Horticultural produce is biological entity with various physiological activities like transpiration and respiration continuing even after harvesting.

faqs.question: What is the status of horticulture in Assam?
faqs.answer: Area: Horticulture Crops: Vegetables: Assam data was reported at 306.240 ha th in 2022. This records a decrease from the previous number of 334.500 ha th for 2021.

faqs.question: What are the high value crops in Assam?
faqs.answer: High value crops like Straw berry, Passion fruit and Apple ber are gradually becoming popular for cultivation because of higher return. In addition Mushroom production is being considered as profitable farming activities for unemployed youths.

faqs.question: What is canning in fruit preservation?
faqs.answer: Canning, the process of placing foods in jars or cans and heating properly to a specified temperature, is a way to preserve many different foods. The high heat destroys microorganisms and inactivates enzymes to preserve the safety and quality of the food.

faqs.question: What are the 4 ways of preserving fruits?
faqs.answer: You can preserve late-summer fruits and vegetables in four basic ways. These include freezing, canning, pickling and drying or dehydrating. Freezing is the simplest way to save produce.

faqs.question: Which state is no 1 in in horticulture?
faqs.answer: In fiscal year 2021, Uttar Pradesh produced the largest share of horticultural crops in India, accounting for 13 percent. West Bengal came in second at over ten percent.

faqs.question: What are the requirements for horticulture in Assam?
faqs.answer: Eligibility criteria: Minimum 55% marks or 5.5/10 CGPA or equivalent at Graduation level. Qualifications: B.Sc (Agriculture) / B.Sc (Horticulture) with knowledge of computer (MS Word/ Excel/ Power Point etc.).

faqs.question: What is the national fruit of Assam?
faqs.answer: The national fruit of Assam is the delicious and nutritious Golden Apple, also known as the Mishing Kothal. Explanation: The tasty and nourishing Golden Apple, also known as the Mishing Kothal, is the state fruit of Assam, a region in northeastern India.

faqs.question: Which crop is largest producer in Assam?
faqs.answer: Assam is the largest producer of Tea in India, followed by West Bengal, Himachal Pradesh and other states of North India.

faqs.question: Which fruit crop is high value?
faqs.answer: Citrus is the highest valued fruit crop. Citrus orchards flourish well in light soils with excellent drainage properties.

faqs.question: What are the 2 types of canning?
faqs.answer: There are two home canning methods: water bath canning and pressure canning.

name: Construction of Dudhghar/ Godown (Scheduled Tribe Area)
department: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department
description: The scheme "Construction of Dudhghar/ Godown (Scheduled Tribe Area)" introduced by the Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department, Gujarat, aims to provide financial support to Village Milk Producer Co-operative Societies in Scheduled Tribe areas that lack their own milk storage or cattle feed storage infrastructure. It also promotes installation of bulk milk coolers and similar equipment.
benefits: Name of the Component Standard of assistance Remarks Minimum Time Limit (in Years) for Reclaiming Benefits Dudhghar/ GodownUnit price (₹10,00,000/-)or actual expenditure occurs for construction, out of that 50% of whichever is less.Maximum ₹5,00,000/-Once in lifetime
eligibility: The Society must not already own a Dudhghar or Godown.. The Society must have its own land available for the construction of the Dudhghar or Godown.. The Society must not have availed of the benefit earlier under this or any other scheme for a similar purpose..
documents: Copy of Bank Passbook or cancelled cheque. Proof of own land for construction of Dudhghar/Godown. Certificate of not availing benefit earlier in same scheme/other scheme with similar purpose by Managing Director of Dairy Union.
Copy of Bank Passbook or cancelled cheque.
Proof of own land for construction of Dudhghar/Godown.
Certificate of not availing benefit earlier in same scheme/other scheme with similar purpose by Managing Director of Dairy Union.

faqs.question: What is the objective of the "Construction of Dudhghar/ Godown (Scheduled Tribe Area)" scheme?
faqs.answer: The objective of the scheme is to support Village Milk Producer Co-operative Societies of Scheduled Tribe area in constructing Dudhghars and Godowns to ensure hygienic milk production and proper storage of cattle feed.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Only Village Milk Producer Co-operative Societies located in Scheduled Tribe areas of Gujarat are eligible to apply for the scheme.

faqs.question: What financial assistance is provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides financial assistance up to ₹5,00,000/- or 50% of the unit cost, whichever is less, for the construction of Dudhghar or Godown.

faqs.question: Is the benefit under the scheme provided more than once?
faqs.answer: No, the benefit under this scheme is provided only once in a lifetime to each eligible society.

faqs.question: Can an individual dairy farmer apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, individual dairy farmers are not eligible. Only registered Village Milk Producer Co-operative Societies can apply.

faqs.question: Is it mandatory for the society to own land for construction?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is mandatory for the society to have its own land for the construction of the Dudhghar or Godown.

faqs.question: How can a society apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: The society can apply online through the iKhedut (https://ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in/) portal.

faqs.question: Is document submission required after online application?
faqs.answer: Yes, the society must upload the required documents online or submit them in hard copy to the concerned office within 7 days of the online application.

faqs.question: What documents are required for application?
faqs.answer: The required documents include a copy of the bank passbook or cancelled cheque, proof of land ownership, and a certificate from the Managing Director of the Dairy Union confirming that the benefit has not been availed earlier.

faqs.question: What happens if the society has already received benefits under a similar scheme?
faqs.answer: If the society has already availed benefits under this or a similar scheme, it will not be eligible for assistance again.

faqs.question: Is there a time limit for submitting documents after application?
faqs.answer: Yes, all required documents must be submitted within 7 days of completing the online application.

faqs.question: Can the society install bulk milk coolers using this assistance?

description: The scheme "Coffee Development Programme in North Eastern Region: Water Augmentation" is a Sub-Component of the Scheme "Integrated Coffee Development Project During the Medium Term Framework (MTF) Period: Development Support to Stakeholders" by the Coffee Board, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry. This scheme aims to improve the productivity and quality of coffee by facilitating the creation of infrastructure for water augmentation for irrigation and wet processing of coffee.
benefits: Subsidy Details The eligible subsidy for water harvesting structures and sprinkler units is 75% of the unit cost, capped at a maximum ceiling of ₹1,25,000 for all related activities combined. For below-ground water storage tanks, the subsidy is based on the lower value between dimension and unit cost applicable to the size of the holding. For above-ground water storage tanks, the subsidy is based on the lower value between the actual cost or the unit cost applicable to the below-ground water tank. faqs.question: What's the precise focus of the "Coffee Development Programme in North Eastern Region: Water Augmentation" scheme by the Coffee Board?
faqs.answer: The scheme concentrates on enhancing coffee quality and productivity by creating infrastructure for water augmentation, aiding irrigation, and wet coffee processing.

faqs.question: Could you clarify the specific eligibility criteria for applicants under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Eligibility involves being a tribal grower without prior Water Augmentation subsidies during the XII plan period and possessing land records certified by Village/State Authorities.

faqs.question: What activities are deemed eligible for subsidy under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Installing water storage tanks, open wells, and irrigation equipment like sprinklers or drip systems to boost coffee production and quality qualify for subsidies.

faqs.question: What's the subsidy percentage available for water harvesting structures and sprinkler units?
faqs.answer: The subsidy is set at 75% of the unit cost, capped at a maximum of [?]1.25 lakh for all related activities combined.

faqs.question: Can you explain the construction specifics for water storage tanks in this scheme?
faqs.answer: Water storage tanks can be constructed either above or below ground level, with different subsidy considerations based on the type of tank.

faqs.question: What are the specifications for the location of water augmentation structures under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Water augmentation structures should be situated on the estate or within its vicinity to qualify for the subsidies.

faqs.question: Is it possible for growers to claim subsidies for water harvesting structures and irrigation equipment at different times?
faqs.answer: Yes, growers have the option to claim subsidies for these structures and equipment either simultaneously or at different times.

faqs.question: Could you outline the documents required for claiming the subsidy?
faqs.answer: The required documents include an application in duplicate, the original invoice/bill with TIN No. for sprinkler/drip equipment, and a work completion report signed by the applicant.

faqs.question: What considerations are there for amendments to this scheme?
faqs.answer: The acceptance of an application doesn't assure subsidy approval due to fund availability, and the Coffee Board holds the right to modify terms for efficient execution.

faqs.question: What consequences exist for applicants involved in bribery or misleading practices?
faqs.answer: Applicants engaged in such malpractices face rejection, potential legal action for recovery, and strict consequences under the scheme's terms and conditions.

faqs.question: How is the subsidy amount calculated for water storage tanks, specifically the above-ground and below-ground constructions?
faqs.answer: For below-ground tanks, subsidies are based on the lower value between dimension and unit cost, while for above-ground tanks, it's the lower value between actual cost and the unit cost applicable to below-ground tanks.

faqs.question: What's the role of the Extension Officer in the subsidy claiming process?
faqs.answer: The Extension Officer scrutinizes documents, conducts field inspections, and forwards application reports and verification to the Joint Director (Extension) or Deputy Director for subsidy approval or rejection.

faqs.question: What actions lead to the release of the eligible subsidy to the beneficiary?
faqs.answer: Upon fulfilling the claim's admissibility, the Joint Director or Deputy Director facilitates the subsidy release to the beneficiary through Electronic Fund Transfer (EFT).

name: Coconut Development Scheme

benefits: > Assistance for Coconut Cultivation: Financial support of ₹37,500/- per hectare, covering 75% of the total cost (₹50,000/- per hectare). > Promotion of Integrated Pest Management (IPM) and Integrated Nutrient Management (INM): Financial support of ₹5,000/- per hectare, covering 50% of the total cost (₹10,000/- per hectare).

faqs.answer: The "Coconut Development Program" aims to support farmers by providing quality coconut saplings at reasonable prices and financial assistance for coconut cultivation. faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for the "Coconut Development Program"?

faqs.answer: The scheme provides financial assistance for coconut cultivation and supports sustainable farming practices through Integrated Pest Management (IPM) and Integrated Nutrient Management (INM).

faqs.question: How much financial assistance is provided for coconut cultivation?

faqs.question: What financial assistance is available for IPM and INM practices?
faqs.answer: Farmers receive [?]5,000/- per hectare, covering 50% of the total cost ([?]10,000/- per hectare), to implement Integrated Pest Management (IPM) and Integrated Nutrient Management (INM).

faqs.question: Where can a farmer check the status of the application?

name: COP-5 Financial Assistance to Agricultural Credit Co-operative Banks (PACS/LAMPS) for Reconstruction and Reestablishment (General/Tribal Area)
department: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department
description: The scheme "COP-5 Financial Assistance to Agricultural Credit Co-operative Banks (PACS/LAMPS) for Reconstruction and Reestablishment (General/Tribal Area)" introduced by the Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department, Gujarat, aims to make economically weak but functionally efficient PACS/LAMPS financially viable. These societies play a foundational role in the three-tier cooperative credit system, and their performance impacts District and State Cooperative Banks. The scheme incentivizes societies based on their growth in credit disbursement, loan recovery, and deposit mobilization over the past three years (two years for LAMPS).
benefits: Incentive admissible over and above the average amount of the last three years Percentage of the grant of incentive on the excess amount For growth from 10% to 15% 1 %For growth above 15% and up to 20% 1.5 %For growth above 20% 2% or a maximum of ₹.50,000/- whichever is less (on deposits up to a ₹2,00,000/- whichever is less) > Note: The benefit of the scheme is available only once in a financial year.
eligibility: The applicant must be a registered Agricultural Co-operative Credit Society, either a Primary Agricultural Credit Society (PACS) or a Large-sized Adivasi Multi-Purpose Society (LAMPS).. The society must have been operational and performing for the required duration:. PACS: At least the last three years.. LAMPS: At least the last two years.. Increase in deposit collection..
documents: Growth and recovery records of the last three years (two years for LAMPS). Audit reports or financial statements. Proof of credit disbursed and deposits collected. faqs.question: What is the objective of this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides financial assistance to Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) and Large-sized Agricultural Multi-Purpose Societies (LAMPS) in General and Tribal areas to help them restructure and reestablish their operations.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Only registered Agricultural Co-operative Credit Societies (PACS/LAMPS) that have been operational for the last three years (or two years in the case of LAMPS) are eligible to apply for this scheme.

faqs.question: How often can a society avail the benefits of the scheme?
faqs.answer: A society can avail the benefits of the COP-5 scheme only once during a financial year.

faqs.question: What is the minimum operational period required for a society to apply?
faqs.answer: A PACS must be operational for at least three years, and a LAMPS must be operational for at least two years to be eligible for the scheme.

faqs.question: What kind of financial performance is rewarded under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Societies that show growth in short and medium-term credit disbursement, loan recovery, and deposit collection over the previous years are rewarded under the scheme.

faqs.question: What is the maximum financial assistance that can be availed through this scheme?
faqs.answer: The maximum financial incentive under this scheme is 2% of the excess amount or ₹50,000/-, whichever is less, applicable on deposits up to ₹2,00,000/-.

faqs.question: Are societies located in Tribal areas also eligible under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, the scheme is applicable to societies in both General and Tribal areas.

faqs.question: Can newly registered societies apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: No, newly registered societies are not eligible. The society must be operational for a minimum of three years (or two years for LAMPS).

faqs.question: Where should a society submit its application for the scheme?
faqs.answer: The application must be submitted to the District Registrar’s Office along with the required supporting documents.

faqs.question: Is the scheme available through an online application process?
faqs.answer: No, there is no online application process. All applications must be submitted in person through the District Registrar’s Office.

name: Compensation for Livestock Loss Caused by Wild Animals
description: The “Compensation for Livestock Loss Caused by Wild Animals” scheme is launched by the Forest Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh. The scheme aims to provide financial relief to individuals whose livestock is injured or killed by wild animals. The scheme applies to both urban and rural areas and covers a variety of livestock including cows, buffaloes, camels, goats, sheep, donkeys, mules, and pigs.
benefits: Compensation Amounts: Dairy animals (cow, buffalo, camel): ₹30,000 Sheep/Goat: ₹3,000 Non-dairy animals (bull, buffalo, camel, horse): ₹25,000 Young animals (calf of cow/buffalo/horse/camel), Donkey/Mule: ₹16,000 Pig: ₹3,000 Injury Compensation: 50% of the amount payable for injury under revenue circular provisions. Mode of Disbursement: Compensation is paid directly to the beneficiary via e-payment. Expected Time of Disbursement: Compensation is provided within 30 working days of claim verification.
eligibility: The applicant must be a resident of Madhya Pradesh.. The applicant should be the owner of the livestock injured or killed by wild animals..
documents: Identity Proof Resident Proof Bank Account Details Death Certificate Treatment Bills Other Necessary Documents, if required

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply?
faqs.answer: Any livestock owner in Madhya Pradesh whose animals are killed or injured by wild animals.

faqs.question: Which animals are covered?
faqs.answer: Cow, buffalo, camel, bull, horse, sheep, goat, donkey, mule, and pig.

faqs.question: What is the compensation for injury to livestock?
faqs.answer: 50% of the applicable compensation amount under revenue circular provisions.

faqs.question: What is the application fee?
faqs.answer: The application is free of cost.

faqs.question: Where should the application be submitted?
faqs.answer: At the nearest Forest Range Office or online at mpedistrict.gov.in

faqs.question: Within what time should the incident be reported?
faqs.answer: The incident be reported within 48 hours of occurrence.

faqs.question: What is the expected time for payment?
faqs.answer: Payment within 30 working days of verification.

faqs.question: How is the compensation disbursed?
faqs.answer: Directly to the beneficiary via e-payment.

faqs.question: What if my application is rejected?
faqs.answer: A first appeal can be filed within 30 days, and a second appeal within 60 days.

faqs.question: Are urban livestock owners eligible?
faqs.answer: Yes, both urban and rural livestock owners are eligible.

faqs.question: Can I move the dead animal before verification?
faqs.answer: No, the dead animal must remain at the site for verification by the Forest Officer.

name: Craft & Gear (Unit: Boats of Appropriate Sizes Including Nets, Fish & Ice Holding Boxes, Etc.)
description: The scheme “Craft & Gear (Unit: Boats of Appropriate Sizes Including Nets, Fish & Ice Holding Boxes, Etc.)” was introduced by the Directorate of Fisheries, Government of Goa. The scheme aims to uplift the sizeable community of traditional Fishermen by providing them financial help in the form of a subsidy for carrying out fishing activities in inland waters of Goa. The subsidy amount shall be disbursed directly into the applicant’s bank account.
benefits: Financial Assistance/Subsidy Financial assistance is provided for the purchase or construction of New Fiberglass Reinforced Plastic or wooden canoes below 26 feet, including nets, accessories, and insulated fish and ice holding boxes. For the General Category, financial assistance is up to 40% of the unit cost, limited to ₹40,000/-. For Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribes, Women, and their Co-operatives, financial assistance is up to 60% of the unit cost, limited to ₹60,000/-. The unit cost considered for the Craft & Gear (Unit: Boats of appropriate sizes including nets, fish & ice holding boxes etc.) is ₹1,00,000/-. Disbursement The subsidy amount shall be disbursed in favor of the applicant in his or her Bank account. Conditions The fishing canoe must be registered under the Captain of Ports Department. The nets and its accessories purchased through the scheme must be duly registered with the Directorate of Fisheries under the Goa, Daman and Diu Fisheries Rules, 1981. The beneficiary shall not sell, mortgage, or transfer the Fishing canoe, nets, accessories, or insulated ice holding boxes purchased through the scheme for a period of five years from the date of its purchase.
eligibility: The applicant must be a fisherman.. The applicant must possess the No Objection Certificate issued by the Directorate of Fisheries for the purchase or construction of a wooden or Fiberglass Reinforced Plastic Fishing Craft of below 26 feet, including fishing net and ice holding boxes.. The applicant must produce the original Goods and Services Tax bill from the authorized dealer towards the purchase or construction of the new canoe, gill net and its accessories, and insulated fish and ice holding box to claim the subsidy.. The applicant must not be a fishing trawler owner.. The applicant must not be a defaulter of the Department.. Reservation/Priority: Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribes, Women, and their Co-operatives are eligible for a higher rate of assistance (60% of unit cost, limited to ₹60,000/-).. Relaxation: The Government is empowered to relax all or any of the clauses provided in this scheme if found deemed fit, for reasons to be recorded..
documents: No Objection Certificate (Issued By The Directorate Of Fisheries) Original Goods And Services Tax Bill (From Authorized Dealer). Bank Account Details (For Subsidy Disbursal). Registration Certificate Of Fishing Canoe (Registered Under Captain Of Ports Department). Registration Certificate Of Nets And Accessories (Registered With The Directorate Of Fisheries Under The Goa, Daman And Diu Fisheries Rules, 1981).
No Objection Certificate (Issued By The Directorate Of Fisheries)
Original Goods And Services Tax Bill (From Authorized Dealer).
Registration Certificate Of Fishing Canoe (Registered Under Captain Of Ports Department).
Registration Certificate Of Nets And Accessories (Registered With The Directorate Of Fisheries Under The Goa, Daman And Diu Fisheries Rules, 1981).

faqs.question: If I am purchasing or constructing a new fishing craft, what are the mandatory requirements regarding its size and construction material?
faqs.answer: The craft must be a New Fiberglass Reinforced Plastic or wooden canoe, and its size must be strictly below 26 feet in length.

faqs.question: Which specific community of people is this financial assistance program intended to support for their day-to-day work?
faqs.answer: The scheme is introduced to uplift the sizeable community of traditional Fishermen by providing financial help in the form of a subsidy for carrying out their activities.

faqs.question: Is there any restriction regarding past financial history with the Department that would disqualify me from submitting an application?
faqs.answer: Yes, an applicant shall not be categorized as a defaulter of the Department responsible for administering this particular scheme.

faqs.question: What specific reservation groups (including gender) are eligible to receive a higher rate of financial assistance under the scheme provisions?
faqs.answer: Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribes, Women, and their Co-operatives are eligible for assistance covering 60% of the unit cost, limited to ₹60,000/-.

faqs.question: Does the governing body retain the authority to make discretionary changes or exceptions to the established scheme rules if necessary?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Government is empowered to relax all or any of the clauses provided in this scheme if it is found deemed fit, provided reasons are recorded.

faqs.question: After acquiring the required unit (canoe, nets, and boxes), what specific type of invoice documentation is required to claim the approved subsidy amount?
faqs.answer: You must produce the original Goods and Services Tax bill from the authorized dealer towards the purchase or construction of the new canoe, gill net, and accessories.

faqs.question: After receiving the new fishing canoe, is there a mandatory requirement for registering this particular craft with any specific governmental authority?
faqs.answer: Yes, the fishing canoe purchased or constructed under the scheme must be legally registered under the Captain of Ports Department.

faqs.question: For the purpose of calculating the subsidy percentage and the maximum limit, what is the fixed unit cost utilized by the scheme?
faqs.answer: The unit cost considered for the entire Craft & Gear unit, including nets and insulated fish and ice holding boxes, is fixed at ₹1,00,000/-.

faqs.question: If an applicant currently owns a large marine vessel used for fishing, such as a deep-sea trawler, are they still eligible for this subsidy program?
faqs.answer: No, an essential requirement for eligibility is that the applicant shall not be a fishing trawler owner.

faqs.question: What mandatory certificate must the applicant possess from the state's Fishery governing body before applying for the purchase or construction subsidy?
faqs.answer: You must possess the No Objection Certificate issued by the Directorate of Fisheries for the construction or purchase of the wooden or Fiberglass Reinforced Plastic fishing craft, net, and ice holding boxes.

faqs.question: Once I have purchased the unit using the government subsidy, for what duration am I restricted from transferring or selling the equipment?
faqs.answer: The beneficiary shall not sell, mortgage, or transfer the subsidized fishing canoe, nets, accessories, or insulated ice holding boxes for a period of five years from the date of its purchase.

faqs.question: Are there any geographical restrictions on where the fishing activities must be conducted using the subsidized craft and gear?
faqs.answer: Yes, the fishing activities must be carried out in the inland waters of Goa using the subsidized craft and equipment.

faqs.question: Besides the primary craft, must the fishing nets and related accessories acquired through the scheme also be formally registered?
faqs.answer: Yes, the nets and their accessories must be duly registered with the Directorate of Fisheries under the Goa, Daman and Diu Fisheries Rules, 1981.

faqs.question: How exactly will the approved financial subsidy amount be remitted to the successful applicant upon the successful verification of documents?
faqs.answer: The entire subsidy amount sanctioned shall be directly disbursed in favor of the applicant into his or her personal Bank account.

name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Rural Entrepreneurs to set up Custom Hiring Centres (CHC) of Farm Machinery
description: “Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Rural Entrepreneurs to set up Custom Hiring Centres (CHC) of Farm Machinery” under the Farm Mechanization Umbrella Scheme, was launched on 22nd October 2014, by the Agriculture Department, Government of West Bengal with the purpose to provide opportunity to rural entrepreneurs for setting up of Custom Hiring Centres to enable the farmers to hire different high end farm machinery from them at a reasonable rate with the objective of rural employment, enhanced productivity and risk mitigation during calamities. > Area of Operation: The scheme is applicable uniformly throughout the State, except Kolkata district. > Choice of Machinery: List of Machinery/implements that can be selected for CHC s furnished in Annexure-V (Page No. 38). List of available models of different farm machinery registered in Matirkatha portal with their indicative price will be published by the SPMT before starting of online application of the beneficiary so that the applicant can choose at least four types of Machinery / implements and maximum 2 (Two) nos. of tractors in a particular type from that list. The list is indicative but not exhaustive, any suitable farm machinery not included in the list may also be included in the project as per latest SMAM guideline supportive to local situation with the approval of SPMT. For any non-listed machinery, latest SMAM guidelines will be followed for arriving at subsidy portion of that particular machinery with the approval of SPMT.
benefits: > Pattern Of Assistance: The maximum subsidy will be limited to 40% of the Total Financial Outlay(TFO) (TFO = indicative cost of machinery including transportation + AMC for 3 years + cost of open shed + insurance for 1 year). Minimum TFO would be ₹20,00,000/- and the maximum would be as per SMAM Guideline and SPMT recommendation. An individual entrepreneur shall avail subsidy amounting ₹16,00,000/- or 40% of the TFO whichever is less to set up CHC. The maximum amount allowed for the cost of open shed for machinery will be limited to 5% of the TFO and total ancillary cost (other than machinery) should not exceed 10% of TFO. An individual entrepreneur shall avail subsidy amounting ₹16,00,000/- or 40% of the TFO whichever is less. Note: The applicant will have to deposit margin money of a minimum amount of 25% of TFO to the financing bank before release of subsidy by the DDA (Admn.) to the Bank and remaining amount will be bank loan. No machine/equipment will be procured by the Government. The Government will only release subsidy as back ended subsidy against procurement by the beneficiaries as per their choice under CHC with Bank Loan. The subsidy will be released through DBT mode to the concerned bank branch to subsidy reserve fund/loan account for CHC. The subsidy will only be applicable for purchase of farm machinery/equipment from the approved Farm machinery Manufacturers and Dealers as enlisted in the Departmental portal. A beneficiary or his/her spouse will not be eligible to apply afresh before completion of 4(four) years from release of the last subsidy for CHC scheme from the State under this Guidelines. The subsidy will be provided from SDS and different CSS like RKVY- Cafeteria, SMAM, NFSM( Pulse/Rice/Nutri Cereals), TRFA ( Pulse/Coarse Cereals), NMEO for implementation of CHC.
eligibility: Individual farmers registered under Krishak Bandhu (New) Scheme.. Groups like SKUS/PACS/FPO/FPC/FIG/SHG duly graded /LAMPS etc. approved/recognized by any Govt. Institutions/Departments are eligible to set up CHC.. The project cost/Total Financial Outlay (TFO) should be between minimum ₹20,00,000/-to maximum as per SMAM Guideline (https://agrimachinery.nic.in/Files/Guidelines/smam.pdf) and SPMT recommendation.- The applicant should have sufficient land under his possession (own land/leased/hired) for setting up the CHC.. The land in question must belong to “commercial or bastu or viti” category.. The age of the beneficiary should be minimum 18 years at the time of application..

faqs.question: What is the objective of the scheme?
faqs.answer: "One Time Assistance to Small and Marginal Farmers for Purchase of Small Farm Implements (OTA-SFI)" by the Agriculture Department, Government of West Bengal aims to aid the farmers in procuring manually operated small farm implements necessary for agricultural operations.

faqs.question: Which department has launched this scheme?
faqs.answer: Department Of Agriculture, Government of West Bengal has launched this scheme.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Individual farmers registered under Krishak Bandhu (Natun) Scheme. Or, Groups like SKUS/PACS/FPO/FPC/FIG/SHG duly graded /LAMPS etc approved/recognized by any Govt. Institution/Departments.

faqs.question: How to avail the benefits of the scheme?
faqs.answer: Bonafide farmers can apply online in Matirkatha/ FMS portal after due advertisement in leading dailies, Departmental website: https://wbfms.matirkatha.net/applicants/sign up . After successful submission of online application, hard copies of print out of the application with acknowledgement receipt, recent passport size photograph and other prescribed documents (self-attest, if required) will have to be submitted to the office of the Deputy Director of Agriculture of the concerned District within the stipulated period.

faqs.question: What is the mode of selection of beneficiaries?
faqs.answer: Computerized lottery/random selection (GP wise) of valid applications will be done for preparation of priority list by the DLSC with the help of the IT Personnel engaged for software maintenance to give equal opportunity to all the applicants within the GP.

faqs.question: Is there any fee or charges to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, there are no charges to apply for this scheme.

faqs.question: Is there any age restriction?
faqs.answer: The age of the beneficiary should be minimum 18 years at the time of application.

faqs.question: Is there any priority for female applicants?
faqs.answer: No.

faqs.question: Is there any income criteria for the farmers to be eligible for this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, there is no specific income criteria for the farmers to be eligible for this scheme.

faqs.question: Whether an employee/retired employee of State Government/Statutory Bodies/Government Undertakings are eligible to apply?
faqs.answer: No, an employee/retired employee of State Government/Statutory Bodies/Government Undertakings are not eligible to apply.

faqs.question: How will the subsidy be released to the beneficiary?
faqs.answer: Disbursement should be done through NEFT/ RTGS/ Cheques by the Bank directly to the dealer/ supplier/manufacturers as per quotation/ estimate chosen by the entrepreneur for CHC & which is received by the Bank from the DDA(Admn.)'s office as per approval of DLSC.

faqs.question: What is the pattern of assistance?
faqs.answer: The maximum subsidy will be limited to 40% of the Total Financial Outlay(TFO) which will be provided to the beneficiary.

name: Compensation for Human Death or Injury Caused by Wild Animals
description: The “Compensation for Human Death or Injury Caused by Wild Animals” scheme is launched by the Forest Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh. The scheme aims to provide financial relief to the families of deceased persons or individuals injured due to attacks by wild animals. The scheme covers both urban and rural areas and ensures quick assistance through a time-bound process.
benefits: Compensation Amount: In case of death: ₹4,00,000 is paid to the deceased’s legal heir or family member after deducting any temporary assistance already given and the actual cost of medical treatment before death.- In case of injury: Actual medical expenses are reimbursed, along with ₹500 per day (maximum ₹50,000) if hospitalized, after deducting any temporary assistance already provided. Expected Time of Disbursement: Within 3 working days in case of death. Within 7 working days in case of injury. Mode of Disbursement: The payment is made directly to the beneficiary’s bank account via e-payment.
eligibility: The applicant must be a resident of Madhya Pradesh.. The applicant should be a victim of a wild animal attack, resulting in injury or death.. The applicant should submit proof that the injury or death was caused by a wild animal (excluding snakes, monitor lizards, and other poisonous creatures).. In the case of death, the applicant must be a legal heir, family member, or relative of the deceased person..
documents: Identity Proof Resident Proof Bank Account Details Death Certificate Treatment Bills Other Necessary Documents, if required

faqs.question: Who can apply under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Any person or family affected by a wild animal attack, excluding snake or poisonous animal cases.

faqs.question: What is the compensation amount for death cases?
faqs.answer: ₹4,00,000 after adjusting temporary assistance and medical expenses.

faqs.question: What is the compensation for injury cases?
faqs.answer: Actual treatment expenses and ₹500 per day (up to ₹50,000) if hospitalized.

faqs.question: Is there any application fee?
faqs.answer: No, the application process is free of cost.

faqs.question: Where can I apply?

name: Chhatraon Ke Liye Protsahan Rashi

This includes learning about innovative farming techniques, crop management practices, breeding strategies, and technological advancements that can increase yields and efficiency in agricultural production. Students learn about food safety standards, quality control measures, food processing techniques, and foodborne pathogens to ensure the safety and integrity of the food supply.

Postgraduate Level: Girls pursuing M.Sc. Agriculture (2 years) will receive a scholarship of ₹25,000 per year. PhD Level: Girls pursuing PhD in Agriculture (maximum 3 years) will receive a scholarship of ₹40,000 per year.
