faqs.question: How much is the unit cost for Arabica and Robusta under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The unit cost for Arabica is [?]2,75,000 per hectare, and for Robusta, it is [?]2,00,000 per hectare.

faqs.question: What percentage of subsidy is provided to coffee growers under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Coffee growers are eligible for a 40% subsidy of the unit cost.

faqs.question: Are there any special provisions for SC/ST community coffee growers?
faqs.answer: Yes, SC/ST community coffee growers with holdings up to 4.00 hectares are eligible for an additional 10% support of the unit cost.

faqs.question: How is the subsidy released for clean replanting?
faqs.answer: For clean replanting, the first instalment is 70% of the applicable unit cost, and the second instalment is 30% of the applicable unit cost.

faqs.question: What is the subsidy release process for replantation by interlining method?
faqs.answer: In the case of replantation by interlining, the first instalment is 30% of the applicable unit cost, and the second instalment is 70% of the applicable unit cost.

faqs.question: What are the age criteria for coffee plants that can be replanted under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Arabica plants aged 25 years, Robusta plants aged 40 years, and Arabica dwarfs aged 15 years can be replanted.

faqs.question: Is there a specific requirement for the removal of old plants in the case of interlining?
faqs.answer: Old and unproductive plants should preferably be removed after one harvest but not beyond two harvests to ensure vigorous growth of the newly interlined plants.

faqs.question: Does the choice of coffee variety depend on the elevation of the plantation?
faqs.answer: Yes, in Arabica zones with an elevation of 1000 meters above MSL, only disease-tolerant, high-yielding Arabica varieties should be replanted. In other areas, both Arabica and Robusta can be replanted.

faqs.question: What is the subsidy calculation for coffee grown with intercrops like pepper and banana?
faqs.answer: The subsidy is based on the actual extent of the area replanted with coffee or the maximum extent mentioned in the land documents, including other intercrops, whichever is less.

faqs.question: Are there any recommendations for planting designs?
faqs.answer: Growers are encouraged to adopt planting designs suitable for mechanization. Modified planting designs amenable to mechanization can be considered for the entire area of replanting.

faqs.question: Are there any exclusions for those who have previously received subsidies?
faqs.answer: A grower who has availed subsidy for one activity/component cannot avail subsidy for the same activity/component during the MTF period until new beneficiaries are covered.

faqs.question: What is the exclusion related to Arabica replaced with Robusta?
faqs.answer: Arabica replaced with Robusta at a higher elevation of more than 1000 meters is not eligible for support.

faqs.question: When can a grower claim the first instalment of the subsidy?
faqs.answer: The first instalment can be claimed during the same financial year of replanting as far as possible.

faqs.question: What documents are required for claiming the first instalment of the subsidy?
faqs.answer: The required documents include a claim statement, a sketch of the replanted area, and an expenditure statement.

name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing
description: The scheme "Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing" is a Sub-Component of the Scheme "Integrated Coffee Development Project During the Medium Term Framework (MTF) Period: Development Support to Stakeholders" by the Coffee Board, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The objective of the scheme is to extend support to small and tiny growers, incentivizing them to form collectives/ Self Help Groups/ Cooperatives, thus encouraging them to take up marketing of coffee produced on a community-based approach through suitable financial incentives. This way, they will not only be able to improve the quality of coffee but also realize better value for their coffees. It is expected to provide a mechanism for better price realization for the group, arising out of both the improvement of quality as well as collective bargaining.
benefits: Scale of Subsidy: ₹4.00 per kg of Clean Coffee.
eligibility: The applicant should belong to Small Growers'. Collectives / Self Help Groups (SHGs) / Co-operatives in traditional coffee-growing states.. faqs.question: Can a grower who has availed subsidy under one activity/component claim subsidy for the same activity/component again during the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) period?
faqs.answer: No, a grower who has availed subsidy under one activity/component is not eligible to claim subsidy for the same activity/component during the MIDH period unless new beneficiaries are covered.

faqs.question: What additional documents are required for coffee exported directly?
faqs.answer: For coffee exported directly, additional documents include an export permit with Customs endorsement, ICO certificate of origin with customs endorsement, and the Bill of Lading (BL).

faqs.question: What additional documents are necessary for coffee marketing through auction platforms or commodity exchanges?
faqs.answer: For coffee marketed through auction platforms or commodity exchanges, additional documents include a registration certificate as a member of ICTA or other recognized marketing auction platform, and proof of coffee sold, attested by the auctioneers.

faqs.question: What are the mandatory documents required for claiming the subsidy?
faqs.answer: The required documents include the application in the prescribed format, certificate of incorporation/registration, complete member details, member-wise coffee sales details, and certificates indicating membership in the Growers' Collective/SHG/Cooperative and VAT registration certificate from the state Government commercial tax department where applicable.

faqs.question: When is the subsidy disbursed to the individual members of small growers' collectives/SHGs/Cooperatives?
faqs.answer: The subsidy is disbursed only after the sale of coffee is completed by small growers' collectives/SHGs/Cooperatives, and it is released directly to the individual members' bank accounts through National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) in cases where the application is complete in all respects.

faqs.question: What is the procedure for claiming subsidy under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Small growers' collectives/SHGs/Cooperatives should furnish their claim for reimbursement along with supporting documents after marketing their coffee. The application for subsidy should be submitted to the concerned Deputy Director (Extension) during the same financial year of completing the activity.

faqs.question: How much subsidy is provided per kilogram of clean coffee under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The subsidy is [?]4.00 per kilogram of clean coffee.

faqs.question: What are the acceptable methods of marketing coffee under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Coffee marketing should be carried out either through recognized public auction platforms like the Indian Coffee Trade Association (ICTA), direct export by the organization, or through recognized Commodity Exchanges with physical delivery of coffee.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to benefit from the "Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing" scheme?
faqs.answer: All Small Growers' Collectives, Self Help Groups (SHGs), and Cooperatives in traditional coffee-growing states are eligible.

faqs.question: What is the objective of the scheme "Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Support to Small Growers' Collectives/ SHGs/ Cooperatives for Coffee Marketing"?
faqs.answer: The scheme aims to support small and tiny coffee growers in forming collectives, Self Help Groups (SHGs), or cooperatives, thus encouraging them to engage in the marketing of coffee produced through a community-based approach, with financial incentives to improve coffee quality and enhance its value.

faqs.question: Are there any special provisions for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe (SC/ST) community growers?
faqs.answer: Yes, SC/ST community growers with smaller holdings can receive additional support during the MIDH period.

faqs.question: What is the role of the Coffee Board in implementing this scheme?
faqs.answer: The Coffee Board oversees the approval and disbursement of subsidies to eligible growers.

faqs.question: How can a small grower ensure eligibility for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Small growers should market coffee in the name of their collectives/SHGs/Cooperatives through recognized channels.

faqs.question: Can you explain the importance of recognized public auction platforms?
faqs.answer: Recognized auction platforms provide a transparent and efficient way to sell coffee and realize better prices.

faqs.question: Can individuals benefit from this scheme, or does it require collective action?
faqs.answer: Both individual small growers and collectives/SHGs/Cooperatives can benefit from this scheme.

faqs.question: Is this scheme applicable to non-traditional coffee-growing areas?
faqs.answer: This scheme is primarily aimed at traditional coffee-growing states.

faqs.question: What is the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) period?
faqs.answer: The MIDH period is the timeframe during which the subsidy cannot be availed again for the same activity/component by growers who have already received it.

faqs.question: How can small growers realize better value for their coffee through this scheme?
faqs.answer: They can achieve better value by marketing coffee on a community-based approach and through financial incentives.

faqs.question: What is the significance of forming collectives or SHGs for coffee marketing?
faqs.answer: Forming collectives or SHGs helps small growers improve coffee quality and realize better prices through collective bargaining.

faqs.question: What documents are required if coffee is exported directly?
faqs.answer: For direct export, documents such as an export permit, ICO certificate of origin, and Bill of Lading are needed.

name: Distribution Of Tractor Unit Under CMSGUY
description: The "Distribution of Tractor Unit" Scheme is a Component under the Umbrella Scheme of "Chief Minister Samagra Gramya Unnayan Yojna (CMSGUY)" by the Govt. of Assam. CMSGUY is a village development scheme launched by Hon'ble Chief Minister Sarbananda Sonowal on 5th February 2017 in Guwahati. The scheme is being implemented in a mega mission mode in all villages of Assam. CMSGUY will be implemented through a saturation model by covering each revenue village through focused interventions in direct economic activities, logistic support including market linkages, and community support. The main objective of the "Distribution of Tractor Unit" scheme is to revive the agricultural sector and help in doubling the farmer’s income by 2022. Under the new revised tractor scheme, the government will provide one tractor along with some necessary accessories in each revenue village at subsidized rates. The state govt. will distribute approx 10,109 tractors in the first phase. This tractor distribution scheme will cover all 26,000 villages of the entire state in a phase-wise manner. A group of 8-10 people who are actual adult farmers can apply to this scheme. The state govt. has allotted ₹ 1,000 Crore for the successful implementation of this scheme.
benefits: Provision of Subsidy: 70% subsidy will be provided to the selected groups on the price of the tractor, and its accessories including implements (as opted by the beneficiary group) subject to a maximum of ₹ 5,50,000. 20% of the total price will be a bank loan. 10% of the total price will be the beneficiary share. Provided that subsidy will be admissible on the lowest price of the tractor in the Govt. notified list of tractors for the category (HP range) concerned. Similarly, the lowest approved prices of implements, if and as opted, will be applicable for subsidy on implements. The group will provide tractors to the farmers on a rental basis. Tractor Unit: Each tractor unit shall consist of one tractor (35 to 50 HP) with standard accessories and Matching Implements (as opted by beneficiary group) as follows - Standard Accessories (1 Set): a) Trailering Hook; Matching Implements (Optional): a) Rotavator (1) Standard Accessories (1 Set): b) Stabilizer Assembly; Matching Implements (Optional): b) Disc Harrow (1) Standard Accessories (1 Set): c) Hitch Assembly; Matching Implements (Optional): c) Cultivator (1) Standard Accessories (1 Set): d) Hood; Matching Implements (Optional): d) Trailer (1) Standard Accessories (1 Set): e) Tool kit; Matching Implements (Optional): e) Cage Wheel (1 Pair) Choice of the Applicant Groups: All the applicant groups who have already applied for the tractor unit will be required to furnish their choice as under: a) Whether they will avail bank finance for the beneficiary share: Yes/No. b) Name of the brand and model out of the list notified by the State Govt. c) Names of the implements out of the 5 (five) implements. (NOTE: The applicant group is free to choose all/any/none of the implements. The subsidy at the rate of 70% will be available to the applicant group on the total cost of the tractor unit so opted subject to a maximum of ₹ 5,50,000.) Duration of Service: The group shall be liable to provide tractor units (fully or partially as per the need of the farmer) to the farmers of the village on a rental basis for a minimum period of five years at a reasonable rate which may be fixed by the District Level Committee (DLC).

faqs.question: What is the objective of the "Diesel VAT Relief Scheme for Fishermen" scheme?
faqs.answer: The "Diesel VAT Relief Scheme for Fishermen" provides financial assistance by subsidizing the VAT levied on high-speed diesel used in fishing boats. This helps reduce the operational cost of fishermen using mechanized boats.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to get benefit from this scheme?
faqs.answer: Fishermen who own mechanized fishing boats that are less than 20 meters in length and possess a valid diesel card issued by the government are eligible for this scheme.

faqs.answer: Fishermen must purchase diesel from government-approved diesel pumps to be eligible for the VAT subsidy.

faqs.answer: Yes, the government sets a fixed diesel quota per fisherman, which determines the amount of diesel that can be purchased at the subsidized rate.

name: National Agriculture Market
description: The "e-National Agriculture Market (e-NAM)" is a pan-India electronic trading platform launched on 14th April 2016 to integrate APMC mandis across the country under the “One Nation One Market” initiative. Implemented by the Small Farmers Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC) under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, the platform provides online trading facilities for agricultural commodities. It offers services such as commodity arrival information, quality assaying, e-bidding, and direct e-payment to farmers through a single-window system. The scheme aims to improve transparency, efficiency, and better price discovery in agricultural marketing. In Jammu & Kashmir, 11 mandis have been integrated with the e-NAM platform since May 2020.
benefits: > For Farmers: Access to Pan-India Markets through a digital trading platform. Real-time Price Discovery based on demand and supply. Transparency in auction and payment processes. Better Prices through wider buyer participation. Online Payment directly to farmers' bank accounts. Free Quality Testing (Assaying) of produce in markets. Reduced Information Asymmetry—farmers can see prices and make informed decisions. > For Markets (APMCs/RMCs): One-time Grant of up to ₹30 lakh per market for hardware, internet, assaying labs, etc. Free e-NAM Software is provided with customization for each state. Support Staff (1 person per market) provided for 1 year at no cost. Provision to use Cold Storages & Warehouses as market sub-yards. Infrastructure Support for setting up: e-auction halls. assaying labs. electronic weighbridges. training facilities. > For State Governments / UTs: Eligibility for Central Funding upon adopting key APMC Act reforms: Single trading license for the state. Single-point market fee. Legal provision for e-trading. Support for Soil Testing Labs (STLs) under related schemes (NMSA/RKVY). Training, Dispute Resolution Mechanism, and linking more markets to e-NAM.
eligibility: The applicant State/UT must allow a single trading license valid across the State, issued through suitable legislation or executive orders.. The process should be liberal, without barriers like high deposits, quantity restrictions, or mandatory purchase centers.. The applicant State/UT must ensure single-point levy of market fee, applicable only at the first wholesale transaction.. No additional charges should be levied on subsequent wholesale transactions of the same produce.. The applicant State/UT must provide legal and infrastructural support for e-auction/e-trading, through relevant amendments or executive provisions.. The applicant must submit proposals in the prescribed format and fulfill all three core reforms above to be eligible for the one-time grant for infrastructure setup (hardware, internet, assaying equipment, etc.).. The applicant must commit to:. Trading 100% of selected commodities through e-NAM in the proposed markets.. Providing or linking markets to Soil Testing Laboratories (STLs).. Covering extra implementation costs beyond the sanctioned amount.. Bearing costs of software maintenance after 5 years.. Registering the implementing agency on the PFMS portal and submitting necessary bank details to the Department.. The applicant State/UT, if lacking an APMC Act or not enforcing it, must:. Identify an appropriate institution/organization.. Frame enforceable guidelines to enable e-trading, including trader registration, transaction norms, and infrastructure provisioning.. The applicant private market, if applying, must:. Be recommended by the concerned authority.. Provide all necessary infrastructure and services (e.g., analyst, assaying facilities) at its own expense..

faqs.question: What is the purpose of this online trading platform for agricultural markets?
faqs.answer: It is designed to integrate existing markets across the country into a single online system, enabling unified trading for agricultural commodities and promoting “One Nation One Market.”

faqs.question: How does this platform improve price discovery for farmers?
faqs.answer: It enables real-time price discovery through e-auctions and e-trading based on demand and supply, helping farmers secure better prices.

faqs.question: How does the system ensure transparency in agricultural trade?
faqs.answer: It offers clear, online auction processes, quality testing results, and direct electronic payments, reducing the scope for manipulation or hidden charges.

faqs.question: What services are provided to farmers through this platform?
faqs.answer: Farmers get single-window services including commodity arrival details, quality assaying, e-bidding for price discovery, and direct e-payment to their bank accounts.

faqs.question: How does quality testing work on this platform?
faqs.answer: Free assaying (quality testing) is offered at markets to help ensure standardized pricing based on the quality of produce.

faqs.question: What advantages does wider buyer participation offer to farmers?
faqs.answer: It increases competition among buyers, which helps farmers get better prices for their commodities.

faqs.question: What role do assaying labs and electronic weighbridges play?
faqs.answer: They help standardize and verify quality and quantity, making trading more reliable for both farmers and buyers.

faqs.question: How are market committees or boards supported for integration?
faqs.answer: They receive infrastructure support like e-auction halls, assaying labs, electronic weighbridges, internet, and training facilities to enable online trading.

faqs.question: Is software support provided to markets joining the platform?
faqs.answer: Yes, free software with state-level customization and support staff is provided to help markets manage online trading.

faqs.question: How does this system reduce information gaps for farmers?
faqs.answer: By showing arrival data, auction prices, and quality testing results online, farmers can make more informed selling decisions.

name: Establishment of Broiler Farms
description: The scheme “Establishment of Broiler Farms” was introduced by the Department of Animal Husbandry, Government of Uttarakhand. benefits: Under this scheme: A subsidy of ₹15/- per bird is provided for 6 batches, amounting to a total subsidy of ₹45,000/- per beneficiary. faqs.question: Are women and self-help groups given preference?
faqs.answer: Yes, women and members of self-help groups (SHGs) are given priority in the selection process.

faqs.answer: Beneficiaries receive a subsidy of ₹15/- per bird for 6 batches, totaling ₹45,000/-, and an additional ₹15,000/- grant for fence construction, making the total subsidy ₹60,000/- per beneficiary.

name: Ecomark Scheme of India (ECOMARK)
department: Ministry Of Environment,forests and climate change
description: The scheme "Ecomark Scheme of India (ECOMARK)" was launched by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India. The scheme provides an "Ecomark" label for products that meet specified environmental criteria with respect to resource consumption and environmental impacts, enabling consumers to make informed purchase decisions. The applicant must submit an application for the grant of Ecomark to the Central Pollution Control Board in Form 1. The scheme is implemented by the Central Pollution Control Board. The applications for this scheme are accepted online through the Ecomark web portal.
benefits: The scheme grants an Ecomark label to the product. The Ecomark granted to the product shall be valid for a period of three years or until a change in the Ecomark criteria for the product, whichever is earlier. Conditions Every holder of Ecomark shall submit an annual report to the Central Pollution Control Board online through the web portal on or before the 31st May of every year. Every person who has been granted an Ecomark in respect of a product shall affix on such product an Ecomark label granted under these rules. The holder of Ecomark shall allow the Central Pollution Control Board or the registered agencies to undertake such inspection and verification as may be considered necessary for ensuring compliance. The holder of the Ecomark shall grant access to the premises in which the product concerned is produced or kept to the Central Pollution Control Board and the registered agency.
eligibility: The applicant must be a producer, manufacturer, exporter, or importer of products specified under the First Schedule of the rules.. The applicant must have a license or a certificate of conformity of Indian Standards granted under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016.. The applicant must comply with the mandate of the Quality Control Orders issued by the Central Government, if applicable.. The applicant must fulfill the criteria for the grant of Ecomark specified under the corresponding entries of the First Schedule..

faqs.question: When my business manufactures automotive lead-cid or dry cell batteries, what specific documentary evidence must I supply to prove I handle post-consumer waste appropriately?
faqs.answer: You must provide a certificate or declaration proving you have established a collection pay back system for used batteries.

faqs.question: I understand that various government mandates apply to manufacturing quality. What specific central government directives must I ensure my product complies with before seeking this environmental certification?
faqs.answer: Your product must strictly adhere to the mandates of any Quality Control Orders issued by the Central Government, if they are applicable to your specific goods.

faqs.question: Once I successfully obtain the environmental label for my product, what recurring yearly obligation must I fulfill online to maintain my good standing and compliance?
faqs.answer: You are required to submit an annual report to the Central Pollution Control Board through the web portal on or before the 31st May of every succeeding year.

faqs.question: I am interested in applying for this environmental label, but I am unsure about the required business profile. What specific roles must an individual or company fulfill to be considered eligible for the certification?
faqs.answer: The applicant must be either a producer, manufacturer, exporter, or importer of the specific products listed under the First Schedule of the rules.

faqs.question: If my company produces plastic products, particularly those meant for food or cosmetics, what specific regulatory acts must I provide documentary evidence of compliance for?
faqs.answer: You must provide evidence demonstrating compliance with the regulations under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, and the Drugs and Cosmetic Act, 1940.

faqs.question: Before submitting my application for the environmental label, what specific documentation regarding product standardization must I have already acquired from the national standards body?
faqs.answer: You must possess a valid license or a certificate of conformity to Indian Standards granted under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016.

faqs.question: After receiving the official environmental certification for my manufactured goods, what action must I physically take regarding the packaging or the product itself to show my compliance?
faqs.answer: Every person granted the certification must appropriately affix the designated label directly onto the approved product.

faqs.question: Environmental regulations strictly monitor water usage and discharge. Which specific statutory document must I obtain regarding water pollution control to satisfy the documentation requirements for this application?
faqs.answer: You are required to submit a valid Consent Clearance as mandated by the provisions of the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974.

faqs.question: Following the approval of my product's certification, what access must I provide to the authorities or their designated agencies when they wish to verify my ongoing compliance?
faqs.answer: You must grant full access to the premises where the concerned product is produced, kept, or stored to the Central Pollution Control Board and their registered verification agencies.

faqs.question: I am reviewing the criteria required to qualify for the label. Where exactly can I find the specific environmental standards that my product must fulfill to be eligible?
faqs.answer: Your product must fulfill the exact environmental criteria outlined under the corresponding entries of the First Schedule of the rules.

faqs.question: In addition to air and water pollution clearances, what broader environmental statutory authorization might I need to attach to my application file, if it is applicable to my industry?
faqs.answer: You must include an authorisation under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, and the corresponding rules made thereunder, if your specific operations require it.

faqs.question: Once I am successfully granted the environmental certification for my product, how long will this approval remain valid before it either expires or requires a renewal process?
faqs.answer: The granted label remains valid for a period of three years, or until there is a change in the specified environmental criteria for that product, whichever occurs earlier.

faqs.question: Manufacturing operations often involve emissions. To prove that my factory complies with emission standards, which exact consent clearance document must be included in the submission?
faqs.answer: You need to provide a Consent Clearance in accordance with the provisions of the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981.

faqs.question: As a manufacturer operating within the textile sector, what specific proof of compliance regarding working conditions and auditory environments must I supply during the application process?
faqs.answer: You must submit documentary evidence demonstrating compliance with the provisions related to noise level and occupational health under the Factories Act, 1948.

name: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
description: The "Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry" is a component under the Sub-Mission on Breed Development of Livestock and Poultry, part of the National Livestock Mission (NLM). This initiative is introduced by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India. Under this scheme, the Entrepreneurship will be developed by inviting the individual, Self Help Group (SHG)/Framers Producer Organizations (FPO)/Farmers Cooperatives (FCOs)/Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) and Section 8 companies for establishment of Parent Farm, Rural Hatchery, brooder cum mother unit for Production of Hatching Eggs, and Chicks and rearing of the said chick upto four weeks in the mother unit. Emphasis will be given to those entrepreneurs who will be able to establish forward and backward linkage (Hub and Spoke). The scheme is implemented by State Implementing Agency and Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India. Objectives: Bringing unorganized rural poultry farming into the organized sector. Promoting entrepreneurship in rural poultry farming sustainably. Establishing forward and backward linkages. Popularizing non-conventional, low-cost feeding alternatives.
benefits: Financial Assistance: One Time 50% capital subsidy of the total project cost will be provided with maximum subsidy up to ₹25 lakhs for each unit. Note 1: The Central Government will provide 50% capital subsidy for the cost of the project for establishment of Parent Farm, Rural hatchery and Mother Unit with minimum 1000 parent layers. Note 2: Subsidy will be the capital subsidy and provided in two equal instalments. First instalment will be released upfront to the scheduled bank or financial institutions like NCDC etc. by SIDBI to be credited to the Entrepreneur/ Eligible Entities’ account after the bank or financial institution releases First Instalment of loan to the beneficiary and its confirmation by State Implementing Agency. Note 3: Beneficiaries will be eligible for release of the second instalment by SIDBI after completion of the project and certified so by the State Implementing Agency. Note 4: In case of the self-financing project, the project needs to be appraised by the bank where the Entrepreneurs/Eligible Entity have account. The first instalment of 50% subsidy will be provided into the lending bank by SIDBI where the beneficiary has account. The subsidy will be released only when the beneficiary has made expenditure of 25% cost for the project towards infrastructure and has been verified by the State Implementing Agency. Note 5: Remaining amount of 50% subsidy will be provided y SIDBI after completion of the project and verified by State Implementing Agency. Note 6: The Entrepreneurs / Eligible Entities interested in taking benefit under the entrepreneurship project in self-financing mode, need to provide Bank Guarantee from the scheduled bank valid for three years for the remaining cost of the project beyond the cost of subsidy sought for support. This Bank Guarantee shall be provided in the name of the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. Note 7: The Entrepreneurs / Eligible Entities need to arrange the remaining amount through bank loan or from the financial institution or self-financing.
eligibility: The applicant should be an individual, Self Help Group (SHG), Farmers Producer Organization (FPO), Farmers Cooperative (FCO), Joint Liability Group (JLG), or a Section 8 company.. The applicant should establish a Parent Farm, Rural Hatchery, or Brooder cum Mother Unit with at least 1,000 parent layers.. The applicant should arrange the remaining project cost through bank loans, financial institutions, or self-financing.. The bird maintained in the parent farm should be of Low Input Technology Birds or any sustainable bird for free-range management.. Note 1: Central Poultry Development Organizations, Central Avian Research Institutions, Directorate of Poultry Research and State Veterinary Universities and other private organizations with certificates of guaranteed production will be eligible to supply birds to the entrepreneurs. Necessary Technical specifications for birds will be issued separately. A list of Low input technology birds is at Annexure VI (https://www.dahd.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-11/NLMGuidelinesFinalApprovedByEC.pdf).. Note 2: No subsidy will be provided for working capital, personal vehicle, purchase of land, cost for rent and lease of land.. Essential requirements of beneficiaries to avail benefit under the submission:. Entrepreneurs/ Eligible Entities either have obtained training or have trained experts or have sufficient experience in the relevant field in managing and running the project or have technical experts with sufficient experience in the relevant field of managing and running the project.. The Entrepreneurs/ Eligible Entities have got the sanction loan for project by the bank or financial institutions furnished bank guarantee from scheduled bank along with appraisal of project for its validity by bank where it is holding the account.. The Entrepreneurs/ Eligible Entities should have own land or lease land where the project will be established.. The Entrepreneurs/ Eligible Entities have all the relevant documents for KYC..

faqs.question: Who can apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Individuals, Self Help Groups (SHGs), Farmers Producer Organizations (FPOs), Farmers Cooperatives (FCOs), Joint Liability Groups (JLGs), and Section 8 companies can apply.

faqs.question: How is the subsidy disbursed?
faqs.answer: For bank-financed projects, the subsidy is released in two installments—first after the loan disbursement and confirmation, and second after project completion and verification.

faqs.question: Is the scheme available for self-financed projects?
faqs.answer: Yes, self-financed projects are eligible, but applicants must provide a bank guarantee valid for three years for the remaining project cost beyond the subsidy amount.

faqs.question: What kind of poultry can be reared under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Only Low Input Technology Birds or those that can be sustained in a free-range management system are permitted.

faqs.question: What are the essential project components covered under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Parent Farms, Rural Hatcheries, and Brooder cum Mother Units with a minimum of 1,000 parent layers are covered.

faqs.question: How long does it take for the second installment of the subsidy to be released?
faqs.answer: The second instalment is released after project completion and verification by the State Implementing Agency.

faqs.question: Who verifies the project for subsidy disbursement?
faqs.answer: The State Implementing Agency verifies the project and confirms eligibility for the second instalment of the subsidy.

faqs.question: Can private organizations supply birds for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, private organizations with certificates of guaranteed production, along with designated research institutions, can supply birds.

faqs.question: What documents are required for application?
faqs.answer: Applicants must provide identity proof, address proof, business entity registration, a detailed project report, bank loan approval (if applicable), a bank guarantee (for self-financing), and a declaration form.

faqs.question: Can an applicant avail of this subsidy multiple times?
faqs.answer: The guidelines do not specify multiple availments; applicants should check with the State Implementing Agency for clarification.

faqs.question: Where can one apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Applications must be submitted through the designated online portal or the relevant State Implementing Agency.

faqs.question: What expenses are not covered under the subsidy?
faqs.answer: The subsidy does not cover working capital, personal vehicles, land purchase, rent, or lease costs.

name: Establishment of Entrepreneur for Breed Development in Small Ruminant Sector (Sheep and Goat Farming)
description: Launched in the Financial Year 2014-15, the scheme "National Livestock Mission" by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, aims towards employment generation, entrepreneurship development, increase in per animal productivity and thus targeting increased production of meat, goat milk, egg and wool. The excess production will help in the export earnings after meeting the domestic demands. The concept of the NLM Scheme is to develop the entrepreneur in order to create the forward and backward linkage for the produce available in the unorganized sector and to link with the organized sector. "Establishment of Entrepreneur for Breed Development in Small Ruminant Sector (Sheep and Goat Farming)" is a component of the "Sub-mission on Breed Development of Livestock and Poultry" scheme of the National Livestock Mission. The objectives of this component are: To develop entrepreneurs in the small ruminant sector. To develop a sustainable business model on sheep-goat. To incentivize individual entrepreneurs, FPOs, FCOs, SHGs, JLGs, and Section 8 companies for the development of an integrated rural sheep-goat production system. Conversion of the small ruminant sector from unorganised sector to organised sector through promotion of entrepreneurship & investment and creation of forward & backward linkages. Spreading awareness about scientific rearing practices, nutrition, disease prevention etc. Promotion of stall feeding model of sheep and goat rearing. The Entrepreneurs / Eligible Entities can establish sheep and goat breeding unit with a minimum of 500 females and 25 males. The sheep and goat unit to be established with the High Genetic Variety used for producing Goat milk, meat and fine wool quality. The breed of sheep and goat can be selected from the list provided with this guideline or in consultation with the State Government.
benefits: CAPITAL SUBSIDY STRUCTURE Maximum capital subsidy of Rs. 50 lakh offered, split into two equal instalments. Subsidy is specifically for capital expenditure, not operational costs. Instalments are released through SIDBI based on project milestones. DISBURSEMENT PROCESS FOR BANK-FINANCED PROJECTS First instalment released after bank provides initial loan and SIA confirmation. Second instalment provided after project completion and SIA certification. SIDBI manages fund transfer through scheduled banks/financial institutions. SELF-FINANCING PROJECT REQUIREMENTS Project requires bank appraisal where entrepreneur holds account. First 50% subsidy released after verified 25% infrastructure expenditure. Remaining subsidy provided post-project completion and SIA verification. BANK GUARANTEE SPECIFICATIONS Three-year bank guarantee required for self-financing projects. Guarantee must cover project cost beyond subsidy amount. Original document held by State Implementing Agency with copies for online portal. EXCLUSIONS FROM SUBSIDY Subsidy not applicable for working capital needs. Personal vehicles and land purchase not covered. Rental and lease costs ineligible for subsidy support.

faqs.question: What is the objective of this scheme?
faqs.answer: The primary objective is to develop entrepreneurs in the small ruminant sector, create sustainable business models for sheep and goat farming, and promote the transition from an unorganized to an organized sector through entrepreneurship and investment.

faqs.question: Who are the eligible beneficiaries under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Eligible beneficiaries include Individuals, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), Farmer Cooperatives (FCOs), Self Help Groups (SHGs), Joint Liability Groups (JLGs), and Section 8 companies.

faqs.question: What is the financial assistance provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides up to 50% back-ended subsidy for the capital cost of the project, with a maximum subsidy of [?] 50 lakh per unit. Subsidy is provided in two equal instalments.

faqs.question: What are the essential documents required to apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Essential documents include the application form, project proposal, identity proof, address proof, entity registration documents (if applicable), bank account details, loan sanction letter (if applicable), bank guarantee (for self-financing projects), declaration form, technical specifications, proof of expenditure, and land ownership/lease documents.

faqs.question: How is the subsidy disbursed?
faqs.answer: Subsidy is disbursed in two instalments: First Instalment: Released upfront to the scheduled bank or financial institution after confirmation of the first instalment of the loan by the State Implementing Agency. Second Instalment: Released after completion of the project and its verification by the State Implementing Agency.

faqs.question: Can urban residents apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: While the scheme primarily focuses on rural development, urban residents may apply if their projects align with the rural development objectives of the scheme. It is advisable to consult with the State Implementing Agency for specific eligibility criteria.

faqs.question: What is the follow-up process after the project is completed?
faqs.answer: The State Implementing Agency will follow up on the project for a period of two years after completion to monitor its operation and sustainability.

faqs.question: Are there any restrictions on the use of the subsidy?
faqs.answer: Yes, the subsidy cannot be used for working capital, personal vehicles, purchase of land, or the cost of rent and lease of land.

faqs.question: What support is provided for technical aspects of sheep and goat farming?
faqs.answer: The scheme includes spreading awareness about scientific rearing practices, nutrition, disease prevention, and promoting stall feeding models for sheep and goat rearing.

faqs.question: Who should I contact for more information about the scheme?
faqs.answer: For more information, contact the State Implementing Agency or the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry, and Dairying (MoFAHD), Government of India.

name: Exhibition Fair and Publicity

benefits: Awareness Creation: Farmers receive knowledge about horticulture schemes and technologies related to fruit, flower, vegetable, and spice crops. - Scheme Promotion: Departmental schemes are publicized to ensure more participation and benefit utilization among farmers.

faqs.question: What is the objective of this scheme?
faqs.answer: The objective of the scheme is to spread awareness about horticultural technologies and departmental schemes among farmers.

faqs.answer: The Horticulture and Food Processing Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh, implements this scheme.

faqs.question: What type of events are organized under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Exhibitions and seminars are organized at the district and block levels.

faqs.question: Who can participate in these exhibitions and seminars?

name: Establishment of 50 Milch Animals Dairy Unit
department: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department

faqs.question: What is the objective of the "Establishment of 50 Milch Animals Dairy Unit" scheme?
faqs.answer: The "Establishment of 50 Milch Animals Dairy Unit" scheme has been implemented to encourage the breeding and rearing of Gir and Kankrej cows while creating self-employment opportunities in rural areas.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Any livestock owner who plans to establish a new dairy farm with 50 Gir or Kankrej cows is eligible to apply for the scheme.

faqs.question: What financial assistance does the scheme provide?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides a 7.5% interest subsidy for up to 5 years, financial support for shed construction, animal insurance, and subsidies for essential dairy equipment like electric chaff cutters, fogger systems, and milking machines.

faqs.question: Can an applicant who already owns a dairy farm apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, the scheme is intended for setting up new dairy farms and does not provide assistance for renovating or expanding existing dairy farms.

faqs.question: Is it mandatory for applicants to purchase 50 dairy animals?
faqs.answer: Yes, purchasing 50 Gir or Kankrej cows is a mandatory requirement to qualify for the benefits of the scheme.

faqs.question: What is the maximum financial assistance available for shed construction?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides a subsidy of up to 50% of the actual expenditure, with a maximum limit of ₹5.00 lakh for shed construction.

faqs.question: How much subsidy is provided for animal insurance under this scheme?
faqs.answer: A 75% subsidy on the premium for three years is provided, up to a maximum amount of ₹1,80,000.

faqs.question: From where the applicant need to get the loan approval?
faqs.answer: Applicants must obtain a loan from a Reserve Bank-recognized institution or bank to qualify for the scheme’s financial assistance.

faqs.question: Can an applicant receive a subsidy only for purchasing equipment under this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, the scheme mandates that applicants must avail of benefits for livestock purchase, dairy farm establishment, and insurance. Equipment subsidies are also provided.

faqs.question: What is the process for applying for the scheme?
faqs.answer: The applicant must first secure a loan for purchasing 50 dairy animals and then apply online through the I-khedut (https://ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in/) portal by submitting the required documents.

name: PMMSY: Establishment of New Freshwater Fin Fish Hatcheries-Haryana
description: The scheme "Pradhan Mantri Matasya Sampada Yojana: Establishment of New Freshwater Fin Fish Hatcheries" by the Ministry Of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of India, aims to support the establishment of new freshwater finfish hatcheries. Through this scheme, financial assistance in the form of subsidies is provided to beneficiaries for setting up these hatcheries.
benefits: > The project cost for one unit is ₹25,00,000/-. The subsidy will be limited to 40% of the project cost for beneficiaries belonging to the General Category. The subsidy will be limited to 60% of the project cost for beneficiaries belonging to the Scheduled Caste (SC) category or women beneficiaries.
eligibility: The applicant should have a Parivar Pehchan Patra (PPP).. The freshwater finfish hatchery should have a minimum capacity of 15 million fry per year per unit or 6.00 crore spawn per year per unit.. The hatchery should have a minimum area of 0.50 hectares.. The fish hatchery should be managed by qualified technical staff.. The applicant will ensure the supply of seed produced from the centrally assisted hatcheries to farmers at an affordable and reasonable price.. The fish hatchery will include a brooder pond, nursery ponds, rearing tanks, a small laboratory, water and electric supply, and required infrastructure facilities.. The cost of accreditation of the hatchery must be mandatorily included in the project estimates.. The projects having land on long-term registered lease will also be considered for Central financial assistance under the scheme.. The lease period or agreement shall not be less than a minimum period of 10 years.. The applicant, having their own land, must furnish revenue records with a clear land title..
documents: Agreement Deed between the beneficiary and the Fisheries Department. Date Of Birth Certificate (Voting Card/Birth Certificate/Aadhar Card/Matriculation Certificate). Caste Certificate (from first
class Magistrate/Tehsildar). Training Certificate of the beneficiary. Land Record from Tehsil (Own Land

Jamabandi, Nakal Akshizra, Farad) or Registered Lease Deed of minimum 10 years. Bills/Receipts/Vouchers. Photographs of the hatchery with the beneficiary. Details of Bank Account and Permanent Account Number (PAN) Card. Detailed Project Report (DPR)/Self Contained Proposal (SCP) as per Pradhan Mantri Matasya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) guidelines.

faqs.question: What is the minimum capacity required for a freshwater finfish hatchery under this scheme in terms of fry production?
faqs.answer: A freshwater finfish hatchery should have a minimum capacity of 15 million fry per year per unit.

faqs.question: What is the minimum capacity required for a freshwater finfish hatchery under this scheme in terms of spawn production?
faqs.answer: A freshwater finfish hatchery should have a minimum capacity of 6.00 crore spawn per year per unit.

faqs.question: What is the minimum area required for a freshwater finfish hatchery to be eligible for this scheme?
faqs.answer: The minimum area required for a freshwater finfish hatchery is 0.50 hectares.

faqs.question: Who is responsible for managing the fish hatchery according to the scheme's requirements?
faqs.answer: The fish hatchery should be managed by required qualified technical staff.

faqs.question: What is the beneficiary's responsibility regarding the supply of seed produced from the hatcheries?
faqs.answer: The beneficiary should ensure the supply of seed produced from the centrally assisted hatcheries to farmers at an affordable and reasonable price.

faqs.question: What are some of the essential facilities that a fish hatchery must include?
faqs.answer: A fish hatchery should include a brooder pond, nursery ponds, rearing tanks, a small laboratory, water and electric supply, and required infrastructure facilities.

faqs.question: Is the cost of accreditation of the hatchery included in the project estimates?
faqs.answer: Yes, the cost of accreditation of the hatchery will be mandatorily included in the project estimates.

faqs.question: Can projects on leased land be considered for financial assistance under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, projects having land on long-term registered lease can be considered for Central financial assistance under the scheme.

faqs.question: What is the minimum required lease period for land to be considered for this scheme?
faqs.answer: The lease period or agreement shall not be less than a minimum period of 10 years.

faqs.question: What document must a beneficiary with their own land furnish?
faqs.answer: The beneficiary, having their own land, should furnish a revenue record with a clear land title.

faqs.question: What documents can be submitted as proof of date of birth?
faqs.answer: Voting Card, Birth Certificate, Aadhar Card, or Matriculation Certificate can be submitted as proof of date of birth.

faqs.question: From whom should the Caste Certificate be obtained?
faqs.answer: The Caste Certificate should be obtained from a first-class Magistrate (Tehsildar).

faqs.question: What land records are required for beneficiaries with their own land?
faqs.answer: For their own land, Jamabandi, Nakal Akshizra, and Farad from the Tehsil are required.

department: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department

faqs.question: What is the objective of this "Establishment of Goat Unit (10 +1)" scheme?
faqs.answer: The "Establishment of Goat Unit (10+1)" scheme aims to promote the social and economic upliftment of goat breeders by encouraging goat breeding and genetic improvement through pure breeding.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Individuals belonging to the Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST women), and General category are eligible to apply. Priority is given to widowed and abandoned women from the Scheduled Tribe category.

faqs.question: Is the scheme available more than once for the same person?
faqs.answer: No, the benefit of the scheme can be availed only once in a lifetime per eligible individual.

faqs.question: Is there any age restriction for applicants?
faqs.answer: While there is no specific mention of an age limit, applicants must submit a valid date of birth certificate as part of the required documents.

faqs.question: Is there a difference in subsidy amounts based on category?
faqs.answer: No, all eligible categories (ST women, SC, and General) receive the same subsidy amount, which is 50% of the unit cost or a maximum of ₹45,000.

faqs.question: How will the subsidy be provided to the beneficiaries?
faqs.answer: The subsidy amount will be directly transferred to the beneficiary’s bank account after successful verification and approval of the application.

faqs.question: Is there a specific minimum time limit to reapply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: No, as the benefit is only available once in a lifetime, reapplication is not permitted.

faqs.question: Where can applicants submit their applications?
faqs.answer: Applicants can apply online through the iKhedut (https://ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in/) Portal or submit an offline application at the Gram Panchayat or the nearest Government Veterinary Dispensary.

faqs.question: Who should be contacted for more details about the scheme?
faqs.answer: Applicants can visit the official iKhedut Portal, Gram Panchayat, or the nearest Government Veterinary Dispensary for more details and assistance regarding the scheme.

faqs.question: What are the mandatory documents required for the application?
faqs.answer: Applicants must submit a copy of their Aadhaar Card, bank passbook or canceled cheque, barcoded ration card, caste certificate (if applicable), election card or any government-approved photo ID, certificate of date of birth, guarantee sheet, and a widow/desertion/disability certificate (if applicable).

name: PMMSY: Establishment of Medium RAS / Biofloc culture system - Haryana
description: The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana: Establishment of Medium RAS / Biofloc Culture System, introduced by the Ministry Of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of India, aims to provide capital assistance to fish farmers and entrepreneurs for establishing medium-scale Recirculatory Aquaculture Systems (RAS) and Biofloc systems. These models promote high-density fish production in controlled environments, significantly reducing land and water usage. It is a centrally funded scheme with a 50:50 cost-sharing pattern between the Central and State Governments. For RAS: Minimum 6 tanks of 30 m³ each (10 tons/crop)- For Biofloc: 25 tanks of 4 m diameter and 1 m height
benefits: The project cost is ₹25,00,000/- > Subsidy Distribution: 40% subsidy for General Category beneficiaries. 60% subsidy for SC and Women category beneficiaries.
eligibility: The applicant must be a permanent resident of Haryana and possess a valid Parivar Pehchan Patra (PPP).. The applicant must have access to own land or hold a registered lease for a minimum period of 10 years.. The applicant must ensure that the land is free from any legal and financial encumbrances.. The applicant must have access to a reliable water source such as a canal, tube well, river, or similar.. The applicant must provide a valid training certificate in fisheries or aquaculture.. The applicant must agree to manage and maintain the system at their own cost after setup.. The applicant must submit a Detailed Project Report (DPR) or a Self-Contained Proposal (SCP).. The applicant must sign an agreement with the Department of Fisheries to avail benefits under the scheme..

faqs.question: If I belong to the General Category, how much subsidy am I eligible for?
faqs.answer: As a General Category applicant, you are eligible for a 40% subsidy on the project cost.

faqs.question: Being a woman applicant, what subsidy benefit can I get under this scheme?
faqs.answer: As a woman applicant, you are eligible for a 60% subsidy on the project cost.

faqs.question: Can I apply if I don’t have a Parivar Pehchan Patra (PPP)?
faqs.answer: No, having a valid Parivar Pehchan Patra (PPP) is mandatory for applying.

faqs.question: Will my leased land be accepted for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you have a registered lease deed for at least 10 years, your leased land will be accepted.

faqs.question: I have a borewell on my land. Can I use it for this project?
faqs.answer: Yes, water from borewells, open wells, canals, rivers, springs, etc., is acceptable for the project.

faqs.question: Will the government take care of the maintenance after construction?
faqs.answer: No, you will be responsible for operating, managing, and maintaining the unit after construction at your own cost.

faqs.question: Do I need to include anything specific in the infrastructure setup?
faqs.answer: Yes, your setup must include all essential requirements, especially water treatment units for RAS/Biofloc.

faqs.question: Are there any service charges I should be aware of?
faqs.answer: Yes, you need to pay ₹10/- to the Atal Seva Kendra and an additional ₹10/- as service charges.

faqs.question: How long will it take for my application to be processed?
faqs.answer: Your application will be processed within 50 days as per the Right to Service (RTS) timeline.

faqs.question: Do I have to prepare a project report while applying?
faqs.answer: Yes, you need to submit a Detailed Project Report (DPR) or a Self-Contained Proposal (SCP) as per the guidelines.

name: Establishment of 1 to 20 Milch Animal Farm
department: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department
description: The "Establishment of 1 to 20 Milch Animal Farm" scheme introduced by the Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department, Gujarat, provides financial assistance in the form of an interest subsidy to livestock farmers to take up animal husbandry as a sustainable business. The scheme benefits livestock farmers by reducing their financial burden, thereby promoting large-scale dairy farming.
benefits: Interest Subsidy: Eligible farmers receive an interest subsidy of 12% on the unit cost fixed by NABARD or banks.
eligibility: The applicant must be a livestock farmer, which includes agricultural laborers, small and marginal farmers, landless people, Maldhari (pastoralists), and educated unemployed individuals.. The applicant should have taken a loan from a bank for dairy farming (1 to 20 milch animals).. Note:. Availability of the Land, livestock and water facilities with the Livestock Owners.. As per the above scheme, the scheme of interest subsidy on establishment of units of 1 to 20 milch animals (cows and buffaloes) is also available for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes animal owners of the state..

faqs.question: What is the objective of the "Establishment of 1 to 20 Milch Animal Farm" scheme?
faqs.answer: The "Establishment of 1 to 20 Milch Animal Farm" scheme aims to provide financial assistance in the form of an interest subsidy to livestock farmers.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Any livestock farmer, including agricultural laborers, small and marginal farmers, landless individuals, Maldhari (pastoralists), and educated unemployed individuals, is eligible to apply.

faqs.question: What is the primary benefit of this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides a 12% interest subsidy on loans taken for setting up dairy farms with 1 to 20 milch animals (cows and buffaloes), reducing the financial burden on farmers.

faqs.question: Is this scheme available for Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) livestock owners?
faqs.answer: Yes, the scheme is available for SC and ST livestock owners, ensuring inclusivity and financial support for marginalized communities.

faqs.question: Is land ownership mandatory for eligibility under this scheme in certain cases?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Livestock Owners must have land or access to land along with necessary livestock and water facilities to be eligible for the scheme.

faqs.question: What type of animals are covered under this scheme?
faqs.answer: This scheme is applicable to milch animals such as cows and buffaloes for dairy farming purposes.

faqs.question: Can an individual apply without taking a bank loan?
faqs.answer: No, it is mandatory for the applicant to take a loan from a bank in order to be eligible for the interest subsidy under this scheme.

faqs.question: Where should the applicant submit their application?
faqs.answer: The application must be submitted online through the I Khedut (https://ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in/) portal for further processing and verification.

faqs.question: What documents are required to apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: The applicant must submit proof of land or house ownership, bank loan approval documents, and other necessary documents required by the bank.

faqs.question: Who verifies the application after submission?
faqs.answer: The application is verified by the Veterinary Officer at the local veterinary dispensary and then sent to the Deputy Director of Animal Husbandry, District Panchayat for approval.

name: National Livestock Mission: Genetic Improvement of Pig breeds - Establishment of Pig Semen Collection and Processing Lab
description: The “Establishment of Pig Semen Collection and Processing Lab” is a component under the Genetic Improvement of Pig Breeds activity of the Sub-Mission on Breed Development of Livestock and Poultry under the National Livestock Mission. The scheme is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India through State Animal Husbandry Departments. Under the scheme, financial assistance of up to ₹150.00 lakh is provided as one-time Central share for establishment of semen laboratories and maintenance of breeding boar units. An additional ₹30.00 lakh is provided for procurement of consumables, medicines, chemicals, and other items required for initial semen processing activities. The scheme aims to improve pig productivity through artificial insemination, reduce inbreeding, and control sexually transmitted diseases in pigs.
benefits: > Establishment of Semen Processing Laboratory: Assistance is provided for setting up a semen processing laboratory at government pig farms to produce high-quality liquid boar semen for artificial insemination. > Financial Assistance for Laboratory Setup: One-time grants-in-aid of up to ₹1.5 crore are provided as the Central share for the construction of semen laboratories and maintenance of breeding boar units. > Support for Initial Operational Expenses: Financial assistance of ₹30 lakh is provided for the procurement of consumables, medicines, chemicals, and other materials required for initial semen processing activities. Funding Pattern: General States: Funding is shared in the ratio of 60:40 between the Central Government and the State Government. North Eastern & Himalayan States: Funding is shared in the ratio of 90:10 between the Central Government and the State Government. > Mode of Disbursement: The funds are provided as a one-time grant to the concerned state government through its Animal Husbandry Department. > Frequency of Disbursement: One-time disbursement. > Validity: The financial assistance is granted for the establishment of the laboratory and the first-time procurement of necessary materials.
eligibility: Eligible Entity:. State Livestock Agencies,. Animal Husbandry Department, State Government.
documents: Proof of Land Ownership or Lease Agreement

faqs.question: What is the purpose of the Establishment of Pig Semen Collection and Processing Lab scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme aims to increase per-animal productivity, reduce inbreeding, and prevent sexually transmitted diseases in pigs by providing high-quality boar semen for artificial insemination.

faqs.question: Who is responsible for implementing this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme is implemented by the State Implementing Agencies of the State Animal Husbandry Department and the State Animal Husbandry Departments.

faqs.question: What type of semen is used for artificial insemination under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Since frozen semen technology is not effective for pigs, artificial insemination is carried out using liquid boar semen, which remains viable for a longer duration when processed scientifically.

faqs.question: What assistance is provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Financial assistance is provided to establish semen processing laboratories at government pig farms to produce high-quality liquid boar semen for artificial insemination.

faqs.question: How much financial support is provided for setting up a semen processing lab?
faqs.answer: A one-time grant-in-aid of up to ₹1.5 crore is provided for constructing the lab and maintaining breeding boars. An additional ₹30 lakh is provided for the first-time procurement of consumables, medicines, and chemicals.

faqs.question: What is the funding pattern for the scheme?
faqs.answer: For most states, the funding is shared in a 60:40 ratio between the Central and State Governments. However, for the North Eastern Region (NER) and Himalayan states, the ratio is 90:10.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme is open to State Livestock Agencies and the Animal Husbandry Departments of State Governments.

faqs.question: Can private farms or organizations apply for assistance under this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, only State Livestock Agencies and the State Animal Husbandry Departments are eligible to receive assistance.

faqs.question: How does the scheme help in reducing inbreeding among pigs?
faqs.answer: By providing access to high genetic merit boar semen for artificial insemination, the scheme reduces the chances of inbreeding, which improves the overall genetic quality of pig populations.

faqs.question: Why is liquid boar semen preferred over frozen semen for pigs?
faqs.answer: Unlike large ruminants, frozen semen technology does not work well for pigs. Liquid semen, when processed hygienically, has a success rate of 60% in artificial insemination.

faqs.question: What kind of expenses are covered under the ₹30 lakh grant?
faqs.answer: The ₹30 lakh grant is meant for the procurement of consumables, medicines, chemicals, and other essential items required for the initial processing of boar semen.

faqs.question: Is the financial assistance provided on a recurring basis?
faqs.answer: No, the assistance is provided as a one-time grant to help set up the semen processing lab and procure initial supplies.

faqs.question: Where will the semen processing labs be set up?
faqs.answer: The labs will be established at government pig farms to ensure the production and availability of high-quality liquid boar semen.

faqs.question: Whom should an interested agency contact for more details?
faqs.answer: Agencies should reach out to their respective State Animal Husbandry Department for detailed guidelines, application procedures, and support.

name: Establishment of Regional Semen Production Laboratory and Semen Bank for sheep and goat
description: Launched in the Financial Year 2014-15, the scheme "National Livestock Mission" by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, aims towards employment generation, entrepreneurship development, increase in per animal productivity and thus targeting increased production of meat, goat milk, egg and wool. The excess production will help in the export earnings after meeting the domestic demands. The concept of the NLM Scheme is to develop the entrepreneur in order to create the forward and backward linkage for the produce available in the unorganized sector and to link with the organized sector. "Establishment of Regional Semen Production Laboratory and Semen Bank for Sheep and Goat (Genetic Improvement of Sheep and Goat Breeds)" is a component of the "Sub-mission on Breed Development of Livestock and Poultry" scheme of the National Livestock Mission. The objectives of this component are: Genetic improvement of Indigenous descript breeds of sheep/goat through selective breeding Genetic upgradation of non-descript sheep/goat breeds through cross-breeding with high genetic rams or bucks to increase productivity. Reducing negative selection and inbreeding among sheep & goat breeds by propagation of superior male germplasm through artificial insemination and other developed assisted reproductive technologies. The Central Government will provide assistance for the establishment of a Frozen Semen production laboratory for goat and a liquid semen production laboratory for sheep at regional level in a strategic location to cater the semen of elite animals to the nearby states in the said region. This Establishment of Regional Semen Station will be based on the Expression of Interest from the States in the said Region which can produce semen and supply semen for the states at the region. Also the regional semen station will work as regional semen bank for frozen semen for goat. The semen labs will need to adhere to the guidelines of Minimum standard protocols for semen processing while preparing the project proposals. The semen produced in this laboratory will be distributed to the neighbouring states.
benefits: The funding pattern will be 60:40 for all the states except NER & Himalayan States where it will be 90:10 and 100% for UTs. One-time grants-in-aid up to Rs. 4,00,00,000 as Central Share will be provided to the concerned state eligible for the establishment of Regional Semen Station for construction of semen laboratory, maintaining of breeding bucks and rams, sourcing of locally available high genetic merit animals and processing of semen. Rs. 30,00,000 will also be provided as a one-time expenditure towards procurement of consumables, medicines, chemicals etc. required for first-time processing of semen. The regional semen bank shall have to generate its own resources for running of the semen station. No recurring expenditure will be provided for running expenses of the semen station.

faqs.question: What is the objective of this scheme?
faqs.answer: The objective is to genetically improve indigenous sheep/goat breeds through selective breeding, upgrade non-descript breeds by cross-breeding with high genetic rams or bucks, and reduce negative selection and inbreeding by propagating superior male germplasm through artificial insemination and other reproductive technologies.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: State Livestock Agencies are eligible to apply for this scheme.

faqs.question: What financial assistance is provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides a funding pattern of 60:40 for most states, 90:10 for North Eastern Region (NER) and Himalayan States, and 100% for Union Territories (UTs). It includes a one-time grants-in-aid up to [?] 400 lakh for the establishment of the laboratory and [?] 30 lakh for the initial procurement of consumables, medicines, and chemicals.

faqs.question: What are the key components of the project?
faqs.answer: Key components include the establishment of a Frozen Semen production laboratory for goats, a liquid semen production laboratory for sheep, and adherence to Minimum Standards for Sheep and Goat Semen Processing (MSP) guidelines.

faqs.question: What is the funding pattern for this scheme?
faqs.answer: The funding pattern is 60:40 for all states except for NER & Himalayan States where it is 90:10, and 100% for UTs.

faqs.question: What documents are required to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Required documents include the application form, project proposal, identity proof, address proof, entity registration documents, bank account details, land ownership/lease documents, technical specifications, detailed cost estimates, approval letters, environmental clearances (if applicable), a declaration form, and an Expression of Interest (EOI) from the state.

faqs.question: What is the process for subsidy disbursement?
faqs.answer: Subsidy is disbursed in two instalments: the first instalment is released upfront after the bank or financial institution confirms the first instalment of the loan, and the second instalment is released after project completion and verification by the State Implementing Agency.

faqs.question: Is recurring expenditure covered under this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, the scheme does not cover recurring expenditure for running the semen station. The regional semen bank is expected to generate its own resources for operational expenses.

faqs.question: What are the responsibilities of the State Implementing Agency?
faqs.answer: The State Implementing Agency is responsible for verifying the submitted documents, assessing project feasibility, disbursing funds, and conducting follow-up verification after project completion.

faqs.question: Where can I get more information about the scheme?
faqs.answer: For more information, contact the State Implementing Agency or the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry, and Dairying (MoFAHD), Government of India.

faqs.question: What are the Minimum Standards for Sheep and Goat Semen Processing (MSP)?
faqs.answer: The MSP guidelines provide the structure, requirements of logistics, equipment, and protocols for semen processing that the semen labs must adhere to when preparing project proposals.

faqs.question: Can the funding be used for purchasing land?
faqs.answer: No, the funding cannot be used for purchasing land, working capital, personal vehicles, or the cost of rent and lease of land.

faqs.question: How long will the State Implementing Agency follow up on the project?
faqs.answer: The State Implementing Agency will follow up on the project for a period of two years after its completion to monitor its operation and sustainability.

name: Establishment of Small Scale Poultry Unit (Layer) for livestock owner of Daman & Diu

Administration of Daman & Diu. It aims Economic up-liftmen of the SC/ST, SMF, and BPL Families. Financial assistance in the form of 50% subsidy is provided for the construction of a poultry shed, purchase of pullets (18–21 weeks), poultry equipments and feed for 4 months. The scheme beneficiaries can avail the benefit for two years or till becoming self-sufficient. Units must be operated on scientific lines, and beneficiaries must supply surplus eggs to nearby schools under the Mid-Day Meals Scheme, with fortnightly payment made by the Extension Officer (Dairy) or Veterinary Officer (DP). > Objectives Economic upliftment of the SC/ST, SMF, and BPL Families. To provide protein-rich food to the SC/ST, SMF, and BPL through eggs. To provide a regular supply of healthy eggs under the Scheme of Mid-Day Meals to nearby schools.

Purchase cost of reared pullets up to the age of 18-21 weeks old. Poultry equipments. Purchase cost of feed for the period of 4 months (till the beneficiary starts earning from the sale price of egg produce). Each beneficiary will be provided 50% subsidy to the total cost of the unit (i.e., total cost of purchase of Pullets, poultry feed, poultry equipments and construction of poultry shed, etc.), limited to ₹30,000/- per unit. The financial assistance should be used only for the purpose for which it may be granted. > Disbursement of Funds Subsidy will be paid directly to the individual or to the suppliers or to the body supplying goods or to an approved agency or institution. Subsidy shall be disbursed after completion of the poultry unit. The beneficiary will be entitled to get the benefit of the scheme for a period of two years or till he becomes self-sufficient.

The applicant must have the back ground of poultry farming, or in other cases, the participants must undergo practical training.. The applicant must operate the units on the scientific lines as per the technical guidance and services provided by the Department of Animal Husbandry &. Veterinary Services, Daman &.
