faqs.question: Can an applicant be considered if they or their family member has benefited from the scheme previously?
faqs.answer: No, applicants or their family members should not have benefited under the scheme previously to be considered eligible.

faqs.question: What is the role of the Deputy Director of Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare in the Selection Committee?
faqs.answer: In Puducherry region, the Deputy Director of Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare (Inland) serves as a member and convener of the Selection Committee.

faqs.question: How is the commencement of the rules for the subsidy determined?
faqs.answer: The rules come into force on the date of their publication in the official gazette.

faqs.question: Can an applicant specify the size of the aquarium they want to purchase under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, applicants should specify the size of the aquarium they want to purchase, as shown in the application form, for subsidised rate consideration.

faqs.question: What is the methodology of selection recommended by the Field Officers?
faqs.answer: Field Officers recommend applications based on the location of the applicant's house or residential place to the Selection Committee.

faqs.question: What is the target group for the aquarium subsidy scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme targets residents of the Union territory of Puducherry who fulfill the specified eligibility criteria.

faqs.question: What is the significance of the term "KFCMU" in the guidelines?
faqs.answer: "KFCMU" stands for 'The Karaikal Fishermen Co-operative Marketing Union, Karaikal,' one of the designated offices for obtaining Form-I in Karaikal region.

faqs.question: What is the Pattern of Assistance for purchasing an aquarium under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The unit cost is [?]7,000, with a 50% subsidy by the government ([?]3,500), and the beneficiary contributes the remaining 50% to the Secretary/Administrator of PSFCF/KFCMU/Fishermen Co-operative Societies.

faqs.question: Can you explain the role of the Pondicherry State Fishermen Co-operative Federation Limited (PSFCF) in the application process?
faqs.answer: PSFCF is one of the designated offices where applicants can obtain Form-I for benefiting under the scheme, and it plays a role in the application submission process.

faqs.question: What is the scope of an aquarium, as mentioned in the guidelines?
faqs.answer: An aquarium is described as an artifact that adds beauty to its surroundings, brings solace to the aged, soothes children, and helps reduce stress.

faqs.question: What is the maximum subsidy provided by the government for the purchase of an aquarium?
faqs.answer: The government provides a maximum subsidy of [?]3,500, covering 50% of the total unit cost of [?]7,000.

faqs.question: What is the role of the Selection Committee in the process of beneficiary selection?
faqs.answer: The Selection Committee, chaired by the Director of Fisheries, reviews recommended applications, ensuring the necessary documents are enclosed, and selects beneficiaries.

name: Grant of Subsidy for Purchase of 'Electric Vehicles' to Consumers in State of Goa
description: The scheme "Grant of Subsidy for Purchase of 'Electric Vehicles' to Consumers in State of Goa" was launched by the Department of New and Renewable Energy, Government of Goa. The scheme provides financial assistance in the form of a subsidy for the purchase or conversion of Electric two-wheelers, three-wheelers, and four-wheelers, along with scrapping incentives for old vehicles, incentives for local manufacturing in Goa, and low-cost loans provided by Convergence Energy Services Limited (CESL). The scheme is implemented by the Goa Energy Development Agency (GEDA). The applications for this scheme are accepted on a First Come First Serve (FCFS) basis.
benefits: State Subsidy (Quantum of Subsidy per kilowatt-hour) Financial Year 2021-2022: ₹10,000/- per kilowatt-hour (kWh) for Two Wheelers, Three Wheelers, and Four Wheelers. Financial Year 2022-2023: ₹8,000/- per kilowatt-hour (kWh) for Two Wheelers, Three Wheelers, and Four Wheelers. Financial Year 2023-2024: ₹6,000/- per kilowatt-hour (kWh) for Two Wheelers, Three Wheelers, and Four Wheelers. Financial Year 2024-2025: ₹4,000/- per kilowatt-hour (kWh) for Two Wheelers, Three Wheelers, and Four Wheelers. Financial Year 2025-2026: ₹2,000/- per kilowatt-hour (kWh) for Two Wheelers, Three Wheelers, and Four Wheelers. Capping of State Subsidy (Maximum amounts) Two Wheeler: Not exceeding ₹30,000/- (for a maximum of 3,000 vehicles). Three Wheeler: Not exceeding ₹60,000/- (for a maximum of 50 vehicles). Four Wheeler: Not exceeding ₹3,00,000/- (for a maximum of 300 vehicles). Scrapping Incentives (Goa Government Incentive for scrapping of vehicle) Two Wheeler: ₹5,000/-. Three Wheeler: ₹10,000/-. Four Wheeler: ₹10,000/-. Other Contribution for Scrapping of Vehicle by Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) or Convergence Energy Services Limited (CESL) Two Wheeler: ₹5,000/-. Three Wheeler: Not applicable (NIL). Four Wheeler: Not applicable (NIL). Incentive for Vehicle Manufactured in Goa: Two Wheeler: ₹5,000/-. Three Wheeler: ₹10,000/-. Four Wheeler: ₹15,000/-. Central Government Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Hybrid and Electric Vehicles (FAME)-II Scheme Subsidy: Provided as applicable. Low Cost Loans: Convergence Energy Services Limited will provide low cost loans to the consumer for the purchase of an Electric Vehicle if the vehicle is purchased from Convergence Energy Services Limited. Training and Capacity Building: Convergence Energy Services Limited will provide training/capacity building to local youths in the field of servicing of electric vehicles. Benefit Disbursal Conditions The total amount of financial subsidy will be decided by the Department of New and Renewable Energy. Disbursement will be done on a First Come First Serve (FCFS) basis. The subsidy shall be disbursed in a single installment to the beneficiary concerned, which is 100% on purchase or conversion of the vehicle. The Purchase Incentive for conversion of an Old Internal Combustion Engine vehicle into an Electric Vehicle by a retrofitting kit will be provided as per the capacity of the battery or maximum up to the capping of the State subsidy, whichever is lower. If a consumer opts to purchase an Electric Vehicle directly from a dealer and avail benefits from the Government of Goa, the financial assistance from Convergence Energy Services Limited will not be available. Post-Selection Obligations The beneficiary must ensure that the purchase incentive for conversion is subject to the approval of the retrofitting kit by the Regional Transport Office. The registered owner of an Electric Vehicle claiming a Scrapping Incentive must obtain confirmation of scrapping and de-registration of the old Internal Combustion Engine vehicle by the Regional Transport Office, as reimbursement is subject to this confirmation.
eligibility: The applicant must be a permanent resident of Goa.. The applicant must be the registered owner of the Electric Vehicle for which the Purchase Incentive is claimed.. The applicant must ensure the vehicle is an Electric Two Wheeler, Three Wheeler, or Four Wheeler purchased or converted in the State of Goa.. The applicant must purchase the Electric Vehicle from Convergence Energy Services Limited to avail of their low-cost loans and financial incentives..
documents: Copy Of Registration Certificate Book. Insurance Documents. Required To Substantiate Eligibility: (Inferred from explicit eligibility criteria) Aadhar Card Issued In Goa. Driving License Issued In Goa. For Specific Incentives/Conditions Confirmation Of Scrapping And De

Registration Of The Internal Combustion Engine Vehicle By The Regional Transport Office. (Required for reimbursement of Scrapping Incentive). Approval By The Regional Transport Office For The Retrofitting Kit. (Required for availing the Purchase Incentive for conversion of an old Internal Combustion Engine vehicle).
Required To Substantiate Eligibility: (Inferred from explicit eligibility criteria)
Confirmation Of Scrapping And De-Registration Of The Internal Combustion Engine Vehicle By The Regional Transport Office. (Required for reimbursement of Scrapping Incentive).
Approval By The Regional Transport Office For The Retrofitting Kit. (Required for availing the Purchase Incentive for conversion of an old Internal Combustion Engine vehicle).

faqs.question: What are the mandatory residency and documentation requirements applicants must fulfill to be eligible for financial assistance under this promotional effort?
faqs.answer: The applicant must be a permanent resident of Goa. They must also possess an Aadhar Card and a Driving License that have both been issued in Goa.

faqs.question: Are there any supplementary financial incentives provided for purchasing new vehicles that are specifically manufactured locally within the State of Goa?
faqs.answer: Yes, an incentive is provided if the vehicle is Manufactured in Goa. This incentive is ₹5,000/- for a Two Wheeler, ₹10,000/- for a Three Wheeler, and ₹15,000/- for a Four Wheeler.

faqs.question: What is the maximum total amount of subsidy available from the State Government that an eligible applicant can receive for the purchase of different categories of vehicles?
faqs.answer: The State Subsidy is capped, meaning it will not exceed ₹30,000/- for a Two Wheeler, ₹60,000/- for a Three Wheeler, or ₹3,00,000/- for a Four Wheeler.

faqs.question: How exactly will the various financial benefits, including subsidies and manufacturer contributions, be combined to help reduce the total upfront cost of the vehicle for the consumer?
faqs.answer: The Convergence Energy Services Ltd. (CESL) will club the incentives from the Faster Adoptions and Manufacturing of Hybrid and Electric Vehicles (FAME) II scheme of the Central Government, the State Government subsidy, and the contribution from the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM).

faqs.question: Who is responsible for determining the final financial subsidy amount, and what operational basis is used for deciding the sequence of disbursement to beneficiaries?
faqs.answer: The total financial subsidy amount will be decided by the Department of New and Renewable Energy. Disbursement of this assistance will be done based on a First Come First Serve (FCFS) approach.

faqs.question: Can applicants receive the contribution for scrapping an old vehicle provided by the Original Equipment Manufacturer or the Convergence Energy Services Ltd. for all vehicle types?
faqs.answer: No, the other contribution for scrapping, provided by the Original Equipment Manufacturer/Convergence Energy Services Ltd. (OEM/CESL), is limited to ₹5,000/- and is available only for the Two Wheeler category.

faqs.question: What specific financial incentives are offered by the Government of Goa to consumers who elect to scrap and de-register an old vehicle when purchasing a new electric model?
faqs.answer: The Goa Government Incentive for scrapping a vehicle is ₹5,000/- for a Two Wheeler and ₹10,000/- for both a Three Wheeler and a Four Wheeler.

faqs.question: Which specific categories of vehicles are eligible to receive the purchase incentive provided in the form of a subsidy under the scope of this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme's scope covers providing an incentive in the form of a subsidy to prospective users for the purchase or conversion of Electric Two Wheelers, Three Wheelers, and Four Wheelers in the State of Goa.

faqs.question: What is the specified method and required documentation for receiving the approved financial assistance after the purchase or conversion has been completed?
faqs.answer: The subsidy shall be disbursed in a single installment (100%) to the beneficiary concerned. This happens upon production of the documents of purchase/conversion, specifically a copy of the Registration Certificate book and Insurance by the beneficiary.

faqs.question: How is the exact amount of the Purchase Incentive calculated when converting an old Internal Combustion Engine vehicle into an Electric Vehicle using a retrofitting kit?
faqs.answer: The incentive is calculated based on the capacity of the battery or the maximum capping of the State subsidy, whichever amount is lower. This is provided subject to the retrofitting kit being approved by the Regional Transport Office (RTO).

faqs.question: If an applicant chooses to purchase their Electric Vehicle directly from a registered dealer, will they still be able to utilize all aspects of the available financial assistance?
faqs.answer: The consumer can opt to purchase the Electric Vehicle directly from a dealer and still avail benefits from the Government of Goa. However, in such a case, the financial assistance, specifically the low-cost loans, from the Convergence Energy Services Ltd. (CESL) will not be available.

faqs.question: Are there specific conditions under which the applicant will be eligible to receive low-cost loans offered by the Convergence Energy Services Ltd. (CESL)?
faqs.answer: The financial assistance, including low-cost loans, from Convergence Energy Services Ltd. (CESL) will be available only if the Electric Vehicle is purchased from CESL.

faqs.question: What is the specific financial calculation used to determine the rate of the subsidy provided by the Government of Goa for vehicles purchased during the 2021-2022 financial year?
faqs.answer: For the 2021-2022 financial year, the quantum of subsidy is calculated at ₹10,000/- per kilowatt-hour (kWh). This rate applies uniformly to Two Wheelers, Three Wheelers, and Four Wheelers.

faqs.question: Are there any predetermined limits set by the State Government regarding the maximum number of new vehicles for which subsidies will be provided across different categories?
faqs.answer: Yes, the subsidy is limited to 3,000 Two Wheelers, 50 Three Wheelers, and 300 Four Wheelers. Once these numbers are reached for each category, further subsidies will likely cease.

name: Grant of Subsidy for Purchase of Mobile Sea Food Van
department: Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department, Puducherry
description: Launched in 2010, the scheme "Grant of Subsidy for Purchase of Mobile Sea Food Van" is a subsidy scheme under the "Puducherry Development of Shore Based Facilities, Ice Plants, Service Unit, Infrastructural Facilities, and Quick Transport Facilities Rules, 2010" by the Department of Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare, Government of Puducherry. The scheme aims to provide fisherwomen, fisherwomen self-help groups, and Fisherwomen Co-operative Societies in the Union territory of Puducherry with a mobile seafood van. This van, financed through a combination of bank loan and departmental subsidy (25% and 75%, respectively), is intended for the sale of fresh and processed fish and fishery products in areas not served by regular markets. It focuses on maintaining hygiene and offering competitive prices to the public.
benefits: The scheme provides a subsidy of 75% on the cost of the mobile seafood van, including fabrication of the body, procurement of an insulated ice-box, a two-burner stove, cooking utensils, and accessories. The remaining 25% is expected to be covered by a bank loan. > MODE OF DISBURSEMENT The subsidy portion will be released to a separate account of the beneficiary in the bank.
eligibility: The applicant should belong to the fishermen community.. The applicant should be a resident of the Union territory of Puducherry by birth/domicile.. The applicant should be a non-overdue member of the Primary Fisheries Co-operative Society concerned.. The applicant should be between 18 and 50 years old.. The applicant should not be employed in Government, Government Undertaking, or societies, either part-time or full-time.. The applicant should be a registered Fisherwomen Co-operative Society in the Union territory of Puducherry, or a group under SHGs registered under District Rural Development Agency and Puducherry Urban Development Agency fold..
documents: Aadhaar Card. Proof of Age. Residential Certificate of the Union Territory of Puducherry. Copy of Food Sharing Card. Birth Certificate/ Voter ID. Caste Certificate. Registration Certificate of the Cooperative/SHG. Proof of Membership with the Cooperative/SHG. Price Quotations of the Equipment Used for Fish Preparation. Certificates of Training on Fish Product Preparation. Proof of Experience in Fish Product Preparation.
Residential Certificate of the Union Territory of Puducherry.
Proof of Membership with the Cooperative/SHG.
Price Quotations of the Equipment Used for Fish Preparation.
Certificates of Training on Fish Product Preparation.
Proof of Experience in Fish Product Preparation.

faqs.question: Is there a provision for extending the age limit beyond 50 under special circumstances?
faqs.answer: No, the age limit of 18 to 50 years is a fixed criterion, and there are no provisions for exemptions or extensions under special circumstances.

faqs.question: Can a fisherwoman self-help group apply directly for the scheme, or does it have to be under the umbrella of a registered Cooperative/SHG?
faqs.answer: A fisherwoman self-help group can apply directly if it is registered under the District Rural Development Agency or Puducherry Urban Development Agency fold.

faqs.question: How does the scheme ensure that the fish products are sold at competitive prices?
faqs.answer: The scheme focuses on maintaining hygiene and offering competitive prices to the public through the sale of fresh and processed fish by the beneficiaries.

faqs.question: Can individuals outside the age range of 18 to 50 apply for an exemption?
faqs.answer: No, individuals must fall within the specified age range of 18 to 50 to be eligible for the subsidy scheme.

faqs.question: What is the primary role of the Joint Director of Fisheries in the fund disbursement process?
faqs.answer: The Joint Director of Fisheries, along with regional officials and concerned banks, is responsible for withdrawing funds from the beneficiary's account for creating the mobile sea food van asset.

faqs.question: Is there any specific training requirement for applicants to qualify for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Applicants are required to provide certificates of training on fish product preparation as part of the documentation.

faqs.question: How does the scheme address the issue of areas without regular markets for fish products?
faqs.answer: The scheme addresses this by providing mobile sea food vans to fisherwomen, enabling them to sell fresh and processed fish in areas not served by regular markets.

faqs.question: Can the subsidy be used for purposes other than the purchase of the mobile sea food van?
faqs.answer: No, the subsidy is specifically intended for covering 75% of the cost of the mobile sea food van and associated equipment.

faqs.question: What role does the field enquiry play in the application process, and who conducts it?
faqs.answer: The field enquiry is a crucial step conducted by the Department to shortlist applicants. It is part of the selection process to ensure the eligibility of candidates.

faqs.question: Can a Fisherwomen Co-operative Society from outside the Union territory of Puducherry apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: No, the Fisherwomen Co-operative Society must be registered in the Union territory of Puducherry to be eligible.

faqs.question: How is the subsidy amount linked to the bank loan, and what is the role of the Department in this process?
faqs.answer: The subsidy amount is released to the bank once the letter of intent for the loan is received. The Department plays a crucial role in offsetting the loan amount of the beneficiary.

faqs.question: How does the Department ensure the quality of applicants during the selection process?
faqs.answer: The Departmental Selection Committee, with officials from different regions, shortlists applicants based on field enquiries before forwarding applications to the nationalized bank.

name: Grant of Subsidy for Procurement of Vehicle
department: Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department, Puducherry
description: Launched in 2010, the scheme "Grant of Subsidy for Procurement of Vehicle" is a Sub-Scheme under the Umbrella Scheme "Puducherry Development of Shore Based Facilities, Ice Plants, Service Unit, Infrastructural Facilities and Quick Transport Facilities" is a development scheme by the Department of Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare, Government of Puducherry. The scheme aims to facilitate the quick transportation of fish catches from landing centers to marketing places, thereby preventing/minimizing spoilage of fish. It provides a 50% subsidy for the procurement of specified vehicles.
benefits: 50% subsidy for the purchase of auto goods carrier up to 1-ton capacity (maximum subsidy of ₹75,000). 50% subsidy for the purchase of a mini truck with 1-3 ton capacity (maximum subsidy of ₹1,50,000). 50% subsidy for the purchase of a mini lorry with 3-5 ton capacity (maximum subsidy of ₹3,50,000). 50% subsidy for the purchase of an insulated fish van with 5-10 ton capacity (maximum subsidy of ₹5,00,000). 50% subsidy for the purchase of a moped with an insulated ice-box (maximum subsidy of ₹15,000). 50% subsidy for the purchase of engine spares for boats (maximum subsidy of ₹2,000 per boat per annum). > Mode of Disbursement The subsidy amount will be released to the bank and credited to the account of the beneficiary for whom the loan amount was sanctioned by the bank.
eligibility: The applicant should belong to the fishermen's community and must be a resident of the Union Territory of Puducherry by domicile or birth.. The applicant's age should not be less than 18 years old or more than 50 years of age.. The applicant should not have availed the benefit of a loan/subsidy under the scheme earlier for the purpose for which the subsidy is sought.. The applicant should be a member of a Fishermen Cooperative Society and should not have any overdue with the society/department.. The applicant should possess a driving license issued by the Transport Authority for driving a moped/auto goods carrier or transport vehicle.. The applicant should not be employed in Government/Government undertakings/Societies either on a regular/part-time or temporary basis..
documents: Loan Sanction Order From the Bank. Quotation From the Dealer for the Vehicle. Driving License and Badge for Driving Moped/auto Goods Carrier or Transport Vehicle. Purchase Invoice Copies and Rc Book for Vehicle Verification.
Copies of Mortgage Documents in Respect of the Beneficiary for Official Record.

faqs.question: What is the role of the Fishermen Cooperative Society in the application process?
faqs.answer: Being a member of a Fishermen Cooperative Society is a prerequisite, and applicants should not have any overdue with the society/department to be eligible for the subsidy.

faqs.question: Are there any specific guidelines for the verification of mortgage documents?
faqs.answer: Copies of mortgage documents in respect of the beneficiary are required for official record-keeping and verification purposes.

faqs.question: Is there any provision for reconsideration if an applicant's subsidy is initially declined?
faqs.answer: The scheme does not specify a provision for reconsideration once the Departmental Selection Committee has completed the shortlisting process.

faqs.question: Is there a specific format for submitting the application?
faqs.answer: Applicants need to submit the application in the prescribed format issued by the Department of Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare.

faqs.question: Can the subsidy amount be utilized for purposes other than vehicle procurement?
faqs.answer: The subsidy is specifically intended for the purchase of specified vehicles and engine spares for boats as outlined in the scheme.

faqs.question: Is there a specific format for submitting the application?
faqs.answer: Applicants need to submit the application in the prescribed format issued by the Department of Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare.

faqs.question: Can the subsidy be used for the purchase of engine spares for boats?
faqs.answer: Yes, the scheme offers a 50% subsidy for the purchase of engine spares for boats, with a maximum subsidy of [?]2,000 per boat per annum.

faqs.question: Are there any specific conditions for the driving license required for eligibility?
faqs.answer: The applicant should possess a driving license issued by the Transport Authority for driving moped/auto goods carrier or transport vehicle.

faqs.question: Is there a deadline for producing documentary evidence for verification after vehicle purchase?
faqs.answer: Beneficiaries need to produce documentary evidence for verification within 60 days of vehicle purchase.

faqs.question: What is the maximum subsidy amount for the purchase of a mini lorry?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides a 50% subsidy for the purchase of a mini lorry with 3-5 ton capacity, with a maximum subsidy of [?]3,50,000.

faqs.question: Can a fisherman apply for subsidy without being a member of a Fishermen Cooperative Society?
faqs.answer: No, the applicant must be a member of a Fishermen Cooperative Society to be eligible for the subsidy.

faqs.question: How is the subsidy amount disbursed to the beneficiary?
faqs.answer: The subsidy amount is released to the bank and credited to the account of the beneficiary, as sanctioned by the bank.

name: Generator Subsidy-Tamil Nadu
description: The “Generator Subsidy” scheme provides a 25% subsidy or maximum ₹1,50,000/- on the cost of generator sets up to 125 KVA capacity for manufacturers in Tamil Nadu. The subsidy must be claimed within six months from the date of purchase or installation of the generator.
benefits: Quantum of Assistance: 25% subsidy or maximum ₹1,50,000/- on the cost of generator sets (up to 125 KVA capacity).
eligibility: Beneficiaries must be new and existing Micro, Small and Medium Manufacturing Enterprises.. The generator set must have a capacity of up to 125 KVA.. Subsidy claims must be made within six months from the date of purchase or installation..
documents: Proof of purchase or installation of the generator set. Invoice and receipt of the generator. Proof of enterprise registration (MSME registration certificate). Bank account details for subsidy transfer. Installation certificate from a certified technician. Any other documents (if required).
Proof of purchase or installation of the generator set.
Invoice and receipt of the generator.

faqs.question: What is the "Generator Subsidy" scheme?
faqs.answer: The Generator Subsidy scheme provides a 25% subsidy or maximum [?]1,50,000/- on the cost of generator sets up to 125 KVA capacity for Micro, Small, and Medium Manufacturing Enterprises (MSMEs) in Tamil Nadu.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the Generator Subsidy?
faqs.answer: New and existing Micro, Small, and Medium Manufacturing Enterprises (MSMEs) registered in Tamil Nadu are eligible.

faqs.question: What is the maximum capacity of the generator covered under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides a subsidy for generator sets with a capacity of up to 125 KVA.

faqs.question: How much subsidy is provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: A 25% subsidy is provided on the cost of the generator set.

faqs.question: How long is the subsidy claim period?
faqs.answer: The subsidy claim must be made within 6 months from the date of purchase or installation of the generator set.

faqs.question: What documents are required to apply for the subsidy?
faqs.answer: Applicants must provide proof of purchase, an installation certificate, an MSME registration certificate, and bank account details for the transfer of the subsidy.

faqs.question: Is the subsidy available for both new and existing MSMEs?
faqs.answer: Yes, both new and existing MSME manufacturing enterprises in Tamil Nadu are eligible.

faqs.question: Is there a deadline to apply for the subsidy after purchasing or installing the generator?
faqs.answer: Yes, the subsidy must be claimed within 6 months of purchasing or installing the generator set.

faqs.question: Can the subsidy be availed for multiple generators?
faqs.answer: The subsidy is available for generator sets up to 125 KVA, but manufacturers should verify if multiple generators are covered based on their enterprise's requirements.

faqs.question: What happens if an MSME misses the six-month deadline for applying?
faqs.answer: If the deadline is missed, the MSME will no longer be eligible for the subsidy.

faqs.question: Where can manufacturers submit their applications for the Generator Subsidy?
faqs.answer: Applications along with the required documents must be submitted to the relevant state authority in Tamil Nadu Regional Joint Director of Industries and Commerce Industrial Estate, Chennai-600 032.

name: Gausevak Training (Initial and Refresher)
description: The scheme "Gausevak Training (Initial and Refresher)" by the Animal Husbandry Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh, aims to empower educated unemployed rural youth with self-employment opportunities and the skills to provide primary veterinary services in remote rural areas. Under this scheme, the department provides a 100% stipend of ₹6,000 for initial training and ₹500 for refresher training. Additionally, a kit worth ₹1,200 for initial training and study material worth ₹100 for refresher training are also fully funded by the department.
benefits: Initial Training: Training cost: ₹6,000. Stipend: ₹1,200 for six months at ₹1,000 per month. Total: ₹7,200 per Gausevak. Refresher Training: Stipend: ₹500. Study material: ₹100. Total: ₹600 per Gausevak.
eligibility: The applicant should be in the age group of 18 to 35 years.. The applicant should be unemployed.. The applicant should be from a rural area.. The applicant should have passed the 10th standard.. The applicant should be a cow-helper..
documents: size Photograph Aadhaar card Domicile certificate of Madhya Pradesh Caste certificate Previous class passing certificate/marksheet Samagra ID Bank account details/Bank Passbook Other necessary documents if required

faqs.question: What is the objective of the Gausevak Training scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme aims to train educated unemployed rural youth for self-employment and equip them to provide primary veterinary services in remote rural areas.

faqs.question: Who implements this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme is implemented by the Animal Husbandry Department, Madhya Pradesh.

faqs.question: What are the eligibility criteria for initial training?
faqs.answer: Applicants must be educated, unemployed rural youth who have passed 10th standard, are between 18 to 35 years of age, and are residents of Madhya Pradesh.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for refresher training?
faqs.answer: Gausevaks who have previously completed initial training are eligible for refresher training based on seniority.

faqs.question: What is the duration of the initial training?
faqs.answer: The initial training is conducted over six months.

faqs.question: What stipend is provided during the training?

name: Him Kukkut Palan Yojna
description: The scheme “Him Kukkut Palan Yojna” was launched by the Department of Animal Husbandry, Government of Himachal Pradesh to provide the subsidy to the entrepreneurs/farmers who are interested and engaged in poultry farming in the state. Since more and more poultry farmers have shown an inclination towards adopting poultry as per occupation consequent to their success in backyard schemes, they want the department to focus on commercial broiler farming in the state as well. For the benefit of such entrepreneurs/farmers and seeing the benefits of poultry rearing as an enterprise, such farmers need to be incentivized by way of assistance through Government by Broiler scheme on a subsidy basis in the state. The following aims and objectives will also be achieved:- To provide a good diet to the people of the state. It will be possible to make poultry available at reasonable rates if it is produced locally. Large rural populations face the problem of protein-calorie malnutrition, thus needing animal proteins with high biological values which can be met through poultry meat. To augment the income of the rural people where poultry farming along with livestock rearing is being carried on as a mixed farming complementary to crop production. Doubling of income of farmers. To increase the employment opportunities for the rural population since most of them are unemployed or grossly underemployed. To produce manure of high grade at a minimal cost.
benefits: The government shall be providing funds against Capital Investment in this scheme under a subsidy component as per approved norms on a first come first serve basis as per the availability of budget. For the subsidy on total capital investment, 60% will be the subsidy assistance while a maximum of 40% will be the component to be provided by the beneficiary/banks to the beneficiaries belonging to SC, ST & General Category. Since the beneficiary may not be able to raise 3000 chicks at one go due to constraints, so provision is being kept to provide chicks in installments of 1000 chicks as per requirement. To produce manure of high grade at a minimal cost.
eligibility: The beneficiary should be a permanent resident of Himachal Pradesh.. The beneficiary/farmer belonging to SC/ST/General categories who have undertaken training in poultry farming from Government Poultry farms.. Approximately 100 farmers per year will be assisted under the scheme.. The poultry breeders who have been assisted earlier (more than two years) under different commercial broiler scheme run by the department may also apply for benefits under the scheme with condition that he/she is running the scheme successfully and the established unit is still viable.. The beneficiary has not availed of any such benefit earlier under Commercial Broiler Schemes. He/she will not discontinue the scheme during course of the project and if he/she discontinues the scheme or flout any of the terms and condition of scheme, shall have to refund the entire amount of scheme along with interest @ 12%. The said amount shall be recovered from the balance capital subsidy from them.. The beneficiary has to provide the certified/authenticated copy of documents establishing ownership/ possession of land on which the shed is constructed/to be constructed.. In order to avail subsidy for construction of shed &. store, the beneficiary has to submit the completion certificate duly verified by the officer of the rank of the Junior Engineer or above concerned Block/HPPWD sub-division.
documents: Identity proof i.e. Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Voter ID Card, etc. Copy of the Bank Passbook Shed Construction Estimate (in case of No Shed Constructed) Proof of Shed Construction (in case of Shed Constructed) Unemployment Certificate, BPL Certificate Training Certificate Cast Certificate (if SC, ST) Note: Files size should be less than or equal to 200 KB and must be in pdf or jpg.
Identity proof i.e. Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Voter ID Card, etc.
Shed Construction Estimate (in case of No Shed Constructed)
Proof of Shed Construction (in case of Shed Constructed)
Note: Files size should be less than or equal to 200 KB and must be in pdf or jpg.

faqs.question: What is the objective of the scheme?
faqs.answer: The objective of this scheme is to (1) To provide a good diet to the people of the state (2) To augment the income of the rural people where poultry farming along with livestock rearing is being carried on as a mixed farming complementary to crop production. (3) Doubling of income of farmers. (4) To increase the employment opportunities for the rural population since most of them are unemployed or grossly underemployed.

faqs.question: By which department was this scheme launched?
faqs.answer: Department of Animal Husbandry, Government of Himachal Pradesh

faqs.question: Who is eligible under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The target groups under this scheme will be farmers belonging to SC/ST/General categories who have undertaken training in poultry farming from Government Poultry farms. Also, the poultry breeders who have been assisted earlier (more than two years) under different commercial broiler schemes run by the department may also apply for benefits under the scheme with the condition that he/she is running the scheme successfully and the established unit is still viable.

faqs.question: How many farmers will be assisted under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Approximately 100 farmers per year will be assisted under the scheme.

faqs.question: Will the farmer need to submit any undertaking along with the application?
faqs.answer: Yes, the farmer/applicant has to submit the undertaking along with the application that he/she will abide by the term and conditions of the scheme and also has not availed any such benefit earlier under Commercial Broiler Schemes.

faqs.question: Shall any penalty impose on the beneficiary if he/she discontinues the scheme or flout any of the terms and conditions of the scheme?
faqs.answer: If the beneficiary discontinues the scheme or flouts any of the terms and conditions of the scheme shall have to refund the entire amount of the scheme along with interest @ 12%. The said amount shall be recovered from the balance capital subsidy from them.

faqs.question: Is it mandatory for a beneficiary to provide the certified/authenticated copy of documents establishing ownership/possession of the land?
faqs.answer: Yes, the beneficiary has to provide the certified/authenticated copy of documents establishing ownership/ possession of the land on which the shed is constructed/to be constructed.

faqs.question: What is the benefit of the scheme?
faqs.answer: Under the scheme, the government shall be providing funds against Capital Investment in this scheme under a subsidy component as per approved norms on a first come first serve basis as per the availability of budget.

faqs.question: How much percentage of subsidies will be given to the beneficiary as assistance?
faqs.answer: 60% of the total capital investment will be the subsidy assistance to be provided to the beneficiaries.

faqs.question: How much percentage of subsidies will be given to the beneficiary for the components?
faqs.answer: The maximum 40% of total capital investment will be the subsidy on the component to be provided by the beneficiary/banks to the beneficiaries belonging to SC, ST & General Category.

faqs.question: Can a beneficiary raise the chicks in installments?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the beneficiary may not be able to raise 3000 chicks at one go due to constraints, so provision is being kept to provide chicks in installments of 1000 chicks as per requirement.

faqs.question: How can I apply under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The beneficiary may apply online mode. (https://hpahdbt.hp.gov.in/Home/Him Kukkut Palan Yojna)

name: Horticulture Mission for North Eastern Hill Scheme- Meghalaya

name: Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom: \Small Cardamom Replanting/New Planting: Karnataka (Ha.) and other States
description: Under the “Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom” implemented by the Spices Board India during the 15th Finance Commission period (2021–22 to 2025–26), assistance is provided for Small Cardamom Replanting/New Planting in Karnataka and other states to motivate growers to improve production and productivity through systematic replanting of diseased, old, and senile plantations, as well as to promote area expansion, in accordance with the modalities and scheme guidelines approved by the Competent Authority.
benefits: 33.33% of cost of cultivation of subject to a maximum of ₹75,000/- per Ha for General Category and 75% of cost of cultivation ₹1,68,000/- per Ha for SC/ST payable in two annual installments of ₹37,500/- and 84,000/- each year respectively. Individual registered cardamom growers having a land holding size of 0.10 Ha to 8 Ha. Minimum area to be replanted under the programme is 0.10 Ha in a continuous block and the maximum area is limited to 2 Ha per beneficiary per year and a maximum of 8 Ha. in block year of 5 years from 2021-2026.The plant population is minimum 3000 Nos. per ha for closer planting [pure crop] and 1500 Nos in intercropped plantations. Replanting cycle is considered as 8 years and a second time benefit for the same area replanted by a beneficiary will be available only on completion of 8 years except on exclusive circumstances like natural calamities, devastating pest and disease attacks as jointly certified by a committee constituted by Board.
eligibility: The applicants from Karnataka and other states having potential areas suitable for Small Cardamom cultivation are eligible to apply under the scheme.. The applicants undertaking replanting/new planting as a pure crop using suckers will be given preference, subject to final inspection and recommendation by the designated officials..
documents: a) Document of ownership or legal possession of land b) Current year land tax receipt /RTC c) CRC endorsement d) Aadhar card e) Copy of Bank Pass book f) Survey plan issued by V.O/registered surveyor g)For other States, land documents prescribed by the State Govt.

b) Current year land tax receipt /RTC
e) Copy of Bank Pass book
f) Survey plan issued by V.O/registered surveyor

faqs.question: What is the main objective of the Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom, particularly for small cardamom replanting and new planting activities?
faqs.answer: The objective of the scheme is to motivate growers in Karnataka and other cardamom-growing states to improve production and productivity through systematic replanting of diseased, old, and senile plantations, as well as to encourage area expansion under scientifically managed cultivation practices.

faqs.question: Who are the eligible beneficiaries under this scheme for undertaking small cardamom replanting or new planting activities?
faqs.answer: Individual registered cardamom growers having land holdings ranging from 0.10 hectares to 8 hectares are eligible under the scheme, provided they meet all prescribed guidelines and documentation requirements.

faqs.question: What is the minimum and maximum land area allowed for availing assistance under the replanting and new planting programme for small cardamom cultivation?
faqs.answer: The minimum eligible area for replanting is 0.10 hectares in a continuous block, while the maximum limit is 2 hectares per beneficiary per year, with an overall ceiling of 8 hectares during the 5-year block period from 2021–2026.

faqs.question: What types of land and plantation conditions are considered eligible for assistance under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme supports replanting of diseased, old, and senile plantations, as well as new planting activities in suitable areas, with preference given to pure crop cultivation using healthy suckers under recommended agronomic practices.

faqs.question: What is the financial assistance or subsidy pattern provided under this scheme for general category and SC/ST beneficiaries?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides 33.33% of the cost of cultivation subject to a maximum of Rs. 75,000 per hectare for General Category beneficiaries, and 75% of the cost of cultivation subject to a maximum of Rs. 1,68,000 per hectare for SC/ST beneficiaries.

faqs.question: In what manner is the subsidy amount disbursed to the beneficiaries under the scheme guidelines?
faqs.answer: The eligible subsidy is released in two annual installments based on compliance with scheme conditions, field verification, and recommendations of designated officials after inspection.

faqs.question: What is the required plant population density for small cardamom cultivation under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme mandates a minimum plant population of 3,000 plants per hectare for pure crop (closer planting) and 1,500 plants per hectare for intercropped plantations to ensure optimum productivity.

faqs.question: What type of planting method is encouraged or given preference under this replanting and new planting programme?
faqs.answer: Preference is given to replanting or new planting as a pure crop using healthy suckers, as this method ensures better plant establishment, higher productivity, and improved crop quality.

faqs.question: How is the selection of eligible beneficiaries finalized under the scheme implementation process?
faqs.answer: Final selection is carried out after field inspection by designated officials who verify compliance with scheme norms and recommend eligible cases for assistance.

faqs.question: Are farmers from all states eligible to participate in the scheme, or is it limited to specific regions only?
faqs.answer: Farmers from Karnataka and other states having suitable agro-climatic conditions for small cardamom cultivation are eligible, subject to fulfillment of state-specific documentation requirements.

name: Indian Agricultural Research Institute - Scholarship
subcategory: Education and training grants, fellowship, stipend
department: Department of Agriculture Research and Education
description: The Awards shall be made by the Dean and Joint Director (Education) of the Institute on the advice of the “Standing Committee on Scholarships Financial Assistance and Academic Progress”, which shall take into consideration the merit of each applicant based initially on his admission and subsequently on his performance at the Post Graduate School. Duration The normal duration of junior scholarships for M.Sc. course will be two years and that of senior scholarships for Ph.D. course will be three years. However, on the recommendation of the Chairperson of the student and Professor of the Division based on appraisal of the progress and details of justification for the extension needed, the period of junior/senior scholarships is extendable in exceptional cases for period not exceeding three months/six months, respectively. In the case of SC/ST/PC students, the scholarships are extendable upto a period of six months/one year, respectively. The students who have undergone introductory courses on agriculture in the first year of their study at IARI shall be provided Institute scholarship for a period of one year in addition to the provisions mentioned above. The scholarships shall be awarded initially for a period of one academic year from the date of joining the Post Graduate School or the commencement of the academic year, whichever is later, and can be renewed for another year in the case of M.Sc. and two years in the case of Ph.D. students, subject to the earning of Overall Grade Point Average for continuing in the Post Graduate School. Requests for extension beyond these limits will be examined by the Dean on their merits. The total period for which scholarships shall be awarded including extension period shall not exceed three years and three months in the case of M.Sc. students, and four years and six months in the case of Ph.D. students. The payment of scholarship/fellowship should be reviewed at the end of 3rd trimester and only those students will e permitted to continue getting fellowship who maintain the OGPA of 6.50 out of 10.00 at the end of 3rd trimester. All M.Sc./ Ph.D. students will be required to maintain the minimum OGPA of 6.00 out of 10.00 at the end of 3rd trimester to continue on the Post Graduate School rolls. The scholarship shall be paid only for the period of residence of the recipient at Post Graduate School (inclusive of the summer vacation, the trimester breaks and such other leave as may be sanctioned under the rules) upto the date of final viva-voce (i.e. till they are on the rolls), subject to the condition that the maximum period of scholarship prescribed shall in no case be extended and provided he/she continues to reside in the Post Graduate Hostel and marks his/her attendance in the concerned division.
benefits: Benefits The value of the M.Sc. and Ph.D. scholarship will be ₹ 7,560/- and ₹ 10,500/- per month, respectively. The scholarship shall be drawn in the extension period also where such extension beyond two/three years, respectively, has been granted. The scholarship will be inclusive of all fees and other charges of the teaching institution. In addition to the monthly amount of junior/senior scholarship a contingent grant of ₹ 6,000/- per academic year for M.Sc. students, and ₹ 10,000/- per academic year for Ph.D. students will be paid towards the cost of experimental material, books, the thesis and the study tours required for the study as recommended by the Chairperson/Professor concerned. Scholarship to the In-service Candidates/ Departmental Students As per ICAR norms, the In-service candidates joining M.Sc./Ph.D. course on study leave/ deputation who are in receipt of study allowance/ halting allowance/deputation allowance, etc. in addition to full leave salary, the scholarship amount will be adjusted so that they will get a maximum benefit of ₹ 3,000/- p.m. only in addition to full leave salary. This is in addition to the payment of the contingent grant. Those in-service candidates who are not in receipt of JRF/SRF and receiving a partial salary (half or leave without pay) will also be eligible to get an Institute Scholarship of ₹ 3,000/- p.m. provided they are employed by ICAR/SAU system, either nominated by ICAR or selected for admission by any university and who opt to join at a place other than the one where working and provided further that the third degree is not from the same institute.
eligibility: For the M.Sc./M.Tech. (Agricultural Engineering only) Courses:. Only those candidates who had their Bachelor’s Degree Programmes under 10+2+4 OR 10+2+3 OR 10+1+4 system (OR awarded B.Sc. degree under 10+2+2 system prior to 1985) and fulfill the qualifications as prescribed in the Information Bulletin are eligible to apply for admission.. For the Ph.D. Courses:. Candidates must have obtained at least 60% marks OR an Overall Grade Point Average (OGPA) of 7.50 out of 10.00 OR 3.75 out of 5.00 OR 3.00 out of 4.00 OR 2.25 out of 3.00 (For SC/ST/PC candidates: 55% marks OR OGPA of 7.00 out of 10.00 OR 3.50 out of 5.00 OR 2.80 out of 4.00 OR 2.10 out of 3.00) in M.Sc. / M.Tech. degree program. In no case, the conversion of OGPA into percentage will be considered for the calculation of marks where the OGPA is awarded.. The scholarships will be admissible to students of Indian Nationality as defined in the constitution of India or persons domiciled in India, irrespective of sex, race, or religion.. A fellow will devote his/her whole time to the approved study and will not be allowed to accept or hold another appointment paid or otherwise.. Age Limit. The minimum age limit for admission to Ph.D. shall be 21 years. The age shall be reckoned as of 31st July of the year of admission and no further relaxation will be given to the candidates.

faqs.answer: The Code of Conduct requires interns to demonstrate sincerity, punctuality, courtesy, cooperative attitude, willingness to learn, proper etiquette, appropriate attire, and maintain workplace decorum throughout their internship.

faqs.question: What Are The Expected Responsibilities Of Interns During Their Internship At NPC/IPL/ICRO?
faqs.answer: Interns are expected to perform their assigned tasks/duties with due care and diligence, following the instructions given to them during the internship.

faqs.question: Is There Any Requirement For Interns To Submit A Report At The End Of Their Internship?
faqs.answer: Yes, interns are required to submit a project/assignment report/paper to the concerned Head(s) regarding their learning experience.

faqs.question: What Is The Non-Disclosure Policy For Interns During And After Their Internship?
faqs.answer: Interns are not allowed to disclose any proprietary or confidential information related to NPC/IPL/ICRO or its clients without prior written consent. Violation of this policy may result in necessary action by NPC/IPL/ICRO.

faqs.question: Can NPC/IPL/ICRO Terminate An Intern's Engagement Or Program During The Internship?
faqs.answer: Yes, NPC/IPL/ICRO may terminate an intern's engagement or program at any time for reasons of discipline or misconduct without assigning any specific reason.

faqs.question: Can Interns Leave The Internship Program If They Choose To Do So?
faqs.answer: Yes, interns can leave the program by giving a prior notice of seven (07) working days to the concerned Head. However, they will not be awarded a certificate in such cases.

faqs.question: Does The Internship Guarantee Employment With NPC/IPL/ICRO?
faqs.answer: No, the internship program does not assure any employment with NPC/IPL/ICRO.

faqs.question: How Are Interns Selected For The Internship Program At NPC/IPL/ICRO?
faqs.answer: The internship offer is based on the information provided by interns in their application and resume. NPC/IPL/ICRO may terminate the offer if any material error is discovered.

faqs.question: Can Interns Claim Any Rights On The Work Performed During Their Internship?
faqs.answer: No, the copyright of the work performed during the internship remains with NPC/IPL/ICRO. Interns cannot claim any rights on the work.

faqs.question: What Is The Objective Of The Collaboration Between IPL And NPC?
faqs.answer: The collaboration aims to foster rural outreach and capacity development of farmers and youth by providing solutions for improving productivity and competitiveness through various services like consultancy, training, action research, and evaluation studies.

faqs.question: How Has IPL Contributed To Agrarian Growth And Farmers' Prosperity In India?
faqs.answer: IPL's dedicated field work has led to the acceptance of potash among Indian farmers, which was previously unknown. Their vast network and services have enabled them to provide agricultural inputs and services directly to farmers across the country.

faqs.question: How Many Regional Offices Coordinate IPL's Services Across India?
faqs.answer: IPL's services are coordinated by 15 Regional Offices located in various State capitals.

faqs.question: What Kind Of Services Does NPC Provide To Organizations To Improve Their Productivity And Competitiveness?
faqs.answer: NPC provides a range of services, including consultancy, training, action research, and evaluation studies customized to suit the needs of organizations to improve their productivity and competitiveness.

faqs.question: What Is The Significance Of Adhering To The Code Of Conduct During The Internship?
faqs.answer: Adhering to the Code of Conduct demonstrates professionalism and commitment, which can contribute to a positive and productive internship experience.

faqs.question: How Does NPC Ensure The Confidentiality Of Its Proprietary Information?
faqs.answer: NPC requires interns to sign a non-disclosure agreement, and any violation of this agreement may result in necessary action to protect the interests of the organization.

name: Infrastructure Development Scheme for Dairy Co-operatives
description: The scheme "Infrastructure Development Scheme for Dairy Co-operatives" was approved by the Government of Goa, Department of Co-operation, Office of the Registrar of Co-operative Societies. The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to Dairy Co-operative Societies for their development, smooth functioning of business, and other allied activities, enabling them to become stable and create better infrastructure. The scheme provides financial support in the form of grant or subsidy to cover administrative and managerial expenses, including staff salaries, allowances, wages, office expenses, rent, rates, taxes, and the purchase of equipment. The applications for this scheme are accepted by submitting the proposal to the concerned Office of the Assistant Registrar.
benefits: The financial support is provided to meet administrative/managerial expenses on staff salaries and allowances, wages, office expenses, rent rates and taxes, and equipment. The Registering Authority shall verify the utilization of the grants released. General Category Dairy Co-operative Societies Above 500 liters per day: ₹1,50,000/-. 300–500 liters per day: ₹1,00,000/-. 150–300 liters per day: ₹75,000/-. 50–150 liters per day: ₹30,000/-. Tribal Sub Plan/Schedule Caste Sub Plan Dairy Co-operative Societies Above 1,250 liters per day: ₹3,75,000/-. 1,000–less than 1,250 liters per day: ₹3,00,000/-. 750–less than 1,000 liters per day: ₹2,25,000/-. 500–less than 750 liters per day: ₹1,75,000/-. 300–less than 500 liters per day: ₹1,25,000/-. 75–less than 300 liters per day: ₹1,00,000/-. 25–less than 75 liters per day: ₹50,000/-.

faqs.question: If I represent a co-operative that is not primarily involved in dairy activities, or is located outside the State, are we eligible to seek financial support?
faqs.answer: No, the scheme is specifically approved by the Government of Goa to provide financial assistance only to the Dairy Co-operative Societies located within the State.

faqs.question: What is the mandatory requirement regarding the consistency of my society’s business operations to qualify for this particular type of financial grant?
faqs.answer: The co-operative society must ensure it is regularly supplying milk to the Milk Union to be eligible for this financial support.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum operational period or registration duration that the co-operative society must fulfill before applying for benefits under this program?
faqs.answer: Yes, the scheme applies only to co-operative societies after they have completed a minimum of one year following their official registration.

faqs.question: If our Daily Collection of Milk falls within the range of 50 liters up to 150 liters, what is the exact amount of grant entitlement per year?
faqs.answer: Societies in the General Category collecting 50 liters to 150 liters per day are entitled to a grant of ₹30,000/- per year.

faqs.question: Our co-operative society manages to collect between 150 liters and 300 liters of milk every day; how much financial assistance will we receive annually?
faqs.answer: For General Category societies collecting 150 liters to 300 liters per day, the entitled yearly financial grant is ₹75,000/-.

faqs.question: Could you specify the yearly grant amount available to societies under the General Category whose daily milk collection is between 300 liters and 500 liters?
faqs.answer: If your daily milk collection is between 300 liters and 500 liters, your co-operative society will receive a yearly grant of ₹1,00,000/-.

faqs.question: What is the highest level of financial support in the form of a grant offered for General Category societies that collect daily milk volumes above 500 liters?
faqs.answer: Dairy Co-operative Societies under the General Category collecting above 500 liters per day are entitled to the maximum grant of ₹1,50,000/- per year.

faqs.question: For what specific types of expenses or activities can the co-operative society utilize the grant/subsidy provided through this particular development scheme?
faqs.answer: The grant/subsidy is intended to meet administrative and managerial expenses such as staff salaries, allowances, wages, office expenses, rent, rates, taxes, and equipment costs.

faqs.question: Which report must be mandatorily submitted along with the official proposal when applying to avail of the financial assistance for a specific period?
faqs.answer: The society must submit the Milk Supply Report from the Milk Union that covers the specific period for which the financial assistance is being requested.

faqs.question: Before submitting the final proposal to the concerned office, is there any internal approval required from the society’s members or management?
faqs.answer: Yes, the society must ensure the proposal for Government assistance is formally approved in the General Body or Special General Body meeting.

faqs.question: How does the scheme define a Tribal Sub Plan or Scheduled Caste Sub Plan Co-operative Society to determine if we qualify for assistance under that category?
faqs.answer: To qualify for Tribal Sub Plan/Scheduled Caste Sub Plan assistance, the society must have a minimum of 15% of its shareholders belonging to the Scheduled Tribe or Scheduled Caste category.

faqs.question: If we are applying under the reserved categories for additional financial support, what documentation is needed to verify the shareholder percentage?
faqs.answer: The society is required to submit a comprehensive list of its Scheduled Tribe/Scheduled Caste members to confirm the required percentage of shareholders.

faqs.question: Who is the designated authority responsible for monitoring and ensuring that the financial grants released under this scheme have been utilized correctly?
faqs.answer: The Registering Authority is responsible for conducting the verification of the utilization of all grants that have been successfully released to the society.

faqs.question: For a society registered under the Tribal Sub Plan/Scheduled Caste Sub Plan category, what is the annual subsidy if the daily milk collection is 25 liters to less than 75 liters?
faqs.answer: If collecting 25 liters to less than 75 liters per day, the society is entitled to a yearly subsidy amount of ₹50,000/-.

faqs.question: How is the eligible subsidy amount disbursed to beneficiaries in the Integrated Farming scheme?

name: Integrated Horticulture Development Plan Scheme for Scheduled Caste Families

name: Integrated Horticulture Development Program for Tribal Area Farmers (TASP) HRT-3
department: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department
description: The scheme "Integrated Horticulture Development Program for Tribal Area Farmers (TASP) HRT-3" by the Agriculture and Co-operation Department, Government of Gujarat, aims to strengthen horticulture-based livelihoods and promote modern horticultural practices among tribal farmers through financial assistance for farm mechanization, processing units, crop protection, post-harvest management, and export-related infrastructure. Financial support for organizing and participating in exhibitions, competitions, and seminars. Subsidy for organizing or participating in Krishi Melas and payment for stall rentals. > Farm Mechanization Support: Subsidy for purchase of power tillers and mini tractors to enhance horticultural productivity. Subsidy for setting up new processing units for cashew and other fruit crops. faqs.answer: The selection procedure for internship at the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau involves scrutiny of applications by a Selection Committee, with due importance given to the academic performance of the applicant. The meeting of the Selection Committee is held two times in a year, and its decision is final and binding.

faqs.question: How does the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau assist the customs authorities in inspecting consignments of flora & fauna?
faqs.answer: The Wildlife Crime Control Bureau assists and advises the Customs authorities in the inspection of consignments of flora & fauna as per the provisions of the Wildlife Protection Act, CITES, and EXIM Policy governing such an item.

faqs.question: What role does the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau play in advising the Government of India on issues relating to wildlife crimes?
faqs.answer: The Wildlife Crime Control Bureau advises the Government of India on issues relating to wildlife crimes having national and international ramifications, relevant policy, and laws.

The scheme is extended to all the regions of the Union territory of Puducherry. The scheme is introduced with the objective of extending financial assistance to the fishermen's families to compensate for the loss due to the missing breadwinner and to support them financially to run their family.

faqs.answer: The standing committee recommends the release of the relief amount, and the Director of Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare acts on this recommendation.

faqs.question: What happens if the missing person is not found, and the prescribed period lapses?
faqs.answer: The balance amount is released in favor of the next of kin (legal heir) after the prescribed 9-month period, assuming no further information is received.

faqs.question: How is the eligibility of the missing fisherman determined?
faqs.answer: The missing fisherman should have lost his/her life while fishing, be in the age group of 18-60, and not be a beneficiary of the old age pension scheme.

faqs.answer: No, the application form must be submitted with all mandatory documents, self-attested if required, to the concerned authority.

faqs.question: Is there any specific procedure for the release of the balance 50% of the relief amount?
faqs.answer: The balance 50% is released to the next of kin (legal heir) after the prescribed 9-month period and is deposited in a joint account in their name.

faqs.question: How is the term "family (legal heir)" defined in the context of the scheme?

faqs.answer: The relief is disbursed in two installments of [?] 50,000 each, with the first installment released within 3 months, and the balance deposited in a joint account after the prescribed 9-month period.

name: Integrated Scheme on Agriculture Cooperation
description: The Integrated Scheme on Agriculture Cooperation (ISAC) is a Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India. The scheme is being implemented through the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC). The main objectives of the scheme are Provide financial assistance to cooperatives to improve their economic conditions. Remove regional imbalances and speed up cooperative development in agricultural and allied sectors. Help cotton growers to get better prices for their produce by adding value to it and ensuring that decentralized weavers have access to quality yarn at reasonable rates. Promote overall development of selected districts in the country through cooperative efforts in agriculture and allied sectors. Assist National Level Cooperative Federation/Multi State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) in the agriculture and allied sector to undertake promotional and skill development activities Components of the Scheme Financial assistance will be provided for the following components under the component of Assistance to NCDC Programmes for Development of Cooperatives: Marketing, Processing, Storage, Consumer, Weaker Section Programmes of Cooperatives, Computerization of Primary Agricultural Cooperative Credit Societies (PACS), District Central Cooperative Banks (DCBs), State Cooperative Banks (SCBs) and Technical & Promotional (T&P) Cell Scheme for strengthening Management of State Cooperative Federations [subsidy on tapering basis]. Assistance for cotton development including ginning and pressing and establishment of new and modernization/ expansion/ rehabilitation of existing cooperative spinning mills. Integrated Cooperative Development Projects in selected districts (ICDP):
benefits: Grant-in-aid under the ISAC scheme for projects related to weaker sections/women cooperatives and labour cooperatives: Cooperatively least developed states {Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Jammu & Kashmir, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, and Tripura} : 25% Cooperatively under-developed states {Andhra Pradesh , Chhattisgarh, Goa, Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Rajasthan, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Andaman & Nicobar Islands (UT) and Lakshadweep (UT)}: 20% Cooperatively developed states {Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra, Punjab, Tamilnadu, Chandigarh (UT), Dadra & Nagar Haveli (UT), Daman & Diu (UT), Puducherry (UT), Delhi } : 15%
eligibility: Eligible Sectors for NCDC’s assistance.. Agricultural Marketing, Processing, Storage, Computerization and weaker sections’ Programmes, and input supply, Plantation/ horticultural crops, SC &. ST cooperatives, tribal cooperatives, hill area cooperatives, dairy, poultry, livestock, fisheries, handloom coir, jute, cash crops, sericulture, computerization of cooperatives including PACS, DCCB and State Cooperative Banks, Spinning Mills, modernization/expansion of existing mills, rehabilitation of sick Cooperative Spinning Mills, Margin money assistance to cooperative spinning mills.. Eligible Organizations for seeking assistance. Societies should not be less than three years older, having positive balance net worth for last three years and having rich experience in the field for which project is proposed under the scheme. In the case of government sponsored projects for cooperatives, this condition could be relaxed on case to case basis by Managing Director, NCDC. Cooperatives Sectors/Organizations must :. Be registered under the Cooperative Societies Act of the respective state.. Be undertaking activities related to agriculture and allied sectors, such as marketing, storage, processing of agricultural produce, and supply of agricultural inputs.. Be financially viable and have a good track record.. Be eligible for financial assistance from the NCDC..

faqs.question: What is the ISAC scheme?
faqs.answer: The ISAC scheme is a Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India. The scheme is being implemented through the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC).

faqs.question: What are the objectives of the ISAC scheme?
faqs.answer: The main objectives of the ISAC scheme are to: Provide financial assistance to cooperatives to improve their economic conditions. Remove regional imbalances and speed up cooperative development in agricultural and allied sectors. Help cotton growers to get better prices for their produce by adding value to it and ensuring that decentralized weavers have access to quality yarn at reasonable rates. Promote overall development of selected districts in the country through cooperative efforts in agriculture and allied sectors. Assist National Level Cooperative Federation/Multi State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) in the agriculture and allied sector to undertake promotional and skill development activities.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the ISAC scheme?
faqs.answer: Be registered under the Cooperative Societies Act of the respective state. Be undertaking activities related to agriculture and allied sectors, such as marketing, storage, processing of agricultural produce, and supply of agricultural inputs. Be financially viable and have a good track record. Be eligible for financial assistance from the NCDC.

faqs.question: What types of projects are eligible for financial assistance under the ISAC scheme?
faqs.answer: Construction of godowns, cold storages, and processing units Purchase of machinery and equipment Development of marketing infrastructure Training and capacity building of cooperative members

faqs.question: What is the amount of financial assistance available under the ISAC scheme?
faqs.answer: The amount of financial assistance available under the ISAC scheme varies depending on the type of project and the location of the cooperative. For example, cooperatives located in cooperatively least developed states are eligible for a higher grant-in-aid than cooperatives located in cooperatively developed states.

faqs.question: How can cooperatives apply for financial assistance under the ISAC scheme?
faqs.answer: Cooperatives can apply for financial assistance under the ISAC scheme by submitting a project proposal to the NCDC. The project proposal must include a detailed description of the project, its cost, and its benefits.

faqs.question: What is the selection process for the ISAC scheme?
faqs.answer: The selection process takes into account the following factors: The technical feasibility of the project The financial viability of the project The benefits of the project to the cooperative and its members The impact of the project on the overall development of the region

faqs.question: When are the results of the ISAC scheme selection process announced?
faqs.answer: The results of the ISAC scheme selection process are typically announced within a few weeks of the deadline for submitting project proposals.

faqs.question: What are the benefits of the ISAC scheme for cooperatives?
faqs.answer: The ISAC scheme provides a number of benefits to cooperatives, including: Financial assistance to improve their economic conditions Access to technology and training Support for developing new markets Help to expand their operations and reach

faqs.question: What is the purpose of this scheme?
faqs.answer: The purpose of this scheme is to provide financial relief to sugar cooperative societies by subsidizing the interest on loans taken for clearing sugarcane arrears for the 2018-19 season.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Only sugar cooperative societies that have taken a bank loan to pay sugarcane arrears for the 2018-19 season are eligible to apply.

faqs.question: What kind of financial assistance is provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides interest subvention for a maximum period of 4 years. The Government of India pays the first year's interest, while the state government provides a subsidy of up to 7% or the actual interest paid, whichever is lower, for the remaining period.

faqs.question: Can private sugar mills apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, only sugar cooperative societies are eligible under this scheme. Private sugar mills do not qualify for the benefits.

faqs.question: What is the maximum duration for which interest subvention is provided?
faqs.answer: The interest subvention is provided for a maximum period of four years or until the loan is fully repaid, whichever comes earlier.

faqs.question: Can a sugar cooperative society apply for this scheme if it has already repaid the loan?
faqs.answer: No, the scheme is applicable only for ongoing loans taken for sugarcane arrears of the 2018-19 season. Societies that have already repaid their loans are not eligible for interest subvention.

faqs.question: Can a sugar cooperative society apply for multiple loans under this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, a sugar cooperative society can avail of interest subvention only for a single loan taken for clearing sugarcane arrears of the 2018-19 season.

faqs.question: How is the interest subvention amount calculated?
faqs.answer: The interest subvention amount is calculated based on the actual interest paid on the loan or 7%, whichever is lower, for a maximum period of four years or until the loan is repaid.

faqs.question: What is the process for applying under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Eligible sugar cooperative societies must submit their proposals through the District Registrar of the concerned district. The proposal is then forwarded to the Director of Sugar, Gujarat State, Gandhinagar, for approval.

faqs.question: Where can sugar cooperative societies get more information about this scheme?
faqs.answer: Sugar cooperative societies can contact the District Registrar of their area or the office of the Director of Sugar, Gujarat State, Gandhinagar, for more details about the scheme.

name: Integrated Sheep Development Scheme
description: The Integrated Sheep Development Scheme (ISDS) was launched in the year 2020-21 by the J&K Government to promote income generation through the establishment of sheep & goat units. The scheme is implemented through Sheep Husbandry Department and monitored by the concerned Director. The support shall be available for the following activities - a) Establishment of Sheep/goat units under participatory mode comprising 10 ewes/does b) Establishment of Sheep/goat units on subsidy mode (20-200 ewes/does) c) Establishment of shearing units The beneficiary can be an Individual / Group of Individuals / Self Help Groups / Cooperative Societies / FPOs, etc. Efforts will be made to cover 20% SC/ST and 10% women beneficiaries. The guidelines will be in force till 31st March 2023 or replaced by a new set of guidelines whichever is earlier. This scheme is innovative & self-sustaining as fresh units shall be established in a continuous cyclic manner from the retrieved livestock of previous beneficiaries. The beneficiary must have basic infrastructure & grazing avenues available, to maintain the unit. Around 1200 sheep/goat units are to be established with the creation of employment opportunities for around 2400 people. 200 elite crossbred imported merino sheep to be introduced for genetic upgradation of local sheep for the production of more than 8000 elite lambs which will lead to an increase in carcass yield from prevalent 18 kg to 21 kg besides incrementing fine wool production from the existing 2 Kg to 2.5 Kg per sheep.

faqs.question: Is It Necessary To Send The Livestock To Highland Pastures During Summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is important to send your livestock to Highland Pastures, the sheep is an animal which is Heat Stress Prone, so it is very difficult for such an animal to remain in plains during high temperature.
