name: Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom: New Subcomponents: Basic quality testing of spices
description: The Basic Quality Testing of Spices subcomponent is part of the Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom, implemented by the Spices Board, India, under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India. Based on consultations with various R&D institutes, State Agricultural Universities (SAUs), and entrepreneurs, it was found that devices for instant basic quality testing, such as moisture content meters and curcumin content testers for turmeric, have been developed and are being used by some groups and institutions. To help farmers assess the basic quality of their spice produce before trading, increase their confidence in negotiating prices, and ensure they receive a fair share for their efforts in improving and maintaining product quality, such devices are required at the field level. The scheme is being implemented in accordance with the modalities and guidelines approved by the Competent Authority under the Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom during the 15th Finance Commission period (2021–22 to 2025–26).
benefits: > 50% of the cost subject to a maximum of ₹10.00 Lakh for basic quality testing at AMC/APMC yards and 75% for Spice Producer's Groups subjected to maximum of ₹ 15.00 Lakh. Eligibility will be for spice trading centers legally existing spice producing or spice handling or spice trading groups. Assistance will be extended based on MoU with Spices Board.
eligibility: All spice growing States and regions in India.. All spice growing States and regions in India preferably in the ODOP (One District One Product) and clusters of Spices under AEP of MoC and operational area of collaborative national and international projects of Spices Board. On receipt of application with documents, the Officer concerned will visit the Reg. Office of the AMC/APMC/group and evaluate the status, facility and arrangements available with the group for taking up the activity component successfully.. Eligible application will be recommended to Divisional Officer/Regional Officer as the case may be for further scrutiny and issue of permission letter to sign MoU with the Board. Recommending Officer will arrange signing of MoU and collection of documents proving purchase and physically verify the installation of the equipment/device and recommend Eligible case for sanction of assistance.. The AMC/APMC/group also need to enter into MoU with the supplying firm on annual maintenance of device, training of man power for operating the device and collection of any software charges etc. which is to be ensured by the officers concerned of the Board before recommending the case..

faqs.question: What is the Basic Quality Testing of Spices scheme?
faqs.answer: It is a subcomponent of the Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom that provides financial assistance for setting up basic quality testing facilities for spices.

faqs.question: What is the objective of the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme aims to promote field-level basic quality testing of spices so that farmers can assess the quality of their produce, negotiate better prices, and receive fair value.

faqs.question: Which organization implements the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme is implemented by the Spices Board, under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply?
faqs.answer: Legally existing AMC/APMCs, spice trading centres, spice-producing groups, spice-handling groups, and spice trading groups are eligible to apply.

faqs.question: Which areas are covered under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme is available in all spice-growing States and regions of India, with preference given to ODOP (One District One Product) areas, Spice Clusters under AEP of the Ministry of Commerce, and operational areas of collaborative national and international projects of the Spices Board.

faqs.question: What types of quality testing devices are supported?
faqs.answer: The scheme supports devices for instant basic quality testing, such as moisture meters, curcumin content testing devices for turmeric, and similar spice quality testing equipment.

faqs.question: Is an MoU with the Spices Board mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes. Financial assistance is provided only after signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Spices Board.

faqs.question: How is the application evaluated?
faqs.answer: After receiving the application and supporting documents, the concerned officer visits the applicant's premises to assess the available facilities and verify readiness for implementation.

faqs.question: What happens after the inspection?
faqs.answer: Eligible applications are recommended to the Divisional Officer/Regional Officer for further scrutiny and issuance of a permission letter to sign the MoU.

faqs.question: Is an annual maintenance agreement required?
faqs.answer: Yes. The applicant must sign an Annual Maintenance Contract (AMC) with the equipment supplier covering maintenance, operator training, and applicable software support.

faqs.question: Why are basic quality testing devices important?
faqs.answer: They help assess the quality of spice produce before trading, improving farmers' confidence in price negotiations and ensuring better returns for quality produce.

faqs.question: Can Spice Producer's Groups receive higher assistance?
faqs.answer: Yes. Spice Producer's Groups are eligible for 75% financial assistance, subject to a maximum of ₹15 lakh.

faqs.question: What is the objective of the Internal Control System (ICS) assistance scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme aims to support grower groups and Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) in establishing grower group certification systems for organic spices. It helps farmers with group formation, organic regulations, certification procedures, training, documentation, internal inspection, and aggregation of produce.

faqs.question: Which organization implements this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme is implemented by Spices Board India under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Grower groups, farmer groups, and FPOs involved in organic spice cultivation are eligible to apply under the scheme.

faqs.question: In which areas is the scheme applicable?
faqs.answer: The scheme is applicable in all spice-growing States, regions, and Union Territories (UTs) of India.

faqs.question: How many times can an ICS receive assistance?
faqs.answer: An ICS is eligible for assistance a maximum of three times during the five-year block period from 2021–22 to 2025–26, either consecutively or in a staggered manner, subject to fund availability.

faqs.question: Is the assistance automatic every year?
faqs.answer: No. Assistance is subject to eligibility, submission of required documents, and availability of funds under the scheme component.

faqs.question: Which groups receive preference under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Preference is given first to groups producing organic spices.

faqs.question: Is there any additional preference criteria?
faqs.answer: Yes. Additional preference is given to groups where more than 50% of the farmers in the approved list cultivate organic spices under any cropping system.

faqs.question: Can the Spices Board inspect or verify the applicants?

faqs.question: What is a Scope Certificate?
faqs.answer: A Scope Certificate is a document issued by the Certification Body confirming that the grower group or ICS complies with the prescribed organic certification standards.

faqs.question: What financial assistance is available for General Category beneficiaries?

faqs.question: What assistance is available for Spice Producers' Groups in identified clusters?

faqs.question: How does the use of a seed spice thresher benefit farmers?
faqs.answer: The equipment helps reduce labour costs, improve threshing efficiency, minimize contamination, reduce post-harvest losses, and ensure better-quality produce for the market.

faqs.question: Is inspection of the installed equipment mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes. Designated officials conduct a final inspection of the installed thresher and recommend eligible cases before assistance is sanctioned.

name: Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom: Small Cardamom Irrigation Land Development : Irrigation equipment (Nos.)
description: The scheme for Irrigation Equipment (Nos.) implemented by the Spices Board under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, and as per the modalities and scheme guidelines approved by the Competent Authority for the implementation of the “Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion and Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom” during the 15th Finance Commission period (2021–22 to 2025–26), financial assistance is provided to motivate growers to bring more area under irrigation and land development. The scheme aims to increase productivity and improve the quality of small cardamom through the adoption of different irrigation methods. Assistance is provided for the installation of the following equipment: (a) Gravity Irrigation Equipment, (b) Irrigation Pump Sets (IP Sets), and (c) Sprinkler, Drip, and Micro-sprinkler Sets.
benefits: 50 % of cost of equipments subject to maximum of ₹ 5000 (Gen) and, ₹11250 (SC/ST) for Gravity; ₹15,000 (Gen) and ₹45,000 (SC/ST) for IP set and ₹ 32,000/- (Gen) and ₹ 95,000/- (SC/ST) for Sprinkler/ micro sprinkler sets. Registered cardamom growers having land holding size of 0.10 Ha to 8 Ha are eligible for Gravity and Irrigation pump set (IP Set). Registered cardamom growers having land holding size of 0.4 Ha to 8 Ha are eligible for Sprinklers / Drip / Microirrigation equipments. Note: Any farmer who has availed this benefit earlier is not eligible to avail the benefit.
eligibility: The applicant should be a small cardamom grower from the states of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, or Karnataka.. The applicant should install the approved irrigation equipment, and the installation must be inspected and recommended as eligible by the designated officials..

faqs.question: Can quotations from local dealers be submitted?

name: Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom : Small Cardamom Irrigation Land Development : Irrigation / Water Storage Structure (nos)
description: The Small Cardamom Irrigation Land Development: Irrigation / Water Storage Structure Scheme under the Spices Board India, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, is intended to motivate growers to bring more area under irrigation and land development by constructing water storage structures, thereby increasing productivity and improving the quality of small cardamom, as per the modalities and scheme guidelines approved by the competent authority for the implementation of the “Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom” during the 15th Finance Commission period (2021–22 to 2025–26).
benefits: 50 % of cost of construction subject to a maximum of Rs 30,000 per unit for General Category and 75% subject to maximum of ₹ 45,000/- per unit for SC/ST. The minimum capacity of irrigation structure should be 25 cubic metre for availing maximum subsidy under the programme. Any farmer who has availed this benefit earlier is not eligible to avail the benefit. Registered cardamom growers having land holding size of 0.10 Ha to 8 Ha are eligible to avail this scheme.
eligibility: The applicant should be a small cardamom grower from Kerala, Tamil Nadu, or Karnataka.. The applicant should undertake irrigation and land development activities by constructing irrigation or water storage structures.. The applicant should ensure that the proposed structure does not obstruct the natural flow of water or create objections from local communities or concerned authorities, subject to final inspection by designated officials..

a) Document of ownership or legal possession of land viz. patta

faqs.question: What is the objective of the Irrigation / Water Storage Structure Scheme?
faqs.answer: The objective of the scheme is to encourage small cardamom growers to bring more area under irrigation and land development by constructing water storage structures. The scheme aims to improve the productivity and quality of small cardamom cultivation.

faqs.question: Who can apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Registered small cardamom growers having land holdings between 0.10 hectare and 8 hectares are eligible to apply for this scheme. The scheme is applicable only to growers located in Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka.

faqs.question: What is the minimum capacity required for the irrigation structure?
faqs.answer: To avail the maximum subsidy under the programme, the irrigation or water storage structure should have a minimum capacity of 25 cubic metres.

faqs.question: Can a farmer who already received assistance earlier apply again?
faqs.answer: No, farmers who have already availed benefits under this scheme earlier are not eligible to receive assistance again under the same programme.

faqs.question: Is a technical estimate required for the proposed structure?
faqs.answer: Yes, the applicant must submit a plan and cost estimate for the proposed irrigation or water storage structure prepared by a qualified registered/licensed or Government civil engineer using Government-approved construction rates.

faqs.question: In which states is the scheme implemented?
faqs.answer: The scheme is implemented in the major small cardamom growing states of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka.

faqs.question: How are applications verified under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Designated officials conduct a final inspection of the proposed or completed structure and verify whether the applicant satisfies all eligibility conditions before recommending the case for sanction.

faqs.question: What kind of constructions are not eligible for assistance?
faqs.answer: Structures that block the natural flow of water, including streams, or constructions that are objectionable to local communities or concerned authorities will not be considered for financial assistance under the scheme.

faqs.question: Why is irrigation support important for small cardamom cultivation?
faqs.answer: Proper irrigation and water storage facilities help maintain adequate soil moisture, especially during dry periods, which improves crop growth, increases productivity, and enhances the quality of small cardamom.

faqs.answer: Registered small cardamom growers having land holdings from 0.10 hectare to 8 hectares are eligible to apply.

faqs.question: What type of assistance is provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Financial assistance is provided for constructing rain water harvesting structures for irrigation and land development purposes.

faqs.answer: The assistance is provided for a rain water harvesting structure having a capacity of 200 cubic metres lined with silpauline sheet.

name: Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom: \Small Cardamom Replanting/New Planting: For Kerala & Tamilnadu
description: The scheme “Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom – Small Cardamom Replanting/New Planting for Kerala & Tamil Nadu” is implemented by the Spices Board under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India. The scheme aims to motivate growers to improve production and productivity through the systematic replanting of diseased, old, and senile plantations, along with area expansion initiatives, as per the modalities and guidelines approved by the Competent Authority for the 15th Finance Commission period (2021–22 to 2025–26).
benefits: 33.33% of cost of cultivation of subject to a maximum of ₹1,00,000/- per Ha for General Category and 75% of cost of cultivation ₹2,10,000/- per Ha for SC/ST payable in two annual installments of ₹50,000/- and ₹1,05,000/- each year respectively. Individual registered cardamom growers having a land holding size of 0.10 Ha to 8 Ha. Minimum area to be replanted under the programme is 0.10 Ha in a continuous block and the maximum area is limited to 2 Ha per beneficiary per year and a maximum of 8 Ha. in block year of 5 years from 2021-2026. The plant population is minimum 1100 Nos. per ha. Replanting cycle is considered as 8 years and a second time benefit for the same area replanted by a beneficiary will be available only on completion of 8 years except on exclusive circumstances like natural calamities, devastating pest and disease attacks certified by a committee constituted by the Board.
eligibility: The applicant should belong to Kerala or Tamil Nadu and undertake Small Cardamom replanting/new planting activities under the scheme.. The plantation/site will be subject to final inspection by the Designated Officials, and only eligible cases recommended by them will be considered for assistance..

faqs.question: What is the objective of this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme aims to improve the production and productivity of Small Cardamom through systematic replanting of diseased, old, and senile plantations and by promoting area expansion.

faqs.question: Which states are covered under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme is applicable only in Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

faqs.question: What is the minimum area required for replanting/new planting?
faqs.answer: The minimum area required is 0.10 hectare in a continuous block.

faqs.question: What is the maximum area eligible for assistance?
faqs.answer: A maximum of 2 hectares per beneficiary per year is eligible, subject to an overall limit of 8 hectares during the scheme period from 2021–2026.

faqs.question: What financial assistance is provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: General Category growers are eligible for 33.33% of the cost of cultivation, subject to a maximum of ₹1,00,000 per hectare. SC/ST growers are eligible for 75% of the cost of cultivation, subject to a maximum of ₹2,10,000 per hectare.

faqs.question: Is Aadhaar mandatory for availing benefits?
faqs.answer: Yes, submission of Aadhaar Card is mandatory for processing the application.

faqs.question: What is the minimum plant population required?

faqs.question: Can a beneficiary avail the scheme benefit again for the same land?

faqs.question: Under which period is this scheme implemented?
faqs.answer: The scheme is implemented during the 15th Finance Commission period from 2021–22 to 2025–26.

name: Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom: New Subcomponents:FRESH-IT (Farmer’s Research & Enterprise in Spice Holdings for Innovative Technology)
description: The FRESH-IT (Farmer's Research & Enterprise in Spice Holdings for Innovative Technology) subcomponent is part of the Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom, implemented by the Spices Board under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India. The scheme aims to motivate spice farmers to take up innovations and improvements on their farms to develop promising spice varieties and new post-harvest improvement machinery/equipment for the spice farming community of the country at an affordable cost, thereby increasing the production, productivity, and quality of spices. The scheme is being implemented in accordance with the modalities and guidelines approved by the Competent Authority under the Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom during the 15th Finance Commission period (2021–22 to 2025–26).
benefits: > Grant-in-aid subject to a maximum of ₹ 7, 50,000/- per innovation in two installments of ₹ 3, 75,000/- in two phases based on the progress / completion of the innovation as recommended by the technical committee constituted for the purpose of evaluating the innovation by the farmer in development of new clones/ cultivars/ variety and machines/ post-harvest improvement equipments developed for improving quality of spices.
eligibility: All spice growing States and regions in India. Secretary Spices Board will constitute the Technical Committee with Director (Dev.) Spices Board as Chairperson of the Committee drawing members from ICRI, ICAR-IISR, identified SAUs of the State of reported innovation and concerned Regional Officer of Spices Board, on production aspects. and members of the Committee for evaluating innovations on post-harvest equipments will be the members of the already existing Regional Evaluation Committes constituted. Assistance will be extended based on MoU with Spices Board.. Concerned Officer of the Board who identified the innovation will forward the case to Director (Dev.) through proper channel for a preliminary scrutiny by a team of Officers nominated by Director (Dev.) and qualified cases will be presented to the technical committee for consideration and evaluation..
documents: a) Aadhaar card b) Bank details c)MoU in prescribed form

faqs.question: What is the FRESH-IT scheme?
faqs.answer: FRESH-IT is a subcomponent of the Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom that supports innovative ideas developed by spice farmers.

faqs.question: What is the objective of the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme aims to encourage spice farmers to develop innovative spice varieties and affordable post-harvest machinery/equipment to improve the production, productivity, and quality of spices.

faqs.question: Which organization implements the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme is implemented by the Spices Board, under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India.

faqs.question: Who can apply under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Spice farmers from all spice-growing States and regions in India who have developed innovative spice varieties or post-harvest machinery/equipment can apply.

faqs.question: What financial assistance is provided?
faqs.answer: Eligible applicants can receive grant-in-aid up to ₹7,50,000 per innovation.

faqs.question: How is the financial assistance released?
faqs.answer: The grant is released in two installments of ₹3,75,000 each, based on the progress and completion of the innovation as recommended by the Technical Committee.

faqs.question: Is there any agreement to be signed before receiving assistance?
faqs.answer: Yes. Assistance is provided based on a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) executed with the Spices Board.

faqs.question: Who evaluates the innovation?
faqs.answer: The innovation is evaluated by a Technical Committee constituted by the Secretary, Spices Board.

faqs.question: How are applications processed?
faqs.answer: The concerned officer who identifies the innovation forwards the proposal to the Director (Development). After preliminary scrutiny, eligible proposals are presented before the Technical Committee for evaluation.

faqs.question: Is the scheme available across India?
faqs.answer: Yes. The scheme is available in all spice-growing States and regions of India.

faqs.question: What is the Weather-Based Insurance Scheme for Small Cardamom?
faqs.answer: The Weather-Based Insurance Scheme provides financial protection to registered small cardamom growers against crop losses caused by adverse weather conditions such as deficient or excess rainfall, high temperature, and variations in relative humidity.

faqs.question: Who implements this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme is implemented by the Spices Board under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India.

faqs.question: What is the objective of the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme aims to protect small cardamom growers from weather-related risks that may adversely affect crop production and income.

faqs.question: Is there any limit on the number of years a beneficiary can receive assistance?
faqs.answer: Yes. Assistance is available for three consecutive years within the five-year block period (2021–2026).

faqs.question: What happens if the State Government does not contribute its share of the premium?
faqs.answer: If the State Government does not contribute its 15% share, the beneficiary must bear the additional cost, increasing the beneficiary's contribution from 10% to 25%.

faqs.question: Where is the scheme currently being implemented?
faqs.answer: The scheme is currently being implemented on a pilot basis in Idukki district of Kerala.

faqs.question: How is the insurance premium paid?
faqs.answer: The Spices Board and the beneficiary farmer pay their respective shares of the premium directly to the Insurance Company.

faqs.question: Who provides the insurance policy terms and conditions?
faqs.answer: The Insurance Company provides the insurance term sheet and policy details at the time of application.

faqs.question: Can farmers with more than 8 hectares of land apply under this scheme?
faqs.answer: No. Only registered small cardamom growers with landholdings between 0.10 hectare and 8 hectares are eligible for assistance under the scheme.

name: Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom: Post-Harvest Improvement: Polisher for Small Cardamom, Large Cardamom, Turmeric, etc (nos)
description: The Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom: Post-Harvest Improvement – Polisher for Small Cardamom, Large Cardamom, Turmeric, etc. (Nos.) is implemented by the Spices Board, India, under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India. The scheme aims to encourage spice growers to adopt proper polishing methods for spices such as small cardamom, large cardamom, and turmeric to improve their appearance, quality, and marketability. By promoting the use of modern polishing equipment, the scheme helps produce high-quality spices that meet export standards and enhances the competitiveness of Indian spices in international markets. The scheme is being implemented in accordance with the modalities and guidelines approved by the Competent Authority under the Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom during the 15th Finance Commission period (2021–22 to 2025–26).
benefits: 50 % of cost of unit, subject to a maximum of ₹ 94,000/- per unit for General Category and 75% subject to maximum of ₹ 1,40,000 per unit for NE/SC/ST & 90% Spice Producer's Groups in Identified Clusters subjected to maximum of ₹ 1,70,000/- Individual farmers having minimum of 0.40 ha - 8 ha of spices. Assistance for groups/FPOs will be as in QGBG
eligibility: All spice growing States and regions in India/UT. Spices Board with recommendation of Regional Officer..

a) Current year land tax receipt / Chitta Adangal / RTC / Percha / Possession Certificate

faqs.question: What is the objective of the Polisher for Spices scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme aims to encourage spice growers to adopt proper polishing methods for spices such as small cardamom, large cardamom, turmeric, and other suitable spices. The use of polishing equipment helps improve the quality, appearance, and marketability of spices, making them more suitable for export.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Individual farmers cultivating spices on land holdings ranging from 0.40 hectare to 8 hectares are eligible to apply for assistance under the scheme.

faqs.question: Can Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) and farmer groups avail assistance?
faqs.answer: Yes. Farmer groups and FPOs engaged in spice cultivation are eligible to receive assistance as per the provisions applicable to group beneficiaries under the scheme guidelines.

faqs.question: What financial assistance is available for General Category beneficiaries?
faqs.answer: General Category beneficiaries are eligible for assistance equal to 50% of the cost of the polishing unit, subject to a maximum limit of ₹94,000 per unit.

faqs.question: What financial assistance is available for NE, SC, and ST beneficiaries?
faqs.answer: Beneficiaries belonging to the North-Eastern Region, Scheduled Castes, and Scheduled Tribes can receive assistance equal to 75% of the cost of the unit, subject to a maximum limit of ₹1,40,000 per unit.

faqs.question: What assistance is available for Spice Producers' Groups in identified clusters?
faqs.answer: Spice Producers' Groups operating in identified clusters can receive assistance equal to 90% of the cost of the unit, subject to a maximum limit of ₹1,70,000 per unit.

faqs.question: Is Aadhaar mandatory for availing assistance?
faqs.answer: Yes. Aadhaar is a mandatory document required for identity verification and processing of the application.

faqs.question: In which areas is the scheme implemented?
faqs.answer: The scheme is implemented in all spice-growing states, regions, and Union Territories across India.

faqs.question: Which spices can be polished using the equipment?
faqs.answer: The equipment is primarily intended for small cardamom, large cardamom, turmeric, and similar spices. It may also be used for polishing other suitable spices with the necessary approvals.

description: The "Implementation of Scheme for Providing Implements/Machinery on Subsidy to the Farmers of Scheduled Caste Category (SB-89)" has been launched by the Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Department, Government of Haryana. The scheme aims to promote agricultural mechanization among Scheduled Caste farmers, increase their income, generate employment opportunities, and make them eligible for other mechanization schemes where tractor ownership is mandatory. > Scheme Implementation: The scheme is implemented by the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Haryana, through the District Level Executive Committee (DLEC), Deputy Directors of Agriculture, and Assistant Agriculture Engineers.

name: "Interest Subvention on Working Capital" under the "Assam Tea Industries Special Incentives Scheme"
description: The "Interest Subvention on Working Capital" component of "Assam Tea Industries Special Incentives Scheme (ATISIS)" by the Finance (Institutional Finance) Department, Government of Assam, aims to ensure long-term financial sustainability of the Tea industry and to incentivize manufacturers to move from Crush, Tear, Curl tea to Orthodox tea production. The component provides interest subvention on working capital loans at 3% per annum. The scheme is implemented by the Finance Department and the Industries & Commerce Department, Government of Assam, through multiple implementing agencies, including banks and the District Industries & Commerce Centre. The applications for this scheme are accepted online through a dedicated portal with a Direct Benefit Transfer mechanism for reimbursement.
benefits: Benefit Amount: Interest subvention of 3% per annum on Working Capital Loan. Maximum Claimable Amount: ₹20,00,000/- per annum per unit (garden). Validity Period: Extended for five years till the end of the Financial Year 2027-28. Applicable Financial Years: 2023-24, 2024-25, 2025-26, 2026-27, and 2027-28. Disbursement Mode: Direct Benefit Transfer as reimbursement. Claim Period: On completion of every financial year.
eligibility: General Eligibility. The applicant must be a tea plantation across all sizes. The applicant must be a tea manufacturing unit manufacturing Crush, Tear, Curl Tea, Orthodox Tea, or Speciality tea including Green tea, Oolong Tea, White tea, Yellow tea and Purple tea. The applicant must be located entirely in Assam. The applicant must not have any part of the plantation or manufacturing facility located outside the State of Assam. Interest Subvention Specific Eligibility. The applicant must have taken loan from a Scheduled Commercial Bank or a Public Financial Institution.. The applicant must have taken Working Capital Loan for activities directly related to plantation or manufacturing of Tea.. The applicant must have Working Capital sanctioned or renewed on or after 1st April of the financial year in which claim is to be made (2023-24, 2024-25, 2025-26, 2026-27 and 2027-28).. The applicant must not have loan accounts declared as Non-Performing Asset as per Reserve Bank of India guidelines on the date of filing claim.. The applicant must not have availed any interest subsidy under any other scheme..
documents: Working Capital Loan Sanction Letter Bank Statement showing Working Capital Loan details Interest Certificate from a Scheduled Commercial Bank or a Public Financial Institution Self
availing of interest subsidy under any other scheme Loan Account Classification Certificate (confirming Non
Performing Asset status) Tea Plantation or Manufacturing Unit Registration Documents
Bank Statement showing Working Capital Loan details
Interest Certificate from a Scheduled Commercial Bank or a Public Financial Institution
Self-Attestation regarding non-availing of interest subsidy under any other scheme
Loan Account Classification Certificate (confirming Non-Performing Asset status)
Tea Plantation or Manufacturing Unit Registration Documents

faqs.question: What types of tea plantation sizes are eligible to apply for the interest subvention benefit on working capital loans?
faqs.answer: Tea plantations of all sizes are eligible to apply for this benefit, with no minimum or maximum size restrictions specified.

faqs.question: Can manufacturing units producing different varieties of tea beyond the traditional types qualify for this working capital interest subvention?
faqs.answer: Yes, manufacturing units producing Crush, Tear, Curl Tea, Orthodox Tea, or Specialty tea including Green tea, Oolong Tea, White tea, Yellow tea and Purple tea are all eligible.

faqs.question: Is it mandatory for both the tea plantation and manufacturing facility to be located entirely within the state boundaries for eligibility?
faqs.answer: Yes, the applicant must be located entirely in Assam and must not have any part of the plantation or manufacturing facility located outside the State of Assam.

faqs.question: What is the specific interest rate reduction provided on working capital loans under this financial assistance program?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides interest subvention of 3% per annum on Working Capital Loan taken from eligible financial institutions.

faqs.question: What is the maximum financial benefit amount that can be claimed per unit annually under this working capital support scheme?
faqs.answer: The maximum claimable amount is ₹20,00,000/- per annum per unit or garden under this interest subvention component.

faqs.question: Which specific financial years are covered under the current validity period of this working capital interest subvention scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme covers financial years 2023-24, 2024-25, 2025-26, 2026-27, and 2027-28, extending till the end of Financial Year 2027-28.

faqs.question: What types of banking institutions are acceptable for taking working capital loans to qualify for this interest subvention benefit?
faqs.answer: Applicants must have taken loans from a Scheduled Commercial Bank or a Public Financial Institution to be eligible for the interest subvention.

faqs.question: What specific activities or purposes should the working capital loan be used for to qualify for this interest subvention?
faqs.answer: The Working Capital Loan must be taken for activities directly related to plantation or manufacturing of Tea to qualify for the benefit.

faqs.question: What is the minimum timing requirement for working capital loan sanction or renewal to be eligible for claims in specific financial years?
faqs.answer: The Working Capital must be sanctioned or renewed on or after 1st April of the financial year in which the claim is to be made.

faqs.question: What loan account status is required to maintain eligibility for this interest subvention benefit throughout the claim period?
faqs.answer: The applicant must not have loan accounts declared as Non-Performing Asset as per Reserve Bank of India guidelines on the date of filing claim.

faqs.question: Can applicants who have already received interest subsidies from other government schemes apply for this working capital interest subvention?
faqs.answer: No, applicants must not have availed any interest subsidy under any other scheme to be eligible for this benefit.

faqs.question: When is the appropriate time to submit claims for reimbursement under this working capital interest subvention scheme?
faqs.answer: Claims can be submitted on completion of every financial year for reimbursement of the interest subvention amount.

name: Janta Juth Accidental Insurance Scheme
department: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department
description: "Janta Juth" is a Farmer's Accidental Insurance Scheme launched by the Govt. of Gujarat on 26th January 1996 to provide economic assistance of upto ₹ 2,00,000 to Farmers in case of Death or Disability. It is a 100% state-sponsored scheme. The main objective is to assist the successor of the farmer in case of death or disability due to an accident. In this scheme, insurance premium is paid by the State Government for all farmers. This scheme is implemented under the Gujarat Community Group-Janta Accidental Insurance Scheme from 01/04/08 through Director of Insurance, Gandhinagar. In case of accidental death or permanent disability, all registered farmers, any child (son/daughter) of the farmer and husband/wife of the farmer having age of 5 to 70 years are beneficiaries for the scheme.
benefits: In case of accidental death or permanent disability 100% assistance of ₹ 2,00,000. In case of accidental loss of two eyes / two limbs / hand and leg / one eye and one hand or leg 100% assistance of ₹ 2,00,000 (100% full sight loss in case of eye, In case of hand- loss of upper part of the wrist and in case of the leg- totally cut off from the knee). In case of accidental loss of one eye or one limb 50% assistance of ₹ 1,00,000.
eligibility: The Deceased or the Person with Permanent Disability Should Be a Registered Farmer (Have Individual or Joint Name Land) or Child of a Registered Farmer (Son or Daughter) or the Husband/ Wife.. The Death or Permanent Disability Must Be Due to an Accident.. The Deceased or the Person with Permanent Disability should be between the age of 5 to 70 years.. The Application Should Be Made Within 150 Days to the Office of the Concerned District Agriculture Officer.. The sequence of the beneficiary under the scheme in chronological order:. Husband/Wife: In his/her absence. Children Son/Daughter: In their absence. Parent Father/Mother: In their absence. Grandson/Grandaughter: In the absence of 1, 2, 3. Unmarried/ Widow/ Exiled Sister who is dependent and living with the beneficiary. Any heirs declared under the Heirs Act applied to the beneficiary involved in other than above mentioned cases and controversial case. Note: Suicide or Natural Death Are Not Covered in This Scheme..
documents: A, Form No: 6 (certified extract after death date) Post Mortem Report F.I.R & Spot Panchnama Police Inquest Report or Court Order Death Certificate & Age Proof Case Approval report of Sub Divisional Magistrate. Disability certificate of Medical board/Civil Surgeon in the case of permanent disability and Photograph of disablement shown. Valid Driving License in case of Deceased was driving at the time of accident. Indemnity Bond Hereditary Report (Pedhinamu) Hereditary Report (Pedhinamu) in Successor case (When the husband/wife are not Successor) Any other proof asked by Director of Insurance

name: Jharkhand Krishi Rin Mafi Yojana
department: Department of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry & Co-operative
description: The "Jharkhand Krishi Rin Mafi Yojana" was launched by the Department of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry & Cooperative, Government of Jharkhand on 7th January 2021, to provide relief from the debt burden to short-term agricultural loan holders in the state. Under this scheme, outstanding loan amounts of up to ₹50,000/- in standard crop loan outstanding accounts as of 31st March 2020, will be waived. Standard crop loan borrowers as of 31st March 2020, will be eligible to avail the benefits of this scheme. The main objectives of the scheme are as follows: To improve the loan eligibility of crop loan holders. To ensure receipt of new crop loan. To stop the migration of farming communities. To strengthen the agricultural economy. Salient features of the scheme: Details of standard KCC loans covered under Aadhaar card and ration card are being uploaded by the bank on the loan waiver portal. The scheme will be implemented online through the web portal. This will minimize contact between the applicant and officials. Identification of correct beneficiaries using the Aadhaar number of the applicant and paperless application process. Easy online application process. The process of receiving applications through the Common Service Centre and Banks so as to provide scheme facilities to the applicants near their homes. Redressal of grievances of applicants through online mode.
benefits: Under this scheme, outstanding loan amounts of up to ₹50,000/- in standard crop loan outstanding accounts as of 31st March 2020, will be waived. Note: Repayment of outstanding loan through DBT.
eligibility: The applicant should be a permanent resident of Jharkhand.. The age of the farmer should be more than 18 years.. The applicant should be a farmer who self-cultivates their land or cultivates leased land.. The applicant should be a small or marginal farmer who has availed of the loan through the Kisan Credit Card.. The farmer should have a valid Aadhaar number.. The applicant should be a valid ration card holder.. The applicant should be a Kisan Credit Card holder.. The applicant should be a short-term crop loan holder.. The crop loan should be issued by a recognized bank located in Jharkhand.. The family of the deceased debtor is also eligible under the scheme.. The applicant should have a standard crop loan account.. Only one member per family holding a crop loan will be eligible.. This scheme will be voluntary for all crop loan holders.. Note: The applicant has to pay ₹1/- only for the application.. Eligibility for banks, criteria, determining outstanding loans and deadlines, eligible loan accounts, and exceptions:. Qualified Banks - Commercial Banks, Scheduled Co-operative Banks and Rural Banks. Qualifying Loan - Short-Term Crop Loan. Eligible period for disbursement - Upto 31.03.2020. Qualifying Loan Account - Single &. Joint. Loans taken for crop diseases.
documents: size photograph Proof of age Ration card Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Bank account details/bank passbook Other necessary documents if required

name: Jharkhand Rajya Fasal Rahat Yojana
department: Department of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry & Co-operative
description: The "Jharkhand Rajya Fasal Rahat Yojana" was launched by the Department of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry & Cooperative, Government of Jharkhand. This scheme is mainly to provide financial assistance to the farmers in the event of crop damage due to any natural calamity and natural accidents. The scheme is not a crop insurance scheme but a compensation scheme provided to farmers in case of crop damage. This will fulfill the objective of providing security coverage to farmers in case of crop loss due to natural calamities and providing a certain financial assistance. This scheme will cover both the land owner and the landless farmer. Farmers will not need to pay any kind of crop insurance premium under this scheme and they will be provided financial assistance directly by the government in the event of crop loss. Objective: To provide financial assistance to farmers affected by crop damage due to unforeseen natural calamities or events. To strengthen the income of the farmers to continue the agricultural work. Ensuring financial flow for agricultural work. To pave the way for food security, crop diversification, rapid growth, and competition in agriculture. The following types of natural calamities, which may affect the crop, will be included in this scheme: Flood and Water Logging Earthquake Volcanic Eruption Landslide Drought or dry winds (if drought has not been declared by the State Government) Widespread Epidemic Naturally Caught Fire Thunderstorm Storm Torrential Rain Cyclone The following risks will not be considered under the scheme: Losses caused by war/nuclear risks, Malicious losses and other preventable risks, such as unscientific farming practices by farmers etc. Loss due to attack by wild animals (Under this, the loss caused to the crop will be covered under the schemes of Forest, Environment and Climate Change Department, Government of Jharkhand).
benefits: Under this scheme, assured financial assistance is provided to eligible farmers in the event of crop loss occurring due to natural calamity. In the event of 30-50% loss: ₹3,000/- per acre maximum upto 5 acres In the event of >50% loss: ₹4,000/- per acre maximum upto 5 acres Note 1: Both Kharif (Paddy & Maize) and Rabi (Wheat, Mustard, Gram, and Potato) season crops are covered under this scheme. Note 2: No intermediary role of insurance companies and no premiums are required to be paid by applicant farmers. Note 3: Loss estimation through data of Crop Cutting Experiment.
eligibility: The applicant should be a permanent resident of Jharkhand.. The applicant should be a small or marginal farmer.. The applicant should be a ‘Raiyat’ or ‘Bataidaar’ farmer.. The age of the farmer should be at least 18 years.. The farmer should have a valid Aadhaar Number.. Farmers cultivating on government or non-majorua land with lease or settlement documents from the Revenue Department are also eligible.. The farmer should possess requisite land papers (LPC/Land Receipts).. Farmers can avail benefits for agricultural land ranging from a minimum of 10 decimals to a maximum of 5 acres under the scheme.. Crop assistance will be provided to farmers only in case of crop loss of at least 20%.. This scheme will be voluntary for all farmers.. Note: Under the scheme, special efforts will be made to ensure maximum coverage of SC/ST/Women/Paharia Tribe/Primitive Tribe farmers..
documents: size photograph Proof of age Bank account details/bank passbook Land papers (LPC/Land Receipts/ Vansawali)/Bandobasti Patta issued by Circle Office Sahmati Patra from Raiyat in case the applicant is a Bataidaar Farmer Complete details of selected crops for sowing along with land area Other necessary documents if required
Land papers (LPC/Land Receipts/ Vansawali)/Bandobasti Patta issued by Circle Office
Sahmati Patra from Raiyat in case the applicant is a Bataidaar Farmer
Complete details of selected crops for sowing along with land area

faqs.question: Is this scheme a crop insurance scheme?
faqs.answer: No, this scheme is not a crop insurance scheme but a compensation scheme to provide financial assistance directly to farmers in case of crop damage.

faqs.question: What are the objectives of the scheme?
faqs.answer: The objectives are to provide financial assistance to affected farmers, strengthen their income, ensure financial flow for agricultural work, and support food security, crop diversification, rapid growth, and competition in agriculture.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Eligible applicants are permanent residents of Jharkhand who are small or marginal farmers, 'Raiyat' or 'Bataidaar' farmers, aged at least 18 years, with a valid Aadhaar Number, and possess requisite land papers.

faqs.question: What types of natural calamities are covered under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme covers flood, waterlogging, earthquake, volcanic eruption, landslide, drought or dry winds, widespread epidemic, naturally caught fire, thunderstorm, storm, torrential rain, and cyclone.

faqs.question: What risks are not considered under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Losses caused by war/nuclear risks, malicious losses, preventable risks such as unscientific farming practices, and crop loss due to wild animal attacks are not covered under the scheme.

faqs.question: What benefits are provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Financial assistance of [?]3,000 per acre (for 30-50% crop loss) and [?]4,000 per acre (for >50% crop loss) is provided, up to a maximum of 5 acres.

faqs.question: Are both Kharif and Rabi season crops covered?
faqs.answer: Yes, both Kharif (Paddy & Maize) and Rabi (Wheat, Mustard, Gram, and Potato) season crops are covered under this scheme.

faqs.question: Do farmers need to pay any premium for this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, farmers do not need to pay any crop insurance premium under this scheme.

faqs.question: Who are excluded from participating in this scheme?
faqs.answer: Exclusions include former and present members of Rajya Sabha/Lok Sabha/Legislative Assembly, ministers, chairpersons of municipal bodies/Zilla Parishad, certain government employees, pensioners with monthly pensions of [?]10,000 or more, income tax payers, and practicing professionals like doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants, and architects.

faqs.question: How can farmers apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers can apply by visiting the official website of the Jharkhand Rajya Fasal Rahat Yojana at https://jrfry.jharkhand.gov.in/.

faqs.question: Are farmers cultivating on government or non-majorua land eligible?
faqs.answer: Yes, farmers cultivating on such lands with lease or settlement documents from the Revenue Department are eligible.

faqs.question: Is the scheme voluntary for farmers?
faqs.answer: Yes, participation in the scheme is voluntary for all farmers.

faqs.question: What is the minimum crop loss required to receive assistance?
faqs.answer: Farmers must have a crop loss of at least 20% to receive assistance under this scheme.

faqs.question: How much agricultural land can be covered under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers can avail benefits for agricultural land ranging from a minimum of 10 decimals to a maximum of 5 acres.

faqs.question: What if a farmer faces losses due to wild animal attacks?
faqs.answer: Losses due to wild animal attacks are not covered under this scheme but under the schemes of the Forest, Environment and Climate Change Department, Government of Jharkhand.

name: Krushak Assistance For Livelihood And Income Augmentation
description: Financing agriculture and insuring the cultivators is essential to eradicate poverty and to boost shared prosperity of the state. Through the implementation of Krushak Assistance for Livelihood and Income Augmentation - KALIA Scheme , the State Government aims to lend farmers with an all inclusive and flexible support system, ensuring accelerated agricultural prosperity. At the heart of a progressive scheme like KALIA lies the motivation to empower the farmers of the state with finance options that will enable the growth and development of agriculture in Odisha. Enhancement of the accessibility to suitable financial services will further ensure agricultural productivity and increase income among farmers , particularly the small and marginal land holders. Amounting to over 10,000 crore the scheme has been tailored to relieve the debt ridden farmers from the debt trap, keeping a pragmatic vision to directly attack poverty by providing financial assistance to the vulnerable agriculture households, landless labourers as well as marginal cultivators of the state. Proposed by the Government of Odisha , KALIA scheme brings under its umbrella 92% of cultivators of the state and almost all needy landless cultivators , who can avail the benefits of this scheme through Direct Benefit Transfer Mode.
benefits: Financial Assistance of Rs.12,500/-will be provided to each landless Agricultural Household for Agricultural allied activities like for small goat rearing unit, mini-layer unit, duckery units, fishery kits for fisherman, mushroom cultivation and bee-keeping, etc. This will particularly benefit to SC & ST population of our State. Vulnerable cultivators/landless agricultural laborers will get financial assistance of Rs. 10,000/- per family per year to enable them to take care of their sustenance. The vulnerable cultivator/landless Agricultural Laborers who are in old age, having disability/ disease and are vulnerable for any other reason Life insurance cover of Rs. 2.00 lakh at a very nominal premium of Rs.330/- will be provided to all savings bank account holder of age between 18-50 years. Government of Odisha will bear farmers’ share of annual premium of Rs.165/-. Personal accident cover of Rs.2.00 lakh at a very nominal annual premium of Rs.12/- for all savings bank account holder aged between 18-50 years. Out of Rs.12/- towards premium, Rs.6/- is the farmers’ share, which will be borne by the Govt. of Odisha. In respect of the above beneficiary whose age is between 51-70 years, the entire amount of Rs.12/- towards annual premium will be borne by Govt. of Odisha. Vulnerable landless laborers, cultivators, share croppers and agricultural families identified by Gram Panchayats will be provided with cop loans up to Rs 50,000 made available at 0% interest. A direct attack at poverty, this all-inclusive efficient scheme passionately believes in responsibly lending relevant borrowers ensuring development and growth in agriculture.
eligibility: Residency: The applicant must be a permanent resident of Odisha.. Agricultural activities: The applicant must be engaged in agricultural activities, such as farming, cultivation, horticulture, or animal husbandry, either as a landowner, tenant farmer or sharecropper.. Household status: The applicant's household should be categorized as "deprived". or "vulnerable". under the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011 or any other state government survey.. Landownership: The applicant must either own cultivable land or be a sharecropper/tenant farmer cultivating someone else's land.. Age: There is no age limit for applying for the KALIA Scheme.. Income: The applicant's annual income should be less than Rs. 00 lakhs per annum.. Bank account: The applicant must have a bank account in his/her name and a valid Aadhaar number linked to the account.. Criminal record: The applicant must not have any criminal record or involvement in any illegal activities..
documents: Aadhaar Card: A copy of your Aadhaar card is mandatory to apply for the KALIA Scheme. The Aadhaar number must be linked to your bank account. Bank Account Details: You need to provide your bank account details, including the bank name, branch name, account number, and IFSC code. Land Documents: If you own cultivable land, you need to submit the land documents, such as the land passbook or land tax receipt. If you are a sharecropper, you need to submit the sharecropping agreement. Income Certificate: You need to provide an income certificate issued by a competent authority to prove that your annual income is less than Rs.
lakhs per annum. Identity Proof: You need to submit a copy of your identity proof, such as a Voter ID card, PAN card, or Driving License. Photograph: You need to submit a recent passport

name: Krushy Aranya Protsaha Yojane (kapy)
description: The Karnataka Forest Department launched the 'Krushi Aranya Protsaha Yojane (KAPY)' program in 2011-12 to encourage farmers and the general public to increase forest and tree cover. The program provides subsidized seedlings to farmers for planting on their lands. Farmers are paid an incentive of Rs 35 for every surviving seedling at the end of the first year, Rs 40 after the completion of the second year, and Rs 50 after the completion of the third year. This is done to encourage the farmers to nurture the seedlings for at least three years. The amount of money provided as an incentive (Rs 125/- per seedling) more than compensates the cost incurred by the farmer in procuring and planting the seedling. The incentive is quite substantial when the farmer plants more seedlings. In addition to the financial incentive, the farmers are entitled to get handsome returns from the grown-up trees in the form of fruits, seeds, fodder, firewood, pole, timber, and other useful products.
benefits: Increased forest and tree cover: The main benefit of the Krushi Aranya Protsaha Yojane (KAPY) scheme is the promotion of the cooperation of farmers and the general public in the task of increasing forest and tree cover. Subsidized seedlings: Under the scheme, farmers are provided seedlings at subsidized rates from the nearest nurseries of the Forest Department for planting in their lands. Monetary incentive: The farmers are paid an amount of Rs 35 as an incentive for every surviving seedling at the end of the first year, Rs 40 for the second year, and Rs 50 for the third year. Encourages nurturing: The incentive is given to encourage the farmer not only to plant the seedlings but also to nurture them at least for three years. Compensates cost: The total amount of money provided (Rs 125/- per seedling) more than compensates the cost incurred by the farmer in procuring and planting the seedling. Restriction on ineligible species: The scheme has restrictions on ineligible tree species, which helps promote the planting of appropriate tree species and prevents the proliferation of invasive species.

name: Krishak Bakri Palan Yojna
description: The Department of Animal Husbandry, Government of Himachal Pradesh has introduced a scheme named " Krishak Bakri Palan Yojna " with the aim to increase income generation opportunities for economically weaker segments of the society as well as to increase meat production. Goat farming is a traditional occupation of economically weaker segments of the society (small and marginal farmers, mainly nomads and landless laborer's) in Himachal Pradesh. This species is considered to be major source of economic sustenance for these categories of people. Adaptability of goats to wide range of agro climatic conditions has rendered it suitable for poor farmers. Under this scheme it has been proposed to distribute units of 11 goats (10 females +1male), 5 goats (4 females +1 male) and 3 goats (2 females +1 male) of Beetal/Sirohi/Jamanapari/White Himalayan breeds on 60% subsidy. Objectives of this scheme: Increase Income Generation: The scheme aims to enhance income generation opportunities for economically weaker sections through goat farming. 1. Boost Meat Production: By providing high-quality goat breeds, the scheme aims to increase meat production in the state. 1. Support Economically Disadvantaged Families: The scheme offers a 60% subsidy on goat units, making it easier for financially weaker families to start goat farming. 1. Promote Rural Development: Encouraging goat farming contributes to the overall development of rural areas in Himachal Pradesh. 1. Ensure Sustainable Livelihoods: The scheme provides a sustainable livelihood to small farmers and landless laborers, reducing their economic vulnerability.
benefits: Financial Assistance: Farmers receive goat units on a 60% subsidy, significantly reducing the initial investment required for goat farming.1. Improved Livelihoods: The scheme helps improve the livelihoods of small farmers by providing a steady source of income through goat farming.1. Increased Meat Production: By distributing high-quality goat breeds, the scheme boosts meat production in the state, contributing to the local economy.1. Sustainable Farming Practices: The scheme promotes sustainable farming practices, ensuring long-term economic benefits for farmers.1. Empowerment of Marginalized Communities: By targeting economically weaker sections, the scheme empowers marginalized communities, promoting social and economic inclusion.
eligibility: Farmers belonging to all categories like general/SC/ST/BPL/Women and Landless persons of Himachal Pradesh are eligible. Training/awareness in skills of goat husbandry is mandatory for all applicants. Concerned Senior Veterinary Officer will provide training to interested persons/applicants.. The preference will be given to:. Unemployed SC, ST, Women and General category persons. At least 30 percent beneficiaries should be women.. Families where no member is in Government job.. name: Krishak Bandhu Scheme
description: Launched in 2019, the scheme "Krishak Bandhu Scheme" by the Department of Agriculture, Government of West Bengal, aims to provide financial assistance to farmers for agricultural sustainability and risk mitigation. The scheme offers ₹5,000/- per acre per year as direct income support and ₹2,00,000/- as death benefit to the family of deceased farmers. Eligible beneficiaries include small and marginal farmers owning up to 2 acres of land and all farmer families in case of death or disability. The scheme is implemented by the Department of Agriculture, Government of West Bengal, and applications are accepted both online and offline.
benefits: Direct Income Support Farmers with one acre or more of cultivable land receive ₹10,000/- per annum, payable in two equal installments of ₹5,000/- each (one for Kharif and one for Rabi season). Farmers with less than one acre of cultivable land receive assistance on a pro-rata basis, subject to a minimum of ₹4,000/- per annum, paid in two equal installments. Death/Disability Benefit In the event of the death of a farmer between the ages of 18 and 60 years, a one-time lump sum grant of ₹2,00,000/- is provided to the legal heirs of the deceased. The farmer must have been enrolled under the Krishak Bandhu scheme at the time of death. A one-time lump sum grant of ₹2,00,000/- for permanent disability of the farmer due to accident. Disbursement Conditions Income support is linked to land ownership records. Death benefit requires submission of legal heir certificates. Disbursed via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to the beneficiary's bank account.
eligibility: For Income Support. The applicant must be a resident of West Bengal.. The applicant must own cultivable land (up to 2 acres).. The applicant must be actively engaged in farming.. For Death/Disability Benefit. The deceased/disabled person must have been a farmer aged 18–60 years.. The applicant must be the legal heir (for death benefit)..
documents: Record of Rights (RoR) of Cultivable Land / RoR recorded with Barga / Patta Record / Forest Patta (Latest). Voter Identity Card (Mandatory). Aadhaar Card (Optional). Bank Passbook (First page and last page) / Cancelled Cheque. Passport Size Recent Photograph (Original). Self Declaration with Land Documents & Warison Certificate (if needed). Bank account and Aadhaar linked mobile number. Death Certificate (For Death Benefit). Legal Heir Certificate (For Death Benefit). Disability Certificate (For Disability Benefit).
Record of Rights (RoR) of Cultivable Land / RoR recorded with Barga / Patta Record / Forest Patta (Latest).
Bank Passbook (First page and last page) / Cancelled Cheque.
Self Declaration with Land Documents & Warison Certificate (if needed).
Bank account and Aadhaar linked mobile number.

name: Kisan Credit Card
department: Ministry Of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
description: The KCC Scheme was introduced with the objective of providing adequate and timely credit to the farmers for their agricultural operations. The Government of India provides interest subvention of 2% and Prompt Repayment Incentive of 3% to the farmers, thus making the credit available at a very subsidized rate of 4% per annum. The scheme was further extended for the investment credit requirement of farmers viz. allied and non-farm activities in the year 2004 and further revisited in 2012 by a working Group under the Chairmanship of Shri T. M. Bhasin, CMD, Indian Bank with a view to simplify the scheme and facilitate issue of Electronic Kisan Credit Cards. The scheme provides broad guidelines to banks for operationalizing the KCC scheme. Implementing banks will have the discretion to adopt the same to suit institution/location-specific requirements. Objective / Purpose The Kisan Credit Card scheme aims at providing adequate and timely credit support from the banking system under a single window with the flexible and simplified procedures to the farmers for their cultivation and other needs as indicated below : To meet the short term credit requirements for the cultivation of crops; Post-harvest expenses; Produce marketing loan; Consumption requirements of farmer household; Working capital for maintenance of farm assets and activities allied to agriculture; Investment credit requirement for agriculture and allied activities Type of Card A magnetic stripe card with PIN (Personal Identification Number) with an ISO IIN (International Standards Organization International Identification Number) to enable access to all banks ATMs and micro ATMs In cases where the Banks would want to utilize the centralized biometric authentication infrastructure of the UIDAI (Aadhaar authentication), debit cards with magnetic stripe and PIN with ISO IIN with biometric authentication of UIDAI can be provided. Debit Cards with magnetic stripes and only biometric authentication can also be provided depending on the customer base of the bank. Till such time, UIDAI becomes widespread, if the banks want to get started without inter-operability using their existing centralized bio metric infrastructure, banks may do so. Banks may choose to issue EMV (Europay, MasterCard and VISA, a global standard for the interoperation of integrated circuit cards) and RUPAY compliant chip cards with magnetic stripe and pin with ISO IIN. Further, biometric authentication and smart cards may follow the common open standards prescribed by IDRBT and IBA. This will enable them to transact seamlessly with input dealers and also enable them to have the sales proceeds credited to their accounts when they sell their output at mandies, procurement centres, etc Delivery Channels : The following delivery channels shall be put in place to start with so that the Kisan Credit Card is used by the farmers to effectively transact their operations in their KCC account. Withdrawal through ATMs / Micro ATM Withdrawal through BCs using smart cards. PoS machine through input dealers Mobile Banking with IMPS capabilities / IVR Aadhaar enabled Cards
benefits: Fixation of credit limit/Loan amount The short-term limit to arrive for the first year: For farmers raising a single crop in a year: Scale of finance for the crop (as decided by District Level Technical Committee) x Extent of area cultivated + 10% of limit towards post-harvest / household/consumption requirements + 20% of limit towards repairs and maintenance expenses of farm assets + crop insurance, PAIS & asset insurance.1. Limit for second & subsequent year : First-year limit for crop cultivation purposes arrived at as above plus 10% of the limit towards cost escalation/increase in the scale of finance for every successive year ( 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th year) and estimated Term loan component for the tenure of Kisan Credit Card, i.e., five years.1. For farmers raising more than one crop in a year, the limit is to be fixed as above depending upon the crops cultivated as per the proposed cropping pattern for the first year and an additional 10% of the limit towards cost escalation/increase in the scale of finance for every successive year (2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th year). It is assumed that the farmer adopts the same cropping pattern for the remaining four years also. In case the cropping pattern adopted by the farmer is changed in the subsequent year, the limit may be reworked. 1. Term loans for investments towards land development, minor irrigation, purchase of farm equipment and allied agricultural activities. The banks may fix the quantum of credit for the term and working capital limit for agricultural and allied activities, etc., based on the unit cost of the asset/s proposed to be acquired by the farmer, the allied activities already being undertaken on the farm, the bank’s judgment on repayment capacity vis-a-vis total loan burden devolving on the farmer, including existing loan obligations.1. The long-term loan limit is based on the proposed investments during the five-year period and the bank’s perception of the repaying capacity of the farmer 1. Maximum Permissible Limit : The short-term loan limit arrived for the 5th year plus the estimated long-term loan requirement will be the Maximum Permissible Limit (MPL) and treated as the Kisan Credit Card Limit.1. Fixation of Sub-limits for other than Marginal Farmers: Short-term loans and term loans are governed by different interest rates. Besides, at present, short-term crop loans are covered under Interest Subvention Scheme/ Prompt Repayment Incentive scheme. Further, repayment schedules and norms are different for short-term and term loans. Hence, in order to have operational and accounting convenience, the card limit is to be bifurcated into separate sub-limits for short-term cash credit limit cum savings account and term loans. - The drawing limit for short-term cash credit should be fixed based on the cropping pattern and the amounts for crop production, repairs and maintenance of farm assets and consumption may be allowed to be drawn at the convenience of the farmer. In case the revision of the scale of finance for any year by the district-level committee exceeds the notional hike of 10% contemplated while fixing the five-year limit, a revised drawable limit may be fixed and the farmer is advised about the same. In case such revisions require the card limit itself to be enhanced (4th or 5th year), the same may be done and the farmer be so advised. For term loans, instalments may be allowed to be withdrawn based on the nature of the investment and the repayment schedule drawn as per the economic life of the proposed investments. It is to be ensured that at any point in time, the total liability should be within the drawing limit of the concerned year. - Wherever the card limit/liability so arrived warrants additional security, the banks may take suitable collateral as per their policy.
eligibility: Farmers - individual/joint borrowers who are owner cultivators;. Tenant farmers, oral lessees &. share croppers;. Self Help Groups (SHGs) or Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) of farmers including tenant farmers, share croppers etc.
documents: Application Form. Two Passport Size Photographs. ID proof such as Driving License / Aadhar Card / Voter Identity Card / Passport. Address Proof such as Driving License, Aadhar Card. Proof of landholding duly certified by the revenue authorities. Cropping pattern (Crops grown) with acreage. Security documents for loan limit above Rs.
lakhs, as applicable. Any other document as per sanction.

description: Under this scheme, while expanding the definition of a farmer, along with the Khatauni registered account holder / co-account holder, such earning members of their family whose main source of livelihood is agricultural income from the land registered in the name of the account holder / co-account holder and such landless persons. benefits: In this scheme, the Uttar Pradesh government will provide the following amount / financial assistance or compensation amount to the farmers if they are victims of the accident – Compensation for loss of both hands and legs of the farmer – Rs 5 lakh. In case of loss of 1 hand and 1 foot – Rs.5 lakh. In case of disability of one leg and one hand – financial assistance ranges from 2 to 3 lakhs. In case of the death of a farmer in an accident – ​​a compensation amount of up to Rs.5 lakh will be given.
