The grant amount will be deposited directly into the farmer's account.
benefits: Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST), small, and marginal farmers will get 70 percent of the unit cost or a maximum of ₹73,500/- on raw form pounds and 90 percent or ₹1,35,000/- on plastic lining form pounds and other category farmers. The subsidy is available on 60 percent of the cost or a maximum of ₹63,000/- on raw form pounds and 80 percent or ₹1,20,000/- on plastic lining form pounds, whichever is less. > The subsidy is payable only on farm ponds of a minimum 400 cubic meter capacity.
eligibility: The applicant should be a Farmer.. The applicant should be a native of Rajasthan.. The applicant farmer should have a minimum cultivable land of 0.3 hectares at one place in his name.. In the case of the joint account holder, the minimum land in one place should be 0.5 hectares..
documents: Bank Passbook. Land Proof. Jan Aadhar card. Mobile Number.

faqs.question: What is the objective of the scheme?
faqs.answer: The state government gives subsidy to the farmers on the construction of farm ponds so that the farmers can irrigate their fields by collecting rain water by making farm ponds in their fields.

faqs.question: Who Can Get The Benefits Of The Scheme ?
faqs.answer: Farmers will get the benefits.

faqs.question: Under which department does this scheme come?
faqs.answer: Agriculture Department.

faqs.question: How do I know if a field in the application form is mandatory?
faqs.answer: "Fields marked with an asterisk ( ) are mandatory."

faqs.question: Is there any cubic meters criteria in this scheme?
faqs.answer: The minimum size of the farm pond should be 400 cubic meters.

faqs.question: What is Bhamashah Card?
faqs.answer: The Bhamashah card provided by this yojana is linked to a bank account in the name of the housewife. The card also provides women with biometric identification and core banking functions, as well as a variety of cash benefits that are directly transferred to their bank account.

faqs.question: How can i apply online?
faqs.answer: The farmer will be able to apply himself or by visiting the nearest e-Mitra online centre.

faqs.question: Can applicants from outside Rajasthan apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: No, this scheme only for Rajasthan people.

faqs.question: What is the Supporting Documents in this scheme?
faqs.answer: Janaadhar Card.Bank Passbook.Land Proof.

name: Silkworm Rearing Equipment
description: The scheme “Silkworm Rearing Equipment” was launched by the Department of Sericulture, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to support individuals in silkworm rearing by providing necessary equipment, financial assistance, and technical guidance.
benefits: Under this scheme, selected beneficiaries are provided ₹40,000/- (in an 80:10:10 ratio) to purchase equipment necessary for silkworm rearing. Beneficiaries are required to contribute 10% of this amount themselves for the installation of the leaf chamber, while other rearing materials are provided by the department.
eligibility: The beneficiary must be a resident of Uttarakhand.. The beneficiary must belong to a cluster or group.. In hilly areas, a minimum of 25 farmers is required to form a cluster, while in plain areas, at least 50 farmers are mandatory.. The beneficiary must be willing to engage in sericulture.. Preference will be given to farmers who are already engaged in sericulture or who have mulberry seedlings available.. Under the Silk Samagra Yojana, saplings are planted on the boundaries of farmers’ fields, with a standard of 300 saplings per acre.. All farmers in the selected cluster are required to plant the saplings..
documents: Voter ID Card/Ration Card Bank Account Details Land Documents / Ownership Proof Photographs of the Plantation Area Other supporting documents as required

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Eligibility is for individuals willing to engage in silkworm rearing, preferably those already involved in sericulture or having mulberry edible plants.

faqs.question: What financial assistance is provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Selected beneficiaries receive ₹40,000/- (in an 80:10:10 ratio) to purchase equipment necessary for silkworm rearing.

faqs.question: Is the beneficiary required to contribute financially?
faqs.answer: Yes, beneficiaries are required to contribute 10% of the amount themselves, specifically for installing the leaf chamber.

faqs.question: What equipment is provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides leaf chambers and other rearing materials necessary for silkworm cultivation, while farmers contribute only for the leaf chamber installation.

faqs.question: How are beneficiaries organized?
faqs.answer: Beneficiaries are organized into clusters or groups. A minimum of 25 farmers in hilly areas and 50 farmers in plain areas is required per cluster.

faqs.question: What is the standard for planting mulberry saplings?
faqs.answer: Under the Silk Samagra Yojana, 300 saplings per acre are planted on the boundaries of farmers' fields.

faqs.question: How are beneficiaries selected?
faqs.answer: Beneficiaries are selected through publicity seminars, meetings, and training programs organized by representatives of cooperative societies or silk self-help groups affiliated with Chowki centers and center/range in-charges.

faqs.question: How is the grant disbursed to beneficiaries?
faqs.answer: Grant funds are provided after verification of the work completed, including leaf chamber setup and plantation activities, under departmental supervision.

name: Krishak Utpadak Kshati Sahayata Yojana
description: The scheme “Krishak Utpadak Kshati Sahayata Yojana” is implemented by the Uttarakhand Agricultural Production & Marketing Board under the Department of Agriculture, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide financial assistance and compensation to farmers in the event of loss or damage to crops, livestock, or agricultural land caused by fire, flood, or heavy rains in the notified areas of the state.
benefits: Damage caused by fire accidents to standing crops, harvested crops in the field, crops stored in barns for threshing, or residual produce in the notified market areas of Uttarakhand State, as well as damage to property and livestock due to fire in the farmer’s house, and damage to agricultural land due to floods or rain-induced soil erosion, all such losses make farmers eligible to receive compensation under this scheme.
eligibility: The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.. The applicant must be a minimum of 18 years of age to submit and receive a claim..
documents: Documents are required in accordance with the Mandi Committee/ Mandi Board for claiming the compensation under the scheme.

faqs.question: Who can benefit from this scheme?
faqs.answer: All resident farmers and agricultural producers of Uttarakhand who suffer damage to crops, livestock, or agricultural property due to fire, flood, or heavy rains in the notified market areas can benefit from this scheme.

faqs.question: What types of damages are covered under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme covers: Fire damage to standing crops, harvested crops, or crops kept in barns for threshing. Damage to property and livestock due to fire in the farmer’s house. Damage to agricultural land due to floods or rain-induced soil erosion.

faqs.question: Is there any age limit to apply for compensation?
faqs.answer: Yes, the minimum age to apply for compensation under the scheme is 18 years.

faqs.question: Where can farmers get the application form?
faqs.answer: Farmers can obtain the application form free of cost from the concerned Mandi Samiti office.

faqs.question: Within how many days must the incident be reported?
faqs.answer: The affected farmer or producer must report the incident within 7 days of its occurrence by submitting the application form.

faqs.question: To whom should the application be submitted?
faqs.answer: The application should be submitted to the Secretary, Chairman, Administrator, or Tehsildar of the concerned Mandi Samiti area.

faqs.question: How is the compensation amount paid to the farmer?
faqs.answer: The Mandi Board prepares a bank draft in the name of the claimant and sends it to the Secretary of the concerned Mandi Committee for disbursement to the farmer.

name: Karma Veer Dadasaheb Gaikwad Sabalikaran & Swabhiman Yojana
department: Social Justice and Special Assistance Department
description: Being implemented particularly for the Scheduled Caste Communities, the "Karma Veer Dadasaheb Gaikwad Sabalikaran & Swabhiman Yojana" is a scheme by the Department of Social Justice & Special Assistance, Govt. of Maharashtra. The main objective of this scheme is to improve the financial condition of the scheduled castes and Nav-Buddhists who are landless workers and are from "Below Poverty Line". Only citizens who are permanent residents of the state of Maharashtra are eligible to apply for this scheme. This scheme is 100% funded by the Govt. of Maharashtra.
benefits: The beneficiary is provided with 2-acre irrigated land or 4-acre non-irrigated land on 50% of the subsidy and 50% is loan.
eligibility: The applicant should be a citizen of India.. The applicant should be a permanent resident of Maharashtra State.. The applicant should be in the 18 to 60 years age group.. The applicant should be from Scheduled Caste or should be a Nav-Buddhists.. The applicant should be landless.. The applicant should be from the "Below Poverty Line". category..
documents: BPL Card Aadhaar Card. Proof of Age (Birth Certificate, Marksheet of Class 10th/12th, etc) 2

Passport Sized Photograph (Signed Across) Residential Certificate / Domicile Certificate of the State of Maharashtra. Caste Certificate and/or Certificate mentioning "Nau Bouddha" or "Converted Buddhist" or "Neo Buddhist" issued by the Revenue Department, Govt. of Maharashtra. Details of the Bank Account (Bank Name, Branch Name, Address, IFSC, etc). Any other document required by the District Social Welfare Office.

faqs.question: What Percentage Of The Scheme Benefit Is Provided As A Subsidy?
faqs.answer: 50% of the scheme benefit is provided as a subsidy.

faqs.question: What Percentage Of The Scheme Benefit Is Provided As A Loan?
faqs.answer: 50% of the scheme benefit is provided as a loan.

faqs.question: What Should Be The Area In Case The Beneficiary Is Provided With Irrigated Land?
faqs.answer: If the beneficiary is provided with irrigated land, its area should be 2 acres.

faqs.question: What Should Be The Area In Case The Beneficiary Is Provided With Non-Irrigated Land?
faqs.answer: If the beneficiary is provided with irrigated land, its area should be 4 acres.

faqs.question: Who Are The Neo-Buddhists?
faqs.answer: In 1956, when Dr. B R Ambedkar adopted Buddhism, thousands of Scheduled Castes peoples, especially those belonging to the Mahar caste, joined him and embraced Buddhism. Since then they are known as Neo-Buddhists. However, those who were following Buddhism before 1956 are known as Buddhists. (Source: https://ncert.nic.in/degsn/pdf/elementary-report.pdf)

faqs.question: Who Are The Target Beneficiaries Of This Scheme?
faqs.answer: For this scheme, the target beneficiaries are the scheduled castes and Nav-Buddhists who are landless workers and are from "Below Poverty Line".

faqs.question: What Are The Objectives Of This Scheme?
faqs.answer: The main objective of this scheme is to improve the financial condition of the scheduled castes and Nav-Buddhists who are landless workers and are from "Below Poverty Line".

faqs.question: What Is The Full Form Of SJSA?
faqs.answer: The full form of SJSA is "Social Justice & Special Assistance".

faqs.question: Is This A State Funded Or A Centrally Funded Scheme?
faqs.answer: This is a 100% State Funded scheme.

faqs.question: Can Applicants From The Neighboring States Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Etc Also Apply To This Scheme?
faqs.answer: No, only the citizens who are permanent residents of the state of Maharashtra are eligible to apply.

faqs.question: Where Can I Find The URL To The Website Of The Dept. Of Social Justice & Special Assistance?
faqs.answer: The URL to the official website of the Department of Social Justice & Special Assistance, Government of Maharashtra is - https://sjsa.maharashtra.gov.in/

faqs.question: Where Can I Find The Link To The Scheme Guidelines?
faqs.answer: The Scheme Guidelines can be found at this link - https://sjsa.maharashtra.gov.in/en/scheme-category/awards

faqs.question: What Is The Address Of The Department Of Social Justice & Special Assistance, Government Of Maharashtra?
faqs.answer: The address of the Department of Social Justice & Special Assistance, Government of Maharashtra is: 437, Shankar Sheth Rd, Police Colony, Swargate, Pune, Maharashtra 411042

faqs.question: Where Can I Find The Addresses Of The District Social Welfare Offices?
faqs.answer: The addresses of the District Social Welfare Offices can be found at - https://sjsa.maharashtra.gov.in/en/contacts

faqs.question: Is There An Age-Related Criterion For This Scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, the applicant should be in the 18 to 60 years age group.

faqs.question: Where Can I Post My Grievances Related To This Scheme?
faqs.answer: You can post your grievances at the Grievance Redressal Portal by the Govt. of Maharashtra: https://grievances.maharashtra.gov.in/en

faqs.question: Is There An Income-Related Criterion For This Scheme?
faqs.answer: No, there is no income-related criterion for this scheme.

name: Kisan Vriksha Mitra Yojana
description: The scheme "Kisan Vriksha Mitra Yojana" by the Department of Forest, Environment, and Climate Change, Government of Chhattisgarh, aims to promote commercial tree plantation on private lands of farmers and other stakeholders. The scheme seeks to increase farmers' income, reduce the financial burden on the government, and generate employment opportunities. Eligible beneficiaries include farmers, private educational institutions, private trusts, panchayats, and leased landholders. The scheme is implemented by the Department of Forest, Environment, and Climate Change in collaboration with private companies and supportive organizations.
benefits: > Financial Assistance 100% financial assistance for plantation on up to 5 acres of land (maximum 5,000 plants). 50% financial assistance for plantation on more than 5 acres of land (maximum 1,000 plants per acre). 50% financial assistance for private educational institutions, private trusts, panchayats, and leased landholders. > Buyback Assurance The government ensures buyback of produce like eucalyptus, bamboo, and other economically beneficial trees at a predetermined support price. The scheme also involves private companies and supportive organizations for financial collaboration and buyback assurance. > Employment Generation The scheme aims to create employment opportunities through plantation activities. > Mode of Disbursement Financial assistance is disbursed directly to the beneficiaries' accounts after verification of plantation work. > Frequency of Disbursement Assistance is provided over three years, with yearly disbursements based on the survival rate of plants.
eligibility: The following are eligible -. Farmers with private land.. Private educational institutions.. Private trusts.. Panchayats.. Leased landholders.. Priority is given to farmers and stakeholders who are willing to plant commercially viable tree species like eucalyptus, bamboo, and others..
documents: Land Ownership Documents. Bank Account Details. Aadhaar Card. Proof of Identity (for Private Institutions and Trusts). Lease Agreement (for Leased Landholders).
Proof of Identity (for Private Institutions and Trusts).

faqs.question: What is the maximum financial assistance for a farmer with 10 acres of land?
faqs.answer: A farmer with 10 acres of land can receive 50% financial assistance for up to 10,000 plants (1,000 plants per acre).

faqs.question: How is the support price for the produce determined?
faqs.answer: The support price for the produce is determined annually by a state-level committee.

faqs.question: What is the financial assistance for private trusts in the third year?
faqs.answer: Private trusts receive 50% financial assistance in the third year based on the survival rate of the plants.

faqs.question: What is the role of the forest department in this scheme?
faqs.answer: The forest department verifies applications, monitors plantations, and disburses financial assistance to beneficiaries.

faqs.question: How is the financial assistance for leased landholders disbursed?
faqs.answer: Financial assistance for leased landholders is disbursed directly to their bank accounts after verification.

faqs.question: What is the financial assistance for panchayats in the second year?
faqs.answer: Panchayats receive 50% financial assistance in the second year based on the survival rate of the plants.

faqs.question: Can farmers plant trees other than eucalyptus and bamboo?
faqs.answer: Yes, farmers can plant other economically beneficial tree species as per the scheme guidelines.

faqs.question: What is the maximum number of plants supported for up to 5 acres?
faqs.answer: For up to 5 acres, the maximum number of plants supported is 5,000.

faqs.question: How is the survival rate of plants calculated for disbursement?
faqs.answer: The survival rate is calculated based on the number of live plants after each year of plantation.

faqs.question: What is the financial assistance for private institutions in the first year?
faqs.answer: Private institutions receive 50% financial assistance in the first year for plantation activities.

faqs.question: Is there a committee to determine the support price for the produce?
faqs.answer: Yes, a state-level committee determines the support price for the produce annually.

faqs.question: What is the role of private companies in this scheme?
faqs.answer: Private companies collaborate financially and provide buyback assurance for the produce from the plantation.

faqs.question: How long does the monitoring and evaluation of the plantation last?
faqs.answer: The plantation is monitored for three years, and subsequent disbursements depend on the survival rate of the plants.

faqs.question: Is there any priority given to specific beneficiaries under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Priority is given to farmers and stakeholders willing to plant commercially viable tree species like eucalyptus and bamboo.

name: Krishi Vidya Nidhi Yojana
description: The scheme "Krishi Vidya Nidhi Yojana" has been implemented by the Department of Agriculture & Farmers’ Empowerment, Government of Odisha. It aims to extend financial assistance to the children of the beneficiaries under CM-KISAN for pursuing Professional/ Technical courses. It will lead to better access to Higher Education for children of Small & Marginal farmers (SF/MF) and Landless Agricultural households (LAH). Krishi Vidya Nidhi Yojana will support SF/MF & LAH in empowering their families. > Key Features: In order to ensure proper higher education of their children, support will be provided in the form of Krishi Vidya Nidhi Yojana. The scholarship will be given purely on a merit basis to those who are studying professional/technical courses like Medical and Engineering. Agriculture & Allied, Nursing, Diploma, and different trades in ITI in Government, Private Institutions, and Premier Institutions.
benefits: > Scholarship Support: Scholarship is provided to students pursuing eligible professional, technical, diploma, postgraduate, and doctoral courses. The scholarship is awarded purely on a merit basis. > Course-Based Financial Assistance: For the students of Government Institutions, the tuition fees, annual fees, one-time fees, hostel charges, and any other fees deposited by the student in the colleges/universities/institutions except the caution money/ any other refundable money as admissible shall be released to the concerned student account. Scholarship amount for the students studying in Private Institutes of the State shall be released to the student as per the course fee structure enclosed in Annexure-1 (https://agri.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2025-03/6728a6c09079e1730717376 0.pdf). > Premier Institutions Support: For students admitted to premier institutions such as National Institute of Technology (NIT), Indian Institute of Technology(NIT), Indian Institute of Management (IIM), All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Indian Council of Agricultural Research institutions (ICAR)( Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), Indian Veterinary Research Institute (IVRI), Central Institute of Fisheries Education (CIFE), and National Dairy Research Institute (NDRI), the scholarship is limited to the lower of actual recommended fees or ₹1,00,000/-. > Hostel and Mess Charges: ₹1,200/- per month for Under Graduate, Post Graduate, Ph.D., and Premier Institution students for 10 months. ₹1,000/- per month for Diploma, Polytechnic, and Industrial Training Institute students for 10 months.
eligibility: The applicant must be a resident/domicile of the State of Odisha.. The applicant should be a child of an eligible beneficiary under the CM-KISAN scheme, including both components, namely Support to Farmers for Cultivation and Livelihood Support to Landless Agricultural Households.. The applicant’s parent must be eligible under CM-KISAN, which will be verified during the student’s application process at the Chief District Agriculture Officer (CDAO) level.. The applicant must have obtained admission on a merit basis in a Government Institution or Private Institution having an AISHE code (All India Survey on Higher Education) of the State, or in a Premier Government Institution, whether located inside or outside the State.. The applicant must have taken admission in any of the following Subjects and courses:. Professional or Technical Undergraduate courses such as M.B.B.S., B.D.S., B.H.M.S., B.A.M.S., B.Pharm, B.Sc. (Nursing), Post Basic B.Sc. Nursing, B.Sc. (Hons) Agriculture, Bachelor of Veterinary Science and Animal Husbandry, B.Sc. (Hons) Horticulture, B.Sc. (Hons) Forestry, B.Sc. (Fisheries Science), B.Sc. (Community Science), B.Tech (Agricultural Engineering), B.Tech/B.E., B.B.A., B.C.A., and other equivalent courses offered by Government Institutions and Private Institutions having an AISHE code (All India Survey on Higher Education) of the State are covered under the Krishi Vidya Nidhi Yojana. Professional or Technical Postgraduate courses such as M.Tech, M.Sc. (Agriculture), M.Sc. (Forestry), Postgraduate courses in Medical Science, M.B.A., M.C.A., M.Pharm, and other equivalent courses forming part of a Master’s programme are also included. The maximum duration of scholarship support shall be 2 years for Postgraduate courses and 4 years for Ph.D. courses. courses must be related to the eligible postgraduate courses and must be pursued only in Government Institutions located within the State. Diploma courses such as Diploma in Pharmacy, Diploma in Medical Laboratory Technology, Diploma in Medical Radiography Technology, Ophthalmic Assistance or Surgical Ophthalmic Assistance, General Nursing and Midwifery, Auxiliary Nurse Midwifery, Psychiatric Nursing, and other equivalent medical courses recommended by the Directorate of Medical Education and Training, as well as courses offered by Polytechnic and Agricultural Polytechnic Institutions, are also included under the Krishi Vidya Nidhi Yojana.. The applicant admitted to self-financing courses in Government or Private Institutions shall be eligible for the scholarship only as per the capped fee structure.. The applicant should not be in receipt of any other scholarship. If the applicant is already availing another scholarship, he or she must shift from the existing scholarship scheme to the Krishi Vidya Nidhi Yojana, if they so choose. Only one scholarship can be availed.. The applicant should apply for only one professional course under this scheme.. The applicant should not avail more than one scholarship for similar courses.. The applicant should not be admitted to a Private Institution located outside the State..
documents: Aadhaar Card Residence Certificate Caste Certificate (if required) Passport
sized photograph Ration Card of the Parent/ guardian CM
KISAN Beneficiary ID of parent/guardian Bank Account Details Institute Declaration Certificate Matriculation Certificate of the Student Marksheet of the last exam passed
Ration Card of the Parent/ guardian
Marksheet of the last exam passed

faqs.question: What is the objective of the scheme?
faqs.answer: The objective of the Krishi Vidya Nidhi Yojana is to extend financial assistance to the children of beneficiaries under the CM-KISAN scheme for pursuing professional and technical courses, thereby improving access to higher education for children of Small and Marginal Farmers and Landless Agricultural Households and supporting the economic and social empowerment of farming families.

faqs.question: Who can apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Children of eligible beneficiaries under the CM-KISAN scheme, including Support to Farmers for Cultivation and Livelihood Support to Landless Agricultural Households, who are residents of Odisha and meet the prescribed eligibility criteria, can apply.

faqs.question: Is the scholarship provided on a merit basis?
faqs.answer: Yes, the scholarship under the Krishi Vidya Nidhi Yojana is awarded purely on a merit basis to students admitted to eligible courses and institutions.

faqs.question: Which courses are covered under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme covers professional and technical undergraduate courses, postgraduate courses, PhD programmes, and diploma courses in fields such as medical, engineering, agriculture, nursing, veterinary science, pharmacy, management, computer applications, polytechnic, and Industrial Training Institute trades, as specified in the scheme guidelines.

faqs.question: Are students studying outside Odisha eligible for the scholarship?
faqs.answer: Students admitted to Premier Government Institutions located both inside and outside the State are eligible. However, students admitted to Private Institutions located outside the State are not eligible.

faqs.question: Can a student avail more than one scholarship under this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, a student can avail only one scholarship. Students receiving any other scholarship must shift to the Krishi Vidya Nidhi Yojana if they wish to avail benefits under this scheme.

faqs.question: What financial support is provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scholarship includes reimbursement of admissible tuition and other non-refundable fees, along with fixed monthly assistance for mess and hostel charges, subject to prescribed limits and conditions.

faqs.question: What is the mess and hostel assistance provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides ₹1,200/- per month for 10 months to Undergraduate, Postgraduate, Ph.D., and Premier Government Institution students, and ₹1,000/- per month for 10 months to Diploma, Polytechnic, and Industrial Training Institute students, towards mess and hostel expenses.

faqs.question: How can students apply for the Krishi Vidya Nidhi Yojana?
faqs.answer: Eligible students must apply online through the State Scholarship Portal of Odisha. Physical applications are not accepted, and only verified online applications are considered for scholarship sanction.

faqs.question: How is the scholarship amount disbursed?
faqs.answer: The scholarship amount is disbursed directly to the student’s bank account through the Direct Benefit Transfer mode after successful verification and approval by the competent authorities.

name: Krishonnati Yojana - Sub Mission On Seed And Planting Material (SMSP)
description: The scheme "Sub Mission on Seed and Planting Material (SMSP)" is a centrally sponsored scheme under the umbrella scheme of "Green Revolution – Krishonnati Yojana". "Green Revolution – Krishonnati Yojana" is an Umbrella Scheme for the agriculture sector that has been implemented since 2016-17 by clubbing several schemes/missions under one umbrella scheme. The Umbrella scheme comprises 11 Schemes/Missions. These schemes look to develop the agriculture and allied sector holistically and scientifically to increase the income of farmers by enhancing production, productivity, and better returns on produce. The Sub-Mission on Seeds and Planting Material (SMSP) aims to increase the production of certified / quality seed, increase SRR, upgrade the quality of farm-saved seeds, strengthen the seed multiplication chain, promote new technologies and methodologies in seed production, processing, testing, etc., to strengthen and modernizing infrastructure for seed production, storage, certification, and quality, etc. Objectives of SMSP - Increasing production of certified/ quality seed Increasing Seed Replacement rate (SRR) more particularly to achieve higher SRR in crops like paddy, gram, groundnut, cotton, etc. as recommended by the Consultative Group of the Ministry of Agriculture Upgrading the quality of farm-saved seeds with a specific objective to cover 60,000 villages and produce 100 lakh quintals of seed each year through farmers' participatory seed production. Creation of Seed Infrastructure facilities in the Public Sector. Encouraging seed treatment, particularly for farm-saved seed. Strengthening the seed multiplication chain through assistance to the public and private sectors. Popularizing new varieties to encourage varietal replacement. Promoting new technologies and methodologies in seed production, processing, testing, etc. Strengthening and modernizing infrastructure for seed production, storage, certification, and quality control particularly to ensure compliance with the provisions of the Seeds Bill 2004/ISTA standards, and OECD certification. Facilitating the movement of seed from India in international trade and increasing its share to 10% by 2020 as envisaged in the new policy on seed development. Assisting and supporting public and private seed-producing organizations in the seed sector and encouraging partnerships. Ensuring availability of seed in contingent situations. Facilitating the dissemination of seed-related information through information, education, and communication. To provide an effective system for the protection of plant varieties, the rights of farmers as well as plant breeders and to encourage the development of new varieties of plants, through PPVFRA. Components of SMSP - Strengthening for Seed Quality Control Strengthening of Grow Out Test(GOT) facilities Support to seed certification agencies Seed Village Programme Certified seed production through seed villages Seed Processing Facilities Seed Storage Facilities Transport subsidy on the movement of Seed to North Eastern States etc. National Seed Reserve Application of Biotechnology in agriculture Public Private Partnership in the seed sector Assistance for boosting seed production in the Private Sector Support to Sub-Mission Director and Survey / Studies Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmer’s Rights Authority (PPVFRA)
benefits: Intervention: Strengthening for Seed Quality Control Pattern of Funding: 100% GOI share, except a new sub-component with 75:25 Centre:State share Rate of Assistance: (i) Seed Testing Laboratories Equipment for Seed Testing Laboratories: Assistance for Rs.60 lakh per laboratory will be available for laboratory equipment. Details of equipment and estimated cost for handling approximately 10,000 samples per year in a laboratory is given in Annexure–II. Renovation of Seed Testing Laboratory: Rs. 20.00 lakh available for renovation of a seed testing laboratory with the capacity of 10,000 seed samples with area of 250 Sqm. Equipment for DNA Finger Printing / Varietal Purity - Testing Laboratory: Assistance for Rs.70 lakh will be available for the DNA fingerprinting facility at one notified seed testing laboratory. Specialized seed health testing units: Assistance for Rs. 55.00 lakh will be available to establish/strengthen one specialized seed health testing laboratory. Payment of ISTA fee: Financial assistance of Rs.15 lakh will be available to the maximum 5 Seed Testing Laboratories functioning under NSRTC, State Government/Union Territories, Seeds Corporations, and Seed Certification Agencies to obtain/run the membership of the International Seed Testing Association (ISTA). (ii) Strengthening of Seed Law Enforcement: Assistance for reimbursement of seed sample cost @ Rs. 10.00 lakh is available. (75% centre : 25 % State) (iii) Support to the National Seed Research and Training Center: Financial assistance of Rs. 12.00 crore will be provided to NSRTC for salary wages, maintenance of facilities and other routine activities, and administrative expenditures for 3 years. Development of Centralized Seed Certification Portal at NSRTC: Financial Assistance will be provided for the development of software and hardware @Rs. 20.00 lakh per State Seed Certification Agency Centralized Seed Certification Portal at NSRTC for giving linkage to the 25 SSC. (iv) Training and workshop: Financial assistance of Rs.2.00 lakh will be available for training on seed-related activities viz. training of 25 persons for 5 days training course. (v) Strengthening of Central Seed Committee and Central Seed Certification Board: Financial assistance of Rs..10.00 lakh per year is available for TA / DA for non-official members of CSC & CSCB and its sub-committees. Intervention: Strengthening of Grow Out Test (GOT) Facilities Pattern of Funding: 100% GOI Rate of Assistance: (i) Grow-out Test Farm: Financial assistance of Rs.50.00 lakhs for strengthening of 5 hectares of GOT farm. (ii) Green House facility: An assistance of Rs.10 lakh will be available for the establishment of a Green House facility for eligible organizations. Intervention: Support to Seed Certification Agencies Pattern of Funding: 25% GOI : 75% State Rate of Assistance: (i) Salary for the Staff: Rs.50.00 lakh, per agency, per year. will be available for staff who are involved in seed management; field inspection; sampling; analysis; monitoring; evaluation, certification, and pre and post-harvesting supervision, etc. (ii) Travelling allowance: 25% of the total cost of traveling allowance is subject to a maximum limit of Rs. 10.00 lakh per agency to conduct of inspection, analysis and certification activities, the mobility of staff through jeep and motorcycle is proposed based on one for every 800 hectares and 400 hectares respectively. faqs.question: What is the pattern of funding for seed storage facilities, and what costs are covered?
faqs.answer: Seed storage facilities receive 100% GOI funding, including the cost of construction, electrification, compound walls, and handling equipment.

faqs.question: What is the pattern of funding for support to R&D and contract research under SMSP?
faqs.answer: It involves 60% funding from the GOI and 40% from the state for eligible projects.

faqs.question: What assistance is available for seed treatment under SMSP, and what's the pattern of funding?
faqs.answer: Financial assistance of up to 75% is provided for seed treatment, with a 25% state share and 75% from the GOI.

faqs.question: Can you explain the components of SMSP related to seed quality control?
faqs.answer: These components involve strengthening seed quality control, grow-out test facilities, support for seed certification agencies, and more.

faqs.question: What is the role of SMSP in facilitating the international trade of seeds?
faqs.answer: SMSP aims to increase India's share in international seed trade to 10% by 2020, as per the new seed development policy.

faqs.question: Can you explain the benefits of the National Seed Reserve under SMSP?
faqs.answer: The National Seed Reserve involves financial assistance for seed procurement, maintenance costs, and storage infrastructure, ensuring seed availability in times of need.

faqs.question: What is the financial assistance for the application of biotechnology in agriculture under SMSP?
faqs.answer: SMSP provides financial assistance of up to Rs. 2.50 crores for the establishment of new Tissue Culture Units and up to Rs. 20 lakhs for the rehabilitation of old tissue culture labs.

faqs.question: What assistance is provided for boosting seed production in the private sector under SMSP?
faqs.answer: The private sector can access credit-linked back-ended subsidies, which can be up to 40% of the capital cost in general areas and 50% in hilly and scheduled areas.

faqs.question: What is the role of PPV&FRA under SMSP, and how is it funded?
faqs.answer: PPV&FRA undertakes activities mandated under the PPVFR Act and is fully funded by the GOI.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to benefit from the Krishonnati Yojana - Sub Mission On Seed And Planting Material (SMSP)?
faqs.answer: Small and marginal farmers are eligible to participate in the SMSP.

faqs.answer: Farmers can apply offline by submitting copies of required documents to the District Agriculture Officer or Agriculture Development Officer.

faqs.question: What documents are needed for farmers to apply for SMSP benefits?
faqs.answer: Required documents include copies of the farmer's B1 khasra/loan book, Aadhaar number, and a copy of the bank passbook.

faqs.question: Are there any income or production-related eligibility criteria for farmers to access SMSP benefits?
faqs.answer: The primary eligibility criteria are based on landholding size, not income or production levels.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Applicants must be residents of Uttarakhand, interested livestock farmers, and eligible for a bank loan under the respective livestock development schemes.

faqs.question: How much loan interest subsidy is provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Under this scheme, the State Government bears 90% of the interest on the bank loan taken by the beneficiary for setting up approved livestock units.

faqs.question: What is the role of the District Level Implementation Unit (DLIA)?
faqs.answer: The DLIA receives and scrutinizes applications, prepares a list of eligible applicants, forwards them for approval, and coordinates with banks and the treasury for payment of interest subsidy.

faqs.question: What happens after the application is submitted?
faqs.answer: The DLIA scrutinizes all received applications, prepares a list of eligible beneficiaries, and grants final approval after verifying the documents and bank loan consent.

faqs.question: How is the interest subsidy disbursed?
faqs.answer: The bank provides quarterly information to the DLIA on the amount of interest subsidy due. The DLIA then prepares a bill and submits it to the treasury for payment to the concerned bank.

name: Livelihood Support To Marine Fishermen During Fishing Ban Period
department: Fisheries and Animal Resources Development Department
description: Livelihood Support to Marine Fishermen during the Fishing Ban Period Scheme under the Department of Fisheries & Animal Resources Development, Government of Odisha aims to support the livelihood of marine fisher families. This scheme is under the state sector Umbrella Scheme Mukhyamantri Maschyajibi Kalyan Yojana (MMKY) . The scheme supports the livelihood of marine fisher families in and around the turtle nesting and breeding areas of the state including round the year fishing ban in Bhitarkanika areas as no alternative is available. As the livelihood earning of fishermen is solely based on sea fishing and the ban on fishing directly prohibits the profession over a long period of seven months in a year (1st November to 31st May) (both days inclusive) along with a Uniform ban from 15th April to 14th June (61 days). Area of Operation: The Scheme shall be implemented in the Marine Districts of Kendrapara, Jagatsinghpur, Puri, and Ganjam along the Coastline of Odisha where the marine Fishers who are affected due to the ban on fishing round the year at Gahirmatha Marine Sanctuary, Bhitarkanika National park and adjoining areas of Devi River and Rushikulya River Mouth for Sea Turtle Conservation.
benefits: Only one member of the affected families shall be assisted with ₹15,000/- annually under the scheme. The amount shall be paid to the beneficiaries between November and March of a financial year in one Installment. The assistance amount shall be released to the beneficiaries through Direct Benefit Transfer.
eligibility: The following are the eligibility criteria for the beneficiary:. The beneficiary must be an active Marine fisherman.. The assistance will be provided to only one member of a family on behalf of the family.. The beneficiary must be in the age group of 18-70 years.. The beneficiary must be a permanent resident of Odisha and must possess identity and residential proof including an Aadhaar card.. The beneficiary must have a bank account in his/her name in the state of Odisha.. The beneficiary must be a boat owner (Motorized Boat)/ a crew member of a Motorized Boat / Fish trader/ engaged in sorting, and grading Fish, and other ancillary activities.. The Fishers should preferably belong to the BPL Category i.e. covered under the National Food Security Act (NFSA) and not belong to the automatically excluded household under the socio-economic and caste census (SECC)-2011.. If the fisherman is a Boat Owner, he must have valid registration (Real Craft) and a valid fishing license.. If the fisherman is a crew member, he must work in a registered fishing boat with a valid date fishing license and will produce a certificate from the boat owner in this respect.. If the fisherman is a Fish trader / engaged in sorting, grading of Fish, and other ancillary activities he must produce a certificate from a registered boat owner in this respect.. Note:. Preference of selection of beneficiaries shall be undertaken in the order of:. Boat Owner.. Crew member of a fishing boat.. workers engaged in sorting, grading, and other ancillary activities..
documents: Photocopy of Aadhaar Card Photocopy of Voter I Card. Photocopy of Ration Card. Photocopy of the Registration Certificate of the Boat. Photocopy of the Fishing License Certificate. Certificate of Boat Owner, while working as a Crew Member/other activities. Photocopy of 1st page of Bank Passbook.

Photocopy of the Fishing License Certificate.
Certificate of Boat Owner, while working as a Crew Member/other activities.
Photocopy of 1st page of Bank Passbook.

name: Madilu Kit
department: Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department
description: The Madilu Programme is a comprehensive initiative implemented by the government to uplift rural communities by providing them with the necessary skills and resources to improve their livelihoods. The program primarily focuses on skill development, entrepreneurship, and capacity building. By equipping individuals with relevant skills, such as agricultural techniques, handicraft production, and small business management, the Madilu Programme aims to create sustainable income-generating opportunities within rural areas. Through targeted training sessions, workshops, and mentorship programs, participants are empowered to harness their potential and establish small-scale enterprises. The Madilu Programme also facilitates access to micro-financing options and provides guidance on market linkages, enabling participants to establish viable businesses and gain financial independence. Additionally, the program emphasizes the importance of gender equality and social inclusion, ensuring that marginalized groups have equal access to opportunities and benefits.
benefits: Empowerment of rural communities through skill development and entrepreneurship. Creation of sustainable livelihoods and reduction of poverty. Enhancement of social and economic well-being in rural areas. Increased income-generating opportunities for participants. Access to micro-financing options and market linkages. Promotion of gender equality and social inclusion. Strengthening of rural economies and local industries.
eligibility: Individuals residing in rural areas are eligible to participate.. Participants should have a willingness to learn and engage in skill development activities.. faqs.question: Who can apply for the Madilu Programme?
faqs.answer: Individuals residing in rural areas who are interested in skill development and entrepreneurship can apply for the Madilu Programme.

faqs.answer: While the Madilu Programme does not provide direct financial grants or subsidies, it facilitates access to micro-financing options for eligible participants.

faqs.answer: The program duration may vary depending on the specific training modules and entrepreneurial support provided. It typically ranges from several weeks to a few months.

faqs.question: Are there any fees or charges associated with the program?
faqs.answer: The Madilu Programme is generally free of charge for selected participants. However, participants may be responsible for their own travel expenses, accommodation, or materials required for certain activities.

faqs.answer: The Madilu Programme is implemented nationwide; however, program availability and specific modules may vary depending on the region and local initiatives.

faqs.answer: Yes, one of the main objectives of the Madilu Programme is to empower participants to establish their own businesses and become self-reliant.

name: Meghalaya Agriculture Response Vehicle Scheme
description: The scheme “Meghalaya Agriculture Response Vehicle Scheme” was launched by the Department of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, Government of Meghalaya, . It aims to employ, engage, and empower the youth and rural communities by promoting entrepreneurship in agriculture logistics, addressing critical gaps in farm-to-market connectivity. The scheme provides easy access to credit through onboarding of multiple partner banks, coupled with substantialgovernment support in the form of upfront capital subsidy and EMI co-payment. By enabling entrepreneurs to procure small commercial vehicles, pickups, trucks, and refrigerated carriers, it seeks to improve transportation efficiency, reduce post-harvest losses, and enhance market access for farmers, especially in remote areas. Implemented by the Department of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, the scheme integrates with 1917iTeams for generating transport demand, GPS-enabled tracking, and providing training and capacity building—ensuring beneficiaries can operate profitably while strengthening the agricultural value chain in Meghalaya. > Objectives of the scheme Economic growth of the state: With 77% of the population involved with agriculture and allied sectors in rural areas, the PRIME ARVS is envisaged to accelerate and sustain economic development of the state through entrepreneurship development, job creation in the rural community. Encourage entrepreneurship among rural youth: The scheme is intended to encourage entrepreneurship among the rural youth by providing them easy credit access and financial grant to buy commercial vehicles. These vehicles can be used by the entrepreneurs to earn their income by providing transportation solution to local farmers, traders, and buyers. Logistics solution to farm produce: To provide a transportation solution to evacuate farms produce to intended destinations such as markets, processing facilities or aggregation centres. Similarly, the vehicles can also transport various farming inputs from the market for timely and successful agricultural operations. Lower transportation cost: Introducing more numbers of commercial goods carriers will potentially help reduce logistics cost for the marginal farmers by fostering competition among the logistics providers. Various farmers groups who will be benefitted with the vehicles under the scheme will significantly reduce the transportation cost of their own grown/ aggregated farm products. Market accessibility to farmers from remote area: The majority of the vehicles are intended for entrepreneurs residing in remote areas so that farmers living in their proximity from nearby villages and clusters can be benefitted. The farmers residing in these areas can quickly avail their transportation services to sell their farm produce and buy back their essentials from the markets. Increase farmer’s profitability: Timely evacuation of farm produce will have a significant impact on farmer’s profitability by minimizing spoilage of perishable products; reducing additional storage costs such as refrigeration, storage facilities; increasing market accessibility; maintaining cash flow through quicker sales and lastly by enhancing customer satisfaction by building trust and long-term relationship with the buyers. Financial grant and easy credit to the entrepreneurs to buy goods carriers Prime Agriculture Response Vehicles (Prime-ARVs) to be distributed across Meghalaya with 50% financial aid on the total cost of the vehicle including the interest charged by the bank to finance the vehicle. Demand creation through 1917iTeams Vehicles will be registered with 1917iTeams who will provide transportation demand calls from customers to the vehicle owners. Vehicles will be pre-fitted with GPS device ensuring trackability of the vehicle by 1917iTeams. The live location of the vehicle will help in immediately connecting the farmers/ aggregators/ buyers to their nearest available vehicle.
benefits: 50% of project cost supported (5% by applicant, 45% by Government of Meghalaya) 5% EMI co-payment support for 12 months Credit linkage through partnered banks (MRB, MCAB, SBI, SCUB) Additional 3% annual interest subvention on reefer trucks with Aadhaar linkage Pre-fitted GPS device with 5-year warranty Branding cost of vehicle borne by the Government Capacity building and training programs by Department,1917iTeams Market linkage through 1917iTeams with live vehicle tracking Eligibility for various vehicle types, including reefer trucks for perishable goods transportation
eligibility: Individuals. The applicant must be between 18 and 58 years of age.. The applicant must have a valid commercial driving license.. The applicant must be a permanent resident of Meghalaya.. The applicant must be involved in the agriculture sector for at least two years.. A certification letter from the Block Development Officer (BDO) is required as proof of agricultural involvement.. The applicant should not be a loan defaulter with any bank.. Registered Entities. The applicant must be a registered entity such as a Cooperative, Farmer Producer Company (FPC), or Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO) under the Government of Meghalaya.. The entity must be engaged in the agriculture sector for at least two years.. A certification letter from the Block Development Officer (BDO) must be provided as proof of agricultural involvement.. The entity should not have availed benefits under the first phase of the PRIME Agriculture Response Vehicle Scheme.. The applicant must submit an Incorporation Certificate or Registration Certificate, as applicable.. At least two members of the entity must have a training certificate in the relevant sector from a recognized institution (preferably a government institute).. faqs.question: Who are the beneficiaries under this scheme?

description: The Meghalaya Agriculture Warehouse Scheme, under the Chief Minister’s CM-ELEVATE Program by the Planning, Investment Promotion & Sustainable Development Department, Government of Meghalaya, focuses on enhancing agricultural infrastructure through the establishment of warehouses across the state. It aims to reduce post-harvest losses, stabilize market prices, and improve farmer incomes. The scheme offers easy credit access via partner banks and substantial government subsidies to ease entrepreneurs’ financial burden. Implemented by the Meghalaya Basin Management Agency (MBMA), it supports individuals and registered entities in creating weatherproof storage for agricultural produce, enabling value addition, market linkages, and long-term storage for the farming community.
benefits: 5% of project cost to be contributed by the entrepreneur 75% of project cost provided upfront by Government of Meghalaya as margin money support to the bank remaining 20% via bank loan. Direct credit linkage with partner banks. Guidance and handholding in the application process through implementing agencies. Support in project realization for the warehouse venture. Training and capacity building for entrepreneurs to manage post-harvest storage effectively. Technical support for maintenance and operations of warehouses.
eligibility: For Individuals:. The applicant should be between 18 and 58 years of age.. The applicant should be a permanent resident of Meghalaya.. The applicant should have ownership of the land where the warehouse is proposed or leased land for at least the next 10 years.. The applicant should not be a credit defaulter of any bank.. For Registered Entities:. The applicant should be based in the village where the program is being availed.. The applicant should have an active bank account and submit the bank statement of the last six months.. The applicant should have been in operation for at least two years.. The applicant should possess land, either self-owned or leased, duly verified by the competent authority..

faqs.question: What is the Meghalaya Agriculture Warehouse Scheme?
faqs.answer: It is a scheme to reduce post-harvest losses, stabilize market prices, and increase farmers’ incomes by supporting warehouse creation.

faqs.question: Who implements the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme is implemented by the Meghalaya Basin Management Agency (MBMA).

faqs.question: Who can benefit from the scheme?
faqs.answer: Both individual farmers and registered entities or groups engaged in agriculture can apply.

faqs.question: How is the project cost shared?
faqs.answer: Entrepreneurs contribute 5%, the government provides 75% upfront, and 20% is via bank loan.

faqs.question: Are government subsidies available?
faqs.answer: Yes, substantial subsidies are provided to reduce the financial burden on entrepreneurs.

faqs.question: Is guidance provided for bank loan applications?
faqs.answer: Yes, implementing agencies provide handholding and guidance throughout the application process.

faqs.question: Does the scheme provide technical support?
faqs.answer: Yes, technical assistance is provided for warehouse maintenance and operations.

faqs.question: What is the age criteria for individuals?
faqs.answer: The applicants must be 18–58 years old.

faqs.question: Do I need land to apply?
faqs.answer: Yes, applicants must own the land or have leased it for at least 10 years.

faqs.question: Where should the entity be located?
faqs.answer: The entity should be based in the village where the scheme is being availed.

faqs.question: Are government employees eligible?
faqs.answer: No, state or central government employees, or pensioners, are generally excluded.

faqs.question: Can public sector employees apply?
faqs.answer: No, employees of public sector undertakings or subsidiaries are excluded.

name: Mukhyamantri Bhed/Bakri (Sheep/Goat) Palak Uthan Yojana for Scheduled Castes
description: The "Mukhya Mantri Bhed/Bakri (Sheep/Goat) Palak Uthan Yojana for Scheduled Castes" scheme is introduced by the Animal Husbandry and Dairying Department, Government of Haryana, which aims to uplift Scheduled Caste beneficiaries by providing them with sheep or goat units. Through this scheme, 10 female and 1 male sheep/goat units are provided free of cost. Through this scheme, free sheep or goat units, veterinary assistance, and assistance for purchasing wool are provided to unemployed residents of Haryana. The scheme is implemented by the Haryana Livestock Development Board (HLDB). > Long-term objectives of this scheme are as follows: To create self-employment opportunities through Sheep and Goat husbandry activities. To upgrade and develop the Sheep and Goat breeds/germ plasm available in the State. To increase income generation opportunities for the economically weaker segment of society.
benefits: Sheep Unit: 20 Ewes and one Ram with Green Fodder cum Salt Block Feeder free of cost. 1. Goat Unit: 20 Does and one Buck with Green Fodder cum Salt Block Feeder free of cost.1. Veterinary Assistance: All animals in the established unit will receive deworming, vaccination, and treatment free of cost by the concerned Veterinary Institution.1. Wool Purchase Assistance: Assistance for purchasing wool from the established unit will be provided by the department. > Financial Assistance in form of subsidy for establishment of Sheep/Goat unit > under the Scheme:- 100% subsidy for the establishment of a Sheep and Goat unit of 10 females and 1 male would be provided to the Scheduled Caste (SC). Initially beneficiary has to bear purchase cost of Sheep and Goat unit by there-own for 25% of the unit cost which will be of ₹17,500/- per unit as margin money (proof for the same should be given by beneficiary), which would be provided to beneficiary account later on as per scheme guidelines. In the case of SC Category, the Haryana Livestock Development Board (HLDB)/Government will provide financial assistance of 75% of the unit cost (₹52,500/- per unit) on the establishment of the livestock unit after the purchase of livestock to the seller within 15 days, upon submission of all requisite documents. The financial assistance of balance 25% of unit cost (₹17,500/- per unit) in case of SC beneficiaries would be provided by the HLDB/Government in form of subsidy to beneficiary after two months of establishment of unit subject to verification of unit after purchase of all cases preferably by Deputy Director concerned himself or its representative not below the rank of Sub Divisional Officer/Semen Bank Officer other than purchase committee. Beneficiaries shall have to purchase a complete/whole Sheep/Goat unit of 10+1 in one slot, and only one beneficiary per household could take the benefit of either Sheep or Goat unit under the scheme. The financial assistance would be provided to the account of the seller through Concerned Semen Bank officer by the Managing Director, HLDB, out of the head of overall receipt of Milk Cess funds after verification and recommendation of the unit established by the Deputy Director concerned or its representative not below the rank of SDO/ SBO. The financial assistance may be delayed due to the unavailability of the budget or any other unforeseen circumstances. The beneficiary would be provided veterinary assistance facilities (Treatment, vaccination and consultancy) by the concerned area veterinary institutions free of cost. Assistance for the purchase of wool from an established unit would be provided by the Department.
eligibility: The applicant should be a Scheduled Caste. The applicant should be of 18 to 55 years of age.. The applicant should be a resident of Haryana. The applicant should be a Parivar Pehchaan Patra (PPP).. The applicant should not be employed even in the Private Sector/ Govt. /Semi Govt. Organizations.. There would be no mandatory educational qualifications or training requirements.. Any group/firm/organisation would not be permitted to apply under the Scheme, as the Scheme being individual beneficiary-oriented.. The applicant would have to submit a Self-Declaration in the format annexed as Annexure-I (Page-9) (https://pashudhanharyana.gov.in/sites/default/files/documents/Scheme%202024-25/BhedBakri%20(SheepGoat)%20Palak%20Utthan%20Yojanafor%20the%20year%202024-25%20(N).pdf) on the portal for being unemployed and for undertaking to abide by other conditions as required under the Scheme.

Declaration Certificate by the applicant. Affidavit regarding return of one male and ten female animals after passing one and half year time from the date of purchase. PAN Card (Mandatory). Postdated Cheque of ₹ 70,000/
duly signed by the person. (Mandatory). Availability of space for the construction of shed (Proof required).

faqs.question: What is the Mukhya Mantri Bhed/Bakri Palak Uthan Yojna scheme about?
faqs.answer: Under this scheme, the Government provides 20 Does and one Buck (Goat unit) with Green Fodder cum Salt Block Feeder or 20 Ewes and one Ram (Sheep Unit) with Green Fodder cum Salt Block Feeder free of cost to the beneficiary.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for the Mukhya Mantri Bhed/Bakri Palak Uthan Yojna?
faqs.answer: Scheduled Caste beneficiaries between 18 and 55 years of age who are residents of Haryana and unemployed are eligible.

faqs.question: Are there any educational qualifications or training requirements to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, there are no mandatory educational qualifications or training requirements for this scheme.

faqs.question: Can a group, firm, or organization apply for the Mukhya Mantri Bhed/Bakri Palak Uthan Yojna?
faqs.answer: No, the scheme is individual beneficiary oriented, so groups, firms, or organizations are not permitted to apply.

faqs.question: What kind of declaration does an applicant need to submit on the portal?
faqs.answer: The applicant needs to submit a Self-Declaration on the portal stating they are unemployed and undertaking to abide by other scheme conditions.

faqs.question: What benefits are provided to beneficiaries under the Mukhya Mantri Bhed/Bakri Palak Uthan Yojna?
faqs.answer: Beneficiaries receive 20 Does and one Buck (Goat unit) or 20 Ewes and one Ram (Sheep Unit) along with a Green Fodder cum Salt Block Feeder, free of cost.

faqs.question: Is there any provision for returning animals after a certain period?
faqs.answer: Yes, after one year, when the beneficiary's flock size reaches 40-50 animals, 10 female and 1 male animal (Half Unit) will be retrieved from them.

faqs.question: What documents are mandatory for applying to the Mukhya Mantri Bhed/Bakri Palak Uthan Yojna?
faqs.answer: A Scheduled Caste Certificate, Aadhar Card, and PAN Card are mandatory documents.

faqs.question: Is there any affidavit required regarding the return of animals?
faqs.answer: Yes, an affidavit regarding the return of one male and ten female animals after one and a half years from the date of purchase is required.

faqs.question: What is the requirement for the Postdated Cheque?
faqs.answer: A Postdated Cheque of Rs. 70,000/-, duly signed by the person, is mandatory.

faqs.question: Are there any charges other than government, Kendra, and Atal Seva Kendra service charges?
faqs.answer: Based on the provided information, no other charges are mentioned apart from the government charges (No Fee), Kendra Service Charges (₹ 10/-), and Atal Seva Kendra (CSC) Service Charges (₹ 30/-).

faqs.question: What is the “Kela Vikash Yojana”?
faqs.answer: The "Kela Vikash Yojana" is a scheme under the "Mukhyamantri Bagwani Yojana" launched by the Department of Agriculture, Bihar, to promote plantain cultivation across 15 districts in the state.

faqs.question: What are the eligible districts for the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme is available to applicants from Arwal, Bhojpur, Buxar, Gopalganj, Jehanabad, Kaimur, Lakhisarai, Madhepura, Nawada, Saran, Shivhar, Sitamarhi, Siwan, Supaul, and Sheikhpura.

faqs.question: What is the minimum and maximum land requirement for applying?
faqs.answer: Applicants must have at least 0.25 acres (0.1 hectares) and can apply for up to a maximum of 10 acres (4 hectares) of agricultural land.

faqs.question: What financial assistance is provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Beneficiaries receive [?]46,875/- per hectare in the first year and [?]15,625/- per hectare in the second year as financial assistance.

faqs.question: What kind of plant material is distributed under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Beneficiaries receive high-quality tissue-cultured plants for cultivation.

faqs.question: How is inclusivity ensured in the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme includes reserved quotas for Scheduled Castes (20%), Scheduled Tribes (1.44%), and women beneficiaries (30%).

faqs.question: Are both ryot and non-ryot farmers eligible to apply?
faqs.answer: Yes, ryot farmers can apply using land documents, while non-ryot farmers can apply using a contract form.

faqs.question: What is the registration process for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Applicants must register on the DBT portal, and after 48 hours of registration, they can apply online using their 13-digit registration number.

faqs.question: What documents are required for application?
faqs.answer: Applicants need land-ownership/revenue receipts, and if the name on the document is unclear, a genealogy document must be attached.

faqs.question: How are payments disbursed under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Financial assistance is disbursed directly to beneficiaries through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system.

faqs.question: What happens if the name on the land document is unclear?
faqs.answer: If the name on the land-ownership or revenue receipt is unclear, the applicant must provide a genealogy document along with the receipt.

faqs.question: Can women beneficiaries apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, women beneficiaries are encouraged to apply, with 30% of the scheme's allocation reserved for their participation.

name: Mukhyamantri Dairy Animal Distribution Programme (Special Backward Tribes Baiga, Bharia & Sahariya)
description: The "Mukhyamantri Dairy Animal Distribution Programme (Special Backward Tribes Baiga, Bharia & Sahariya)" scheme is launched by the Animal Husbandry Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh. The scheme aims to improve the economic status, nutrition, and income of special backward tribal communities by promoting livestock rearing. The beneficiaries from the Baiga, Bharia, and Sahariya tribes receive two high-yielding dairy cows or Murrah buffaloes at a 90% subsidy, with 10% contribution by the beneficiary. > Selected Districts: The scheme targets specific districts including Dindori, Umaria, Shahdol, Anuppur, Mandla, Balaghat, Chhindwara, Gwalior, Datia, Shivpuri, Guna, Ashoknagar, Sheopurkala, Morena, and Bhind.
benefits: Provision of 2 Dairy Animals (cow or Murrah buffalo) per beneficiary at 90% subsidy. Animals sourced from certified breeding tracts, progressive farmers, or NABARD-approved markets, ensuring quality and health. Minimum milk yield requirement: cows – 7 liters/day; buffaloes – 8 liters/day. Animal age limit: calves must be under 2 months. Disease-free, healthy animals with mandatory tagging. Training and guidance on dairy management provided before distribution. Milk route establishment and cluster development support provided.
eligibility: The applicant must be a resident of Madhya Pradesh.. The applicant must belong to special backward tribes: Baiga, Bharia, or Sahariya.. The applicant must be a livestock farmer residing in the designated districts.. The applicant’s selected animals must comply with minimum milk yield and age requirements.. The applicant must participate in pre-distribution training and follow cluster/milk route arrangements..
documents: Identity Proof Residence Proof Caste Certificate Bank Account Details Land or Livestock Ownership Proof

faqs.answer: Only Baiga, Bharia, and Sahariya tribal livestock farmers.

name: Mahila Dairy Vikas Pariyojana - Uttarakhand
description: The scheme “Mahila Dairy Vikas Pariyojana” was launched by the Department of Dairy Development, Government of Uttarakhand. It aims to empower rural women in Uttarakhand by promoting their active participation in the dairy sector through Women Milk Producers Cooperative Societies, enhancing milk production, and providing training, incentives, and awareness programs for sustainable livelihood development.
benefits: Under this scheme, by providing adequate resources to rural women through Women Milk Producers Cooperative Societies at the village level, their direct participation in the state’s economy is encouraged, making them socially and economically self-reliant. The scheme also organizes various training, incentive, and awareness programs for women members to increase milk production. These include training programs for secretaries and management committee members, women encouragement and motivational programs, seminars on clean milk procurement, and special women-focused seminars on the occasion of International Women’s Day. Under the women incentive program to increase milk procurement, first, second, and third prizes are awarded to the women milk producers who supply the maximum milk in the district.
eligibility: The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.. The applicant must be a woman interested in the milk procurement business sector..
documents: Documents are required as per the department’s guidelines prescribed for this scheme.

faqs.question: Who can participate in this scheme?
faqs.answer: All women at the district level in Uttarakhand who are interested in the milk procurement and dairy business sector can participate.

faqs.question: How are Women Milk Producers Cooperative Societies formed?
faqs.answer: After sharing complete information in an open meeting, a Women’s Milk Committee is formed by consensus. From this committee, nine women are selected as Managing Committee members, and a Chairperson is elected from among them.

faqs.question: Who manages the operations of the Milk Committee?
faqs.answer: The Managing Committee appoints a Secretary as an employee to run the Milk Committee’s daily operations.

faqs.question: Are all milk-producing women required to join the Committee?
faqs.answer: Yes, all women who supply milk to the Milk Committee are required to become members of the Committee.

faqs.question: What kind of training is provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides various training programs including Secretary training, management committee training, clean milk procurement seminars, and women empowerment seminars.

faqs.question: How are the Managing Committee members selected?
faqs.answer: Nine women are selected from the Women’s Milk Committee members through consensus during the open meeting process.

faqs.question: How are incentives determined for women milk producers?
faqs.answer: Incentives are given based on the quantity of milk supplied, with the top three producers in each district receiving prizes to motivate increased participation.

faqs.question: What is the Meghalaya Dairy Development Scheme?
faqs.answer: It is a flagship initiative under the CM-ELEVATE Program aimed at promoting dairy entrepreneurship in Meghalaya by providing financial assistance, subsidies, technical training, and market support.

faqs.question: What is the main objective of the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme aims to employ, engage, and empower youth and rural communities by supporting sustainable dairy farming and dairy-based businesses.

faqs.question: Who can apply under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Individuals aged 18–58 years, registered entities like Cooperatives, FPOs/FPCs, and eligible unregistered groups such as SHGs and producer groups can apply.

faqs.question: What financial support is provided?
faqs.answer: The Government supports 50% of the project cost (45% Government subsidy + 5% beneficiary contribution). The remaining amount is arranged through bank credit linkage.

faqs.question: Is there any EMI support?
faqs.answer: Yes. The scheme provides 5% EMI co-payment support for 24 months to ease the repayment burden.

faqs.question: Are banks involved in the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes. Credit linkage is facilitated through partnered banks to provide loans to eligible applicants.

faqs.question: Is training mandatory for applicants?
faqs.answer: Yes. Applicants must possess a training certificate in the dairy sector from a recognized institution, preferably a Government institute.

faqs.question: Is prior experience in dairy required?
faqs.answer: Prior experience is preferred and may give applicants priority in loan approval.

faqs.question: What is required for unregistered entities?
faqs.answer: They must provide eligibility certification from a competent authority and have a constitution/bylaws outlining structure and objectives.

faqs.question: How much contribution is required from the applicant?
faqs.answer: The applicant must contribute 5% of the total project cost.

faqs.question: Is there age relaxation for applicants?
faqs.answer: The age limit is strictly between 18 and 58 years for individuals.

faqs.question: Can multiple members from the same village apply?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided each applicant meets eligibility criteria and project feasibility requirements.

name: Millet Development Scheme
department: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department
description: The "Millet Development Scheme" introduced by the Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department, Gujarat, aims to encourage farmers to adopt millet cultivation. The scheme includes various promotional events, expos, processing units, and financial assistance for demonstration activities. Special preference is given to SC/ST, OBC, and women farmers.
benefits: Name of the Component Standard of Assistance Minimum Time Limit (in Years) for Reclaiming Benefits Millet Demonstration₹6,000/- per Ha, Maximum up to 1 HaOne time in a Year
eligibility: The applicant must be a farmer.. The applicant must have his own bank account.. Note:. All categories will benefit from the scheme.. Priority will be given to SC/ST, OBC, and women farmers..
documents: Voter ID/ Ration card/ Aadhaar card/ Passport as identity proof (Mandatory). Land records details (Mandatory). Bank account details (Mandatory). Any other document if required.
Voter ID/ Ration card/ Aadhaar card/ Passport as identity proof (Mandatory).

faqs.question: What is the objective of the "Millet Development Scheme"?
faqs.answer: The "Millet Development Scheme" aims to promote millet cultivation in Gujarat by organizing promotional activities, expos, processing units, seed/input kit demonstrations, and taluka-level melas. The scheme intends to increase the cultivation area and enhance farmers' income by boosting the value of millet crops.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for the "Millet Development Scheme"?
faqs.answer: Any farmer in Gujarat can apply for the scheme. However, priority is given to SC/ST, OBC, and women farmers.

faqs.question: What financial assistance is provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers receive [?]6,000/- per hectare for millet demonstration, up to a maximum of 1 hectare.

faqs.question: What documents are required for application?
faqs.answer: Farmers must submit land records, identity proof (Voter ID, Ration Card, Aadhaar Card, or Passport), and bank account details.

faqs.question: How is the financial assistance provided to the beneficiary?
faqs.answer: The financial assistance is directly transferred to the farmer's registered bank account.

faqs.question: What is the time limit for reclaiming benefits under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers can avail the benefits of the scheme once per year as per the Government Resolution.

faqs.question: How can farmers apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers must apply online through the iKhedut portal at https://ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in

name: Mukhyamantri Ekeekrit Bagwani Vikas Yojana
description: The scheme “Mukhyamantri Ekeekrit Bagwani Vikas Yojana” is implemented by the Department of Horticulture, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to promote horticulture development in Uttarakhand by providing farmers with subsidized fruit plants, seeds, pesticides, and horticulture infrastructure such as Cool Houses and Refrigerator Vans, thereby increasing productivity, reducing post-harvest losses, and enhancing farmers’ income.
benefits: Under this scheme, the following assistance is provided: 50% subsidy on the cost of fruit plants, open-field vegetable seeds, spice seeds, and flower seeds. No direct monetary assistance is provided; the seeds and plants are supplied at a subsidized rate. 60% subsidy on the cost of pesticides and other plant protection chemicals. No direct cash is given; the medicines are provided at a subsidized rate. 50% subsidy on the total cost of ₹15.00 lakh for Cool Houses with a capacity of 30 MT. 50% subsidy on the total cost of ₹26.00 lakh for Refrigerator Vans with a capacity of 9 MT.
eligibility: The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.. The applicant must be a farmer and hold a valid Udhyan Card.. The farmer must either own agricultural land or have land on lease..
documents: related documents such as Khasra and Khatauni Lease certificate (for leased land) Aadhaar card PAN card Udhyan card Bank account details Mobile number Other supporting documents as required
Land-related documents such as Khasra and Khatauni

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers who have their own or leased agricultural land/garden and hold a valid horticulture card are eligible to apply.

faqs.question: What assistance is provided under the scheme for seeds and plants?
faqs.answer: Farmers receive a 50% subsidy on fruit plants, open-field vegetable seeds, spice seeds, and flower seeds.

faqs.question: Is any monetary assistance provided for seeds and plants?
faqs.answer: No, the seeds and plants are provided at a subsidized rate, not as direct cash.

faqs.question: What assistance is provided for pesticides and other chemicals?
faqs.answer: Farmers receive a 60% subsidy on the cost of pesticides and other plant protection chemicals.

faqs.question: How can farmers obtain the application form?
faqs.answer: The application form can be obtained from Horticulture Mobile Squad Centres or downloaded from the department's website.

faqs.question: When should the application be submitted?
faqs.answer: Applications should be submitted approximately two months before planting saplings or using medicines.

faqs.question: Where should the application be submitted?
faqs.answer: Applications should be submitted to the Horticulture Mobile Squad Centre along with the required documents.

faqs.question: How is the application processed?
faqs.answer: The Centre forwards the application to the district level, which then sends it to the Directorate for approval. Once approved, a government order is issued for implementation.

faqs.question: How is the subsidy for Cool Houses and Refrigerator Vans disbursed?
faqs.answer: The subsidy is provided after the farmer purchases the van or constructs the Cool House, following a site inspection by departmental officials.

faqs.question: How are beneficiaries selected?
faqs.answer: Beneficiaries are selected on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to the availability of budget.
