name: National Scheme Of Welfare Of Fishermen
department: Ministry of Fisheries,Animal Husbandry and Dairying
description: The National Scheme of Welfare of Fishermen is a centrally sponsored scheme that provides financial assistance to fishermen. They can use these for constructing houses and community halls for both recreation and work purposes. Further, through the amount availed under this scheme, fishermen can install tube wells. Objectives- Provide fishermen with basic amenities such as housing, community halls, tube well for drinking water. Ensure Financial And Social Securities Of Fishermen And Their Families. Upgrade The Standard Of Living Of Fishermen. Educate And Train Fishermen In Advanced Technical Technologies So That They Can Learn Scientific Ways Of Fishing.
benefits: Here are the features and benefits that this government scheme for fishermen offers - Housing Facility The National Scheme of Welfare of Fishermen offers fishermen facilities for constructing houses. There is no upper limit for building homes in a particular village as it entirely depends on the number of fishermen residing. States through this scheme ensure equal distribution of houses among all fishermen. Also, this government-backed scheme dictates the house construction with a base area within 35 sq. mt. Also, the cost must not exceed ₹75,000. Construction of Common Facility This government-backed scheme ensures building a community hall in some instances if there are more than 75 houses in a village. This scheme will build a community hall (with two toilets and a tube well) with a base area measuring 200 sq. mt. and within ₹2 lakh. Fishermen can use this community hall as a mending shed and a drying yard. Assurance of Clean Drinking Water This scheme offers a tube well for every 20 houses. Also, depending on the requirement, the number of tube wells is increased. In addition, this scheme provides an alternative option where tubewell installation is not possible. Insurance Facility (For Group Accident Insurance for Active Fishermen)- This scheme provides fisherfolk or licensed or identified or registered with the States or Union Territory ₹50,000 in case of death or permanent total disability. Also, this scheme provides ₹25,000 for partial permanent disability. Here, the insurance cover will continue for 12 months, and FISHCOPFED would take out a policy. Also, under this scheme, the affected fishermen will have to pay an annual premium worth ₹15 (per head). Here, the Central Government will pay 50%, and the State Government will pay the remaining 50% subsidy as grants-in-aid. In the case of Union Territories, the Central Government will bear a 100% premium. On the other hand, those States/UT’s, which subscribed to this Group Accident Insurance for Active Fishermen through FISHCOPFED, will get a Central share of assistance (100% premium for Union Territories) directly through FISHCOPFED and not through States/UT’s. Saving cum relief The National Scheme of Welfare of Fishermen further offers a savings cum relief scheme. This scheme component collects ₹75 from marine fishermen for 8 months in a year. Total ₹600 needs to be collected to match an equal amount worth ₹600 provided by the State and Central Government to segregate on a 50:50 basis. If any fishermen fail to make payment, the authorities will refund the paid amount with interest at the end of the 4th month. Also, the ‘lean months’ provisions vary from a coastal area or marine area, which FISHCOPFED decides entirely. Now that individuals know about this government scheme for fishermen, i.e. the National Scheme of Welfare of Fishermen, they avail funds and construct houses of their own.
eligibility: Eligibility Criteria for Inland Fishermen. Fishermen living in coastal areas and with whom the respective States and Union Territories have officially licensed are eligible for this scheme.. The age of fishermen must be below 60 years old.. Applicant fishermen must belong to the BPL (Below Poverty Line) category.. They must be engaged in full-time activities inland.. Eligibility Criteria for Marine Fishermen. All marine fishermen who operate under State, Union Territories, and FISHCOPFED are eligible for this government scheme for fishermen. However, there are other eligibility parameters marine fishermen must fulfill. These include -. Their respective States and Union Territories must officially license marine fishermen.. They must involve themselves in full-time activities at sea.. They must be a member of the Welfare Society or Federation or Cooperative Society.. Please note that the fishermen under FISHCOPFED can avail of funds available under the insurance component only..
documents: Application in the specific format Photograph of the applicant with spouse (if married) Vessel registration certificate (duly issued by Directorate of Fisheries) Current net license payment receipt Professional cum residential certificate Ration card copy Income certificate Photograph

faqs.question: Can Fishermen Or Members Of Fishermen Families Indulged In Other Income Activities Avail Funds Under The National Scheme Of Welfare Of Fishermen?
faqs.answer: No, fishermen or fishermen family members indulged in other income activities cannot avail funds under the National Scheme of Welfare of Fishermen.

faqs.question: How Many Tube Wells Does This Scheme Provide For A Fishermen Village With More Than 10 Houses But Less Than 20 Houses?
faqs.answer: One tube well will be provided for a fishermen village with more than 10 houses but less than 20 houses.

name: Nandi Shala Yojana
description: The "Nandi Shala Yojana (Provision of Breeding Indigenous Bulls on Subsidy)" is launched by the Department of Animal Husbandry, Government of Madhya Pradesh. The scheme aims to improve the breeds of local non-descript and graded cattle in rural areas through natural insemination services. The progressive livestock owners at the Gram Panchayat level are provided high-quality indigenous breeding bulls of recognized breeds such as Sahiwal, Tharparkar, Haryana, Gir, Gaolao, Malvi, Nimari, and Kenkatha at a subsidized cost. > Objectives To provide indigenous breeding bulls on subsidy for natural insemination services. To improve the productivity of local cattle breeds in rural areas. To support progressive livestock farmers in rural Gram Panchayats.
benefits: > Cost and Subsidy For bulls procured from outside Madhya Pradesh: ₹25,720/- per unit. For bulls procured from within Madhya Pradesh: ₹18,260/- per unit. Subsidy: 75% of the cost. Beneficiary contribution: 25% of the cost.
eligibility: The applicant should be a livestock farmer.. The applicant should be residing in a rural area of Madhya Pradesh.. The applicant should have a minimum of 5 cattle along with sufficient agricultural land.. If the applicant does not have agricultural land, they should have at least 20 cattle.. The applicant should be willing to maintain and use the distributed bull for community natural insemination purposes..

faqs.answer: No, it is only for rural livestock farmers.

faqs.answer: The concerned Gram Panchayat, nearest Veterinary Institution, or the Deputy Director of Animal Husbandry.

faqs.answer: To maintain the bull and provide natural insemination services for local cattle.

name: Nagar Van Yojana
department: Ministry Of Environment,forests and climate change
description: The scheme "Nagar Van Yojana" was launched by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India. The scheme aims to develop 400 Nagar Vans and 200 Nagar Vatikas to create green spaces in urban areas by protecting land from degradation. The scheme provides a one-time development grant of ₹4,00,000/- per hectare up to a maximum of ₹2,00,00,000/- for 50 hectares to cover costs such as fencing, soil-moisture conservation, theme-based plantations, and maintenance of tree cover. The applicant must formulate a detailed project proposal, include a Keyhole Markup Language map on a 1:10,000 or larger scale, ensure a commitment to bear the balance cost, and submit the plan for the identified land. The scheme is implemented by the State Forest Department and the National Afforestation and Eco-Development Board. The applications for this scheme are accepted offline through the concerned State Forest Department offices.
benefits: The Ministry will provide a one-time development and non-recurring grant of ₹4,00,000/- per hectare. The maximum financial assistance for a Nagar Van is limited to ₹2,00,00,000/- for 50 hectares. The State Forest Department is permitted to engage one technical consultant at a cost of ₹40,000/- per month until the completion of the project for monitoring and other works. The State Forest Department will receive a lump sum grant of ₹50,000/- per project for monitoring, evaluation, and meeting overhead expenses. Mode of Disbursal: The funds will be released directly to the respective State Forest Departments from the National Fund under the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority. Frequency and Validity: The grant is a one-time assistance, released in two separate instalments, and financial assistance is provided to each Nagar Van or Nagar Vatika for the first two years only. Components Fencing of the identified area must be undertaken. Establishment and maintenance of woodlots or tree cover with an emphasis on locally appropriate species must be carried out. Theme-based plantations such as Smriti Van or Nakshatra Van may be established. Plants representing floral biodiversity, including ornamental trees, medicinal plants, and fruit trees, must be included. Irrigation and rain water harvesting facilities must be established. Establishment and maintenance of public conveniences, drinking water facilities, benches, walkways, and cycle tracks must be completed. An Information and Extension Centre, including display boards and information brochures, must be established and maintained. Conditions The first instalment of 70% of the sanctioned amount is released to the State Forest Department after the approval of the project by the National Authority. The remaining second instalment of 30% is released after 60% utilization of the first instalment and on the submission of the utilisation certificate and progress report. The State Forest Department must further release the portion of the grant meant for an implementing agency within a period of seven days. A corpus of the entire funds received by the implementing agency must be maintained as an interest-bearing account in a government or public sector bank. Detailed accounts of receipts and expenditures must be maintained by each implementing agency and the State Forest Department. All funds received by the implementing agency must be subjected to an annual audit by a chartered accountant.
eligibility: The applicant must be a Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council, Municipality, Urban Local Body, State Forest Department, Educational Institution, University, Government Organisation, or Non-Government Organisation.. The applicant must have possession of the proposed land.. The applicant must provide a commitment to bear the balance cost of the project beyond the provided grant.. The applicant must ensure that the proposed area is situated on forest land or other vacant non-forest public land.. The applicant must formulate a Development cum Management Plan with year-wise details of works under different components.. For Nagar Van. The applicant must develop the Nagar Van over a minimum area of 10 hectares.. The applicant must restrict the maximum area for grant calculation to 50 hectares.. The applicant must ensure the site is located within a 5-kilometre limit of the Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council, or Municipality.. The applicant must maintain a minimum of 2/3rd of the Nagar Van area under woodland or tree cover.. For Nagar Vatika. The applicant must develop the Nagar Vatika in a minimum area of 1 hectare.. The applicant must restrict the maximum area of the Nagar Vatika to 10 hectares.. The applicant must ensure the site is located strictly within the city limits or congested parts of the cities.. Post-Selection Conditions. The applicant must keep all Nagar Vans and Nagar Vatikas open and accessible to the city dwellers and general public, subject to suitable restrictions.. The applicant should encourage a Public-Private Partnership mode to ensure the active participation of people, students, and other stakeholders in planning, implementation, and management.. The applicant should select trees from species that are best suited for local conditions.. The applicant should place an emphasis on enriching biodiversity, planting fruit-bearing trees, and cultivating medicinal plants.. The applicant should ensure sufficient revenue generation for maintenance by levying user fees, receiving grants from other agencies, and promoting economic activities like the sale of saplings or processed forest products from the first year.. The applicant should encourage the use of locally available material, energy conservation, and waste recycling..

faqs.question: Since the maximum financial assistance is capped at ₹2,00,00,000/- for 50 hectares, what happens to the remaining project expenses that exceed this provided grant?
faqs.answer: The implementing agency must provide a firm commitment to bear any remaining costs using their own resources or other available funding avenues.

faqs.question: When receiving financial grants for the environmental project, are there any specific banking rules or requirements regarding where the received money must be kept?
faqs.answer: The entire amount received must be maintained as a corpus in an interest-bearing account within a government or public sector bank.

faqs.question: In case we intend to establish a smaller green space within the highly congested parts of our city, what are the permissible minimum and maximum land size limits?
faqs.answer: The designated area must be a minimum of 1 hectare and can go up to a maximum of 10 hectares strictly within the city limits.

faqs.question: While planning the landscape and various components of the proposed green space, is there a mandatory proportion of the total land that must be dedicated specifically to woodlands?
faqs.answer: At least two-thirds of the total designated area must be maintained under proper tree cover or woodlands to meet the core environmental objectives.

faqs.question: What specific mapping and geographic documentation must be included along with the detailed project proposal to clearly define the boundaries of the selected land?
faqs.answer: Applicants need to submit a Keyhole Markup Language map on a 1:10,000 or larger scale, which must include accurate Global Positioning System coordinates detailing the boundary.

faqs.question: After the financial assistance has been disbursed and utilized for the project, what are the mandatory financial compliance and auditing rules that the implementing agency must follow annually?
faqs.answer: All project-related funds and accounts maintained by the implementing agency are subject to a mandatory annual audit conducted by a qualified chartered accountant.

faqs.question: If an educational institution, university, or non-government organisation wishes to submit a proposal for financial assistance, what is the appropriate channel for doing so?
faqs.answer: Submissions must be routed through the concerned State Government and State Forest Department for proper scrutiny before being forwarded for further consideration.

faqs.question: If we want to develop a larger forest area outside the immediate city limits, what are the exact area requirements and the maximum limit for calculating the grant?
faqs.answer: The project must cover a minimum of 10 hectares, and while there is no upper size limit, financial support is strictly capped at a maximum of 50 hectares.

faqs.question: To account for future expansion and provide greener surroundings, how far outside the official municipal corporation or municipality boundaries can the proposed forest site be located?
faqs.answer: The selected site can be situated up to a maximum distance of 5 kilometres from the official municipal or city limits.

faqs.question: Before initiating the formal application process and formulating the detailed management plan, what is the most critical prerequisite regarding the legal status of the proposed land?
faqs.answer: The implementing agency must have legal possession of the proposed land, which can be either forest land or other vacant non-forest public land.

faqs.question: Once the environmental project is fully developed and operational, are there any restrictions on whether local residents and visitors can enter and utilize the designated green spaces?
faqs.answer: The developed spaces must remain open and accessible to city dwellers and the general public, although suitable restrictions can be applied for proper management.

faqs.question: When deciding on the types of plants and trees to include in the designated area, what specific types of species should the applicant prioritize for plantation?
faqs.answer: Priority should be given to species best suited for local conditions, including fruit-bearing trees, medicinal plants, and varieties that attract birds and butterflies to enrich biodiversity.

faqs.question: For how many years will the implementing agency receive direct financial support from the government to help establish and maintain the newly created urban forest or garden?
faqs.answer: Financial assistance is provided exclusively for the first two years of the project to support initial development and non-recurring expenses.

faqs.question: Are implementing agencies allowed to collaborate with private entities, industries, or civil society groups to manage and fund the various components of the proposed green space?
faqs.answer: Adopting a Public-Private Partnership model is highly encouraged to ensure active public participation, provided a formal agreement is signed between the different stakeholders.

faqs.question: What are the National Water Awards?
faqs.answer: The National Water Awards are an initiative to recognize and celebrate outstanding achievements and contributions in the field of water resources management, conservation, and sustainability across India.

faqs.question: Who organizes the National Water Awards?
faqs.answer: The awards are typically organized by the Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India, or other relevant government agencies responsible for water resources management.

faqs.question: What types of achievements do the National Water Awards recognize?
faqs.answer: The awards recognize achievements in various areas such as water conservation, rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge, efficient water use, wastewater treatment and reuse, river rejuvenation, and community-based water management.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to participate in Awards?
faqs.answer: Individuals, organizations, institutions, local bodies, NGOs, industries, and government agencies involved in water conservation and management activities in India are eligible to participate.

faqs.question: Can projects/initiatives from all states participate?
faqs.answer: Yes, projects/initiatives from all states and union territories of India are eligible to participate in the National Water Awards.

faqs.question: Is there a fee to participate in the National Water Awards?
faqs.answer: No, there is usually no participation fee required to enter the National Water Awards.

faqs.question: How to apply for visitor’s Award?
faqs.answer: Applicant may log on to the official website of Rashtriya Puruskar Portal i.e., https://awards.gov.in/.

faqs.question: What are the Eligibility of the scheme?
faqs.answer: Any State, District, Village Panchayat, Urban Local Body, School, College, Institution, Industry, Civil Society, Water User Association and an Individual who has done good work in the field of water conservation and management is eligible to apply.

faqs.question: Who can nominate ?
faqs.answer: Self in respect of Best Individual for Excellence, and Secretary/Principal Secretary of concerned State Departments, District Collector/ District Magistrate/ Head of Body, Prinicipal/Head of School/ College, Head of the Institution/ Industry/ Organisation/Association for other categories of awards.

name: Old Age Pension Scheme under Chief Minister’s Uzhavar Padhukappu Thittam
department: Department of Social Welfare and Women Empowerment
description: The 'Old Age Pension Scheme under Chief Minister’s Uzhavar Padhukappu Thittam' is a state scheme that was launched by the Social Welfare and Women Empowerment Department, Tamil Nadu. The scheme aims to give a pension of ₹1,000/- to old-age farmers and destitute agricultural labourers who have membership card under Chief Minister’s Uzhavar Padhukappu Thittam (CMPUT).
benefits: Pension: ₹1,000/- per month. Free Clothes during Pongal and Deepavali: One free dhoti to a male pensioner. One free saree to a female pensioner. Free Rice in Anganwadi Centres: 2kg/month to those who are taking nutritious meal. 4kg/month to those who are not taking nutritious meal.
eligibility: The applicant should be destitute.. The applicant's age should be 60 years and above.. The applicant should be farmer or a landless agricultural labour.. The applicant's fixed assets should not exceed ₹1,00,000/-..
documents: Applicant's Photo. Aadhaar Card. Proof of Age. Aadhaar Consent Form. Smart Ration Card or Any Address Proof. Membership Card under CMPUT. Self–declaration of Applicant. Any Identity Proof (Voter ID Card, Passport, PAN Card, Driving License). Bank Passbook.
Smart Ration Card or Any Address Proof.
Any Identity Proof (Voter ID Card, Passport, PAN Card, Driving License).

faqs.question: I am 58 years old and a registered farmer under CMPUT. Can I apply for the scheme now?
faqs.answer: No, unfortunately, the minimum age requirement to apply for the scheme is 60 years old. You can apply once you reach that age.

faqs.question: I am not completely destitute, but I have very low income from farming. Am I eligible for the scheme?
faqs.answer: While the scheme prioritizes destitute individuals, having some income from farming wouldn't necessarily disqualify you. However, your income level and overall financial situation will be assessed during the application process to determine your eligibility.

faqs.question: I used to be a farmer, but now I work as a security guard. Am I still eligible for the pension?
faqs.answer: No, the scheme is specifically for farmers and landless agricultural laborers. If your primary source of income is no longer related to agriculture, you wouldn't be eligible.

faqs.question: What happens to the free clothes (dhoti/saree) if I cannot attend the distribution event?
faqs.answer: In most cases, the clothes can be collected later from designated distribution centers. However, it's best to check with the CSC or local authorities for specific details and collection timelines.

faqs.question: I am a female farmer. Do I need to show my land ownership documents to apply?
faqs.answer: No, the scheme doesn't differentiate between male and female farmers or require land ownership documents. As long as you have a valid CMPUT membership card and meet the eligibility criteria, you can apply.

faqs.question: Do I need to renew my application every year to continue receiving the benefits?
faqs.answer: No, once approved, you don't need to reapply every year. However, you might need to update your information periodically, as instructed by the authorities.

faqs.question: I live in a remote area with limited access to CSCs. Are there any alternative ways to apply?
faqs.answer: You can inquire with the Social Welfare Department about potential mobile camps or designated application centers closer to your location.

faqs.question: Do I need help from a lawyer or any other professional to complete the application process?
faqs.answer: No, the application process for the Old Age Pension Scheme is designed to be simple and self-explanatory. The CSC staff can also guide you through the process and answer any questions you might have.

faqs.question: Is there a fee associated with applying for the scheme?
faqs.answer: No, applying for the Old Age Pension Scheme is completely free. You shouldn't pay any fees at the CSC or to any individual for processing your application.

faqs.question: How long does it take to process the application and receive the benefits?
faqs.answer: Processing times can vary, but it typically takes around 4-6 weeks for verification and approval. Once approved, you should receive the pension within a month.

faqs.question: Is there a specific time frame during which I can apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: No, the Old Age Pension Scheme is an ongoing initiative, and you can apply at any time.

name: Organizing Block Demonstration

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers cultivating seed farms with Pulses crops are eligible for the scheme.

faqs.question: What is the subsidy amount provided?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides a subsidy of 50% of input costs or [?]2000/- per 5 hectares, whichever is less.

faqs.answer: The subsidy covers 50% of the total input costs, up to a maximum of [?]2,000/- per demonstration on 5 hectares.

faqs.question: Is there a limit to the number of farmers who can benefit from the scheme?

faqs.question: What role does the Assistant Agricultural Officer play in the process?
faqs.answer: The Assistant Agricultural Officer helps farmers with the application process at the village level and ensures the documents are submitted correctly.

faqs.question: What happens if the available funds are exhausted?
faqs.answer: If funds are exhausted, further applications will be processed based on fund availability in the future.

faqs.question: Is it possible to apply online?

faqs.question: Is there a specific time frame for submitting the application?
faqs.answer: The application can be submitted at any time during the scheme's validity period, provided funds are available.

faqs.question: Is a bank account necessary to receive the subsidy?

faqs.question: Can the subsidy be used for crops other than Pulses?
faqs.answer: No, the subsidy is strictly for the demonstration of Pulses crops and cannot be transferred to other crops or schemes.

faqs.question: Can small and marginal farmers apply?

name: "Orthodox or Specialty Tea Production Subsidy" under the "Assam Tea Industries Special Incentives Scheme"
description: Launched in 2020, the scheme "Assam Tea Industries Special Incentives Scheme (ATISIS)" by the Finance (Institutional Finance) Department, Government of Assam, aims to ensure long-term financial sustainability of the Tea industry and to incentivize manufacturers to move from Crush, Tear, Curl tea to Orthodox tea production. The scheme is implemented by the Finance Department and the Industries & Commerce Department, Government of Assam, through multiple implementing agencies, including banks and the District Industries & Commerce Centre. The applications for this scheme are accepted online through a dedicated portal with a Direct Benefit Transfer mechanism for reimbursement.
benefits: Benefit Amount: ₹10/- per kilogram for Orthodox tea, Green tea, White tea, Oolong tea, Singhpo tea, Purple Tea, Yellow tea, or other Specialty tea Special Rate: ₹12/- per kilogram for applications of Financial Year 2023-24 only (tea production year 2022-23). Validity Period: Extended from Financial Year 2023-24 to 2027-28. Disbursement Mode: Direct Benefit Transfer as reimbursement. Claim Deadline: Latest by 30th June on completion of every financial year. Additional Benefit: Provided in addition to any other subsidy claimed from the Tea Board of India or any other agency.
eligibility: General Eligibility. The applicant must be a tea plantation across all sizes. The applicant must be a tea manufacturing unit manufacturing Crush, Tear, Curl Tea, Orthodox Tea, or Speciality tea including Green tea, Oolong Tea, White tea, Yellow tea and Purple tea. The applicant must be located entirely in Assam. The applicant must not have any part of the plantation or manufacturing facility located outside the State of Assam. Production Subsidy Specific Eligibility. The applicant must be manufacturing Orthodox tea, Green tea, White tea, Oolong tea, Singhpo tea, Purple Tea, Yellow tea or other Speciality tea (not manufactured through Crush, Tear, Curl process).. The applicant must have started production on or after 1st of April, 2020..
documents: Returns of Tea Production submitted to Tea Board India. Tea Production Certificate. Tea Manufacturing License. Orthodox/Speciality Tea Production Evidence.
Monthly E-Returns of Tea Production submitted to Tea Board India.

faqs.question: What is the primary objective of this tea industry incentive scheme launched in 2020?
faqs.answer: The scheme aims to ensure long-term financial sustainability of the tea industry and incentivize manufacturers to move from Crush, Tear, Curl tea to Orthodox tea production.

faqs.question: How much financial benefit can I expect to receive per kilogram of Orthodox tea produced under this scheme?
faqs.answer: You will receive ₹10 per kilogram for Orthodox tea, Green tea, White tea, Oolong tea, Singhpo tea, Purple tea, Yellow tea, or other specialty tea varieties.

faqs.question: Is there any special rate available for applications submitted during Financial Year 2023-24?
faqs.answer: Yes, applications for Financial Year 2023-24 receive a special rate of ₹12 per kilogram for tea production year 2022-23.

faqs.question: What is the current validity period for this scheme and until when can I apply?
faqs.answer: The scheme validity has been extended from Financial Year 2023-24 to 2027-28, allowing applications during this period.

faqs.question: How will I receive the subsidy amount once my application is approved?
faqs.answer: The benefit is disbursed through Direct Benefit Transfer as reimbursement directly to your registered bank account.

faqs.question: What is the deadline for submitting claims after completing tea production in a financial year?
faqs.answer: Claims must be submitted latest by 30th June upon completion of every financial year.

faqs.question: Can I claim this benefit along with other subsidies from Tea Board of India or other agencies?
faqs.answer: Yes, this benefit is provided in addition to any other subsidy you may have claimed from Tea Board of India or other agencies.

faqs.question: What size requirements must my tea plantation meet to be eligible for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Tea plantations across all sizes are eligible, meaning there are no minimum or maximum size restrictions for plantation eligibility.

faqs.question: What types of tea manufacturing units are considered eligible to apply for this incentive scheme?
faqs.answer: Eligible units include those manufacturing Crush, Tear, Curl tea, Orthodox tea, or specialty tea including Green tea, Oolong tea, White tea, Yellow tea, and Purple tea.

faqs.question: Where must my tea plantation and manufacturing facilities be located to qualify for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Your tea plantation and manufacturing unit must be located entirely within the State of Assam without any part outside Assam.

faqs.question: Are there any geographical restrictions regarding parts of my plantation or manufacturing facility being located outside Assam?
faqs.answer: No part of your plantation or manufacturing facility should be located outside the State of Assam for eligibility.

faqs.question: Which specific types of tea production qualify for the production subsidy under this scheme?
faqs.answer: You must manufacture Orthodox tea, Green tea, White tea, Oolong tea, Singhpo tea, Purple tea, Yellow tea, or other specialty tea not made through Crush, Tear, Curl process.

faqs.question: What is the minimum date from which my tea production must have started to be eligible?
faqs.answer: Your tea production must have started on or after 1st April, 2020 to qualify for the production subsidy.

faqs.question: What is the first step I need to take to register for this scheme online?
faqs.answer: Visit the dedicated portal of this scheme and click on the "New User Registration" option to begin the registration process.

name: One Time Assistance to Small and Marginal Farmers for Purchase of Small Farm Implements (OTA-SFI)
description: “One Time Assistance to Small and Marginal Farmers for Purchase of Small Farm Implements (OTA-SFI)” under the Farm Mechanization Umbrella Scheme, was launched on 12 February, 2013 by the Agriculture Department, Government of West Bengal with the purpose to aid the farmers in procuring manually operated small farm implements necessary for agricultural operations. > Features: Financial support will be provided mostly for manually operated tools like sprayer, manually operated paddy thresher, cono weeder, weeder, drum-seeder, solar light trap, chaff cutter, seed bin, seed tray, seeder etc. and battery operated sprayers and PVC pipes for carrying water etc. under OTA-SFI. > Area of Operation: The scheme is applicable uniformly throughout the State, except Kolkata district.
benefits: > Pattern Of Assistance: Maximum ₹10,000/- or 50% of total indicative price of purchased manually operated machinery/implement whichever is lower. > Available Equipment: A list of different manually operated machinery/implements is provided in Annexure-III (https://matirkatha.net/rails/active storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBa1lDIiwiZXhwIjpudWxsLCJwdXIiOiJibG9iX2lkIn19--6e05a52aaf58b7fbfa749a5d71be15309a5101ea/FMS Operational%20Guidelines 2024 25.pdf?disposition=attachment) (Page No. 37). Available models of different farm machinery /implements as mentioned in Annexure-III along with indicative price will be published in Matirkatha portal by the SPMT before starting of online application of the beneficiary .Combination of machinery/equipment from the list can be purchased within the subsidy limit. But, maximum two nos. implements of the same item may be chosen by the applicant. However, battery operated sprayers and PVC pipes for carrying water will also be eligible under this component. > Note: No machine/equipment will be procured by the Government. The Government will only release subsidy as back ended subsidy against procurement by the beneficiaries as per their choice under FSSM with Bank Loan. The subsidy will be released through DBT mode to the beneficiaries for OTA-SFI. The subsidy will only be applicable for purchase of farm machinery/equipment from the approved Farm machinery Manufacturers and Dealers as enlisted in the Departmental portal. A beneficiary or his/her spouse will not be eligible to apply afresh before completion of 4(four) years from release of the last subsidy for any type of machinery under OTA-SFI from the State under this Guidelines.

name: One Tea Scheme
department: Planning, Investment Promotion & Sustainable Development Department
description: The One Tea Scheme, implemented by the Planning, Investment Promotion & Sustainable Development Department, Government of Meghalaya, is designed to support tea farmers in the state whose livelihoods have been affected by declining factory gate prices and shrinking cultivated areas. The initiative introduces a single-season price support mechanism that guarantees every registered grower a minimum price of ₹35 per kilogram of fresh tea leaves for conventional tea gardens and ₹40 per kilogram for organically certified tea gardens. By compensating the difference between the factory’s actual purchase price and the guaranteed minimum price, the scheme prevents farmers from being forced to sell their produce at a loss. This support helps ensure fair price realization, provides economic stability for farmers to reinvest in their plantations, and contributes to the preservation of ecological services and traditional knowledge associated with tea cultivation. In addition, the scheme offers a one-time financial benefit to bought-leaf factories to cover the gap between the price they pay for fresh green leaves from both small and large tea growers and the price at which they can profitably process and sell the manufactured tea.

eligibility: The applicant should be 18 years of age or above.. The applicant should be a permanent resident of Meghalaya.. The applicant should be a tea farmer.. The applicant should possess a valid government-issued identity document..

name: Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyay Samoohik Pashudhan Beema Yojana
description: The scheme "Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyay Samoohik Pashudhan Beema Yojana" by the Haryana Livestock Development Board, Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of Haryana, aims to provide socio-economic security to livestock farmers in the state by covering livestock under an insurance scheme. Financial protection against the risk of loss due to animal death is extended to livestock owners, including Scheduled Caste (SC) and Below Poverty Line (BPL) beneficiaries, with subsidised premium rates.
benefits: Financial Protection Coverage for livestock loss due to death, providing financial security to farmers. Sum insured is determined based on the market value of livestock and milk yield. Maximum coverage is up to five large animals or equivalent small animals per household. Subsidized Premiums APL beneficiaries pay ₹100/200/300 per large animal per year based on milk yield or ₹25/- per small animal. BPL beneficiaries receive additional subsidies, and SC beneficiaries have their entire premium covered by the state and central government. Mode and Frequency of Disbursement Claims are settled through direct bank transfers to beneficiaries. Accidental death claims are covered immediately; non-accidental death claims are covered after a 21-day waiting period. Expected Time of Disbursement Insurance companies are required to settle claims within 15 days of document submission. Delays incur a penalty of 12% compound interest per annum.
eligibility: The applicant should be a livestock owner.. The applicant should be above 18 years of age.. The applicant should possess a Parivar Pehchan Patra (PPP), issued by the state of Haryana.. Preference and Relaxations. Applicants from Scheduled Caste and Below Poverty Line categories will be given priority.. Scheduled Caste beneficiaries are exempt from paying premiums. the state and central governments fully subsidize their insurance..
documents: Parivar Pehchan Patra (PPP). Health certificate issued by a registered veterinary practitioner. Photographs of the animal with a visible ear tag. Beneficiary’s share of the premium (if applicable). Scheduled Caste Certificate (for SC beneficiaries). Below Poverty Line Certificate (for BPL beneficiaries). Claim Settlement Documents: FIR with the insurance company and a duly filled claim form. Insurance policy document. Post
mortem report issued by a veterinary surgeon. Intact ear tag and updated bank account details of the beneficiary.

faqs.question: How much financial assistance can I get under the Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyay Samoohik Pashudhan Beema Yojana for insuring my dairy animals?
faqs.answer: For large animals (cows/buffaloes), you need to pay only [?]100-300 per year based on milk yield. For small animals like goats/sheep, the premium is [?] 25 per animal per year. SC beneficiaries get 100% free insurance coverage.

faqs.question: I have 8 milch animals in my household. Can I get insurance coverage for all of them under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme allows insurance coverage for up to 5 cattle units per household/family. You can insure additional animals beyond 5 by paying the full premium without subsidy benefits.

faqs.question: What is the process for filing a claim if my insured animal dies? What documents do I need to submit?
faqs.answer: File FIR within 24 hours of death and inform on toll-free number 1800-419-1415. Submit claim form, insurance policy, post-mortem report, and intact ear tag along with updated bank account details. The surveyor must visit within 4 hours of claim intimation.

faqs.question: I'm from a Scheduled Caste family. Do I need to pay any premium amount to get my livestock insured under this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, SC beneficiaries get 100% free insurance coverage with no premium payment required. The premium cost is shared between Central Government (40%) and State Government SCSP (60%).

faqs.question: What is the maximum insurance value I can get for my Sahiwal cow that gives 16 liters of milk per day?
faqs.answer: For Sahiwal cows giving above 15 liters milk per day, the maximum sum assured is [?] 90,000. The final valuation is done by a committee consisting of the owner, insurer, and veterinary surgeon.

faqs.question: If I sell my insured animal to someone else, what happens to the insurance coverage?
faqs.answer: The insurance can be transferred to the new owner by submitting a request to New India Assurance Company with a transfer fee of [?] 50, along with certification from the area veterinarian.

faqs.question: How long do I have to wait after getting insurance before I can file a claim if my animal dies?
faqs.answer: There is a 21-day waiting period for non-accidental deaths. However, claims for accidental deaths are covered from day one of the policy, provided police intimation is done.

faqs.question: What happens if the insurance company delays settling my claim beyond 15 days after document submission?
faqs.answer: The company becomes liable to pay a penalty of 12% compound interest per annum to the beneficiary for delays beyond 15 days after complete document submission.

faqs.question: I don't have a Parivar Pehchan Patra yet. Can I still apply for livestock insurance under this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, having a Parivar Pehchan Patra is mandatory for all beneficiaries. It's one of the essential documents required along with health certificate and category certificates (for SC/BPL).

faqs.question: If my animal dies during post-mortem examination, will I still get the insurance claim?
faqs.answer: The document doesn't specifically address this scenario. However, since post-mortem is a mandatory part of the claim process conducted by authorized veterinarians, such cases should be eligible for claims.

faqs.question: What is the role of the veterinary surgeon in the insurance process, and do I need to pay them separately?
faqs.answer: Veterinarians issue health certificates ([?] 50 honorarium) and conduct post-mortems ([?] 125 honorarium). These charges are covered under the scheme's central funding and beneficiaries don't pay extra.

faqs.question: If my Jan Dhan account is to receive a claim amount above ₹ 50,000, what should I do?
faqs.answer: You need to convert your Jan Dhan account to a general savings account before submitting the claim documents to ensure smooth processing of the claim amount.

benefits: Increased Productivity: The adoption of bio-floc technology in aquaculture can lead to increased productivity by maintaining optimal water quality conditions. The technology helps in controlling water parameters such as dissolved oxygen, ammonia, and nitrate levels, thereby creating a conducive environment for fish and shrimp growth.1. Water Conservation: Bio-floc technology promotes water conservation by minimizing the need for water exchange in aquaculture systems. The microbial communities formed in bio-floc tanks help in recycling nutrients and reducing water wastage, making it a sustainable approach to aquaculture.1. Cost Reduction: By reducing the dependence on water exchange and minimizing the usage of artificial feeds, the adoption of bio-floc technology can potentially lead to cost savings for fish and shrimp farmers. This can contribute to the economic viability of aquaculture operations.1. Environmental Sustainability: The implementation of bio-floc technology aligns with the goal of environmental sustainability in aquaculture. The technology reduces the release of effluents into natural water bodies, mitigating the potential negative impacts on the environment.1. Skill Development and Capacity Building: The initiative may include training and capacity-building programs for farmers, providing them with knowledge and skills related to bio-floc technology and its application in aquaculture. faqs.question: What is the objective of the "Promotion of Intensive Aquaculture through Introduction of Bio-floc Technology" initiative by the government of Odisha?
faqs.answer: The objective of the "Promotion of Intensive Aquaculture through Introduction of Bio-floc Technology" initiative by the government of Odisha is to promote and enhance aquaculture practices through the introduction of bio-floc technology. The initiative aims to encourage the adoption of sustainable and intensive aquaculture methods using bio-floc technology, which utilizes microbial communities to maintain water quality and support high-density fish and shrimp farming.

faqs.question: What is bio-floc technology, and how does it benefit aquaculture practices?
faqs.answer: Bio-floc technology is a sustainable aquaculture approach that utilizes microbial communities called bio-flocs to improve water quality and enhance productivity in aquaculture systems. In this technique, a carbon source, typically in the form of organic matter or carbohydrate-based feed, is provided to stimulate the growth of beneficial microorganisms. These microorganisms form clusters or aggregates called bio-flocs, which consist of bacteria, protozoa, and other microorganisms.

faqs.question: What is the financial assistance provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers receive an incentive of ₹9,000 per hectare for purchasing organic inputs such as seeds, compost, green manure, biofertilizers, biopesticides, neem oil, PROM, Burmese compost, and waste decomposers.

faqs.question: How are farmers selected for this scheme?

faqs.question: Where should farmers purchase organic inputs from?

name: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN)
description: The scheme "Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN)" implemented by the Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers’ Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, aims to supplement the financial needs of all landholding farmers’ families by procuring various inputs to ensure proper crop health and appropriate yields, commensurate with the anticipated farm income as well as for domestic needs. Under the scheme, an amount of ₹ 6,000/- per year is released by the Central Government online directly into the bank accounts of the eligible farmers under the Direct Benefit Transfer mode, subject to certain exclusions.
benefits: Financial Assistance: An amount of ₹6,000/- per year in 3 equal installments of ₹2,000/- every four months is provided to each eligible family.
eligibility: All landholding farmers'. families, which have cultivable land holding in their names are eligible to get benefit under the scheme..
documents: Aadhaar Card. Landholding papers. Savings Bank Account.

faqs.question: Whether the benefits of the scheme are admissible to only Small & Marginal Farmers' (SMF) families?
faqs.answer: No. The Scheme for all farmer families irrespective of the size of their landholdings

faqs.question: Will any individual or farmer family owning more than 2 hectare of cultivable land get any benefit under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes. The ambit of the scheme has been extended to cover all farmer families, irrespective of the size of their land holdings.

faqs.question: What are the benefit of the scheme?
faqs.answer: Under the PM-KISAN scheme, all landholding farmers' families shall be provided the financial benefit of Rs.6000 per annum per family payable in three equal installments of Rs.2000 each, every four months.

faqs.question: How many times the benefit will be given in a year?
faqs.answer: All landholding farmers' families shall be provided the financial benefit of Rs.6000/- per annum per family payable in three equal installments of Rs.200O/- each, every four months.

faqs.question: How the beneficiaries under the Scheme will be identified and shortlisted for payment of intended benefit?

faqs.question: Who are eligible to get benefits under the Scheme?

faqs.answer: No. if any member of the family is income tax payee in last assessment year is not eligible.

faqs.question: What will happen if the beneficiary gives incorrect declaration for the implementation of the Scheme?
faqs.answer: In case of incorrect declaration, the beneficiary shall be liable for recovery of transferred financial benefit and other penal actions as per law.

name: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha Evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan Yojana (PM-KUSUM) - Uttarakhand
description: The scheme “Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha Evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan Yojana (PM-KUSUM)” is implemented by the Department of Minor Irrigation, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to promote clean and affordable irrigation by replacing diesel pump sets with solar-powered pump sets, reducing farmers’ irrigation costs, enhancing energy security, and increasing farmers’ income through sustainable and efficient use of solar energy. The scheme follows a funding pattern of 50% Central share, 30% State share, and 20% farmer share.
benefits: Under the scheme, farmers receive an 80% subsidy on the cost of a solar pump set from the Government of India and the State Government, while the remaining 20% of the cost is borne by the farmer. The scheme allows individual farmers to convert their diesel pump sets into solar pump sets of up to 7.5 HP capacity, which helps reduce expenditure on diesel and lowers production costs, thereby increasing farmers’ income.
eligibility: The beneficiary must be a resident of Uttarakhand.. The beneficiary must be a farmer engaged in agricultural activities.. As per the guidelines of MNRE, Government of India:. The farmer must agree to contribute 20% of the cost of the solar pump set as the farmer’s share.. The farmer must have his own borewell.. The farmer should currently be using a diesel pump set for irrigation.. A farmer who wishes to install a USPC along with the solar pump set must agree to make 100% payment for the said work..
documents: Documents are required as per the department’s guidelines prescribed for this scheme.

faqs.question: How much subsidy is provided to farmers?
faqs.answer: Farmers receive an 80% subsidy on the cost of the solar pump set from the Central and State governments.

faqs.question: How much does the farmer have to pay?
faqs.answer: The farmer contributes 20% of the total cost of the solar pump set.

faqs.question: What type of pump sets can be converted under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Diesel pump sets used by individual farmers can be converted into solar pump sets of up to 7.5 HP capacity.

faqs.question: Where should farmers submit their applications?
faqs.answer: Applications must be submitted to the Block/Sub-Division Office of the Department of Minor Irrigation in the district.

faqs.question: What happens after the application is submitted?
faqs.answer: A site survey is conducted to determine suitability for installing a solar pump set.

faqs.question: When does the farmer deposit their share of 20%?
faqs.answer: If the site is found suitable after the survey, the farmer deposits 20% of the pump cost at the concerned office.

faqs.question: How is the installation carried out?
faqs.answer: After the farmer’s contribution is received, the department issues a work order to its listed/selected firms, which then conduct a final site survey and install the solar pump.

name: Plastic Mulching
description: The plastic Mulching scheme under the Agriculture Department of the Rajasthan government provided subsidies to farmers. Using plastic mulch helps prevent soil compaction and compaction. This material blocks moisture and heat and limits the loss of plant nutrients. Plastic mulch is the most restrictive of all the mulching materials available on the market, so it is well-suited for drip irrigation. Additionally, the plastic layer prevents people and pets from walking in the area, further strengthening the soil structure. > Other important points Plastic mulching can be constructed only after administrative approval is issued by the Horticulture Department. Verification can be done by the committee formed after construction. The payment of the grant amount will be transferred directly to the farmer's bank account.
benefits: Small/marginal farmers can get a 25% subsidy on up to 2 hectares of land. Other farmers can get a 50% subsidy on up to 2 hectares of land.
eligibility: The applicant should be a farmer.. The applicant should be a native of Rajasthan.. The applicant must have agricultural land ownership and irrigation sources..

name: Pradhan Mantri Adi Adarsh Gram Yojana (PMAAGY)
description: The scheme "Pradhan Mantri Adi Adarsh Gram Yojana (PMAAGY)" by the Ministry Of Tribal Affairs, Government Of India, aims to transform villages with high Scheduled Tribe population into model villages through providing financial assistance for infrastructure gap filling and socio-economic development to the tribal communities. The scheme focuses on villages having at least 50% ST population. It supports the preparation and implementation of Village Development Plans. Funds are utilized for critical infrastructure gaps not covered under other schemes. Convergence with other Central and State schemes is encouraged for holistic development.
benefits: Financial Assistance: ₹20,38,000/- per village for infrastructure gap filling and development activities. - Infrastructure Development: Support for roads, drinking water, sanitation, education, health, and livelihood infrastructure. - Village Development Plan (VDP): Preparation and execution of need-based development plans for selected villages. - Convergence Support: Integration with existing Central and State schemes to maximize development impact. - Awards And Incentives: ₹5,00,000/- per village at State level for best performing villages and ₹10,00,000/- per village at National level for top selected villages.
eligibility: > General Eligibility. The village must have at least 50% Scheduled Tribe (ST) population.. The village must have a population of at least 500 in plain areas. in hilly/tribal areas.. The village must be selected by the State/UT Government based on criteria defined in the guidelines.. > Preference / Priority. Preference is given to villages with higher ST population concentration.. Priority is given to villages with significant infrastructure gaps..

faqs.question: What type of development is supported?
faqs.answer: The scheme supports infrastructure development and socio-economic improvements.

faqs.question: What is a Village Development Plan (VDP)?
faqs.answer: It is a comprehensive plan outlining development needs and activities for the village.

faqs.question: Are funds given directly to individuals?
faqs.answer: No, funds are provided for community infrastructure and development projects.

faqs.question: Are there any awards under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, top-performing villages receive ₹5,00,000/- at State level and ₹10,00,000/- at National level.

name: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
description: With a view to enabling an area-based development approach, a new scheme Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana (PMAGY) was launched during 2009-10. The Scheme aims at integrated development of Scheduled Castes majority villages. The principal objective of PMAGY is the integrated development of SC majority Villages: (a) Primarily through convergent implementation of the relevant Central and State/UT Government Schemes; and (b) By taking up identified activities, which do not get covered under the existing Central and State Government Schemes, through ‘Gap-filling’ funds provided as Central Assistance to the extent of ₹20,00,000/- per village. The implementation of the Scheme was started on Pilot basis in 2009-10 and a total of 1000 villages was selected from 05 States namely Tamil Nadu (225), Rajasthan (225), Bihar (225), Himachal Pradesh (225) and Assam (100) were selected for this phase. All these 1000 villages have so far been declared as ‘Adarsh Gram’ by the respective State Governments. > The vision of an ‘Adarsh Gram' An ‘Adarsh Gram’ is one wherein people have access to various basic services so that the minimum needs of all the sections of society are fully met and disparities are reduced to a minimum. These villages would have all such infrastructure and their residents will have access to all such basic services that are necessary for a dignified living, creating thereby an environment in which everyone is enabled to utilize her/his potential to the fullest.
benefits: > Holistic Village Development Focuses on Scheduled Caste (SC)-majority villages. Aims to transform them into model villages with access to all basic services. > Financial Support ₹20 lakh per village for filling critical gaps in infrastructure and services. > Village Development Plan (VDP) A custom 5-year development plan based on baseline survey and needs. > Convergence of Schemes Integrates multiple central/state schemes like PMAY-G, MGNREGS, Ujjwala, SBM, etc. > Infrastructure Improvements Roads, electricity, sanitation, water, healthcare, schools, Anganwadis, etc. > Social Empowerment Promotes social harmony, inclusion, and awareness among SC communities. > Monitoring Framework Tracks progress across 50+ indicators in education, health, livelihoods, etc. > No Direct Cash Benefit Individuals benefit indirectly through improved village facilities and access to schemes.
eligibility: Village must have ≥50% Scheduled Caste (SC) population, but villages with ≥40% SC population may also be included in some states.. The village must be recognized in the latest Census data.. Ideally villages with ≥500 total population.. Villages already covered under PMAGY earlier phases may not be reselected..

faqs.question: What is the objective of the Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana (PMAGY)?
faqs.answer: The main objective of PMAGY is the integrated development of Scheduled Caste (SC) majority villages through the convergent implementation of existing schemes and additional support using gap-filling funds for unmet needs.

faqs.question: When was the PMAGY launched and in which states was it initially implemented?
faqs.answer: PMAGY was launched in 2009-10 on a pilot basis in 1,000 villages across five states : Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Bihar, Himachal Pradesh, and Assam.

faqs.question: What is the eligibility criteria for a village to be selected under PMAGY?
faqs.answer: Villages must: Have more than 50% SC population .- Have a total population greater than 500. Selection is done in descending order based on the percentage of SC population.

faqs.question: What is the vision of an ‘Adarsh Gram’?
faqs.answer: An Adarsh Gram is a model village where all residents have access to basic services like housing, sanitation, health, education, employment, and no caste-based discrimination , enabling them to live a life of dignity.

faqs.question: What kind of financial support is provided under PMAGY?
faqs.answer: Each selected village receives ₹20 lakh as Central Assistance under PMAGY for gap-filling activities not covered by existing schemes. The balance amount of ₹ 1 lakh per village would be for administrative and other expenses

faqs.question: What are the key focus areas of development under PMAGY?
faqs.answer: Development under PMAGY focuses on: Physical infrastructure (roads, electricity, water) Sanitation & environment Social infrastructure and human development Livelihood and skill development Social harmony and dignity

faqs.question: Are only Central Government schemes used for development under PMAGY?
faqs.answer: No. PMAGY emphasizes convergent implementation of both Central and State/UT Government schemes , along with gap-filling funds to cover uncovered areas.

faqs.question: What is meant by ‘gap-filling’ under PMAGY?
faqs.answer: ‘Gap-filling’ refers to activities and needs of the village that are not covered under existing schemes. PMAGY provides funds specifically to fulfill these unmet needs.

faqs.question: What are the benefits to residents of a PMAGY village?
faqs.answer: Residents benefit from: All-weather roads, safe drinking water, electricity Sanitary living conditions and solid waste management Functional schools, Anganwadi centers, health centers Skill training, employment opportunities, and social equality

faqs.question: How does PMAGY promote social harmony and inclusion?
faqs.answer: The scheme works to eliminate untouchability, caste-based discrimination , and promotes dignity, equal rights , and active community participation through institutions like Gram Sabha, Mahila Mandals, and Youth Clubs.

name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
description: The scheme "Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY)" was launched by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India. The component "Development of Scheduled Caste dominated villages into Adarsh Gram" aims to achieve integrated development of selected villages primarily through implementation of existing Central and State Government schemes in a convergent manner, ensuring access to quality services and infrastructure development in villages having Scheduled Caste population more than 40% and total population ≥ 500. The scheme provides Gap-filling funding of ₹20,00,000/- per village for infrastructure development and administrative expenses of ₹1,00,000/- per village for capacity building, awareness generation, need assessment, and Village Development Plan preparation. The scheme focuses on saturating 50 socio-economic developmental monitorable indicators across 10 domains including drinking water and sanitation, education, health and nutrition, social security, rural roads and housing, electricity and clean fuel, agricultural practices, financial inclusion, digitization, and livelihood and skill development.
benefits: Gap-filling Fund: ₹20,00,000/- per newly selected village for carrying out infrastructure developmental requirements which cannot be carried out through convergence with other schemes.- Administrative Expenses : ₹1,00,000/- per village for technical resource support, training and capacity building, awareness generation, publicity, and Management Information System development and maintenance.- Additional Round Funding: ₹9,50,000/- per village for Gap-filling component and ₹50,000/- for administrative expenses after completion of 5 years for continuous development.- Convergence Support: Access to 3 to 4 times of Gap-filling funds from existing Central and State Schemes or matching grants from State Governments.- Infrastructure Development: Development of adequate infrastructure necessary for socio-economic development including drinking water, sanitation, education, health, rural roads, housing, electricity facilities.- Capacity Building: Training and orientation programs for Village Level Convergence Committee members and other functionaries. Disbursement Direct transfer to State Governments and Union Territory Administrations, then to District Administrations. Released in two installments - First installment (₹80,000/- or ₹40,000/- as applicable) immediately on selection of villages; Second installment (₹20,00,000/- or ₹9,50,000/- as applicable) after Village Development Plan finalization. Administrative expenses released at beginning of financial year; Gap-filling funds released after Village Development Plan approval. Gap-filling funds to be utilized within 2 years from date of release; convergent implementation continues for additional 3 years. Conditions Villages must maintain Open Defecation Free status and achieve score of 70 or above on monitorable indicators for declaration as Adarsh Gram. Village Level Convergence Committee must conduct Need Assessment, data collection, gap analysis and prepare Village Development Plan in online mode. Village Development Plan must be approved by Gram Sabha and District Level Convergence Committee. State Governments and Union Territory Administrations must ensure convergence of at least 3 to 4 times of Gap-filling funds from other schemes. Monthly progress reporting on fulfilling infrastructure and individual needs through prescribed formats. Social audit by Gram Sabha at least once a year for transparency and better utilization. Real-time updating of progress in centralized Management Information System portal. Submission of utilization certificates in prescribed formats as per General Financial Rules 2017.
eligibility: The village must have more than 40% Scheduled Caste population as per the latest available Census data.. The village must have total population ≥ 500 as per the latest available Census data.. The village must be willing to participate in convergence implementation with other Central and State Government schemes.. The village must constitute Village Level Convergence Committee headed by Sarpanch or Pradhan of the village.. The village must complete Need Assessment exercise for all 50 monitorable indicators across 10 developmental domains.. The village must prepare comprehensive Village Development Plan through online portal https://pmagy.gov.in.. The village must obtain approval of Village Development Plan from Gram Sabha.. The village must get Village Development Plan approved by District Level Project Appraisal cum Convergence Committee.. The village should commit to utilize Gap-filling funds within 2 years from date of release.. The village should agree to continue convergent implementation for additional 3 years after fund utilization period.. Selection Process. Villages will be selected in descending order of their Scheduled Caste population percentage.. Priority. Villages having less than or equal to 40% Scheduled Caste population but overall high number of persons belonging to Scheduled Castes shall be taken up after covering eligible villages with more than 40% Scheduled Caste population..
