Registration Details Of Dairy Farm (Including Number Of Milch Animals, State Of Lactation, Milk Yield, Date Of Calving, And Address Of Cowshed Where Located).

faqs.question: What criteria define a "Bachat Gat," or group of farmers, for the specific purpose of participating in this particular scheme, even if the organization is not otherwise formally registered?
faqs.answer: A "Bachat Gat" means a group of two or more farmers who have come together for the common intention of taking benefits under the scheme, provided they register with the Directorate of Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services, Panaji-Goa.

faqs.question: Is it mandatory for farmers applying for this support to have an existing registration status within other relevant Government departments, such as Agriculture?
faqs.answer: Yes, applicants should mandatorily be registered with the Agricultural Department, ensuring their status as an Agriculturist is recorded under the Agricultural Database.

faqs.question: If I am already registered as a beneficiary, am I strictly prohibited from purchasing milk from other individuals or farms and subsequently supplying it to my group?
faqs.answer: Yes, you are strictly prohibited from procuring milk from others and pouring it to the Dairy Co-operative Society, Bachat Gat, or Self Help Group in your name.

faqs.question: Does the individual dairy farmer need a separate registration with the Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services, apart from the farm registration itself?
faqs.answer: Yes, the farmer must be individually registered with the Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services and also register their physical Dairy Farm through the respective Veterinary Dispensary or Hospital.

faqs.question: What specific requirements must my bank account meet in order to successfully receive the monthly composite subsidy payments under this initiative?
faqs.answer: The beneficiary shall open a Bank account in any Bank that has a core banking system or Electronic Clearing System (ECS) to facilitate the payment transfer.

faqs.question: When registering my farm, what detailed factual information about my animals and premises must I provide to the Department of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services?
faqs.answer: You must provide details of the number of animals, the state of lactation of each animal, milk yield, date of calving, and the address of the cowshed where the animals are located.

faqs.question: What form of documentation is required by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services to confirm my status as a recognized member of a registered group?
faqs.answer: The farmer intending to avail of the benefit will have to produce evidence of their membership to a registered Dairy Co-operative Society, Bachat Gat, or Self Help Group as may be required by the Department.

faqs.question: Who are the primary individuals or groups identified as the target recipients for the application of this particular scheme for milk production development?
faqs.answer: The scheme applies exclusively to farmers from Goa who are members of registered Dairy Co-operative Societies, Bachat Gats, or Self Help Groups registered with the Department of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services.

faqs.question: Do I need to demonstrate a minimum period of residency within the State of Goa before becoming eligible to apply for these producer benefits?
faqs.answer: Yes, the farmer must be a bona fide resident of Goa for at least the preceding five years to meet the eligibility criteria.

faqs.question: Is it sufficient for me to simply be a member of any Dairy Co-operative Society, or must the society itself meet a specific government registration requirement?
faqs.answer: The farmer must be a member of the Dairy Co-operative Society, Bachat Gat, or Self Help Group that is mandatorily registered with the Department of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services.

faqs.question: Is possessing and producing a specific identity verification document, such as a Unique Identification card, an absolute prerequisite for receiving the benefits?
faqs.answer: Yes, it shall be mandatory to produce the Unique Identification (UID) card for obtaining any benefit offered under the scheme.

faqs.question: In addition to residing in the state, is it necessary for the applicant to physically own specific infrastructure related to housing the milch animals?
faqs.answer: Yes, the applicant must own a cattle shed with milch animals, and this infrastructure must be located within the State of Goa.

faqs.question: Is there a restriction on where the milk I intend to supply for incentives must originate, specifically regarding the source of the production?
faqs.answer: The incentives apply only to the milk supplied by the members, and this milk must be produced at the beneficiary’s own Dairy Farm.

faqs.question: To which specific organizational entities must the beneficiary supply their produced milk in order for that quantity to qualify for the composite subsidy payments?
faqs.answer: The incentives shall apply to the milk supplied by the members exclusively to the Dairy Co-operative Society, Bachat Gat, or Self Help Group as officially notified for the scheme by the Government from time to time.

name: Rajya Samekit Sahkari Vikas Yojana - Ganga Gaay Mahila Dairy Yojana
description: The “Ganga Gaay Mahila Dairy Yojana” is implemented under the Rajya Samekit Sahkari Vikas Yojana by the Department of Dairy Development, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to promote dairy entrepreneurship among women, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and general category members of cooperative societies by providing financial assistance through subsidies and loans for the purchase of milch cows and buffaloes.
benefits: The following benefits are provided to members of milk-producing cooperative societies for purchasing cows or buffaloes:: For members of the general category: A grant of 50% and a loan of 40% is approved through the District Cooperative Bank for the establishment of a unit of 2, 3, and 5 dairy animals (including animal purchase, insurance, transportation expenses, cattle shed, milk van, etc.), and the remaining 10% is borne by the beneficiary. The dairy department will provide a grant of ₹80,000 for 2 animals, ₹1,23,250 for 3 animals, and ₹2,03,625 for 5 animals. For Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and women members (of any caste): For the establishment of units for 2, 3 and 5 dairy animals (covering animal purchase, insurance, transportation, cattle shed including calf, milk van, etc.), a 75% grant and a 25% loan are approved through the District Cooperative Bank. The dairy department will provide funds of ₹1,20,000/- for 2 animals, ₹1,84,875/- for 3 animals, and ₹3,05,438/- for 5 animals. A minimum of 2 animals must be purchased, and taking a loan is mandatory to receive the subsidy.
eligibility: The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.. The applicant must be a member of a milk-producing cooperative society. (Individuals who are not currently members can become eligible by joining a cooperative society.). The applicant must belong to the General, Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, or Women category.. The applicant must intend to purchase cows (with a minimum milk yield of 12 liters per day) or buffaloes (with a minimum milk yield of 10 liters per day).. The applicant must purchase animals from outside the state.. The applicant must purchase a minimum of two (2) animals.. To avail of the subsidy, it is mandatory to take a loan for the purchase of milch animals..
documents: Aadhaar card Bank account details Caste certificate (if applicable) Cooperative society membership number (if applicable) Movable/immovable property or land certificate (if applicable) Two guarantors (if required) Loan details, if any Other supporting documents as required
Movable/immovable property or land certificate (if applicable)

faqs.question: Who are eligible beneficiaries?
faqs.answer: Women, Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST), and general category members of milk-producing cooperative societies are eligible.

faqs.question: Is membership in a cooperative society mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, applicants must be members of a milk cooperative society. Non-members can become eligible by joining the society and paying a membership fee of ₹25.

faqs.question: What is the minimum age for membership?
faqs.answer: Applicants must be 18 years or older.

faqs.question: What types of animals can be purchased under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Applicants can purchase cows (minimum 12 liters/day milk yield) or buffaloes (minimum 10 liters/day milk yield).

faqs.question: What is the minimum number of animals to be purchased?
faqs.answer: A minimum of two animals is required.

faqs.question: Is it mandatory to take a loan to avail the subsidy?
faqs.answer: Yes, taking a loan is compulsory to receive the subsidy.

faqs.question: Where can applicants get the application form?
faqs.answer: From the milk cooperative society or the nearest District Cooperative Bank.

faqs.question: Who certifies the application?
faqs.answer: The Committee Secretary certifies the application after verifying details.

faqs.question: Who provides recommendations for the application?
faqs.answer: The Manager/Chief Manager of the Milk Producers Cooperative Union Ltd. and the Assistant Director of Dairy provide recommendations after scrutiny.

name: Rotavator/Thresher Machine Equipment Assistance Scheme
description: The “Rotavator/Thresher Machine Equipment Assistance Scheme” was launched by the Tribal Development Department, Government of Gujarat. The scheme aims to strengthen agricultural mechanization and improve the productivity of Scheduled Tribe farmers in tribal areas. Under this scheme, tribal farmers are provided with financial assistance to purchase essential farm machinery such as a 6-feet rotavator or a thresher machine, which they cannot afford due to poor economic conditions.
benefits: Financial assistance to farmers to purchase a rotavator (6 feet) or a thresher machine.
eligibility: The applicant should be a farmer. The applicant should belong to the Scheduled Tribes (ST) category.. The applicant should belong to a Below Poverty Line (BPL) family.. The applicant should be a resident of tribal or forest areas of Gujarat.. The applicant should be a farmer dependent on agriculture as the main source of livelihood.. The applicant should intend to use the machinery for self-employment and agricultural purposes..
documents: size Photos Ration Card 7/12 Certificate Bank Passbook/Cancelled Cheque Death Certificate PH Identity Card Widow Certificate

faqs.question: Who can apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Scheduled Tribe farmers from BPL families living in tribal or forest areas.

faqs.question: What equipment is covered under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The equipment is covered: a rotavator (6 feet) and a thresher machine.

faqs.question: What is the main objective of this scheme?
faqs.answer: To promote agricultural mechanization and support poor tribal farmers.

faqs.question: Is the scheme available to urban farmers?
faqs.answer: No, it is only for tribal and forest area farmers.

faqs.question: Can non-tribal farmers apply?
faqs.answer: No, only Scheduled Tribe farmers are eligible.

faqs.question: What documents are required?
faqs.answer: Aadhaar Card, Caste Certificate, 7/12 Certificate, Bank Passbook, Ration Card, Photos, and special certificates if applicable.

faqs.question: Is the application process offline?
faqs.answer: No, the application process is online.

faqs.question: What is the application fee?
faqs.answer: The application is free of cost.

faqs.question: Where can I apply?
faqs.answer: At the official D-SAG Sahay Portal: https://dsagsahay.gujarat.gov.in/

name: Silk Tree Plantation
description: The scheme “Silk Tree Plantation” was launched by the Department of Sericulture, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to promote mulberry cultivation and silkworm rearing among farmers in Uttarakhand by providing financial assistance, technical support, and organized cluster-based sericulture activities to enhance their income and livelihood.
benefits: Under this scheme, selected farmers in a cluster receive a grant of ₹17,244/- for silk tree plantations, and 2-silk trees are provided free of cost by the department.
eligibility: The beneficiary must be a resident of Uttarakhand.. The beneficiary must belong to a cluster or group.. In mountainous areas, a minimum of 25 farmers is required for a cluster, while in plain areas, at least 50 farmers are mandatory.. The beneficiaries in the group must have land available for the plantation of at least 300 plants.. Silkworm rearing is conducted under departmental supervision. Therefore, clusters must be selected within a 15–20 km radius of departmental silkworm farms. If the distance exceeds this, the selected group must provide one acre of land for a collective rearing center and may conduct silkworm rearing after receiving training.. Priority is given to farmers who already practice sericulture or those who have mulberry saplings available. Mulberry silkworm rearing can be carried out up to an altitude of 4,000 feet, although warmer valley areas are more suitable for this activity.. The department has not specified any particular regions for silkworm rearing. however, most state-run sericulture farms were established in locations where mulberry silk production is feasible..
documents: Voter ID Card or Ration Card Bank Account Details Land Documents / Ownership Proof Photographs of the Plantation Area Other supporting documents as required
Voter ID Card or Ration Card

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme is open to resident farmers of Uttarakhand who belong to a cluster or group and have land available for plantation. Priority is given to farmers already practicing sericulture or those with mulberry saplings.

faqs.question: How is a beneficiary cluster defined?
faqs.answer: A cluster consists of a minimum of 25 farmers in mountainous areas and 50 farmers in plain areas, with each cluster having land for at least 300 plants.

faqs.question: What financial assistance is provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Selected farmers in a cluster receive a grant of ₹17,244 for silk tree plantations.

faqs.question: How is silkworm rearing conducted?
faqs.answer: Silkworm rearing is carried out under departmental supervision in the Chowki centers or on individual farms within 15–20 km of departmental silkworm farms.

faqs.question: What is the suitable altitude for mulberry sericulture?
faqs.answer: Mulberry sericulture can be practiced up to an altitude of 4,000 feet, with warm valley areas being most suitable.

faqs.question: Are there any specific areas selected for sericulture by the department?
faqs.answer: No, the department has not designated specific areas, but most state-run silkworm farms are established where mulberry sericulture is feasible.

faqs.question: How are beneficiaries selected?
faqs.answer: Beneficiaries are selected through publicity seminars and meetings organized by representatives of cooperative societies or silk self-help groups affiliated with Chowki centers.

faqs.question: Who provides technical assistance during plantation and silkworm rearing?
faqs.answer: All activities are carried out with the technical assistance of departmental personnel.

faqs.question: When are grant funds disbursed to farmers?
faqs.answer: Grant funds are provided after completion of plantation and silkworm rearing work, under supervision and verification by departmental staff.

name: Rythu Bima Scheme
description: Rythu Bima is a social security initiative of the Government of Telangana launched on 14th August 2018, aimed at providing financial support to the families of farmers in the event of the farmer's untimely death. The main objective of the scheme to ensure financial security to the families of deceased farmers by offering life insurance coverage for both natural and accidental deaths.
benefits: Insurance Coverage: ₹5,00,000/- per eligible farmer- Coverage Type: Natural and accidental deaths- Claim Settlement Mode: Direct bank transfer to the nominee’s account- Claim Process: Entirely online, farmer families are not required to visit any office
eligibility: The applicant must be a farmer.. The applicant must be a resident of Telangana.. The applicant must be aged between 18 and 59 years.. The applicant’s details should be available in the Dharani database under RoR (Record of Rights) land records.. The applicant should possess a valid Pattadar Pass Book (PPB) or a RoFR (Recognition of Forest Rights) Patta..
documents: Death Certificate. Identity Proof of the deceased farmer. Nominee’s ID Proof. Pattadar Passbook copy. Bank details of the nominee. Other supporting documents, if required.
Identity Proof of the deceased farmer.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to enroll in the Rythu Bima Scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers aged between 18 to 59 years, residing in Telangana, and holding a Pattadar Passbook (PPB) or RoFR Patta are eligible.

faqs.question: Is enrolment under the Rythu Bima Scheme mandatory?
faqs.answer: No, the scheme is voluntary and open to all eligible farmers.

faqs.question: Is there any premium payment required from the farmer?
faqs.answer: No, the entire premium is paid by the Government of Telangana.

faqs.question: What is the insurance coverage provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides a life insurance cover of ₹5,00,000 for both natural and accidental death.

faqs.question: Which organization provides the insurance coverage?
faqs.answer: The Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) is the insurance partner for the scheme.

faqs.question: How is registration carried out under the Rythu Bima Scheme?
faqs.answer: Registration is facilitated through the Agriculture Extension Officer (AEO) who enters the farmer’s data into the Rythu Bima online portal.

faqs.question: What documents are required for registration?
faqs.answer: Required documents include the Pattadar Passbook (PPB)/RoFR Patta, identity proof, and nominee details.

faqs.question: Is the claim process offline or online?
faqs.answer: How are land ownership details verified during registration?

faqs.question: What documents are required for registration?
faqs.answer: Required documents include the Pattadar Passbook (PPB)/RoFR Patta, identity proof, and nominee details.

faqs.question: How is the claim amount disbursed?
faqs.answer: Upon successful verification, the ₹5,00,000 claim amount is directly transferred to the nominee’s bank account, and an SMS confirmation is sent.

faqs.question: Is SMS notification provided during the registration and claim process?
faqs.answer: Yes, SMS alerts are sent to the farmer or nominee at each key stage, including LIC ID generation and claim status.

faqs.question: What is the objective of the "Scheme of Assistance for Common Environment Infrastructure"?
faqs.answer: The scheme "Scheme of Assistance for Common Environment Infrastructure" under the Gujarat Industrial Policy aims to provide incentives for environmental compliance to ensure long-term economic and ecological balance.

faqs.question: What is the objective of the "Scheme of Assistance for Strengthening the Regulation and Environmental Compliance" component?
faqs.answer: The component aims to support environmental sustainability by funding scientific research, pollution control initiatives, environmental monitoring, and capacity-building programs.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Industries, industrial associations, government agencies, public sector undertakings (PSUs), and other eligible institutions involved in environmental management can apply for assistance.

faqs.question: What types of projects are supported under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Scientific report/ Pilot projects on cleaner production and technology through institutions such as IITs, NITs, Science & Engineering Colleges of the State, Scientific and R & D institutions and GPCB/GEMI/GCPC are supported under this scheme.

faqs.question: What is the maximum financial assistance provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides need-based financial assistance of up to [?]50,00,000/- per project, subject to approval by the State Level Empowered Committee (SLEC).

faqs.question: What kind of research projects can receive funding?
faqs.answer: The scheme funds research projects focused on cleaner production technologies, environmental impact assessment, pollution control methods, and real-time environmental monitoring systems.

faqs.question: What are environment clinics under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Environment clinics serve as platforms where industry representatives, environmental professionals, and experts collaborate to find cost-effective solutions to environmental challenges in real time.

faqs.question: Can multiple institutions collaborate on a single project?
faqs.answer: Yes, the scheme encourages collaboration between multiple institutions, including IITs, NITs, R&D organizations, and government bodies, to enhance the effectiveness of environmental projects.

faqs.question: What is the role of the State Level Empowered Committee (SLEC)?
faqs.answer: SLEC is responsible for reviewing project proposals, approving financial assistance, and ensuring that the projects align with environmental compliance goals.

faqs.question: Are training and skill development programs eligible for funding?
faqs.answer: Yes, the scheme provides financial assistance for establishing training centers and conducting skill development programs for industry professionals, instructors, and operators.

faqs.question: What is the objective of the "Scheme of Assistance for Common Environment Infrastructure"?
faqs.answer: The scheme "Scheme of Assistance for Common Environment Infrastructure" under the Gujarat Industrial Policy aims to provide incentives for environmental compliance to ensure long-term economic and ecological balance.

faqs.question: What is the objective of the "Scheme for Development of Green Estate" component?
faqs.answer: The purpose of the component is to facilitate the relocation or retrofitting of polluting industrial units to designated green estates, thereby improving environmental sustainability and compliance with pollution control norms.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Any institution or group of industries that operates polluting industrial units and has received a recommendation from the Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB) for relocation or retrofitting is eligible to apply for the scheme.

faqs.question: Who appoints the professional agency for feasibility studies?
faqs.answer: The Industries Commissioner, based on the recommendation of GPCB, appoints a professional agency to assess pollution load, effluent quality, and the environmental benefits of relocating polluting industries.

faqs.question: What types of expenses are covered under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme covers expenses related to infrastructure development, including internal roads, power distribution lines, water supply systems, sewage and drainage lines, effluent treatment facilities, and other approved facilities necessary for the green estate.

faqs.question: What is the role of the State Level Expert Committee (SLEC) in the scheme?
faqs.answer: The State Level Expert Committee (SLEC) reviews the feasibility study report submitted by the professional agency and decides whether to approve the relocation or retrofitting project.

faqs.question: Can an industry apply for the scheme without a recommendation from GPCB?
faqs.answer: No, industries cannot apply for the scheme without a formal recommendation from GPCB. The recommendation is essential for determining the necessity of relocation or retrofitting.

faqs.question: What happens after SLEC approves the project?
faqs.answer: Once the project is approved by SLEC, the eligible institution or industrial group can proceed with the relocation or retrofitting process and begin developing the necessary infrastructure within the green estate.

faqs.question: Can an industry relocate independently without financial assistance from the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, an industry can relocate independently. However, financial assistance under the scheme is only available for industries that receive GPCB's recommendation and SLEC's approval for relocation.

faqs.question: What is the main benefit of relocating to a green estate under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The main benefit of relocating to a green estate is the opportunity to operate in an environmentally sustainable manner with improved infrastructure, better compliance with pollution norms, and financial support for essential facilities.

name: Scheme to Assist for Infrastructural Facilities for Gaushalas & Panjrapole
department: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department
description: The “Scheme to Assist for Infrastructural Facilities for Gaushalas & Panjrapole” launched by the Department of Agriculture, Farmers Welfare & Co-operation, Government of Gujarat, aims to provide financial aid to registered gaushalas and panjrapoles for building essential infrastructure like cattle sheds, water facilities, and storage areas, ensuring better care for non-productive livestock.
benefits: Financial assistance of up to 75% of the total cost or ₹4,00,000/-, whichever is lower, for each of the following: Cattle Shed. Compound Wall. Grass Godown. Water Bore (Electric Motor / Submersible Pump). Overhead or Underground Water Tank. > Note: The benefit of this scheme will be available to an organization for a period of five years for different purpose-components.
eligibility: Any panjarapol and gaushala of the state registered under Public Charity Act.. At least 3 (three) acres of land on which the organization has to construct the development work, must be in the name of the organization or on lease of 99 years. There is no limit on the maximum land.. A gaushala must have more than 50 cows of local origin While Panjarapol must have more than 100 livestock..
documents: rights land records (own/lease land). Lease agreement (minimum 99 years, if applicable). Estimate and plan/map of the proposed construction work (as per taluka S.O.R.). Registration certificate under the Public Charity Act. Any other documents as required.
Copy of 7/12, 8-A, and 6-rights land records (own/lease land).
Estimate and plan/map of the proposed construction work (as per taluka S.O.R.).
Registration certificate under the Public Charity Act.

faqs.question: What is the objective of the "Scheme to Assist for Infrastructural Facilities for Gaushalas & Panjrapole"?
faqs.answer: The scheme aims to support animal welfare organizations like gaushalas and panjrapoles by offering financial assistance for the development and construction of essential infrastructure.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Any gaushala or panjrapole that is registered under the Public Charity Act and meets the specified land and livestock requirements is eligible to apply for the scheme.

faqs.question: What type of financial assistance is provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides up to 75% of the total cost or a maximum of ₹4.00 lakh for each infrastructure component such as cattle sheds, compound walls, water facilities, and storage units.

faqs.question: Can an organization apply for multiple infrastructure components at once?
faqs.answer: An organization can apply for different components, but financial assistance will be granted for only one component in a given year.

faqs.question: Is it necessary for the organization to own the land where construction will take place?
faqs.answer: No, the organization may either own the land or have it leased for a minimum of 99 years to qualify for the scheme.

faqs.question: Is the benefit of the scheme available more than once?
faqs.answer: Yes, the organization can reapply for assistance for a different component after a minimum of five years.

faqs.question: What does S.O.R. mean in the construction documentation?
faqs.answer: S.O.R. stands for Schedule of Rates, which refers to the standard government-approved rates used to estimate construction costs.

faqs.question: Is there a maximum land limit for eligibility under the scheme?
faqs.answer: No, there is no maximum land limit, but the organization must have at least 3 acres of land.

faqs.question: Where can the application for this scheme be submitted?
faqs.answer: Applications must be submitted online through the iKhedut (https://ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in/)portal, followed by submission of printed applications with signatures and required documents to the board.

faqs.question: Is any official verification required after submitting the online application?
faqs.answer: Yes, the printed application must be signed and stamped by both the local veterinary officer and the nodal officer of the Gujarat Gauseva and Gauchar Vikas Board.

faqs.question: What is the deadline for submitting the physical copy of the application and documents?
faqs.answer: All required documents must be submitted to the board within 30 days from the date of the online application.

name: Semi-Commercial Duck Farming
department: Fisheries and Animal Resources Development Department
description: The scheme “Semi-Commercial Duck Farming” started under the State Sector Scheme "Encouragement of Commercial Poultry Entrepreneur and Promotion of Backyard Poultry Production" to support small entrepreneurs in setting up Duck farms with a capacity of 1000 ducks. Under this new State plan scheme, individual farmers will be supported for taking up semi-commercial duck rearing with a subsidy of 40% subsidy. Aim: The scheme aims to support 100 individual farmers in setting up semi-commercial duckery units with a capacity of 1000 ducks per unit. Objective: To strengthen the local production systems for enhancing livelihoods and for the generation of additional income among the farmers through duck rearing. To support nutritional requirements through the production of animal protein. To build the capacity of farmers for undertaking semi-commercial duck farming as a profitable enterprise.
benefits: The individual beneficiary will be provided a maximum of 40% subsidy. Training will be organized at the Block Head Quarter level or any other convenient place after the final approval of the list. Each beneficiary will be trained on recommended management practices on feeding and watering, brooding and rearing young ducks, record keeping, etc. The concerned Livestock Inspectors, Gomitras and PraniMitras will guide the beneficiaries in field for managing the duck units. Routine vaccination of birds on a priority basis. The Block Veterinary Officer (BVO) will provide all technical guidance to the farmer for maintaining proper veterinary health care and immunization of the ducks. The beneficiary shall directly procure quality ducklings from reputed sources which will be facilitated by the respective BVOs. Note: The subsidy will be released in two phases through DBT mode to the individual beneficiary. The 1st installment of 40% of the eligible subsidy will be released after the construction of the duck shed and 2nd installment of the eligible subsidy shall be released after the stocking of ducklings.
eligibility: The applicant should be a permanent resident of Odisha.. Individuals, farmers, and entrepreneurs will be eligible to avail of support under the scheme.. All beneficiaries covered under the Scheme should mandatorily be Aadhaar linked to avoid duplication.. The beneficiaries who have availed of subsidy previously in a similar scheme should not be included..

size photograph Land document/lease deed photocopy

name: Scheme for Conservation and Development of Indigenous Cattle and Murrah Development
description: The scheme “Scheme for Conservation and Development of Indigenous Cattle and Murrah Development” is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of Haryana with the objective of encouraging the farmers for conservation and development of the Indigenous breeds of cows and buffaloes. > Long-term objectives: Conservation and up-gradation of valuable indigenous germplasm available in the State of Haryana. Increase in milk production and overall productivity. > Medium-term objectives (5 years Horizon): Identification of top-quality germplasm of indigenous breeds of Cow and buffalo and their insemination with high-quality semen for sustainable genetic improvement. Encouraging the farmers to rear and breed high-yielding animals of genetic merit. > Description of Scheme: Murrah buffaloes meeting the benchmark of 18 kg daily peak yield would be properly identified (with ear tags) along with their progeny. Cash incentives ranging from ₹15,000/- to ₹30,000/- would be provided to owners of these buffaloes. Haryana, Sahiwal and Belahi cows, meeting the benchmark of 8 kg, 10 kg, and 5 Kg peak yield respectively would be properly identified (with ear tags) along with their progeny. The cash incentives ranging from ₹5,000/- to ₹20,000/- would be provided to owners of these cows. The beneficiaries will be under obligation not to sell the buffalo/cow and its progeny for at least one year as the main objective of scheme is to conserve the indigenous breeds of Cow and buffalo. The identified animals would be insured and part of insurance premium will be borne under the prevailing insurance scheme if any, and rest will be paid by the beneficiary as per insurance scheme. If no Livestock Insurance Scheme is in operation then the beneficiary would have to arrange for the insurance of the animals on its own and the insurance premium shall be paid by the beneficiary.
benefits: Cash incentives at the following rates in different slabs would be provided to the owners of the recorded Murrah Buffaloes as below: Sl. No. Slabs of Lactation yield in Kg (Peak Yield in Kg) Incentive Money (₹) 118 to 22 Kg₹15,000/-2>22 to 25 Kg₹20,000/-3Above 25 Kg₹30,000/- 2. Cash incentives at the following rates in different slabs would be provided to the owners of the recorded Cows of different Indigenous breeds as below: (Hariana Cows) Sl. No. Slabs of peak Yield in Kg Incentive Money (₹) 18 to 10 Kg₹10,000/-2>10 to 12 Kg₹15,000/-3Above 12 Kg₹20,000/- 3. Sahiwal Cows Sl. No. Slabs of peak Yield in Kg Incentive Money (₹) 110 to 12 Kg₹10,000/-2>12 to 15 Kg₹15,000/-3Above 15 Kg₹20,000/- 4. Belahi Cows Sl. No. Slabs of peak Yield in Kg Incentive Money (₹) 15 to 8 Kg₹5,000/-2>8 to 10 Kg₹10,000/-3Above 10 Kg₹15,000/-In lieu of the cash incentive provided, the owner would be under obligation not to sell the recorded Indigenous Cow/Murrah Buffalo and its male progeny at least for one year. The beneficiary would be further bound to look after the male calf properly and the Department will have the first right to purchase it. In case, the beneficiary does not abide by the contract i.e. disposes of the identified Indigenous Cow/Murrah Buffalo and/or its male calf, he would not be eligible for the cash incentive. The owners of the recorded cows/buffaloes would be required to breed their animals through artificial insemination by the Government.
eligibility: The applicant must be a resident of Haryana.. The applicant must be of the age of 18 - 55 years.. A Cow or Buffalo eligible to be recorded must be between 05 to 75 days of the date of its Calving as on date of application.. A maximum of two milch animals (two Cows or Two Buffaloes or One Cow and One Buffalo) per applicant/beneficiary would be eligible for the incentive money under this scheme.. The cows must be true to Hariana, Sahiwal, or Belahi breed and buffalo must be of Murrah Breed only.. Incentive for a particular animal could be provided only twice in its life span i.e. if the incentive is provided to a beneficiary for a particular animal twice, such beneficiary would stand debarred for receiving an incentive for that animal in its subsequent calving in the future.. The scheme is individual beneficiary-oriented.. Note 01: A maximum of two milch animals per applicant will be eligible for the incentive money under this scheme. However, the recordings of more than two buffaloes/Cows of an applicant may be carried out for collecting data of the top quality Murrah buffaloes/Indigenous cattle (Hariana, Sahiwal, and Belahi). But incentive money would be provided only for two animals (in the highest slabs) of that applicant in a particular year.. Note 02: In case an applicant lives at a place other than where the animals are kept or intended to be kept, than the jurisdiction area will be the place where animals are kept (Within state of Haryana only).
documents: Copy of Bank Passbook or Cancelled Cheque

faqs.question: What is the objective of the scheme?
faqs.answer: The primary objective is to encourage farmers in Haryana to conserve and develop indigenous breeds of cows and buffaloes.

faqs.question: Who implements the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of Haryana.

faqs.question: What are the long-term goals of the scheme?
faqs.answer: The long-term goals include the conservation and upgrading of valuable indigenous germplasm and increasing milk production and overall productivity.

faqs.question: What are the medium-term goals of the scheme?
faqs.answer: The medium-term goals (within five years) include identifying top-quality germplasm of indigenous breeds and encouraging farmers to rear high-yielding animals of genetic merit.

faqs.question: How are the Murrah buffaloes identified under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Murrah buffaloes meeting a daily peak yield benchmark of 18 kg are identified with ear tags, along with their progeny.

faqs.question: What incentives are provided for Murrah buffalo owners?
faqs.answer: Cash incentives ranging from [?]15,000 to [?]30,000 are provided to owners of identified Murrah buffaloes.

faqs.question: How are Hariana, Sahiwal, and Belahi cows identified under the scheme?
faqs.answer: These cows meeting benchmarks of 8 kg (Hariana), 10 kg (Sahiwal), and 5 kg (Belahi) daily peak yield are identified with ear tags, along with their progeny.

faqs.question: What is the obligation of the beneficiaries under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Beneficiaries are obliged not to sell the identified animals and their progeny for at least one year.

faqs.question: Are the identified animals insured under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, identified animals are insured, and part of the insurance premium is borne under the prevailing insurance scheme, with the rest paid by the beneficiary.

faqs.question: What breeds of cows are eligible under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Only Hariana, Sahiwal, and Belahi breeds are eligible.

faqs.question: What breed of buffalo is eligible under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Only the Murrah breed is eligible.

faqs.question: What is the age eligibility for applicants?
faqs.answer: Applicants must be between 18 and 55 years old.

faqs.question: How many animals can an applicant register under the scheme?
faqs.answer: A maximum of two milch animals (two cows, two buffaloes, or one cow and one buffalo) per applicant are eligible for incentives.

faqs.question: How many times can an incentive be provided for a particular animal?
faqs.answer: Incentives can be provided only twice in an animal's lifespan.

faqs.question: Can organizations apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: No, the scheme is for individual beneficiaries only.

faqs.question: How can one apply online for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Applications can be submitted online via the Antyodaya-SARAL Portal. https://saralharyana.gov.in/

faqs.question: Where can applications be submitted?
faqs.answer: Applications can be submitted on the Antyodaya-SARAL Portal or through Common Service Centres, Antodaya Kendra, Atal Sewa Kendra, and e-disha Centres.

faqs.question: What is the jurisdiction for applicants living in a different place than where the animals are kept?
faqs.answer: The jurisdiction area is the place where the animals are kept within Haryana.

faqs.question: What are the residency requirements for applicants?
faqs.answer: Applicants must be residents of Haryana.

name: State Integrated Cooperative Development Project - Fisheries Sector
description: The “State Integrated Cooperative Development Project” was introduced by the Department of Fisheries, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to promote sustainable fisheries development in Uttarakhand by facilitating the establishment and expansion of cooperative-based fisheries projects in both mountainous and plain regions.
benefits: Under the scheme, the following support is provided: Options for setting up large loan-based projects in both mountainous and plain areas are available for individuals or groups engaged in fisheries through cooperative societies. Facilities are provided for trout farming, angling, and retail outlets on a cluster basis in mountainous districts, and for Pangasius farming, major carp farming, and integrated fisheries in plain districts. Under the project, the cooperative societies will bear 10% of the contribution, while 70% is provided as a loan and 20% as a grant. The project assists the societies in preparing their Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) or Business Development Plans (BDPs) and organizes free training and capacity-building programs periodically. Support is provided for marketing and sale of fish produced by the societies.
eligibility: The applicant must be a cooperative society engaged in fisheries sector.. The cooperative society must be registered in Uttarakhand..
documents: Registration Certificate of the Cooperative Society Resolution Copy Detailed Project Report (DPR) or Business Development Plan (BDP) Bank Account Details Other supporting document as required
Registration Certificate of the Cooperative Society
Detailed Project Report (DPR) or Business Development Plan (BDP)

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Only fisheries-based cooperative societies registered in Uttarakhand under the Uttaranchal Cooperative Act, 2003 (as amended) are eligible to apply.

faqs.question: What types of fisheries projects are supported under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme supports projects such as trout farming, angling, and retail outlets in mountainous districts, and Pangasius farming, major carp farming, and integrated fisheries projects in plain districts.

faqs.question: What is the financial structure of the project?
faqs.answer: Under the project, 70% of the cost is provided as a loan, 20% as a grant, and 10% as a contribution from the cooperative society itself.

faqs.question: What is the current interest rate on the loan amount?
faqs.answer: Currently, the interest rate is 9.61% per annum. However, it may vary from time to time as per NCDC guidelines.

faqs.question: What is the repayment period for the loan?
faqs.answer: The loan amount must generally be repaid within eight years, subject to changes made periodically by NCDC.

faqs.question: Are societies required to prepare project documents before applying?
faqs.answer: Yes. Each cooperative society must prepare a Detailed Project Report (DPR) or Business Development Plan (BDP) while submitting its application.

faqs.question: How can a cooperative society apply for the project?
faqs.answer: The society must submit its proposed work estimate along with the DPR/BDP to the District Assistant Director of Fisheries or the District Fisheries In-Charge.

faqs.question: What is the process of project selection?
faqs.answer: Submitted DPRs/BDPs are evaluated at the district and state levels. Societies found suitable are selected under the project.

faqs.question: How are funds disbursed to the selected societies?
faqs.answer: Funds are released in installments based on the progress of the project and compliance with the prescribed conditions.

name: PMMSY: Construction of Fish Kiosks Including Kiosks of Aquarium/Ornamental Fish-Haryana

name: PMMSY: Construction of New ponds for Saline /Alkaline areas-Haryana
description: The scheme "Pradhan Mantri Matasya Sampada Yojana: Construction of New Ponds for Saline/Alkaline Areas" by the Department of Fisheries, Government of Haryana, aims to expand fisheries in various urban and semi-urban areas. Through this scheme, subsidies for the construction of new ponds and central financial assistance for the initial fish crop on newly constructed ponds are provided to beneficiaries. The scheme considers ponds with a long duration and a registered lease period of at least 7 years for grants.
benefits: The project cost is ₹8,00,000/- per hectare. The subsidy is limited to 40% of the project cost for the General Category and 60% of the project cost for Scheduled Caste (SC) and women beneficiaries.
eligibility: The applicant should have a Parivar Pehchan Patra (PPP).. The construction of new ponds subsidy will be provided by the state government for the expansion of fisheries in various urban/semi-urban areas only under the construction of new ponds under the Pradhan Mantri Matasya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) scheme.. Only central financial assistance will be provided to the beneficiaries for the initial fish crop only on the fertiliser of newly constructed ponds.. Central financial assistance on the construction of new ponds will be provided only on ponds prepared for fisheries.. Under this scheme, ponds whose pond duration will be for a long time, and the registered lease period will be at least 7 years, will be considered for a grant on those ponds..
documents: Agreement Deed (between the beneficiary and the Fisheries Department). Date of Birth Certificate (Voting Card/Birth Certificate/Aadhar Card/Matriculation Certificate). Caste Certificate (from first
class Magistrate/Tehsildar). Training Certificate (of beneficiary). Land Record (from Tehsil

Jamabandi, Nakal Akshizra Farad) or Registered Lease Deed of Minimum 7 Years. Bills/Receipts/Vouchers. Photographs of the Pond with the Beneficiary. Details of Bank Account and PAN Card. Detailed Project Report (DPR)/Self Contained Proposal (SCP) (as per Pradhan Mantri Matasya Sampada Yojana guidelines).
Agreement Deed (between the beneficiary and the Fisheries Department).
Date of Birth Certificate (Voting Card/Birth Certificate/Aadhar Card/Matriculation Certificate).
Land Record (from Tehsil - Own Land-Jamabandi, Nakal Akshizra Farad) or Registered Lease Deed of Minimum 7 Years.
Photographs of the Pond with the Beneficiary.
Details of Bank Account and PAN Card.
Detailed Project Report (DPR)/Self Contained Proposal (SCP) (as per Pradhan Mantri Matasya Sampada Yojana guidelines).

faqs.question: What is the main objective of this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme aims to provide a subsidy for the construction of new ponds for the expansion of fisheries in various urban/semi-urban areas.

faqs.question: What kind of financial assistance is provided for the initial fish crop?
faqs.answer: Only central financial assistance will be provided to the beneficiaries for the initial fish crop on the fertiliser of newly constructed ponds.

faqs.question: What is the minimum registered lease period required for a pond to be considered for a grant?
faqs.answer: The registered lease period must be at least 7 years.

faqs.question: What is the subsidy rate for beneficiaries belonging to the General Category?
faqs.answer: For the General Category, the subsidy will be limited to 40% of the project cost.

faqs.question: What is the subsidy rate for women beneficiaries?
faqs.answer: For women beneficiaries, the subsidy will be limited to 60% of the project cost.

faqs.question: What is the first document required from the beneficiary for this scheme?
faqs.answer: The first document required is an Agreement Deed between the beneficiary and the Fisheries Department.

faqs.question: What options are accepted as proof of date of birth?
faqs.answer: Voting Card, Birth Certificate, Aadhar Card, or Matriculation Certificate are accepted.

faqs.question: Who needs to issue the Caste Certificate for it to be valid?
faqs.answer: The Caste Certificate must be from a first-class Magistrate (Tehsildar).

faqs.question: Is a training certificate mandatory for the beneficiary?
faqs.answer: Yes, a Training Certificate of the beneficiary is required.

faqs.question: Are bills, receipts, or vouchers necessary documents?
faqs.answer: Yes, Bills/Receipts/Vouchers are required.

faqs.question: Are photographs of the pond required for the application?
faqs.answer: Yes, photographs of the pond with the beneficiary are required.

faqs.question: What kind of project proposal does the beneficiary need to submit?
faqs.answer: The beneficiary will submit a Detailed Project Report (DPR) or Self-Contained Proposal (SCP) as per Pradhan Mantri Matasya Sampada Yojana guidelines.

name: Scheduled Caste Sub Plan (SCSP): Electrification of Wells of Scheduled Caste Farmers
description: The scheme "Scheduled Caste Sub Plan (SCSP): Electrification of Wells of Scheduled Caste Farmers" was launched by the Energy and Petrochemicals Department, Government of Gujarat, with financial allocation starting from the year 2016-17, to provide agricultural electricity connection to Scheduled Caste farmers on a priority basis. The scheme provides electrification of agriculture wells of Scheduled Caste Farmers. Free domestic electricity connections are also provided to Scheduled Caste beneficiaries. The applicant must be a Scheduled Caste farmer. The applications for this scheme are accepted at the Subdivisional Office or via the All Discom Website.
benefits: Electrification of agriculture wells of the farmer.
eligibility: The applicant must be a resident of Gujarat.. The applicant must be a farmer.. The applicant must be from a Scheduled Caste..
documents: A. Proof of Identity. Gender Certificate. In case of co
owners/partners, a consent letter on notarized stamp paper as per charter of 7/12 and 6
A. Caste Certificate (obtained from the Social Welfare Department).
Copy of Charter of Record 7/12, 8-A and 6-A.
In case of co-owners/partners, a consent letter on notarized stamp paper as per charter of 7/12 and 6-A.
Caste Certificate (obtained from the Social Welfare Department).

faqs.question: What are the specific charges that I need to pay when applying for an agricultural electricity connection under this electrification initiative for my well?
faqs.answer: You are required to pay only the Registration Charge, Security Deposit, Agreement Fee, and Test Report Fee. The capital costs for High Tension lines, Low Tension lines, and Transformer centers are waived under this scheme.

faqs.question: If I belong to a Scheduled Caste community and own farmland in Gujarat, am I eligible to apply for agricultural electricity connection for my well?
faqs.answer: Yes, you are eligible if you are a Scheduled Caste farmer residing in Gujarat. You must submit the required documents including your Caste Certificate from the Social Welfare Department.

faqs.question: Where can I obtain the application form needed to apply for the agricultural electricity connection, and is there any fee charged for it?
faqs.answer: The application form is available free of cost from the Discom Website or can be collected physically from your nearest Subdivisional Office.

faqs.question: What land-related documents do I need to submit along with my application for getting an electricity connection for my agricultural well?
faqs.answer: You must submit a copy of Charter of Record 7/12, 8-A, and 6-A as land-related documents.

faqs.question: As someone from a Scheduled Caste background engaged in farming, what type of electricity connections can I receive through this government initiative?
faqs.answer: You can receive electrification for your agriculture wells and also free domestic electricity connections.

faqs.question: Is it mandatory for me to hold a caste certificate from a specific department when applying for this agricultural electrification benefit?
faqs.answer: Yes, you must obtain and submit a Caste Certificate from the Social Welfare Department.

faqs.question: After filling out the application form completely with all attachments, where should I submit my application for the agricultural electricity connection?
faqs.answer: The complete application with all required documents must be submitted to the Subdivisional Office.

faqs.question: What documents do I need to provide if my agricultural land has multiple co-owners or partners along with me?
faqs.answer: In case of co-owners or partners, you need to submit a consent letter on notarized stamp paper as per charter of 7/12 and 6-A.

faqs.question: Apart from land records and caste certificate, what other personal documents are required to be submitted for the agricultural electricity connection application?
faqs.answer: You need to submit Proof of Identity of the Applicant and a Gender Certificate along with other documents.

faqs.question: Can I apply for this agricultural well electrification scheme online through the internet, or do I need to visit an office?
faqs.answer: You can apply either online via the All Discom Website or offline by visiting the Subdivisional Office.

faqs.question: What are the major infrastructure costs that are exempted or waived for applicants applying under this particular electrification scheme?
faqs.answer: The capital costs associated with High Tension lines, Low Tension lines, and Transformer centers are completely waived for applicants.

faqs.question: Is there any requirement regarding my place of residence in Gujarat to be eligible for applying for this agricultural electricity connection?
faqs.answer: Yes, you must be a resident of Gujarat to be eligible for this scheme.

faqs.question: What is the primary occupation requirement that I must fulfill to qualify for receiving agricultural electricity connection under this initiative?
faqs.answer: You must be a farmer to qualify for this scheme.

faqs.question: From which specific social category should I belong to be considered eligible for priority agricultural electricity connection under this scheme?
faqs.answer: You must belong to a Scheduled Caste to be eligible for this scheme.

name: Spices Development Ginger, Turmeric, Black Pepper, Cardamom, Coriander, Cinnamon and Chillies
description: The scheme “Spices Development Ginger, Turmeric, Black Pepper, Cardamom, Coriander, Cinnamon, and Chillies” was launched by the Department of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, Government of Meghalaya to encourage farmers to produce good quality and diseased free planting materials and to grow improved varieties of high yielding spices.
benefits: > Pattern of Assistance: The produce from the Government Farm, Umsning are sold directly to the growers through District Horticulture Officers / Implementing Officers at full rate.
eligibility: The applicant/farmer should be a permanent resident of Meghalaya.. The applicant should be a bonafide farmer engaged in agriculture.. The applicant should possess their own or leased land of at least 0.2 (hectares) or more.. Note: The applicant farmer can avail of the benefits of the scheme on a first come first serve basis..
documents: size photograph Identity Proof Bank passbook/account details Documents proof of possessing own or leased land for agriculture Any other document as required
Documents proof of possessing own or leased land for agriculture

faqs.question: What is the key objective of the Scheme?
faqs.answer: To encourage farmers to produce good quality and diseased free planting materials and to grow improved varieties of high yielding spices

faqs.question: Which department has launched this scheme?
faqs.answer: Department of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare, Government of Meghalaya

faqs.question: What is the pattern of assistance?
faqs.answer: The produce from the Govt. Farm, Umsning are sold directly to the growers through District Horticulture Officers / Implementing Officers at full rate.

faqs.question: Who can apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: The bonafide farmers engaged in Agriculture, possessing own or leased land of at least 0.2 (hectares) or more are eligible to apply under the scheme.

faqs.question: How to apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: The bonafide farmers can apply in plain paper through the nearest Horticulture Development Officer of a CD Block/ Horticulture Circle.

faqs.question: What is the beneficiaries’ selection procedure?
faqs.answer: The bonafide farmers shall be selected on a first come first serve basis.

faqs.question: Whom to contact?
faqs.answer: District Horticulture officer Horticulture Development Officer

name: Skill Development Programme- Uttarakhand
description: The scheme “Skill Development Programme” is implemented by the Uttarakhand Council for Biotechnology under the Department of Agriculture, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to enhance the employability and entrepreneurial skills of students, researchers, and farmers in the field of biotechnology, thereby promoting self-employment and entrepreneurship in emerging areas of the biotechnology sector. Under this scheme, various training programmes are conducted in the following areas: Training programme on plant production methods and cultivation through plant tissue culture. Training programme on hydroponic and soilless farming techniques. Training programme on drinking water and soil quality testing. Training programme on biological and molecular genetic engineering techniques. Training programme on the preparation of medicines from natural products derived from Himalayan plants.
benefits: Training programs are organized to promote self-employment under the Skill Development in Critical Areas of Biotechnology. These programs range in duration from 30/45 to 90 days for undergraduate and postgraduate students, and 180 days (Dissertation Program) for postgraduate students. During the training period, selected students conduct their research and practical training in the Council’s modern research laboratories. The trainees receive hands-on training in plant tissue culture, molecular biology and genetic engineering, environmental biotechnology, hydroponics, and soilless farming. After receiving the training, beneficiaries are better able to manage their business, self-employment, and agricultural activities.
eligibility: The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.. The applicant must be a graduate or postgraduate student, researcher, or farmer from subjects such as Biotechnology, Microbiology, Molecular and Genetic Biology, Environmental Biology, B.Tech in Biotechnology, or related fields..
documents: Aadhaar Card High school, intermediate, graduation, and post
graduation certificates and mark sheets as well as any other equivalent degree certificates Permanent residence proof Caste certificate (if applicable)
High school, intermediate, graduation, and post-graduation certificates and mark sheets as well as any other equivalent degree certificates

faqs.question: Who can benefit from this programme?
faqs.answer: Graduate and postgraduate students, researchers, and farmers from subjects such as Biotechnology, Microbiology, Molecular and Genetic Biology, Environmental Biology, B.Tech in Biotechnology, and related fields can avail themselves of the benefits.

faqs.question: What are the areas of training offered under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The training areas include: Plant production methods and cultivation through plant tissue culture Hydroponic and soilless farming techniques Drinking water and soil quality testing Biological and molecular genetic engineering techniques Preparation of medicines from natural products derived from Himalayan plants

faqs.question: What is the duration of the training programmes?
faqs.answer: Training programmes range from 30, 45, to 90 days for undergraduate and postgraduate students. The Research Dissertation Programme runs for 180 days.

faqs.question: When is the Research Dissertation Programme conducted?
faqs.answer: The Research Dissertation Programme is conducted every year from January to June.

faqs.question: Can students undergo short-term training at any time of the year
faqs.answer: Yes. Students and research scholars can undergo short-term training of 30, 45, or 90 days at any time of the year according to their convenience.

faqs.question: How can candidates apply for training?
faqs.answer: Candidates can download the application form and guidelines from the Council’s website www.ucb.ac.in (https://ucb.ac.in/) and submit the completed form (hard copy or soft copy) to the Council after obtaining recommendation from the competent authority, Principal, or HOD.

name: Seed Grant
description: The “Seed Grant” scheme is implemented by Govind Ballabh Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar, under the Department of Agriculture, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to support farmers by providing seeds at a 15% subsidy during Kisan Melas through direct distribution to them.
benefits: Farmers are provided seeds at a subsidy of up to 15% during Kisan Melas.
eligibility: The applicant must be a farmer..

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the scheme?
faqs.answer: All farmers are eligible to receive seeds under the scheme.

faqs.question: How are the seeds distributed?
faqs.answer: Seeds are distributed directly to farmers during Kisan Melas.

faqs.question: What is the subsidy offered under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Seeds are provided at a subsidy of up to 15%.

faqs.question: When are the seeds provided?
faqs.answer: Seeds are provided during Kisan Melas organized by the authorities.

faqs.question: Is there a limit on the quantity of seeds a farmer can receive?
faqs.answer: Distribution is based on availability.

name: Scheme for Establishment of Backyard Poultry Units
description: The scheme “Scheme for Establishment of Backyard Poultry Units” is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of Haryana with an objective to improve the socio-economic and nutritional status of the poor families, small farmers and landless agricultural labourers, and other economically weaker section of the society. Backyard poultry is a handy small enterprise with negligible initial investment, however good economic return along with a provision for improving the nutritional status of the members of the beneficiary family through consumption of food items having high protein content like eggs and meat. Objectives & impact expected: The long-term objective of this Scheme is to provide nutritional security to poor families, which will also play an important role in their social upliftment. To supplement the income of the families of the resource-poor beneficiaries. To improve the nutrition status of beneficiaries and their family members.
benefits: 50 chicks, 10 day old reared at Government Hatchery along with two feeders and two water drinkers are provided free of cost to each beneficiary family at their doorstep.
eligibility: The applicant should be of 18 to 55 years of age and a resident of Haryana.. There are no mandatory educational qualifications or training requirements.. Any applicant who has earlier availed benefits under any Departmental Scheme for the establishment of a livestock unit will not be eligible for availing benefits under the Scheme..

faqs.question: What are the primary objectives of this scheme?
faqs.answer: The primary objectives are to provide nutritional security to poor families, supplement their income, and improve their nutritional status through the consumption of high-protein food items like eggs and meat.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Residents of Haryana aged 18 to 55 years who have not previously availed benefits under any Departmental Scheme for the establishment of livestock units are eligible to apply.

faqs.question: Are there any educational or training requirements to apply?
faqs.answer: No, there are no mandatory educational qualifications or training requirements to apply for this scheme.

faqs.question: Can organizations or groups apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, the scheme is designed for individual beneficiaries only, not for groups, firms, or organizations.

faqs.question: What benefits do beneficiaries receive under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Beneficiaries receive 50 chicks, two feeders, and two water drinkers free of cost, delivered to their doorstep.

faqs.question: How old are the chicks provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The chicks provided are 10 days old and are reared at the Government Hatchery.

faqs.question: What economic benefits can beneficiaries expect from this scheme?
faqs.answer: Beneficiaries can expect good economic returns with negligible initial investment through the sale of eggs and meat.

faqs.question: Is there any cost involved for the beneficiaries to receive the chicks and equipment?
faqs.answer: No, the chicks and equipment are provided free of cost to the beneficiaries.

faqs.question: How can one apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Interested and eligible individuals can apply online through the Antyodaya-SARAL Portal at https://saralharyana.gov.in/.

faqs.question: Is there any other mode of application process available?
faqs.answer: Yes, the applicants may submit their applications through Common Service Centres, Antodaya Kendra, Atal Sewa Kendra, e-disha Centres or any other such centre as provided by the Government from time to time.

faqs.question: How is the delivery of chicks and equipment managed?
faqs.answer: The delivery is managed by the Government Hatchery, ensuring that chicks and equipment are provided to the beneficiaries at their doorstep.

name: Scheme for Establishment of Backyard Poultry Units under Mukhya Mantri Antyodaya Parivaar Utthan Yojana
description: The scheme “Scheme for Establishment of Backyard Poultry Units under Mukhya Mantri Antyodaya Parivaar Utthan Yojana” is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of Haryana. Any unemployed resident of Haryana aged between 18 and 60 years is eligible to avail of the benefits under this scheme.
benefits: chicks, 10 day old reared at Government Hatchery along with two feeders and two water drinkers are provided free of cost to each beneficiary family at their doorstep.
eligibility: The applicant should be a resident of Haryana.. The applicant should be unemployed.. The applicant should be between 18 to 60 years old.. There are no mandatory educational qualifications or training requirements..

faqs.answer: Beneficiaries receive 50 chicks of 10 days old, two feeders, and two water drinkers free of cost.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Unemployed residents of Haryana aged between 18 and 60 years are eligible to apply.

faqs.question: Are there any educational qualifications required to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, there are no mandatory educational qualifications or training requirements.

faqs.question: Can organizations or groups apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, the scheme is individual beneficiary-oriented and not open to any group, firm, or organization.

faqs.question: Where do the chicks come from?
faqs.answer: The chicks are reared at a Government Hatchery Farm.

faqs.answer: No, the chicks, feeders, and water drinkers are provided free of cost.

faqs.question: Can someone who is employed apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: No, the applicant must be unemployed to be eligible.

name: Silage evam Dudharu Pashu Poshan Yojana
description: The scheme “Silage evam Dudharu Pashu Poshan Yojana” was launched by the Department of Dairy Development, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to improve the nutrition of dairy animals and enhance milk production by providing subsidized silage and feed to members of milk cooperative societies.
benefits: Under this scheme, members of milk cooperative societies in hilly and plain rural areas are provided with quality mineral mixtures and probiotics at current rates, receive a 75% subsidy on silage including an upfront subsidy of ₹2.00 per kg. Compact feed blocks are available at a 50% subsidy, costing the beneficiary ₹8.00 per kg.
eligibility: The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.. The applicant must be a member of a milk-producing cooperative society supplying milk to the society..
documents: Documents required as per the directions of the concerned milk cooperative society.

faqs.question: Who are the beneficiaries of this scheme?
faqs.answer: Members of milk-producing cooperative societies in Uttarakhand, particularly those in hilly and plain rural areas, are eligible to benefit from this scheme.

faqs.question: What types of feed are provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides silage, compact feed blocks, quality mineral mixtures, and probiotics to eligible members.

faqs.question: What is the subsidy provided on silage?
faqs.answer: Members receive a 75% subsidy on silage, including an upfront subsidy of ₹2.00 per kg.

faqs.question: What is the subsidy on compact feed blocks?
faqs.answer: Compact feed blocks are available at a 50% subsidy, costing the beneficiary ₹8.00 per kg.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Applicants must be residents of Uttarakhand and members of a milk-producing cooperative society supplying milk to the society.

faqs.question: How does a member apply for fodder under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The member must submit an application for fodder, addressed to the Secretary of their milk cooperative society.

faqs.question: How is the fodder demand processed?
faqs.answer: The Committee Secretary verifies the requirement and forwards the demand to the District Milk Union. The animal nutrition feed is then provided to the member through the cooperative society.

name: Scheme to Encourage Farmers to Add Value to Crops
department: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department
description: The "Scheme to Encourage Farmers to Add Value to Crops" introduced by the Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department, Gujarat, aims to promote value addition in agriculture by helping farmers invest in machinery and equipment. This initiative seeks to improve the profitability of farming by supporting post-harvest processing and mechanization.
benefits: Financial Assistance: 50% of the machinery cost or ₹10,00,000/-, whichever is less.
eligibility: The applicant must be a farmer.. The applicant must be a resident of Gujarat.. The applicant must be involved in agriculture-related activities.. The applicant must intend to purchase machinery for value addition..
documents: 7/12 Certificate. Aadhaar Card. Bank Pass Book/Cancelled Cheque.

faqs.question: What is the objective of the "Scheme to Encourage Farmers to Add Value to Crops"?
faqs.answer: The objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to farmers for purchasing machinery that adds value to their crops, thereby increasing their income.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Any individual who is a farmer and a resident of Gujarat is eligible to apply for this scheme.

faqs.question: How much financial assistance is provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides financial assistance of 50% of the machinery cost or up to ₹10,00,000/-, whichever is lower.

faqs.question: Is the scheme available to farmers of all castes and categories?
faqs.answer: Yes, the scheme is open to farmers of all castes, categories, and economic backgrounds.

faqs.question: Is there any income limit for availing benefits under this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, there is no personal or family income limit for applying to this scheme.

faqs.question: How is the subsidy amount disbursed to the farmer?
faqs.answer: The subsidy amount is directly transferred to the applicant's registered bank account.

faqs.question: Is this scheme applicable throughout Gujarat?
faqs.answer: Yes, the scheme is implemented across all districts of Gujarat.

faqs.question: Where should a farmer apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Applicants can apply on the iKhedut (https://ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in/)portal to avail of the benefits of the scheme.

faqs.question: What documents are required to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: The required documents include an Aadhaar card, a 7/12 land record, and either a bank passbook or a cancelled cheque.

faqs.question: Who should the applicant contact for help or more information about the scheme?
faqs.answer: The applicant should contact the nearest agriculture office or visit the iKhedut (https://ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in/site/)portal for more information.

name: Scheme for Establishment of Hi-Tech and Mini Dairy Units under Mukhya Mantri Antyodaya Parivaar Utthan Yojana
description: The scheme “Scheme for Establishment of Hi-Tech and Mini Dairy Units under Mukhya Mantri Antyodaya Parivaar Utthan Yojana (MMAPUY)” is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of Haryana. Under this scheme, a resident of Haryana who is between 18 and 60 years of age can avail a 25% subsidy on the cost of two milch animals. The subsidy can be availed as a loan for the purchase of these milch animals by the beneficiary for the establishment of dairy units with two milch animals.
benefits: > Financial Assistance under the Scheme: Dairy units of 2 milch animals: % subsidy on the cost of milch animals which has been availed as a loan for the purchase of these milch animals by the beneficiary for the establishment of dairy units of 2 milch animals; > Financial Assistance for Insurance under the Scheme: Insurance assistance will be provided as per the available departmental scheme if operational during the year; otherwise, the beneficiaries will have to arrange for insurance of animals and shall pay the insurance premium.
eligibility: The applicant should be of 18 to 60 years of age and a resident of Haryana.. The applicant must be unemployed.. There would be no mandatory educational qualifications or training requirements.. The applicant can apply for a dairy unit of 2 Milch animals only.. The applicant should have space/shed for keeping milch animals.. The applicant would have to submit a Self-Declaration for being unemployed and for undertaking to abide by other conditions as required under the Scheme..
documents: Copy of Bank Passbook or Cancelled Cheque

faqs.question: Who is eligible for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Residents of Haryana aged 18 to 60 years who are unemployed and have space for keeping milch animals are eligible.

faqs.question: What financial assistance is provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: A 25% subsidy on the cost of two milch animals, availed as a loan, is provided for establishing dairy units.

faqs.question: Is there any assistance for insurance under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, insurance assistance is provided as per the available departmental scheme. If not operational, beneficiaries must arrange and pay for the insurance.

faqs.question: What are the age criteria for applicants?
faqs.answer: Applicants must be between 18 and 60 years of age.

faqs.question: Can educational qualifications or training affect eligibility?
faqs.answer: No, there are no mandatory educational qualifications or training requirements.

faqs.question: How many milch animals can be purchased under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme allows for the purchase of two milch animals.

faqs.question: Can groups, firms, or organizations apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Can groups, firms, or organizations apply for this scheme?

faqs.question: What kind of space is required for keeping the milch animals?
faqs.answer: Applicants should have adequate space or a shed for keeping the milch animals.

faqs.question: Is there any self-declaration required?
faqs.answer: Yes, applicants must submit a self-declaration confirming their unemployment status and agreement to abide by the scheme's conditions.

faqs.question: How can eligible applicants apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: To avail the benefits of the scheme, applicants should visit the Deputy Director's office in their district and collect the application form.

name: Scheme for Establishment of Hi-Tech and Mini Dairy Units
description: The scheme “Scheme for Establishment of Hi-Tech and Mini Dairy Units” is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of Haryana. This is a credit-linked scheme with a primary objective of providing self-employment opportunities. The unemployed persons will be assisted by way of providing financial assistance in the form of subsidies for establishing dairy units of 4, 10, 20, and 50 milch animals like buffaloes, indigenous cows (Hariana, Sahiwal, Belahi, Red Sindhi, Tharparkar, and Gir breeds only) and crossbred cows. Medium-term objectives: To provide gainful self-employment to the unemployed persons. To supplement the income of the families of the beneficiaries. To raise the socio-economic status of the weaker sections/Antyodaya families of the society. To commercialize dairy units by encouraging small dairy unit owners to increase the size of their unit to 20 and 50 milch animals. Long-term objectives: Creation of employment opportunities through Animal Husbandry activities. To increase milk production and Dairy products. To upgrade and develop valuable Breeds/Germplasm available in the State. To increase per Capita milk availability in the state.
benefits: > Financial Assistance for Interest Subvention under the Scheme: Dairy units of 4 and 10 milch animals: 25% subsidy on the cost of milch animals can be availed as a loan for the purchase of these milch animals by the beneficiary for the establishment of dairy units of 4 and 10 milch animals; The subsidy will be provided three months after the purchase/tagging of Milch animals or disbursement of Loan by the bank, whichever is later, and subject to verification of unit by the concerned veterinary surgeon.
