faqs.question: Who is implementing this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of Haryana.

faqs.question: What types of dairy units can be established under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Dairy units with 4, 10, 20, and 50 milch animals, including buffaloes, indigenous cows (Hariana, Sahiwal, Belahi, Red Sindhi, Tharparkar, and Gir breeds), and crossbred cows.

faqs.question: What are the medium-term objectives of the scheme?
faqs.answer: To provide gainful self-employment, supplement the income of beneficiaries' families, raise the socio-economic status of weaker sections/Antyodaya families, and commercialize dairy units by encouraging small unit owners to expand.

faqs.question: What are the long-term objectives of the scheme?
faqs.answer: To create employment opportunities, increase milk production and dairy products, upgrade and develop valuable breeds/germplasm, and increase per capita milk availability in Haryana.

faqs.question: What financial assistance is provided for dairy units of 4 and 10 milch animals?
faqs.answer: A 25% subsidy on the cost of milch animals for loans availed for purchasing these animals.

faqs.question: What financial assistance is provided for dairy units of 20 and 50 milch animals?
faqs.answer: Interest subvention on 75% of the cost of milch animals (with 25% being the margin money).

faqs.question: How is the subsidy disbursed for dairy units of 4 and 10 milch animals?
faqs.answer: The subsidy is provided three months after the purchase/tagging of milch animals or disbursement of the loan, whichever is later, subject to verification by the concerned veterinary surgeon.

faqs.question: What type of assistance is provided for livestock insurance?
faqs.answer: If an operational Livestock Insurance Scheme exists, the insurance of animals is covered under that scheme. Otherwise, the beneficiary or the bank must arrange for the insurance.

faqs.question: How does the department assist beneficiaries in establishing dairy units?
faqs.answer: The department helps in sponsoring loan applications, purchasing animals, tagging and issuing health certificates, providing veterinary health services, and offering dairy husbandry training.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Residents of Haryana aged 18 to 55, who are unemployed and have space for keeping milch animals. Specific land requirements apply for units with 20 and 50 milch animals.

faqs.question: Are there any educational or training requirements to apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: No, there are no mandatory educational qualifications or training requirements.

faqs.question: Can groups or organizations apply under this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, the scheme is intended for individual beneficiaries only.

faqs.question: What are the land requirements for applicants of 20 and 50 milch animal units?
faqs.answer: Applicants must have 2 acres and 5 acres of agricultural land for green fodder production, respectively, either by ownership or long lease.

faqs.question: Can someone who has previously benefited from another departmental livestock scheme apply?
faqs.answer: No, unless the previous benefit was for a unit below 20 milch animals, in which case they can apply for units of 20 and 50 milch animals.

faqs.question: Where should an applicant apply if they live in a different place from where the animals will be kept?
faqs.answer: The application should be submitted to the jurisdiction area Government Veterinary Hospital where the animals will be kept.

faqs.question: How can eligible applicants apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Eligible applicants must apply online through the Antyodaya-SARAL Portal at https://saralharyana.gov.in/.

faqs.question: Can an eligible applicants apply through Common Service Centre?
faqs.answer: Yes, the applicants may submit application themselves on the portal or through Common Service Centres, Antodaya Kendra, Atal Sewa Kendra, e-disha Centres or any other such centre.

name: Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers
description: The scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-wheelers" by the Climate Change Department, Government of Gujarat, aims to encourage the use of clean energy-based vehicles for the transportation of passengers and goods, thereby reducing dependency on petrol and mitigating pollution. Beneficiaries, including rickshaw drivers, women entrepreneurs, startups, unemployed youth, educational institutions, cooperatives, NGOs, local bodies, and yatras, can avail a subsidy on a reimbursement basis after purchasing battery-operated three-wheelers from Gujarat Energy Development Agency (GEDA) authorized manufacturers and dealers.

The applicant must be an individual (such as rickshaw drivers, women entrepreneurs, startups, educated unemployed individuals) or an institution (such as cooperatives, NGOs, educational institutions, local bodies, yatras).. faqs.question: What is the purpose of the scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers"?
faqs.answer: The scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers" has been launched by the Climate Change Department, Government of Gujarat, with the purpose of promoting the adoption of eco-friendly battery-operated three-wheelers by providing a financial subsidy that helps beneficiaries save fuel costs and reduce environmental pollution.

faqs.question: Who is the implementing agency for the scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers"?
faqs.answer: The implementing agency for the scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers" is the Gujarat Energy Development Agency (GEDA), which is responsible for verifying applications, processing subsidy claims, and reimbursing the approved amount to the beneficiaries.

faqs.question: Who can apply under the scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers"?
faqs.answer: Under the scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers," any individual such as rickshaw drivers, women entrepreneurs, startups, educated unemployed persons, and any institution such as cooperatives, NGOs, educational institutes, local bodies, and yatras are eligible to apply.

faqs.question: What financial assistance is provided under the scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers"?
faqs.answer: The scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers" provides a financial subsidy of ₹48,000/- per eligible purchase of a battery-operated three-wheeler, which is reimbursed to the applicant after successful purchase and submission of documents.

faqs.question: What is the process of receiving the subsidy under the scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers"?
faqs.answer: Under the scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers," the applicant purchases a battery-operated three-wheeler from a GEDA-authorized manufacturer or dealer, submits the application with required documents through the authorized dealer, and receives the subsidy on a reimbursement basis after verification.

faqs.question: Are there any specific manufacturers or dealers from whom the vehicle must be purchased under the scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers"?
faqs.answer: Yes, under the scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers," the vehicle must be purchased only from manufacturers and dealers authorized by GEDA, otherwise the applicant will not be eligible for the subsidy reimbursement.

faqs.question: Are there any income criteria under the scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers"?
faqs.answer: No, under the scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers," there are no income-based restrictions, meaning the scheme is open to all eligible applicants regardless of their social or economic background.

faqs.question: From where can the application form for the scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers" be obtained?
faqs.answer: The application form for the scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers" can be obtained free of cost from GEDA offices through vehicle dealers who are appointed by GEDA-authorized manufacturers.

faqs.question: Where should the completed application for the scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers" be submitted?
faqs.answer: The completed application for the scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers" should be submitted through the authorized vehicle dealer, who forwards it to the GEDA office for verification and further processing.

faqs.question: What documents are required to apply for the scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers"?
faqs.answer: To apply under the scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers," the applicant is required to submit a duly filled application form along with Aadhaar Card, Copy of License, and a valid Identity Card.

faqs.question: Is the scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers" applicable throughout Gujarat?
faqs.answer: Yes, the scheme "Subsidy For Battery Operated Three-Wheelers" is applicable across the entire state of Gujarat and can be availed by eligible applicants residing in any district of the state.

name: PMMSY: Fish Feed Plants of Production Capacity of at least 100 Ton/Day - Haryana

The objective is to enhance the availability of high-quality and affordable feed for fish farmers, supporting the expansion of aquaculture in Haryana. This is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, under which the project is jointly funded by the Central and State Governments: 50% of the subsidy amount is contributed by the Central Government, and 50% is provided by the State Government. Beneficiaries are expected to operate and maintain the plant independently and ensure the supply of feed to fishers at affordable prices.

name: Scheme for Integrated Development for Horticulture (HRT-2)

description: The scheme "Scheme for Integrated Development for Horticulture (HRT-2)" by the Agriculture and Co-operation Department, Government of Gujarat aims to ensure the integrated development of horticulture in the state by providing financial support to farmers for activities such as post-harvest management, farm mechanization, crop processing, market linkage, and infrastructure development. faqs.question: What kind of financial support is offered under the “Scheme for Integrated Development for Horticulture (HRT-2)”?
faqs.answer: The scheme offers a wide range of financial support, including subsidies for crop processing units, farm mechanization, greenhouse and polyhouse structures, export promotion through air and sea refrigeration subsidies, electricity bill reimbursement, and assistance for events like exhibitions, krishimelas, and horticulture seminars.

faqs.question: Is there any cost associated with the application process under this scheme?
faqs.answer: There is no cost associated with applying for the “Scheme for Integrated Development for Horticulture (HRT-2)”, and the application can be submitted free of charge through the official online portal.

faqs.question: What documents are mandatory for applying under the “Scheme for Integrated Development for Horticulture (HRT-2)”?
faqs.answer: Applicants must upload scanned copies of essential documents such as the Aadhaar Card, 7/12 land ownership certificate, KHEDUT registration proof, ration card, and a duly filled application form available on the iKhedut portal.

faqs.question: Is land ownership a compulsory requirement for applying under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, the applicant must possess valid land ownership documents such as the 7/12 certificate in order to be eligible for financial assistance under the “Scheme for Integrated Development for Horticulture (HRT-2)”.

faqs.question: Does the scheme provide assistance for export-related infrastructure and activities?
faqs.answer: Yes, the scheme provides specific support in the form of air fridge and sea fridge subsidies to encourage and facilitate the export of fruits, vegetables, flowers, and plants produced by horticulture farmers in Gujarat.

faqs.question: What kind of infrastructure development is supported under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Under the scheme, financial assistance is provided for the development of infrastructure such as hi-tech greenhouses with fan and pad systems, naturally ventilated polyhouses, net houses, water storage tanks for drip irrigation, crop trellising systems, and plug nurseries.

faqs.question: Is there a facility to track the application status once it is submitted online?
faqs.answer: Yes, once the application is submitted through the iKhedut portal, applicants can log in with their credentials to check the real-time status of their application and receive updates regarding approval or disbursement.

faqs.question: Through which platform can a farmer submit an application for the “Scheme for Integrated Development for Horticulture (HRT-2)”?
faqs.answer: Farmers must submit their application online through the Government of Gujarat’s official agricultural service platform, known as the iKhedut portal, which is accessible at: https://ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in/site/signup (https://ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in/site/signup).

name: State Fisheries Input Scheme

faqs.answer: Eligible fish farmers receive a 50% subsidy on the total cost of fishery inputs such as fish feed, medicines, hand nets, hapas, and minikits.

faqs.question: How much subsidy is provided for fish feed for small ponds?
faqs.answer: A subsidy of 1 quintal of fish feed is provided for a 100 square meter pond.

faqs.answer: Fish farmers with ponds ranging from 500 to 2000 square meters receive a subsidy of 6 quintals of fish feed.

name: Sthaniya Fasal Protsahan Karyakram
description: The scheme “Sthaniya Fasal Protsahan Karyakram” was launched by the Department of Agriculture, Government of Uttarakhand, to promote the cultivation of local crops, enhance productivity, ensure the use of quality seeds, and provide fair prices to farmers in the mountain districts of Uttarakhand.
benefits: Under the scheme, the following objectives will be achieved by distributing verified seeds of local crops at 100% subsidy: a. Distribution of certified seeds on subsidy to increase the cultivation area according to the specific region. b. Ensuring the recommended seed replacement rate is met. c. Enhancing production and productivity through the use of quality seeds. d. Promoting and encouraging the cultivation of local pulse crops. e. Ensuring farmers receive a fair price for their produce. Seed production will be carried out by the Agriculture Department in clusters formed under the Traditional Agriculture Development Scheme, through the CLF/LC established under UGVS-REAP, and directly by the Agriculture Department. For crops where traditional clusters are not operational, clusters will be identified through CLF/LC for certified seed production. The Agriculture Department will conduct seed production programs in these areas, and the produced seeds will be distributed region-wise after appropriate allocation. Traditional crops selected under the program: Kidney Beans 2. Gahat 3. Ramdana 4. Red Rice 5. Maize – Nainital and Chakrata region 6. Bhatta 7. Ugal/Phafar 8. Kauni 9. Toor (Pigeon Pea)
eligibility: All farmers from the mountain districts of Uttarakhand are eligible..
documents: Farmers should submit documents as specified in the program guidelines.

faqs.question: What are the main objectives of the scheme?
faqs.answer: Distribute verified seeds at 100% subsidy. Meet the recommended seed replacement rate. Increase production and productivity through quality seeds. Encourage local pulse crops. Ensure fair prices for farmers’ produce.

faqs.question: Which crops are covered under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Traditional crops selected include: Kidney Beans 2. Gahat 3. Ramdana 4. Red Rice 5. Maize (Nainital and Chakrata regions)6. Bhatta 7. Ugal/Phafar 8. Kauni 9. Toor (Pigeon Pea)

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the scheme?
faqs.answer: All farmers from the mountain districts of Uttarakhand are eligible.

faqs.question: How are farmers selected for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers belonging to the selected clusters under the Traditional Agriculture Development Scheme or through CLF/LCs formed under UGVS-REAP are eligible.

faqs.question: What is the subsidy provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Verified seeds of local crops are provided at 100% subsidy.

faqs.question: How will seeds be distributed?
faqs.answer: Seeds produced will be allocated region-wise and made available for distribution to farmers in those areas.

name: Scheme for Fruit and Vegetable Preservation and Training Program in Horticulture Department HRT 5

faqs.question: What is the objective of the “Scheme for Fruit and Vegetable Preservation and Training Program in Horticulture Department HRT 5”?
faqs.answer: The objective of the scheme is to impart practical and technical training to women and urban citizens in the areas of fruit and vegetable preservation, canning, kitchen gardening, and value addition in horticultural produce in order to promote nutritional security, self-reliance, and clean food practices.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?

faqs.question: Is there any financial support given to trainees?
faqs.answer: Yes, under the “Scheme for Fruit and Vegetable Preservation and Training Program in Horticulture Department HRT 5,” each trainee receives ₹250 per day as a stipend for attending the training sessions, which is part of the total sanctioned training cost of ₹500 per trainee per day.

faqs.question: What does the remaining ₹250 of the training cost cover?
faqs.answer: In addition to the ₹250 trainee stipend, the other ₹250 from the daily training cost under the “Scheme for Fruit and Vegetable Preservation and Training Program in Horticulture Department HRT 5” is utilized for covering expenses such as the cost of materials, training literature kits, and honorarium payments to the subject experts and trainers.

faqs.question: Is this scheme only for women participants?
faqs.answer: Although the scheme is especially beneficial to women, the “Scheme for Fruit and Vegetable Preservation and Training Program in Horticulture Department HRT 5” is open to individuals of any gender who are interested in receiving training in horticultural skills and practices.

faqs.question: What is the duration of the training under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The training sessions last for a minimum of 2 days and may extend up to 5 days, depending on the specific training module and program design.

faqs.question: Is the scheme applicable throughout the state of Gujarat?
faqs.answer: Yes, the “Scheme for Fruit and Vegetable Preservation and Training Program in Horticulture Department HRT 5” is implemented across the entire state of Gujarat, making it accessible to eligible applicants from all regions.

faqs.question: What are the steps to apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: To apply for the scheme, the applicant must visit the iKhedut (https://ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in/site/) portal, fill out the online application form, upload the required documents, and submit the form electronically.

faqs.question: What documents are needed to complete the application process?
faqs.answer: Applicants are required to submit documents such as their Aadhaar Card, Bank Pass Book or Cancelled Cheque, and Ration Card while applying for the “Scheme for Fruit and Vegetable Preservation and Training Program in Horticulture Department HRT 5” through the online portal.

It is also called shednet house or net house. > Other important points Construction of shednet house should be done only after administrative approval/work order has been issued by the Horticulture Department. name: Soil Health Card Scheme - Uttarakhand
description: The scheme “Soil Health Card Scheme” is implemented by the Department of Agriculture, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide Soil Health Cards to all farmers in the state, helping them understand the nutrient composition of their soil and the type and quantity of fertilizers suitable for their crops.
benefits: To provide Soil Health Cards to all farmers in the state. The soil of each farmer’s field is tested at soil testing laboratories, which are operational in all 13 districts. Farmers receive detailed information about the nutrient content of their soil, along with recommendations on the type and quantity of fertilizers best suited for their crops. Soil testing is provided free of cost to farmers. In hilly areas, a Soil Health Card is issued for agricultural land up to 2.5 hectares, while in plain areas, it is issued for land up to 10 hectares. Each card is valid for three years.
eligibility: The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.. The applicant must be a farmer.. The farmer must own agricultural land in the state and be actively engaged in farming activities..
documents: Aadhar card Residence certificate Mobile number

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the Scheme?
faqs.answer: All landowning farmers of Uttarakhand who are actively engaged in agricultural work are eligible.

faqs.question: Is soil testing free under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, soil sample testing is free for all farmers under the scheme.

faqs.question: What is the validity of a Soil Health Card?
faqs.answer: The Soil Health Card is valid for three years from the date of issue.

faqs.question: How much land is covered under the scheme?
faqs.answer: In hilly areas, soil health cards are issued for agricultural land up to 2.5 hectares, and in plain areas, up to 10 hectares.

faqs.question: Where can farmers get their soil tested?
faqs.answer: Soil testing laboratories are available in all 13 districts of Uttarakhand. Farmers can submit samples directly to these labs or through their Panchayat’s Assistant Agriculture Officer.

faqs.question: How should farmers collect a soil sample?
faqs.answer: Identify six locations in the field for sampling. Clear the area of grass or debris. Dig a V-shaped pit 6 inches deep, 6 inches long, and 4 inches wide. Collect 1–2 inches of soil from top to bottom along the pit’s edge. Mix soil from all six locations thoroughly, remove stones, pebbles, and roots. Reduce the mixed soil to half a kilogram for testing.

faqs.question: How should the soil sample be stored?
faqs.answer: Place the half-kilogram soil sample in a clean bag with a slip mentioning the farmer’s name, address, Khasra number, mobile number, and crop information. Include Aadhar card and residence certificate.

faqs.question: How is the soil sample submitted?
faqs.answer: Samples can be submitted to the district soil testing laboratory directly or through the Panchayat’s Assistant Agriculture Officer.

name: Solar Inverter Charger
description: The "Solar Inverter Charger" by the Renewable Energy Department, Government of Haryana, aims to promote sustainable energy practices, reduce the dependency on grid electricity, and provide financial support for the installation of solar inverter chargers in domestic households. This initiative targets families with existing inverters who have not yet adopted solar technology, thereby enabling energy-efficient solutions and reducing carbon footprint.
benefits: For 320-watt Solar Inverter Charger System: A subsidy of ₹6,000/- is provided. - For 640-watt Solar Inverter Charger System: A subsidy of ₹10,000/- is provided.
eligibility: Any resident family of Haryana with Pariwar Pahichan Patra (PPP) to apply.. faqs.question: What is the objective of the "Solar Inverter Charger"?
faqs.answer: The "Solar Inverter Charger" by the Renewable Energy Department, Government of Haryana, aims to promote the use of renewable energy and reduce electricity dependence by subsidizing solar inverter chargers. Through this scheme, a subsidy of ₹6,000/- or ₹10,000/- is provided for solar inverter charger systems to eligible households in Haryana.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The following are eligible to apply for this scheme: Any Haryana resident family with Pariwar Pahichan Patra (PPP) to apply. All the households who have domestic inverter and not installed solar inverter charger on his/her existing inverter. Applicants who have not installed Solar Inverter Charger in past 5 years under the Department Scheme.

faqs.answer: Under the scheme, financial assistance in the form of a subsidy is provided, which includes ₹6,000 for a 320-watt solar inverter charger system and ₹10,000/- for a 640-watt system.

faqs.question: Can a person without an inverter apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: A person who does not already have a domestic inverter is not eligible for the scheme, as one of the key conditions is that the applicant must own a conventional inverter prior to installing a solar inverter charger.

faqs.question: Is there any income limit or caste-based reservation for this scheme?

faqs.question: Can a household choose the wattage of the system as per their requirement?

faqs.question: Can residents of urban areas also apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Any resident of Haryana, whether from urban or rural areas, who meets the eligibility criteria and has a valid Pariwar Pahichan Patra (PPP), may apply.

faqs.question: What is the process for applying to the "Solar Inverter Charger"?
faqs.answer: The applicants may visit the Antyodaya-SARAL Portal (https://saralharyana.gov.in/) to apply for the scheme.

faqs.question: Is it mandatory to submit the Pariwar Pahichan Patra (PPP) while applying for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is mandatory for the applicant to submit a valid Pariwar Pahichan Patra (PPP) as it serves as the primary eligibility document for applying to the "Solar Inverter Charger".

faqs.question: What is the offline process for applying the scheme?
faqs.answer: To apply for the "Solar Inverter Charger", the applicant may visit the nearest Atal Seva Kendra (Common Service Centre).

faqs.question: Is there any fee applicable for applying this scheme through Atal Seva Kendra (Common Service Centre) ?
faqs.answer: Yes, a nominal service fee of ₹10/- is charged by the Common Service Centre for the application.

name: Sagar Khedu Sarvangi Vikas Yojana
description: The scheme “Sagar Khedu Sarvangi Vikas Yojana” was launched by the Energy and Petrochemicals Department, Government of Gujarat. The scheme aims to accelerate the process of development in 39 taluks of 15 districts of Sagar Kantha (Coastal Area). The scheme aims to resolve the problem of excessive tripping and faults in coastal areas due to corrosion and humidity, ensuring uninterrupted and quality power supply to consumers. The scheme provides improvement of distribution lines, construction of new 66 Kilovolt sub stations, and repair and modernization of transmission lines, along with provisioning 12,000 new agricultural electricity connections. The scheme is implemented by Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Limited (GUVNL). The Government provides share capital contributions to the corporation for execution.
benefits: The scheme plans for several infrastructure improvements and resultant benefits for consumers in coastal areas: Infrastructure Improvement: Work is planned for the improvement of distribution lines, construction of new 66 Kilovolt sub stations, and repair and modernization of transmission lines. Voltage and Supply: Industrial and residential customers located in the coastal areas will receive adequate voltage and continuous power supply. Reduced Failures: There will be a significant reduction in the rate of electric motor burnout and transformer failure. Reduced Losses: There will be a reduction in transmission loss and power interruption. Crop Protection: Provision of continuous power supply will prevent damage to crops. Safety: Accidents that occur due to the breaking of power lines can be largely avoided. Development: The all-round development of the villages of the taluks located in the Sagar Kantha area can be achieved. New Connections: New agricultural electricity connections are planned to be provided to coastal farmers (with a target of 12,000 connections mentioned for the financial year 2016-2017). Residential Coverage: Electricity supply is planned for approximately 1,00,000 housings.
eligibility: The guidelines of the scheme do not define any specific eligibility criteria. However, the target groups benefiting from the infrastructure and connection provisions will be the following:. Electricity consumers living in the coastal area.. Industrial, residential, or agricultural customers located in the coastal areas.. Consumers residing within one of the 39 taluks of the 15 districts of the Sagar Kantha area.. Farmer seeking a new agricultural electricity connection in the areas of Paschim Gujarat Vij Company Limited (PGVCL) company..
documents: For the Citizens The citizens are not required to submit any documents or forms to access the benefits. For GUVNL During Application Technical Approval of the Competent Authority During Funding Execution Periodic Certificates of Expenditure Utilization (U.T.C.) Monthly Progress Reports and Expenditure Details Quarterly Progress Reports (Historical Requirement) Information on Tribal Area Infrastructure (District
wise) Post Benefit Disbursal (Financial Closure) Statement/Report Detailing Unspent Amounts Surrendered
The citizens are not required to submit any documents or forms to access the benefits.
Technical Approval of the Competent Authority
Monthly Progress Reports and Expenditure Details

faqs.question: The existing electrical setup at my location, including the distribution box and service lines, has deteriorated. Will the scheme address this specific physical degradation?
faqs.answer: Yes, the scheme targets difficulties arising from the corrosion of distribution boxes and the deterioration of service lines caused by the specific weather and humidity conditions in the coastal area.

faqs.question: As a person utilizing electricity for personal use in my home, am I considered an intended beneficiary who will receive improved service quality?
faqs.answer: Yes, the operation is planned to provide residential customers located in the coastal areas with adequate voltage and a continuous, uninterrupted power supply.

faqs.question: If I obtain power through this modernized infrastructure, can I expect tangible improvements in equipment protection at my premises?
faqs.answer: Yes, industrial and residential customers benefiting from the operation can expect a significant reduction in the rate of electric motor burnout and transformer failure.

faqs.question: I am a farmer who has submitted an application for an agricultural electricity connection several years ago. Does this development program address the long pending applications of farmers like me?
faqs.answer: Yes, one of the aims of the plan is to expedite the resolution of agricultural electricity connection applications that have been pending for many years for farmers located in the coastal areas.

faqs.question: As a business owner running an industry in a coastal zone, will my enterprise receive adequate power voltage and supply stability?
faqs.answer: Yes, industrial customers situated in the coastal areas are intended to receive adequate voltage and continuous power supply, which will help prevent damage and loss to their businesses and industries.

faqs.question: Is the primary agricultural benefit focused on upgrading existing infrastructure, or does it specifically involve requests for brand new supply points?
faqs.answer: The state government plans the scheme to provide new agricultural electricity connections to coastal farmers, alongside improvements to existing distribution and transmission lines.

faqs.question: Where is the planned provision of electricity for farming and agricultural use intended to be primarily implemented?
faqs.answer: The provision of agricultural electricity is specifically planned to be carried out within the areas served by the Paschim Gujarat Vij Company Limited (PGVCL) company.

faqs.question: Which specific administrative divisions are included in the scope of accelerating the process of development under this program?
faqs.answer: The plan is designed to accelerate the process of development in 39 (Thirty-Nine) taluks located across 15 (Fifteen) districts of the Sagar Kantha (Coastal) area.

faqs.question: I am concerned about my crops being harmed by erratic electricity delivery. Will continuous power supply be ensured to prevent damage to my agricultural produce?
faqs.answer: Yes, providing a continuous power supply is a specific intended outcome of the scheme, designed to prevent damage to crops that could otherwise occur due to interruptions.

faqs.question: If I reside within the designated developmental area, is it a mandatory prerequisite that I already be categorized as an electricity user?
faqs.answer: Yes, the scheme is aimed at resolving issues for the existing electricity consumers living in the coastal areas who are currently not receiving uninterrupted power supply.

faqs.question: I am a farmer living in the designated region, trying to improve my agricultural operations. Am I explicitly targeted for connection provision under this specific program?
faqs.answer: Yes, agricultural customers and farmers located in the coastal areas are specifically targeted for the provision of new agricultural electricity connections and infrastructure benefits.

faqs.question: Is there a primary geographical requirement related to residing or operating a business near the coastline to qualify for the benefits of infrastructure modernization?
faqs.answer: The applicant or consumer must be located within the coastal areas, often referred to as Sagar Kantha, where the environment causes specific problems like corrosion and high humidity.

faqs.question: Are there any specific goals within the scope of this development program regarding providing coverage to a significant number of households in the area?
faqs.answer: Yes, the comprehensive development plan for the coastal region aims to provide electricity supply to approximately 1,00,000 (One Lakh) housings within the service area.

faqs.question: What is the primary objective of the infrastructure work carried out under this development scheme, specifically regarding power delivery to consumers?
faqs.answer: The objective is to ensure that all types of electricity consumers located in the coastal areas receive a quality-filled and continuous power supply.

name: Grant for Sex-Sorted Semen to Livestock Farmers
description: The scheme "Grant for Sex-Sorted Semen to Livestock Farmers" was introduced by the Department of Animal Husbandry, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to promote breed improvement and increase milk production by encouraging the use of sex-sorted semen for artificial insemination in cows and buffaloes.
benefits: Under this scheme, a grant of ₹400 per dose is provided to cattle farmers for breed improvement through artificial insemination of cows and buffaloes using sex-sorted semen.
eligibility: The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.. The applicant must be engaged in the rearing of cows and/or buffaloes..
documents: No documents are required to be submitted by the cattle rearer.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: All cow and buffalo rearers residing in Uttarakhand are eligible for the scheme.

faqs.question: What financial assistance is provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: A grant of ₹400/- per dose is provided to cattle rearers for artificial insemination using sex-sorted semen.

faqs.question: How can a farmer avail of this benefit?
faqs.answer: Cattle rearers can contact the nearest veterinary hospital, animal service center, or UPSA center to avail of artificial insemination services using sex-sorted semen.

faqs.question: Is any documentation required to avail of the scheme?
faqs.answer: No, the cattle rearer is not required to submit any documents to avail of the benefit.

faqs.question: What type of animals are covered under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme covers cows and buffaloes owned by livestock farmers.

name: Scheme for Loan and Subsidy for Manure and Fertilizer-DNH&DD
state: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu
description: The scheme “Scheme for Loan and Subsidy for Manure and Fertilizer” has been implemented by the Agriculture Department, UT of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. It aims to encourage the use of fertilizers so as to improve productivity. Through this scheme, manure and fertilizers are provided to Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and non-SC/ST small and marginal farmers having land holdings up to 2 hectares on subsidy-cum-loan basis. The scheme is implemented by the Agriculture Department through field-level functionaries. Manures and fertilisers are provided to eligible cultivators on a 40% subsidy and 60% loan basis. The assistance is given in kind and not in cash. The quantity of fertilizers is limited as per the prescribed crop-wise rates. The scheme focuses on supporting small and marginal farmers to enhance agricultural output.
benefits: Provision of Manure and Fertilizers Manures and fertilizers will be provided to eligible cultivators. Assistance is given in kind and not in cash. Subsidy and Loan Component Assistance is provided on a 40% subsidy and 60% loan basis. Crop-wise Fertilizer Quantity (in Nutrients) Paddy: Nitrogen 110, Phosphorus 60, Potash 60 Maize: Nitrogen 100, Phosphorus 50 Groundnut: Nitrogen 25, Phosphorus 50 Castor: Nitrogen 20, Phosphorus 20 Wheat: Nitrogen 100, Phosphorus 50, Potash 50 Sugarcane: Nitrogen 250, Phosphorus 125, Potash 125 Green Manuring Support kg of seeds per hectare will be supplied for green manuring. Loan Recovery Provision The loan amount shall be recovered in one instalment after completion of the season. In case of default, penal interest at 2½% will be charged. Recovery will be made as arrears of land revenue.

name: Sub-Mission on Agricultural Extension (SMAE)
description: The scheme “Sub-Mission on Agricultural Extension” is implemented by the Department of Agriculture, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to promote the adoption of modern and scientific farming practices among farmers across the state through continuous training, practical demonstrations, and exposure visits.
benefits: Farmers are periodically trained in modern agricultural practices. Agricultural exhibitions, fairs, and farmer seminars are organized, and farmers are also taken on exposure visits to enhance their knowledge and skills. Additionally, farmer–scientist interactions are conducted to facilitate the exchange of ideas and innovations. Farm School: Free seeds, fertilizers, and chemicals are provided to farmers for demonstration purposes, and training is imparted to a group of 30 farmers at each Farm School. Progressive farmers who demonstrate excellence and innovation in agriculture are recognized and rewarded. Along with a certificate, the following cash awards are given: Block Level: ₹10,000 – Kisan Shri District Level: ₹25,000 – Kisan Bhushan State Level: ₹50,000 – Kisan Ratna

faqs.question: Who is eligible for this scheme?
faqs.answer: All farmers who are residents of Uttarakhand, possess cultivable land, and whose names are registered in the land records are eligible.

faqs.question: What kind of training is provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers receive periodic training in modern agricultural practices, including crop management, soil health, irrigation techniques, and sustainable farming methods.

faqs.question: Are exposure visits part of the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes. Farmers are taken on exposure visits to model farms, research institutions, and other areas to learn best agricultural practices.

faqs.question: What are Farm Schools under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Farm Schools provide practical demonstrations where free seeds, fertilizers, and chemicals are supplied. Training is conducted for groups of 30 farmers to showcase new techniques and innovations.

faqs.question: How are progressive farmers recognized?
faqs.answer: Farmers demonstrating excellence in agriculture are rewarded with certificates and cash awards at block, district, and state levels.

faqs.question: How can a farmer apply for training or exposure visits?
faqs.answer: A farmer can submit a written request to the Nyaya Panchayat, Assistant Agriculture Officer at district or block level, Agriculture and Soil Conservation Officer at unit level, or Chief Agriculture Officer/Project Director (ATMA) at district level.

faqs.question: How is the Kisan Award application process conducted?
faqs.answer: Advertisements are published in newspapers by district Agriculture Offices. Applications can then be obtained from ADO Agriculture, Development Block Agriculture Office, or District Level Agriculture Office.

faqs.question: Who gives the final approval for the Kisan Award?
faqs.answer: The final approval is given in the ATMA Governing Body Meeting, chaired by the District Magistrate.

name: Sub-mission on Breed Development of Livestock and Poultry
description: Launched in the Financial Year 2014-15, the scheme "National Livestock Mission" by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, aims towards employment generation, entrepreneurship development, increase in per animal productivity and thus targeting increased production of meat, goat milk, egg and wool under the umbrella scheme "Development Programme". The excess production will help in the export earnings after meeting the domestic demands. The concept of the NLM Scheme is to develop the entrepreneur in order to create the forward and backward linkage for the produce available in the unorganized sector and to link with the organized sector. Key Objectives Employment generation through entrepreneurship development in small ruminant, poultry and piggery sector & Fodder sector. Increase of per animal productivity through breed improvement. Increase in production of meat, egg, goat milk, wool and fodder. Increasing availability of fodder and feed to substantially reduce the demand – through strengthening the fodder seed supply chain and availability of certified fodder seeds. Encouraging establishment of fodder processing units to reduce the demand supply gap. The National Livestock Mission has the following three Sub-Missions: Sub-mission on Breed Development of Livestock and Poultry Sub-mission on Feed and Fodder Development Sub Mission on Innovation and Extension "Sub-mission on Breed Development of Livestock and Poultry" Proposes to bring sharp focus on entrepreneurship development and breed improvement in poultry, sheep, goat and piggery by providing the incentivization to the Individual, FPOs, FCOs JLGs, SHGs, Section 8 companies for entrepreneurship development and also to the State Government for breed improvement infrastructure.
benefits: Capital Subsidy Provision One-time 50% capital subsidy offered for total project cost. Maximum subsidy capped at ₹25,00,000 per unit. faqs.question: Are there any special considerations for regions like the Northeast or hilly states, and how does the funding pattern differ for these areas?
faqs.answer: Yes, regions like the Northeast and Himalayan states receive higher central share funding (up to 90%) compared to other states. UTs receive 100% central assistance.

faqs.question: How can beneficiaries track the status of their applications, and is there a system for receiving real-time updates?
faqs.answer: Applicants can track their application status through the NLM portal. Notifications and updates are provided via email or SMS to ensure transparency.

faqs.question: What types of declarations or undertakings must applicants submit to comply with scheme requirements?
faqs.answer: Applicants must submit undertakings confirming compliance with guidelines, including declarations on the proper use of funds and adherence to integrity norms.

faqs.question: Are there any specific initiatives under this scheme for women or marginalized groups in livestock farming?
faqs.answer: Special provisions like higher subsidies or targeted outreach are often extended to marginalized groups, including women, SCs, and STs, as per government norms.

faqs.question: Does the scheme include provisions for grievance redressal, and how can beneficiaries report issues related to their applications or funding?
faqs.answer: Yes, beneficiaries can report grievances through the State Implementing Agency or the NLM portal. A grievance mechanism ensures timely resolution of issues.

faqs.question: Can applicants apply for the scheme in self-financing mode, and what additional requirements must they fulfill in this case?
faqs.answer: Yes, self-financed applicants are required to submit a bank guarantee valid for three years, covering the remaining project cost beyond the subsidy sought.

faqs.question: What kind of infrastructure or equipment is eligible for funding under the subsidy provided by this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme covers infrastructure like parent farms, hatcheries, and mother units, along with equipment for breeding and livestock management as detailed in the guidelines.

faqs.question: Who are the target beneficiaries of this scheme, and how does it aim to uplift rural and small-scale livestock entrepreneurs?
faqs.answer: Target beneficiaries include small-scale livestock farmers, rural entrepreneurs, SHGs, and FPOs. The scheme aims to organize unstructured farming sectors into sustainable business models and increase profitability.

faqs.question: What are the types of benefits provided under this scheme, and how do they support both monetary and non-monetary needs of the applicants?
faqs.answer: The scheme offers monetary benefits like capital subsidies and non-monetary support such as training, capacity building, and access to breed improvement resources.

faqs.question: Are there any deadlines for applying to the Sub-Mission on Breed Development of Livestock and Poultry, and where can one find this information?
faqs.answer: Deadlines for applications are announced periodically through State Implementing Agencies and the NLM portal. Applicants are advised to check these platforms regularly for updates.

faqs.question: How is the subsidy disbursed to beneficiaries, and what conditions must be met to receive the installments?
faqs.answer: The subsidy is provided in two installments: the first after the loan's first disbursement and infrastructure investment of 25%, and the second after project completion and verification by the State Implementing Agency.

faqs.question: What steps are involved in the selection process, and how are applications evaluated and approved under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Applications are initially verified by the State Implementing Agency. Once recommended, they are assessed by financial institutions for loan approval. Finally, the Project Approval Committee reviews and approves the proposals.

faqs.question: If an applicant does not own land but has a lease agreement for the project, can they still be considered eligible for funding under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, applicants with valid lease agreements are eligible, provided they submit documentation confirming the lease duration, land-use permissions, and ownership by the lessor.

faqs.question: What are the essential documents an applicant must submit to apply for the Sub-Mission on Breed Development of Livestock and Poultry?
faqs.answer: Applicants need to provide proof of identity, project proposals, land ownership or lease documents, financial documents such as loan sanction letters or bank guarantees, and KYC details.

faqs.question: Are there any specific components or expenses that are not covered under the subsidy provided by this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme does not provide subsidies for the purchase of land, rent or lease costs, working capital, personal vehicles, or recurring expenses.

name: State Millet Mission
description: The “State Millet Mission” launched by the Department of Agriculture, Government of Uttarakhand, aims to promote millet cultivation, ensure fair prices for farmers, and strengthen food security in the state. The mission seeks to support farmers, particularly in mountain districts, by procuring millet crops like Mandua and Jhangora at the minimum support price through cooperative groups.
benefits: Under the mission, in the first phase, 16,820 metric tonnes of Mandua and Jhangora are being purchased from farmers’ fields at the minimum support price through cooperative groups by the Cooperative Department. Under the National Food Security Act, the Government of India will distribute 1 kilogram per month through the Public Distribution System (ration card) via the Food and Supplies Department in four districts: Udham Singh Nagar, Haridwar, Nainital, and Dehradun. Farmers’ groups, LCs/LCFs, or PACS at established procurement centers are free to offer Mandua for sale. To encourage participation, an incentive of ₹150/- per quintal is provided. Once the PACS accepts the millet crops from the groups, payment will be made through RTGS/NEFT within a maximum of 72 hours.
eligibility: All farmers from the mountain districts of Uttarakhand are eligible..

faqs.question: Which millets are included under the mission?
faqs.answer: The mission primarily focuses on Mandua (finger millet) and Jhangora (barnyard millet).

faqs.question: Who can participate in the mission?
faqs.answer: All farmers from mountain districts of Uttarakhand are eligible to participate.

faqs.question: Is there an application process to join the mission?
faqs.answer: No, there is no application process. Farmers need to make their produce available at the designated purchase centers.

faqs.question: How will the millets be procured?
faqs.answer: Millets are procured from farmers through cooperative groups at the minimum support price (MSP) at established purchase centers at the farmer group/LC/LCF or PACS level.

faqs.question: How will the payment be made to farmers?
faqs.answer: Payments are made through PACS via RTGS/NEFT within 72 hours after the purchase of millets.

faqs.question: Are there any incentives for farmer groups?
faqs.answer: Yes, an incentive of ₹150 per quintal is provided to encourage farmer groups to participate in the purchase process.

faqs.question: Where can farmers sell their millets?
faqs.answer: Millets can be sold at purchase centers established at the farmer group/LC/LCF level or at the PACS level.

name: Scheme to Provide Assistance in Cow Maintenance Expenses to Farmers Practicing Completely Natural Farming Based on Indigenous Cows
department: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department
description: The “Scheme to Provide Assistance in Cow Maintenance Expenses to Farmers Practicing Completely Natural Farming Based on Indigenous Cows” launched by the Department of Agriculture, Farmers Welfare & Co-operation, Government of Gujarat, aims to encourage and support farmers who engage in natural farming practices that rely on indigenous cows. By covering part of the maintenance expenses for one native cow, the government promotes eco-friendly agriculture, reduces the cost of cultivation, and ensures better soil health.
benefits: ₹900/- per month (₹10,800/- annually) assistance for maintaining one indigenous cow. > Note: The benefit is available only once.
eligibility: The applicant must be a farmer.. The applicant must be practicing natural farming on at least 1 acre (40 guntha) of land.. The applicant must own a native (indigenous) cow with an identification tag.. Note:. Priority will be given to farmers practicing natural agriculture and master trainers who have received training in natural agriculture from certified trainers.. Assistance to one beneficiary per account (as per sample number 8-A)..
documents: Proof of natural farming on 1 acre (40 guntha) land. Aadhar Card of the applicant. Bank account details. Proof of ownership of an indigenous cow with an identification tag. Training certificate (if the applicant is a trained master farmer). Certificate of existence of the cow. Any other documents as required.
Proof of natural farming on 1 acre (40 guntha) land.
Proof of ownership of an indigenous cow with an identification tag.
Training certificate (if the applicant is a trained master farmer).
Certificate of existence of the cow.

faqs.question: What is the objective of the "Scheme to Provide Assistance in Cow Maintenance Expenses to Farmers Practicing Completely Natural Farming Based on Indigenous Cows" scheme?
faqs.answer: The purpose of this scheme is to financially support farmers who practice natural farming using indigenous cows by providing maintenance assistance for one native cow.

faqs.question: How much financial assistance is provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides ₹900/- per month, totaling ₹10,800/- annually, as assistance for maintaining one indigenous cow.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to benefit from this scheme?
faqs.answer: Farmers who are practicing natural farming on at least one acre of land and own a native cow with an identification tag are eligible for the scheme.

faqs.question: Can a farmer receive the benefit more than once?
faqs.answer: No, the assistance under this scheme is provided only once to each eligible beneficiary.

faqs.question: Is training in natural farming required to apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: While not mandatory, preference is given to farmers who have received certified training in natural farming or who are recognized as master trainers.

faqs.question: What happens if the cow does not have an identification tag at the time of application?
faqs.answer: If the cow is not tagged, the farmer must ensure the tag is attached within seven days, failing which the application may be rejected.

faqs.question: Where can a farmer apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: A farmer can apply for the scheme through the official iKhedut (https://ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in/)portal.

faqs.question: What is the process of verification after application submission?
faqs.answer: After submission, the documents are verified by BTM/ATM and further validated by a three-member field verification team including officials like Gram Sevak or Horticulture Officer.

faqs.question: Is the assistance applicable for cows of all breeds?
faqs.answer: No, the assistance is strictly provided for indigenous (native) cow breeds only.

faqs.question: Can two farmers from the same family apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: No, only one beneficiary per account or household is allowed to receive assistance under the scheme.

name: Scheme for Management and Purchase of Bulls Provided for Breeding of State Gir/ Kankarej Breed
department: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department
description: The “Scheme for Management and Purchase of Bulls Provided for Breeding of State Gir/ Kankarej Breed” launched by the Department of Agriculture, Farmers Welfare & Co-operation, Government of Gujarat, aims to support pure breeding of Gir and Kankrej cows by providing financial assistance for purchasing and maintaining high-quality bulls. The goal is to enhance calf quality and gradually increase milk production in rural areas by promoting native breed development.
benefits: In Case the bull is provided by the Board: ₹1,18,000/- in the first year.- In Case the bull is purchased by the organization: ₹1,43,000/- in the first year.- Maintenance support: ₹64,800/- for the second and third year. > Note: Assistance provided for three years per eligible organization.
eligibility: A Gram Panchayat or a Gaushala registered must be registered under the Charity Act.. The Gram Panchayat or a Gaushala must have a minimum of 100 breedable cows.. Note: If there is not sufficient number of breeding cows in a single village, then the breeding cows of the neighboring villages should be covered and a guarantee should be given..
documents: Proof of registration under the Charity Act (for Gaushalas). Estimation document. Village map or area plan. Any other documents as required.
Proof of registration under the Charity Act (for Gaushalas).

faqs.question: What is the objective of the "Scheme for Management and Purchase of Bulls Provided for Breeding of State Gir/ Kankarej Breed"?
faqs.answer: The objective of the scheme is to promote the breeding of Gir and Kankrej cows by providing high-quality bulls, thereby improving the quality of calves and gradually increasing milk production in Gujarat.

faqs.question: Who can apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Only Gram Panchayats and registered Gaushalas under the Charity Act with a minimum of 100 breedable cows are eligible to apply.

faqs.question: Can an individual farmer apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: No, individual farmers are not eligible. The scheme is specifically meant for Gram Panchayats and registered Gaushalas.

faqs.question: What is the minimum requirement for breedable cows to qualify for the scheme?
faqs.answer: The applying organization must have at least 100 breedable cows to qualify for assistance under the scheme.

faqs.question: Can neighboring villages combine their cow count to meet the eligibility?
faqs.answer: Yes, if a single village does not have enough breedable cows, neighboring villages can combine their numbers, provided a written guarantee is submitted.

faqs.question: What kind of financial assistance is provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides ₹1,18,000/- in the first year if the bull is supplied by the Board, or ₹1,43,000/- if the bull is purchased by the organization. Additionally, ₹64,800/- is provided for management in the second and third years.

faqs.question: For how many years is the assistance provided?
faqs.answer: The assistance under this scheme is provided for a maximum period of three years.

faqs.question: How can an eligible organization apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Applications must be submitted online through the iKhedut (https://ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in/)portal, followed by submission of printed applications with signatures and required documents to the board.

faqs.question: Is there a deadline for submitting the hard copy of the application?
faqs.answer: Yes, the printed and signed application form along with all required documents must be submitted to the board within 30 days of the online application.

faqs.question: Can the bull be purchased if it is not available from the Board?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the bull is not available from the Board, the organization may purchase it and will receive financial assistance accordingly.

faqs.question: Who approves the application at the district level?
faqs.answer: The Nodal Officer of the Gujarat Gauseva and Gauchar Vikas Board (GGVB) at the district level verifies and stamps the application.

name: Solar Home System (Manohar Jyoti)
description: The scheme "Solar Home System (Manohar Jyoti)" by the Renewable Energy Department, Government of Haryana aims to provide reliable, clean, and affordable electricity to rural households and promote the use of renewable energy across the state. The scheme primarily benefits families with a valid Pariwar Pahichan Patra (PPP), offering them subsidized solar home lighting systems to reduce their dependence on conventional electricity sources and promote environmental sustainability.
benefits: Subsidy for General Category: A subsidy of ₹15,000/- per solar home system is provided to eligible families under the general category. - Subsidy under SCSP: A subsidy covering 90% of the cost is provided to Scheduled Caste families under SCSP component.
eligibility: The applicant should be a resident of Haryana.. The applicant should possess a valid Pariwar Pahichan Patra (PPP)..

faqs.question: What is the main objective of the "Solar Home System (Manohar Jyoti)"?
faqs.answer: The primary objective of the "Solar Home System (Manohar Jyoti)" is to promote renewable energy by providing subsidized solar lighting systems to Haryana families, especially in rural areas, in order to improve energy access and reduce dependency on conventional power sources.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Any family residing in the state of Haryana and possessing a valid Pariwar Pahichan Patra (PPP) is eligible to apply for the "Solar Home System (Manohar Jyoti)".

faqs.question: What type of benefit is provided under the "Solar Home System (Manohar Jyoti)"?
faqs.answer: Under the "Solar Home System (Manohar Jyoti)", the benefit provided is a subsidized solar home lighting system, which includes a solar panel and lighting accessories for domestic use.

faqs.question: What is the subsidy amount offered to general category applicants under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The subsidy amount offered to eligible general category families under the "Solar Home System (Manohar Jyoti)" is ₹15,000/- per solar home system.

faqs.question: What is the subsidy rate offered to Scheduled Caste families under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Scheduled Caste families applying under the Scheduled Caste Sub Plan (SCSP) component of the "Solar Home System (Manohar Jyoti)" are eligible to receive a 90% subsidy on the cost of the solar home system.

faqs.question: Which department is responsible for implementing the scheme?
faqs.answer: The "Solar Home System (Manohar Jyoti)" is implemented by the Renewable Energy Department, Government of Haryana.

faqs.question: Is there any income limit for applicants?
faqs.answer: No, as per the guidelines, there is no income limit for the applicants.

faqs.question: Can residents of urban areas also apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Any resident of Haryana, whether from urban or rural areas, who meets the eligibility criteria and has a valid Pariwar Pahichan Patra (PPP), may apply.

faqs.question: What is the process for applying to the "Solar Home System (Manohar Jyoti)"?
faqs.answer: The applicants may visit the Antyodaya-SARAL Portal (https://saralharyana.gov.in/) to apply for the scheme.

faqs.question: Is it mandatory to submit the Pariwar Pahichan Patra (PPP) while applying for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is mandatory for the applicant to submit a valid Pariwar Pahichan Patra (PPP) as it serves as the primary eligibility document for applying to the "Solar Home System (Manohar Jyoti)".

faqs.question: What is the offline process for applying to the "Solar Home System (Manohar Jyoti)"?
faqs.answer: To apply for the "Solar Home System (Manohar Jyoti)", the applicant may visit the nearest Atal Seva Kendra (Common Service Centre).

faqs.question: Is there any fee applicable for applying this scheme through Atal Seva Kendra (Common Service Centre) ?
faqs.answer: Yes, a nominal service fee of ₹10/- is charged by the Common Service Centre for the application.

name: Seed Multiplication Scheme of Paddy, Millets, Pulses, Oilseeds and Cotton
description: The “Seed Multiplication Scheme of Paddy, Millets, Pulses, Oilseeds, and Cotton” by the Agriculture-Farmers Welfare Department, Tamil Nadu, offers subsidies to farmers to produce seeds under contract with the Department of Agriculture. Farmers receive training, source seeds, and guidelines for maintaining seed quality. After quality checks and processing, farmers are paid based on the quality of seeds produced. A 90% Minimum Support Price payment is made during processing, with the remainder settled after quality certification.
benefits: Premium: On seeds ranges from ₹1/- to ₹3/- per kg. - Foundation Class Seeds: The premium is between 7.5% to 30% over the Local Market Rate per kg, depending on the type of oil seed. - For Certified Class Seeds: The premium is between 5% to 20% over the Local Market Rate per kg, based on the specific oil seed. - Training: The farmer so desirous of enrolling himself/herself will be given a training by the authorities concerned at the beginning of each year
eligibility: The beneficiary should be a Farmer.. The beneficiary should be a resident of Tamil Nadu.. The beneficiary should produce and supply seeds for the Department of Agriculture on a contract basis.. The seed Farms should be registered by the Seed Producer viz., the Assistant Director of Agriculture of the respective Blocks.. Field Run Produce has to satisfy the standards of physical/genetic purity, moisture levels and germination percentage as prescribed in the Certification standards..
documents: Proof of identity (Aadhar card, Voter ID). Land ownership documents or lease agreement. Proof of Seed production and supply to the Department of Agriculture on Contract basis. Seed Farm Registration Details. Certification Tag issued by the Department of Seed Certification. Caste Certificate (for SC/ST applicants). Any other documents (if required).
Proof of identity (Aadhar card, Voter ID).
Land ownership documents or lease agreement.
Proof of Seed production and supply to the Department of Agriculture on Contract basis.
Certification Tag issued by the Department of Seed Certification.

faqs.question: What is the “Seed Multiplication Scheme of Paddy, Millets, Pulses, Oilseeds and Cotton” Scheme?
faqs.answer: The "Seed Multiplication Scheme of Paddy, Millets, Pulses, Oilseeds, and Cotton" offers subsidies to farmers to produce seeds under contract with the Department of Agriculture.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to enroll and register their seed farms under this program?
faqs.answer: All farmers who produce and supply seeds to the Department of Agriculture on a contract basis are eligible. Preference is given to farm women groups, farmers Interest Groups, and separate allocation is provided to SC/ST seed growers.

faqs.question: What is the process for enrolling in this seed farm program?
faqs.answer: Interested farmers must enroll themselves at the beginning of each year. They will receive training from the authorities concerned.

faqs.question: How can farmers obtain the source seed required for their farms?
faqs.answer: The Department of Agriculture will supply the source seed through Agricultural Extension Centres upon payment of the seed cost as per the fixed sale price.

faqs.question: What should farmers do to ensure the quality of their seeds?
faqs.answer: Farmers must follow the guidelines provided by field-level functionaries or Seed Certification officers to maintain quality.

faqs.question: How are seed farms registered?
faqs.answer: Seed farms should be registered by the Assistant Director of Agriculture of the respective blocks upon payment of the requisite fees.

faqs.question: What is the “Field Run Produce” and how is it assessed?
faqs.answer: "Field Run Produce" is the seed produce that meets the field standards during the crop period. It must satisfy standards of physical/genetic purity, moisture levels, and germination percentage as prescribed in the certification standards.

faqs.question: What happens after the seed is moved to the Seed Processing Unit?
faqs.answer: The seed is processed in the presence of the Seed Certification Officer. Samples are drawn and sent to a Seed Testing Lab for quality testing.

faqs.question: What if the seed lot fails to meet the certification standards?
faqs.answer: If the seed lot fails, the farmer must repay the entire advance paid to them before getting back their stock.

faqs.question: Who bears the transport cost for moving the seed to the Seed Processing Unit?
faqs.answer: The farmer is responsible for the transport cost to the Seed Processing Unit.

name: Sub mission on Seeds and Planting Material

faqs.question: Who can benefit from this scheme?
faqs.answer: All categories of farmers, State Agricultural Universities (SAUs), Farmers' Producer Organizations (FPOs), Co-operative enterprises, and Government enterprises are eligible beneficiaries.

faqs.answer: Under the Seed Village Programme, help is provided for distributing foundation and certified seed needed for 1 acre of land.

faqs.question: How is support given for improving seed quality control laboratories?
faqs.answer: Support for strengthening seed quality control laboratories is given on a project basis.

faqs.question: Which organizations can get support for strengthening seed quality control laboratories?
faqs.answer: State Agricultural Universities (SAUs), Farmers' Producer Organizations (FPOs), Co-operative enterprises, and Government enterprises can get this support.

faqs.question: Are Farmers' Producer Organizations (FPOs) allowed to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, Farmers' Producer Organizations (FPOs) are among the eligible applicants for this scheme.

faqs.question: How is support given for setting up seed infrastructure facilities (SPP)?
faqs.answer: Support for the creation of seed infrastructure facility (SPP) is provided on a project basis.

faqs.question: Are State Agricultural Universities (SAUs) eligible to receive benefits from this scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, State Agricultural Universities (SAUs) are eligible to receive benefits, especially for strengthening seed quality control laboratories.

faqs.question: Can farmers apply for the Nursery Premium for multiple hectares of sugarcane nursery?

faqs.question: Are there any restrictions on how farmers can utilize the Nursery Premium?

faqs.question: Is the Nursery Premium a one-time payment, or is it provided at different stages of the nursery development?

faqs.answer: The scheme guidelines do not mention any opening date or closing date for applications.

name: Scheme for the Welfare of Schedule Caste Families in Fisheries Sector: Subsidy on 2nd Year to 5th Year Lease Money

name: "Subsidy for Orthodox & Speciality Tea Unit for Plant & Machinery" under the "Assam Tea Industries Special Incentives Scheme"
description: Launched in 2020, the scheme "Assam Tea Industries Special Incentives Scheme (ATISIS)" by the Finance (Institutional Finance) Department, Government of Assam, aims to ensure long-term financial sustainability of the Tea industry and to incentivize manufacturers to move from Crush, Tear, Curl tea to Orthodox tea production. The scheme is implemented by the Finance Department and the Industries & Commerce Department, Government of Assam, through multiple implementing agencies, including banks and the District Industries & Commerce Centre. The applications for this scheme are accepted online through a dedicated portal with a Direct Benefit Transfer mechanism for reimbursement.
benefits: Benefit Amount: 25% of the cost of Plant & Machinery. Maximum Amount: ₹30,00,000/- or 25% of actual cost, whichever is less. Validity Period: Units starting production on or after 01-04-2020 and before 31-03-2028. Claim Period: Within 12 months of the start of commercial manufacturing activities. Disbursement Mode: Direct Benefit Transfer as reimbursement. Post-Selection Condition: Manufacturing unit shall not sell the machinery before expiry of at least 5 years from start of manufacturing.
eligibility: General Eligibility. The applicant must be a tea plantation across all sizes.. The applicant must be a tea manufacturing unit manufacturing Crush, Tear, Curl Tea, Orthodox Tea, or Speciality tea including Green tea, Oolong Tea, White tea, Yellow tea and Purple tea.. The applicant must be located entirely in Assam.. The applicant must not have any part of the plantation or manufacturing facility located outside the State of Assam.. Plant &. Machinery Subsidy Specific Eligibility. The applicant must be manufacturing Orthodox tea, Green tea, White tea, Oolong tea, Singhpo tea, Purple Tea, Yellow tea or other Speciality tea (not manufactured through Crush, Tear, Curl process).. The applicant must have started production on or after 01-04-2020 and before 31-03-2028.. The applicant must be either an entirely new unit or an existing unit which has expanded its capacity by creating additional infrastructure for production of Orthodox and Speciality Tea.. The applicant must use all new machinery (no subsidy available on second hand machinery or parts of a machine).. The applicant must not have claimed any similar subsidy under any other scheme of the Government of India or the State..

faqs.answer: The scheme aims to establish Farmer Support Centers and computerize market committees to enhance transparency, efficiency, and accessibility to government schemes for farmers.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Registered market committees in Gujarat are eligible to apply for assistance under this scheme.

faqs.question: How much financial assistance is provided for setting up a Farmer Support Center?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides 50% of the cost incurred, including employee salaries, or a maximum of [?]2,00,000/-, whichever is lower.

faqs.question: What financial support is available for computerization of market committees?
faqs.answer: The state government will develop a central software system, and market committees in "K" and "D" categories will receive 90% assistance (up to [?]2,00,000/-) for purchasing 2 computers, 2 printers, and software through the GEM Portal.

faqs.question: Can an individual farmer apply for assistance under this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, individual farmers are not eligible. The scheme is specifically designed for market committees.

faqs.question: Is it mandatory to purchase hardware and software from a specific source?
faqs.answer: Yes, all hardware and software purchases must be made through the GEM Portal to qualify for financial assistance.

faqs.question: Can a market committee apply for both a Farmer Support Center and computerization assistance?
faqs.answer: Yes, a market committee meeting the eligibility criteria can apply for both components of the scheme.

faqs.question: Can a market committee from another state apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, the scheme is exclusively for market committees within Gujarat.

faqs.question: How can a market committee apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: A market committee must submit a proposal to the Deputy Director and District Registrar, Cooperative Societies, through the Director, Agricultural Market and Rural Economy, Gandhinagar. The proposal is then forwarded to the Agriculture, Farmers Welfare, and Cooperation Department for approval.

faqs.question: Where can market committees get more information about the scheme?
faqs.answer: Market committees can contact the Agriculture, Farmers Welfare, and Cooperation Department or visit the nearest District Registrar, Cooperative Societies office for more details.

name: Sardar Patel Agriculture Research Award
department: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department
description: The scheme “Sardar Patel Agriculture Research Award” was launched by the Department of Agriculture, Farmers Welfare & Co-operation, Government of Gujarat on 30.10.1995. In the field of Agriculture, this scheme has been set up by the state government for the farmers of the state who produce good quality yield by their innovative idea and by their own courage as well as research new technique in the agriculture field. The scheme has been implemented by the State government to honour and appreciate farmers’ contribution to the development of agriculture to encourage and accelerate agricultural production. This award is given in five different categories/subjects. Different categories of the award are as below: SUB-1: Develop a new variety by farmers' own innovative skill in all the main crops of Gujarat like Cereal, Oilseed crop, pulse, cotton, sugarcane, tobacco as well as Horticulture crops and spices and condiments, etc., and introducing successfully new crops instead of traditional crops grown in the state. - SUB-2: Achievement in model agriculture by producing higher yield through modern irrigation methods with water management and utilization of irrigation water as well as raising the water table of well/tube well by recharging well/tube well with harvesting rainwater - SUB-3: Achievement for success in dry farming by developing techniques for drought - SUB-4: Develop new methods of Integrated Pest Management for different crops - SUB-5: Development of innovative farm equipment for different methods, such as cultivation, inter-cultivation, weeding, spacing, harvesting, threshing, or other types of farming.
benefits: In this scheme every year ₹51000/- is awarded with the shawl and certificate to the farmer who gains the first position in each category and also first five farmers from each category are appreciated with the shawl & certificate. In addition to this, farmers as in the form of encouragement are appreciated by giving shawls & certificates for the special work done in the field of beekeeping, poultry farming, fisheries, etc.
eligibility: The farmer should be a permanent resident of Gujarat State.. The farmers either Male or Female who possesses Agriculture land in Gujarat are eligible to apply for this scheme..
documents: size photographs Bank Details i.e. Copy of Bank Passbook/Cheque Residence proof Basis (evidence) for land (If applicable) Caste Certificate (If applicable) Colour photographs of work done Audio/Video of work done Copy of award/other certificates received
